statement: Under § 210.7-05, Schedule V, valuation and qualifying accounts, is the schedule prescribed by § 210.12-09, and it shall be filed in support of valuation and qualifying accounts included in the balance sheet, with a cross-reference to § 210.4-02.
quote: Schedule V—Valuation and qualifying accounts. The schedule prescribed by § 210.12-09 shall be filed in support of valuation and qualifying accounts included in the balance sheet (see § 210.4-02).

statement: For a complete termination, the no-cost settlement agreement text says the supplemental agreement either modifies the contract to reflect a no-cost settlement with respect to the dated Notice of Termination or, if the contract was not previously terminated, terminates the contract in its entirety.
quote: (a) This supplemental agreement __________ [insert “modifies the contract to reflect a no-cost settlement agreement with respect to the Notice of Termination dated __________” or, if not previously terminated, “terminates the contract in its entirety”.]

statement: In the partial-termination no-cost settlement text, the parties specify the terminated portion of the contract by line item numbers, descriptions, quantity terminated, unit and total price of the terminated items, and any other explanation needed to avoid uncertainty or misunderstanding.
quote: (1) The terminated portion of the contract is as follows: [Specify (i) line item numbers, (ii) descriptions, (iii) quantity terminated, (iv) unit and total price of terminated items, and (v) any other explanation necessary to avoid uncertainty or misunderstanding.]

statement: The partial-termination no-cost settlement text says that nothing in its paragraph (b)(2) affects any other covenants, terms, or conditions of the contract.
quote: Nothing in this paragraph affects any other covenants, terms, or conditions of the contract.

statement: A settlement of reservations follows an earlier supplemental agreement that settled the termination of the contract and excepted from the settlement certain items, including the items listed in the paragraph (b) of the settlement-of-reservations text.
quote: Supplemental Agreement No. ________, dated ________, was executed to reflect the settlement of the termination of this contract. The supplemental agreement excepted from the settlement certain items described in the agreement including the items described in paragraph (b) below.

statement: The settlement-of-reservations text is inserted in Block 14 of SF 30.
quote: [Insert the following in Block 14 of SF 30 for settlement of reservations.]

statement: Paragraph (a) names section 1372 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 1994 and section 824 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 1997 as the two provisions it goes on to describe; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CLS-0294.
quote: (a) Section 1372 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 1994 (Pub. L. 103-160) and section 824 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 1997 (Pub. L. 104-201)

statement: The section lists, as examples of items considered incidental to the place of performance, office space, desks, chairs, telephones, computers, and fax machines.
quote: Items considered to be incidental to the place of performance include, for example, office space, desks, chairs, telephones, computers, and fax machines.

statement: The definitions in the section apply to the terms as they are used in this part. The quoted sentence is incomplete here and the definitions begin in CL-CLS-0328.
quote: As used in this part—

statement: Production scrap may have value when re-melted or reprocessed, for example textile and metal clippings, borings, and faulty castings and forgings.
quote: Production scrap may have value when re-melted or reprocessed, e.g., textile and metal clippings, borings, and faulty castings and forgings.

statement: The section gives as examples of sensitive property weapons, ammunition, explosives, controlled substances, radioactive materials, hazardous materials or wastes, or precious metals.
quote: Examples include weapons, ammunition, explosives, controlled substances, radioactive materials, hazardous materials or wastes, or precious metals.

statement: For special test equipment with commercial components, agencies shall complete the screening required by paragraph (a) of the section.
quote: Special test equipment with commercial components. (i) Agencies shall complete the screening required by paragraph (a) of this section.

statement: If an agency has no further need for the property and the contractor has not expressed an interest in using or acquiring the property by annotating the inventory disposal schedule, the plant clearance officer shall forward the inventory disposal schedule to the GSA regional office. The quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CLS-0459.
quote: If an agency has no further need for the property and the contractor has not expressed an interest in using or acquiring the property by annotating the inventory disposal schedule, the plant clearance officer shall forward the inventory disposal schedule to the GSA regional office

statement: The GSA regional office to which the plant clearance officer forwards the inventory disposal schedule is the one that serves the region in which the property is located.
quote: that serves the region in which the property is located.

statement: If the contractor has expressed an interest in using the property on another Government contract, the plant clearance officer shall contact the contracting officer for that contract.
quote: If the contractor has expressed an interest in using the property on another Government contract, the plant clearance officer shall contact the contracting officer for that contract.

statement: If the contracting officer concurs with the proposed use, the contracting officer for the contract under which the property is accountable shall transfer the property's accountability to that contract.
quote: If the contracting officer concurs with the proposed use, the contracting officer for the contract under which the property is accountable shall transfer the property's accountability to that contract.

statement: If the contracting officer does not concur with the proposed use, the plant clearance officer shall deny the contractor's request and shall continue the screening process.
quote: If the contracting officer does not concur with the proposed use, the plant clearance officer shall deny the contractor's request and shall continue the screening process.

statement: If the property is contractor-acquired or -produced, the contractor or subcontractor has expressed an interest in acquiring it, and no other party expresses an interest during agency or GSA screening, the property may be sold to the contractor or subcontractor at acquisition cost.
quote: If the property is contractor-acquired or -produced, and the contractor or subcontractor has expressed an interest in acquiring the property, and no other party expresses an interest during agency or GSA screening, the property may be sold to the contractor or subcontractor at acquisition cost.

statement: Agencies shall report all excess printing equipment to the Public Printer, Government Publishing Office, at the street address the paragraph gives, after screening within the agency, with a cross-reference to title 44 of the United States Code, section 312.
quote: Agencies shall report all excess printing equipment to the Public Printer, Government Publishing Office, 732 North Capitol Street, NW., Washington, DC 20401, after screening within the agency (see 44 U.S.C. 312).

statement: If the Public Printer does not express a need for the equipment within 21 days, the agency shall submit the report to GSA for further use and donation screening as described in paragraph (a) of the section.
quote: If the Public Printer does not express a need for the equipment within 21 days, the agency shall submit the report to GSA for further use and donation screening as described in paragraph (a) of this section.

statement: Non-nuclear hazardous materials, hazardous wastes, and classified items shall be screened in accordance with agency procedures, and non-nuclear hazardous materials are to be reported to GSA if the agency has no requirement for them.
quote: Non-nuclear hazardous materials, hazardous wastes, and classified items. These items shall be screened in accordance with agency procedures. Report non-nuclear hazardous materials to GSA if the agency has no requirement for them.

statement: Certain nuclear materials are subject to the regulatory controls of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, and contracting activities shall screen excess nuclear materials in the categories listed in the paragraph; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and the categories follow in CL-CLS-0468, CL-CLS-0469 and CL-CLS-0470.
quote: The possession, use, and transfer of certain nuclear materials are subject to the regulatory controls of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC). Contracting activities shall screen excess nuclear materials in the following categories:

statement: By-product material, one of the nuclear material categories to be screened, is any radioactive material (except special nuclear material) yielded in or made radioactive by exposure to the radiation incident to producing or using special nuclear material.
quote: By-product material. Any radioactive material (except special nuclear material) yielded in or made radioactive by exposure to the radiation incident to producing or using special nuclear material.

statement: Source material, one of the nuclear material categories to be screened, is uranium or thorium, or any combination thereof, in any physical or chemical form, or ores that contain by weight one-twentieth of 1 percent (0.05 percent) or more of uranium, thorium, or any combination thereof; it does not include special nuclear material.
quote: Source material. Uranium or thorium, or any combination thereof, in any physical or chemical form; or ores that contain by weight one-twentieth of 1 percent (0.05 percent) or more of uranium, thorium, or any combination thereof. Source material does not include special nuclear material.

statement: Special nuclear material, one of the nuclear material categories to be screened, is plutonium, Uranium 233, uranium enriched in the isotope 233 or in the isotope 235, any other material that the Nuclear Regulatory Commission determines to be special nuclear material (but not including source material), or any material artificially enriched by any nuclear material.
quote: Special nuclear material. Plutonium, Uranium 233, Uranium enriched in the isotope 233 or in the isotope 235, any other material that the NRC determines to be special nuclear material (but not including source material); or any material artificially enriched by any nuclear material.

statement: The heading of paragraph (a)(2) describes days 21 through 46 of standard screening as 21 days of concurrent screening plus 5 days of donation processing.
quote: Twenty-first through forty-sixth day (21 days concurrent screening plus 5 days donation processing)

statement: The reconciliation describes all significant reconciling items by appropriate captions, with contributions from and distributions to owners shown separately.
quote: with all significant reconciling items described by appropriate captions with contributions from and distributions to owners shown separately.

statement: The note item covers amounts under long-term contracts and programs not yet complete, as well as that portion of such amount which would not be absorbed in cost of sales based on existing firm orders at the latest balance sheet date.
quote: under long-term contracts and programs not yet complete, as well as that portion of such amount which would not be absorbed in cost of sales based on existing firm orders at the latest balance sheet date.

statement: Under the construction changes clause, when a change causes an increase or decrease in the Contractor's cost of, or the time required for, performance of any part of the work (CL-CLS-1091), the Contracting Officer shall make an equitable adjustment and modify the contract in writing.
quote: the Contracting Officer shall make an equitable adjustment and modify the contract in writing.

statement: A settlement should compensate the contractor fairly for the work done and preparations made for the terminated portions of the contract, including a reasonable allowance for profit, and fair compensation cannot be measured exactly.
quote: A settlement should compensate the contractor fairly for the work done and the preparations made for the terminated portions of the contract, including a reasonable allowance for profit. Fair compensation is a matter of judgment and cannot be measured exactly.

statement: The use of business judgment, as distinguished from strict accounting principles, is the heart of a settlement.
quote: The use of business judgment, as distinguished from strict accounting principles, is the heart of a settlement.

statement: The primary objective is to negotiate a settlement by agreement, and the parties may agree upon a total amount to be paid the contractor without agreeing on or segregating the particular elements of costs or profit comprising this amount.
quote: The primary objective is to negotiate a settlement by agreement. The parties may agree upon a total amount to be paid the contractor without agreeing on or segregating the particular elements of costs or profit comprising this amount.

statement: Cost and accounting data may provide guides, but are not rigid measures, for ascertaining fair compensation, and in appropriate cases costs may be estimated, differences compromised, and doubtful questions settled by agreement.
quote: Cost and accounting data may provide guides, but are not rigid measures, for ascertaining fair compensation. In appropriate cases, costs may be estimated, differences compromised, and doubtful questions settled by agreement.

statement: Subject to the general principles in FAR 49.201, the cost principles and procedures in the applicable subpart of Part 31 must be used in asserting, negotiating, or determining costs relevant to termination settlements under contracts with other than educational institutions.
quote: The cost principles and procedures in the applicable subpart of part 31 shall, subject to the general principles in 49.201, (a) be used in asserting, negotiating, or determining costs relevant to termination settlements under contracts with other than educational institutions

statement: Before settlement of a completely terminated contract, the TCO must obtain from the contracting office a list of all related unsettled contract changes.
quote: Before settlement of a completely terminated contract, the TCO shall obtain from the contracting office a list of all related unsettled contract changes.

statement: The TCO must settle, as part of final settlement, all unsettled contract changes after obtaining the recommendations of the contracting office concerning the changes.
quote: The TCO shall settle, as part of final settlement, all unsettled contract changes after obtaining the recommendations of the contracting office concerning the changes.

statement: When a contract has been partially terminated, outstanding unsettled contract changes will usually be handled by the contracting officer, though the contracting officer may delegate this function to the TCO.
quote: When the contract has been partially terminated, any outstanding unsettled contract changes will usually be handled by the contracting officer. However, the contracting officer may delegate this function to the TCO.

statement: Use of the inventory basis for settlement proposals is preferred, and under this basis the contractor may propose only costs allocable to the terminated portion of the contract.
quote: Use of the inventory basis for settlement proposals is preferred. Under this basis, the contractor may propose only costs allocable to the terminated portion of the contract

statement: Under the inventory basis, an allowance for profit or adjustment for loss must complete the gross settlement proposal, and all unliquidated advance and progress payments and known disposal and other credits must then be deducted.
quote: An allowance for profit (49.202) or adjustment for loss (49.203(b)) must be made to complete the gross settlement proposal. All unliquidated advance and progress payments and all disposal and other credits known when the proposal is submitted must then be deducted.

statement: When use of the inventory basis is not practicable or will unduly delay settlement, the total-cost basis on Standard Form 1436 may be used if approved in advance by the TCO.
quote: When use of the inventory basis is not practicable or will unduly delay settlement, the total-cost basis (SF-1436) may be used if approved in advance by the TCO

statement: When the total-cost basis is used under a partial termination, the settlement proposal must not be submitted until completion of the continued portion of the contract.
quote: When the total-cost basis is used under a partial termination, the settlement proposal shall not be submitted until completion of the continued portion of the contract.

statement: Settlement proposals may not be submitted on any basis other than the inventory basis or total-cost basis without prior approval of the chief of the contracting or contract administration office.
quote: Settlement proposals may not be submitted on any basis other than paragraph (a) or (b) above without the prior approval of the chief of the contracting or contract administration office.

statement: The TCO must allow profit on preparations made and work done by the contractor for the terminated portion of the contract but not on settlement expenses, and anticipatory profits and consequential damages are not allowed, subject to the cross-reference to FAR 49.108-5 on judgments and arbitration awards.
quote: The TCO shall allow profit on preparations made and work done by the contractor for the terminated portion of the contract but not on the settlement expenses. Anticipatory profits and consequential damages shall not be allowed (but see 49.108-5).

statement: Profit must not be allowed the contractor for material or services that have not been delivered by a subcontractor as of the effective date of termination, regardless of the percentage of completion.
quote: Profit shall not be allowed the contractor for material or services that, as of the effective date of termination, have not been delivered by a subcontractor, regardless of the percentage of completion.

statement: In negotiating or determining any settlement, the TCO must not allow profit if it appears the contractor would have incurred a loss had the entire contract been completed, and must negotiate or determine the amount of loss and adjust the settlement amount.
quote: In the negotiation or determination of any settlement, the TCO shall not allow profit if it appears that the contractor would have incurred a loss had the entire contract been completed. The TCO shall negotiate or determine the amount of loss and make an adjustment in the amount of settlement

statement: The inventory-basis loss adjustment multiplies a remainder amount by the ratio of the total contract price to the total cost incurred before termination plus the estimated cost to complete the entire contract.
quote: reduced by multiplying the remainder by the ratio of (i) the total contract price to (ii) the total cost incurred before termination plus the estimated cost to complete the entire contract.

statement: The TCO must deduct from the settlement amount payable to the contractor the agreed price for termination inventory purchased or retained by the contractor and proceeds from materials sold that have not been paid or credited to the Government.
quote: From the amount payable to the contractor under a settlement, the TCO shall deduct— (a) The agreed price for any part of the termination inventory purchased or retained by the contractor, and the proceeds from any materials sold that have not been paid or credited to the Government;

statement: The contractor must invoice accepted and delivered completed end items at the contract price in the usual manner and must not include them in the settlement proposal.
quote: The contractor shall invoice accepted and delivered end items at the contract price in the usual manner and shall not include them in the settlement proposal.

statement: When accepted completed end items are not to be delivered under the contract, the contractor must include them in the settlement proposal at the contract price adjusted for freight or other savings, together with credits for purchase, retention, or sale.
quote: When completed end items, though accepted, are not to be delivered under the contract, the contractor shall include them in the settlement proposal at the contract price, adjusted for any saving of freight or other charges, together with any credits for their purchase, retention, or sale.

statement: The total amount payable to the contractor for a settlement, before deducting disposal or other credits and exclusive of settlement costs, must not exceed the contract price less payments otherwise made or to be made under the contract.
quote: The total amount payable to the contractor for a settlement, before deducting disposal or other credits and exclusive of settlement costs, must not exceed the contract price less payments otherwise made or to be made under the contract.

statement: Whenever termination inventory is involved, the contractor must submit complete inventory disposal schedules to the TCO reflecting inventory allocable to the terminated portion of the contract, subject to the terms of the termination clause.
quote: Subject to the terms of the termination clause, and whenever termination inventory is involved, the contractor shall submit complete inventory disposal schedules to the TCO reflecting inventory that is allocable to the terminated portion of the contract.

statement: Inventory disposal schedules must be submitted within 120 days from the effective date of termination unless extended by the TCO based on a written justification supporting the extension.
quote: The inventory disposal schedules shall be submitted within 120 days from the effective date of termination unless otherwise extended by the TCO based on a written justification to support the extension.

statement: Inventory disposal schedules must be prepared on Standard Form 1428, Inventory Disposal Schedule.
quote: The inventory schedules shall be prepared on Standard Form 1428, Inventory Disposal Schedule.

statement: Before execution of a settlement agreement, the TCO must determine the accuracy of the Government property account for the terminated contract.
quote: Before execution of a settlement agreement, the TCO shall determine the accuracy of the Government property account for the terminated contract.

statement: If an audit discloses property for which the contractor cannot account, the TCO must reserve the rights of the Government regarding that property in the settlement agreement or make an appropriate deduction from the amount otherwise due.
quote: If an audit discloses property for which the contractor cannot account, the TCO shall reserve in the settlement agreement the rights of the Government regarding that property or make an appropriate deduction from the amount otherwise due the contractor.

statement: Under the termination clause, after partial termination, a contractor may request an equitable adjustment in the price or prices of the continued portion of a fixed-price contract.
quote: Under the termination clause, after partial termination, a contractor may request an equitable adjustment in the price or prices of the continued portion of a fixed-price contract.

statement: The TCO must forward the equitable adjustment proposal to the contracting officer except when negotiation authority is delegated to the TCO.
quote: The TCO shall forward the proposal to the contracting officer except when negotiation authority is delegated to the TCO.

statement: When the contracting officer retains responsibility for negotiating the equitable adjustment and executing a supplemental agreement, the contracting officer must ensure no portion of a price increase is included in a termination settlement made or in process.
quote: When the contracting officer retains responsibility for negotiating the equitable adjustment and executing a supplemental agreement, the contracting officer shall ensure that no portion of an increase in price is included in a termination settlement made or in process.

statement: The TCO must ensure that no portion of the costs included in the equitable adjustment are included in the termination settlement.
quote: The TCO shall also ensure that no portion of the costs included in the equitable adjustment are included in the termination settlement.

statement: The TCO should attempt to settle in one agreement all rights and liabilities of the parties under the contract except those arising from any continued portion of the contract.
quote: The TCO should attempt to settle in one agreement all rights and liabilities of the parties under the contract except those arising from any continued portion of the contract.

statement: A partial settlement may be entered into if the issues on which agreement has been reached are clearly severable from other issues and the partial settlement will not prejudice the Government's or contractor's interests in disposing of the unsettled part of the settlement proposal.
quote: a partial settlement may be entered into if (a) the issues on which agreement has been reached are clearly severable from other issues and (b) the partial settlement will not prejudice the Government's or contractor's interests in disposing of the unsettled part of the settlement proposal.

statement: Under a partially terminated fixed-price incentive contract, the TCO reimburses the contractor at target price for completed articles in the proposal lacking a final price and includes an appropriate reservation as to final price in the settlement agreement.
quote: The TCO shall reimburse the contractor at target price for completed articles included in the settlement proposal for which a final price has not been established. The TCO shall incorporate in the settlement agreement an appropriate reservation as to final price for these completed articles.

statement: On the terminated portion of a completely terminated fixed-price incentive contract, the provisions of the termination clause govern and the provisions of the incentive clause do not apply.
quote: On the terminated portion of the contract, the provisions of the termination clause (see 52.249-2, Termination for Convenience of the Government (Fixed-Price)) shall govern and the provisions of the incentive clause shall not apply.

statement: The TCO responsible for the termination settlement must ensure that no portion of the costs considered in negotiations under the incentive provisions are included in the termination settlement.
quote: The TCO responsible for the termination settlement will ensure, on the basis of evidence considered proper (including coordination with the contracting officer), that no portion of the costs considered in the negotiations under the incentive provisions are included in the termination settlement.

statement: Under a partial termination of a cost-plus-incentive-fee contract, the TCO must limit the settlement to an adjustment of target fee as provided in the incentive fee clause.
quote: Under a partial termination, the TCO shall limit the settlement to an adjustment of target fee as provided in paragraph (e) of the clause at 52.216-10, Incentive Fee.

statement: Under a partially terminated cost-plus-incentive-fee contract, the settlement agreement must include a reservation regarding any target cost adjustment resulting from the partial termination, and the contracting officer adjusts target cost if required.
quote: The settlement agreement shall include a reservation regarding any adjustment of target cost resulting from the partial termination. The contracting officer shall adjust the target cost, if required.

statement: Under a complete termination of a cost-plus-incentive-fee contract, fee is adjusted on the basis of target fee, and incentive provisions are not applied or considered.
quote: The fee shall be adjusted on the basis of the target fee, and the incentive provisions shall not be applied or considered.

statement: A fixed-price contract with prospective price redetermination provides for a firm fixed price for an initial period of deliveries or performance and prospective redetermination of the price for subsequent periods.
quote: A fixed-price contract with prospective price redetermination provides for (a) a firm fixed price for an initial period of contract deliveries or performance and (b) prospective redetermination, at a stated time or times during performance, of the price for subsequent periods of performance.

statement: A fixed-price contract with prospective price redetermination may be used in acquisitions of quantity production or services when a fair and reasonable firm fixed price can be negotiated for an initial period, but not for subsequent periods of contract performance.
quote: A fixed-price contract with prospective price redetermination may be used in acquisitions of quantity production or services for which it is possible to negotiate a fair and reasonable firm fixed price for an initial period, but not for subsequent periods of contract performance.

statement: Under a fixed-price contract with prospective price redetermination, the initial period should be the longest period for which a fair and reasonable firm fixed price can be negotiated, and each subsequent pricing period should be at least 12 months.
quote: The initial period should be the longest period for which it is possible to negotiate a fair and reasonable firm fixed price. Each subsequent pricing period should be at least 12 months.

statement: The contract may provide for a ceiling price based on evaluation of the uncertainties involved in performance and their possible cost impact.
quote: The contract may provide for a ceiling price based on evaluation of the uncertainties involved in performance and their possible cost impact.

statement: A fixed-price contract with prospective price redetermination shall not be used unless negotiations establish that conditions for a firm-fixed-price contract are not present and a fixed-price incentive contract would not be more appropriate.
quote: This contract type shall not be used unless— (a) Negotiations have established that (1) the conditions for use of a firm-fixed-price contract are not present (see 16.202-2), and (2) a fixed-price incentive contract would not be more appropriate;

statement: The limitations section for this contract type also lists that the contractor's accounting system is adequate for price redetermination, that the prospective pricing periods can be made to conform with operation of that accounting system, and that there is reasonable assurance that price redetermination actions will take place promptly; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CLS-0193.
quote: (b) The contractor's accounting system is adequate for price redetermination; (c) The prospective pricing periods can be made to conform with operation of the contractor's accounting system; and (d) There is reasonable assurance that price redetermination actions will take place promptly

statement: A fixed-ceiling-price contract with retroactive price redetermination provides for a fixed ceiling price and retroactive price redetermination within the ceiling after completion of the contract.
quote: A fixed-ceiling-price contract with retroactive price redetermination provides for (a) a fixed ceiling price and (b) retroactive price redetermination within the ceiling after completion of the contract.

statement: A fixed-ceiling-price contract with retroactive price redetermination is appropriate for research and development contracts estimated at the simplified acquisition threshold or less when it is established at the outset that a fair and reasonable firm fixed price cannot be negotiated, and a further condition stated in the same sentence is also met; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CLS-0676.
quote: A fixed-ceiling-price contract with retroactive price redetermination is appropriate for research and development contracts estimated at the simplified acquisition threshold or less when it is established at the outset that a fair and reasonable firm fixed price cannot be negotiated

statement: A ceiling price shall be negotiated for a fixed-ceiling-price contract with retroactive price redetermination at a level that reflects a reasonable sharing of risk by the contractor.
quote: A ceiling price shall be negotiated for the contract at a level that reflects a reasonable sharing of risk by the contractor.

statement: A fixed-ceiling-price contract with retroactive price redetermination should be awarded only after negotiation of a billing price that is as fair and reasonable as the circumstances permit.
quote: The contract should be awarded only after negotiation of a billing price that is as fair and reasonable as the circumstances permit.

statement: A fixed-ceiling-price contract with retroactive price redetermination shall not be used unless the contract is for research and development estimated at or below the simplified acquisition threshold and the contractor accounting system is adequate for price redetermination.
quote: This contract type shall not be used unless— (a) The contract is for research and development and the estimated cost is the simplified acquisition threshold or less; (b) The contractor's accounting system is adequate for price redetermination;

statement: The limitations section for this contract type also lists reasonable assurance that the price redetermination will take place promptly at the specified time and written approval of its use by the head of the contracting activity or a higher-level official if agency procedures require.
quote: (c) There is reasonable assurance that the price redetermination will take place promptly at the specified time; and (d) The head of the contracting activity (or a higher-level official, if required by agency procedures) approves its use in writing.

statement: A firm-fixed-price, level-of-effort term contract requires the contractor to provide a specified level of effort over a stated period of time on work stated only in general terms and the Government to pay a fixed dollar amount.
quote: A firm-fixed-price, level-of-effort term contract requires (a) the contractor to provide a specified level of effort, over a stated period of time, on work that can be stated only in general terms and (b) the Government to pay the contractor a fixed dollar amount.

statement: Subject to the qualification stated in the next sentence (CL-CLS-0564), a firm-fixed-price, level-of-effort term contract is suitable for investigation or study in a specific research and development area, where the product of the contract is usually a report showing results achieved.
quote: A firm-fixed-price, level-of-effort term contract is suitable for investigation or study in a specific research and development area. The product of the contract is usually a report showing the results achieved through application of the required level of effort.

statement: Under a firm-fixed-price, level-of-effort term contract, payment is based on the effort expended rather than on the results achieved.
quote: payment is based on the effort expended rather than on the results achieved.

statement: A firm-fixed-price, level-of-effort term contract may be used only when the work required cannot otherwise be clearly defined, the required level of effort is agreed upon in advance, and there is assurance the result cannot be achieved by expending less effort; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CLS-0566.
quote: This contract type may be used only when— (a) The work required cannot otherwise be clearly defined; (b) The required level of effort is identified and agreed upon in advance; (c) There is reasonable assurance that the intended result cannot be achieved by expending less than the stipulated effort

statement: One listed condition for using a firm-fixed-price, level-of-effort term contract is that the contract price is the simplified acquisition threshold or less, unless approved by the chief of the contracting office.
quote: (d) The contract price is the simplified acquisition threshold or less, unless approved by the chief of the contracting office.

statement: Cost-reimbursement types of contracts provide for payment of allowable incurred costs, to the extent prescribed in the contract.
quote: Cost-reimbursement types of contracts provide for payment of allowable incurred costs, to the extent prescribed in the contract.

statement: The contracting officer must use cost-reimbursement contracts only in the listed cases, the first being circumstances that do not allow the agency to define its requirements sufficiently to allow for a fixed-price type contract.
quote: The contracting officer shall use cost-reimbursement contracts only when— (1) Circumstances do not allow the agency to define its requirements sufficiently to allow for a fixed-price type contract (see 7.105);

statement: A cost-reimbursement contract may be used only when selection factors have been considered, an acquisition plan is approved at least one level above the contracting officer, and the contractor accounting system is adequate for determining applicable costs; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CLS-0570.
quote: A cost-reimbursement contract may be used only when— (1) The factors in 16.104 have been considered; (2) A written acquisition plan has been approved and signed at least one level above the contracting officer; (3) The contractor's accounting system is adequate for determining costs applicable

statement: One listed condition for using a cost-reimbursement contract is that, prior to award of the contract or order, adequate Government resources are available to award and manage a contract other than firm-fixed-priced.
quote: (4) Prior to award of the contract or order, adequate Government resources are available to award and manage a contract other than firm-fixed-priced (see 7.104(e)).

statement: The use of cost-reimbursement contracts is prohibited for the acquisition of commercial products and commercial services.
quote: The use of cost-reimbursement contracts is prohibited for the acquisition of commercial products and commercial services (see parts 2 and 12).

statement: A cost contract is a cost-reimbursement contract in which the contractor receives no fee.
quote: A cost contract is a cost-reimbursement contract in which the contractor receives no fee.

statement: A cost contract may be appropriate for research and development work, particularly with nonprofit educational institutions or other nonprofit organizations.
quote: A cost contract may be appropriate for research and development work, particularly with nonprofit educational institutions or other nonprofit organizations.

statement: A cost-sharing contract is a cost-reimbursement contract in which the contractor receives no fee and is reimbursed only for an agreed-upon portion of its allowable costs.
quote: A cost-sharing contract is a cost-reimbursement contract in which the contractor receives no fee and is reimbursed only for an agreed-upon portion of its allowable costs.

statement: A cost-sharing contract may be used when the contractor agrees to absorb a portion of the costs, in the expectation of substantial compensating benefits.
quote: A cost-sharing contract may be used when the contractor agrees to absorb a portion of the costs, in the expectation of substantial compensating benefits.

statement: A cost-plus-fixed-fee contract is a cost-reimbursement contract providing for payment of a negotiated fee that is fixed at contract inception, does not vary with actual cost, but may be adjusted for changes in the work.

quote: The property administrator should, in coordination with the plant clearance officer, ensure that contractor scrap disposal processes, methods, and practices allow for effective, efficient, and proper disposition and are properly documented in the contractor's property management procedures.

statement: Absent contract terms and conditions to the contrary, the Government may abandon parts removed and replaced from property as a result of normal maintenance actions or removed from property as a result of the repair, maintenance, overhaul, or modification process.
quote: Absent contract terms and conditions to the contrary, the Government may abandon parts removed and replaced from property as a result of normal maintenance actions or removed from property as a result of the repair, maintenance, overhaul, or modification process.

statement: When the contractor's property management system does not comply with contractual requirements, prompt correction of deficiencies and a corrective action plan, including a schedule for correction of the deficiencies, shall be requested from the contractor.
quote: when the contractor's property management system does not comply with contractual requirements, shall request prompt correction of deficiencies, and shall request from the contractor a corrective action plan, including a schedule for correction of the deficiencies.

statement: The contracting officer shall notify the contractor in writing of any Government decision to apply the remedies described in the paragraphs on revocation of the assumption of risk and on other rights or remedies.
quote: the contracting officer shall notify the contractor in writing of any Government decision to apply the remedies described in paragraphs (b)(1) and (b)(2) of this section.

statement: Abandonment, or destruction of other contractor inventory at the contractor's or subcontractor's premises, may be authorized in accordance with FMR 102-36.305 through 325 and consistent with the criteria that the paragraph lists.
quote: may authorize the abandonment, or order the destruction of other contractor inventory at the contractor's or subcontractor's premises, in accordance with FMR 102-36.305 through 325 (41 CFR 102-36.305-325) and consistent with the following:

statement: One listed criterion is that the property is not considered sensitive, does not require demilitarization, has no commercial value or reutilization, transfer or donation potential, and does not constitute a danger to public health or welfare.
quote: (1) The property is not considered sensitive, does not require demilitarization, has no commercial value or reutilization, transfer or donation potential, and does not constitute a danger to public health or welfare.

statement: Another listed criterion is that the estimated cost of continued care and handling of the property, including advertising, storage and other costs associated with making the sale, exceed the estimated proceeds from its sale.
quote: (2) The estimated cost of continued care and handling of the property (including advertising, storage and other costs associated with making the sale), exceed the estimated proceeds from its sale.

statement: A registrant must file audited balance sheets, consolidated for the registrant and its subsidiaries and covering its predecessors, as of the end of each of the two most recent fiscal years.
quote: There must be filed, for the registrant and its subsidiaries consolidated and for its predecessors, audited balance sheets as of the end of each of the two most recent fiscal years.

statement: A registrant that has been in existence for less than one fiscal year must file an audited balance sheet as of a date within 135 days of the date of filing the registration statement.
quote: If the registrant has been in existence for less than one fiscal year, there must be filed an audited balance sheet as of a date within 135 days of the date of filing the registration statement.

statement: For a filing other than on Form 10-K or Form 10 that is made within 45 days after the end of the registrant's fiscal year, when audited financial statements for the most recent fiscal year are not available, the balance sheets may be as of the end of the two preceding fiscal years; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CLS-0803.
quote: If the filing, other than a filing on Form 10-K or Form 10, is made within 45 days after the end of the registrant's fiscal year and audited financial statements for the most recent fiscal year are not available, the balance sheets may be as of the end of the two preceding fiscal years

statement: The paragraph (b) relief to give balance sheets as of the end of the two preceding fiscal years comes with a requirement that the filing shall include an additional balance sheet as of an interim date at least as current as the end of the registrant's third fiscal quarter of the most recently completed fiscal year.
quote: the balance sheets may be as of the end of the two preceding fiscal years and the filing shall include an additional balance sheet as of an interim date at least as current as the end of the registrant's third fiscal quarter of the most recently completed fiscal year

statement: Paragraph (c) extends the paragraph (b) instruction to filings other than on Form 10-K or Form 10 made after 45 days but within the number of days specified in paragraph (i), provided that the listed conditions are met.
quote: The instruction in paragraph (b) of this section is also applicable to filings, other than on Form 10-K or Form 10, made after 45 days but within the number of days of the end of the registrant's fiscal year specified in paragraph (i) of this section: Provided, that the following conditions are met:

statement: Where the paragraph (c) conditions are not met, for filings made after 45 days but within the number of days specified in paragraph (i), the filing must include the audited balance sheets required by paragraph (a).
quote: For filings made after 45 days but within the number of days of the end of the registrant's fiscal year specified in paragraph (i) of this section where the conditions set forth in paragraph (c) of this section are not met, the filing must include the audited balance sheets required by paragraph (a)

statement: Subject to the requirement stated in the next sentence (CL-CLS-1566), any interim balance sheet provided in accordance with the balance sheet rule may be unaudited and need not be presented in greater detail than is required by section 210.10-01.
quote: (f) Any interim balance sheet provided in accordance with the requirements of this section may be unaudited and need not be presented in greater detail than is required by § 210.10-01.

statement: A registrant must file audited statements of comprehensive income and cash flows, consolidated for the registrant and its subsidiaries and covering its predecessors, for each of the three fiscal years preceding the date of the most recent audited balance sheet being filed; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CLS-0808.
quote: There shall be filed, for the registrant and its subsidiaries consolidated and for its predecessors, audited statements of comprehensive income and cash flows for each of the three fiscal years preceding the date of the most recent audited balance sheet being filed

statement: The period for those audited statements is the three fiscal years or such shorter period as the registrant, including predecessors, has been in existence.
quote: for each of the three fiscal years preceding the date of the most recent audited balance sheet being filed or such shorter period as the registrant (including predecessors) has been in existence.

statement: In a Securities Act registration statement for the initial public offering of its equity securities, an emerging growth company may provide audited statements of comprehensive income and cash flows for each of the two fiscal years preceding the date of the most recent audited balance sheet.
quote: may, in a Securities Act registration statement for the initial public offering of the emerging growth company's equity securities, provide audited statements of comprehensive income and cash flows for each of the two fiscal years preceding the date of the most recent audited balance sheet

statement: Statements of comprehensive income and cash flows shall be provided for any interim period between the latest audited balance sheet and the date of the most recent interim balance sheet being filed, and for the corresponding period of the preceding fiscal year.
quote: (b) In addition, for any interim period between the latest audited balance sheet and the date of the most recent interim balance sheet being filed, and for the corresponding period of the preceding fiscal year, statements of comprehensive income and cash flows shall be provided.

statement: The interim statements of comprehensive income and cash flows required for those interim periods may be unaudited and need not be presented in greater detail than is required by section 210.10-01.
quote: statements of comprehensive income and cash flows shall be provided. Such interim financial statements may be unaudited and need not be presented in greater detail than is required by § 210.10-01.

statement: An analysis of the changes in each caption of stockholders' equity and noncontrolling interests presented in the balance sheets shall be given in a note or separate statement.
quote: An analysis of the changes in each caption of stockholders' equity and noncontrolling interests presented in the balance sheets shall be given in a note or separate statement.

statement: The analysis of changes in equity shall be presented as a reconciliation of the beginning balance to the ending balance for each period for which a statement of comprehensive income is required to be filed; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CLS-0483.
quote: This analysis shall be presented in the form of a reconciliation of the beginning balance to the ending balance for each period for which a statement of comprehensive income is required to be filed

statement: The information required with respect to any statement shall be furnished as a minimum requirement, to which shall be added such further material information as is necessary to make the required statements not misleading in the light of the circumstances under which they are made.
quote: The information required with respect to any statement shall be furnished as a minimum requirement to which shall be added such further material information as is necessary to make the required statements, in the light of the circumstances under which they are made, not misleading.

statement: Financial statements filed with the Commission that are not prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles will be presumed to be misleading or inaccurate, despite footnote or other disclosures, unless the Commission has otherwise provided.
quote: Financial statements filed with the Commission which are not prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles will be presumed to be misleading or inaccurate, despite footnote or other disclosures, unless the Commission has otherwise provided.

statement: An item whose amount is not material need not be separately set forth, and the combination of insignificant amounts is permitted.
quote: If the amount which would otherwise be required to be shown with respect to any item is not material, it need not be separately set forth. The combination of insignificant amounts is permitted.

statement: Sections 210.5-01 to 210.5-04 are applicable to financial statements filed for all persons except those listed, and the first two listed exclusions are registered investment companies and employee stock purchase, savings and similar plans.
quote: Sections 210.5-01 to 210.5-04 shall be applicable to financial statements filed for all persons except— (a) Registered investment companies (see§§ 210.6-01 through 210.6-11). (b) Employee stock purchase, savings and similar plans (see §§ 210.6A-01 to 210.6A-05).

statement: One listed group of exclusions from sections 210.5-01 to 210.5-04 covers insurance companies, bank holding companies and banks, and brokers and dealers when filing Form X-17A-5.
quote: (c) Insurance companies (see §§ 210.7-01 to 210.7-05). (d) Bank holding companies and banks (see §§ 210.9-01 to 210.9-07). (e) Brokers and dealers when filing Form X-17A-5 [249.617] (see §§ 240.17a-5 and 240.17a-10 under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934).

statement: Amounts receivable from customers (trade), from related parties, from underwriters, promoters and employees (other than related parties) which arose in other than the ordinary course of business, and from others shall be stated separately.
quote: (a) State separately amounts receivable from (1) customers (trade); (2) related parties (see § 210.4-08(k)); (3) underwriters, promoters, and employees (other than related parties) which arose in other than the ordinary course of business; and (4) others.

statement: If the aggregate amount of notes receivable exceeds 10 percent of the aggregate amount of receivables, the receivables information shall be set forth separately, in the balance sheet or in a note, for accounts receivable and notes receivable.
quote: (b) If the aggregate amount of notes receivable exceeds 10 percent of the aggregate amount of receivables, the above information shall be set forth separately, in the balance sheet or in a note thereto, for accounts receivable and notes receivable.

statement: If receivables include amounts due under long-term contracts, the listed amounts shall be stated separately in the balance sheet or in a note to the financial statements.
quote: (c) If receivables include amounts due under long-term contracts (see § 210.5-02.6(d)), state separately in the balance sheet or in a note to the financial statements the following amounts:

statement: One listed amount is balances billed but not paid by customers under retainage provisions in contracts.
quote: (1) Balances billed but not paid by customers under retainage provisions in contracts.

statement: One listed amount is the recognized sales value of performance, and such amounts that had not been billed and were not billable to customers at the date of the balance sheet, with a general description of the prerequisites for billing.
quote: (2) Amounts representing the recognized sales value of performance and such amounts that had not been billed and were not billable to customers at the date of the balance sheet. Include a general description of the prerequisites for billing.

statement: One listed amount is billed or unbilled amounts representing claims or other similar items subject to uncertainty concerning their determination or ultimate realization, with a description of the nature and status of the principal items.
quote: (3) Billed or unbilled amounts representing claims or other similar items subject to uncertainty concerning their determination or ultimate realization. Include a description of the nature and status of the principal items comprising such amount.

statement: For the three listed amounts, the amounts included in each item that are expected to be collected after one year are also stated, and the amounts of retainage are stated by year, if practicable, as to when they are expected to be collected.
quote: (4) With respect to (1) through (3) above, also state the amounts included in each item which are expected to be collected after one year. Also state, by year, if practicable, when the amounts of retainage (see (1) above) are expected to be collected.

statement: The amounts of major classes of inventory such as finished goods, inventoried costs relating to long-term contracts or programs, work in process and raw materials shall be stated separately in the balance sheet or in a note, if practicable.
quote: State separately in the balance sheet or in a note thereto, if practicable, the amounts of major classes of inventory such as: (1) Finished goods; (2) inventoried costs relating to long-term contracts or programs (see paragraph (d) of this section); (3) work in process; (4) raw materials

statement: If the LIFO inventory method is used, the excess of replacement or current cost over stated LIFO value shall, if material, be stated parenthetically or in a note to the financial statements.
quote: (c) If the LIFO inventory method is used, the excess of replacement or current cost over stated LIFO value shall, if material, be stated parenthetically or in a note to the financial statements.

statement: The basis of determining the inventory amounts shall be stated, and if cost is used to determine any portion of them, the description of the method shall include the nature of the cost elements included in inventory.
quote: (b) The basis of determining the amounts shall be stated. If cost is used to determine any portion of the inventory amounts, the description of this method shall include the nature of the cost elements included in inventory.

statement: Elements of cost include, among other items, retained costs representing the excess of manufacturing or production costs over amounts charged to cost of sales or delivered or in-process units, initial tooling or other deferred startup costs, or general and administrative costs.
quote: Elements of cost include, among other items, retained costs representing the excess of manufacturing or production costs over the amounts charged to cost of sales or delivered or in-process units, initial tooling or other deferred startup costs, or general and administrative costs.

statement: If any general and administrative costs are charged to inventory, a note shall state the aggregate amount of those costs incurred in each period and the actual or estimated amount remaining in inventory at the date of each balance sheet.
quote: If any general and administrative costs are charged to inventory, state in a note to the financial statements the aggregate amount of the general and administrative costs incurred in each period and the actual or estimated amount remaining in inventory at the date of each balance sheet.

statement: One listed kind of long-term contract or program for the receivables and inventories items is one for which gross profits are recognized on a percentage-of-completion method of accounting or any variant of it.
quote: (d) For purposes of §§ 210.5-02.3 and 210.5-02.6, long-term contracts or programs include (1) all contracts or programs for which gross profits are recognized on a percentage-of-completion method of accounting or any variant thereof (e.g., delivered unit, cost to cost, physical completion)

statement: In either listed case, the contracts or programs have associated with them material amounts of inventories or unbilled receivables and have been or are expected to be performed over a period of more than twelve months.
quote: where, in either case, the contracts or programs have associated with them material amounts of inventories or unbilled receivables and where such contracts or programs have been or are expected to be performed over a period of more than twelve months.

statement: For all long-term contracts or programs, the listed information, if applicable, shall be stated in a note to the financial statements.
quote: For all long-term contracts or programs, the following information, if applicable, shall be stated in a note to the financial statements:

statement: One listed note item is the aggregate amount of manufacturing or production costs and any related deferred costs that exceeds the aggregate estimated cost of all in-process and delivered units on the basis of the estimated average cost of all units expected to be produced; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CLS-0484.
quote: (i) The aggregate amount of manufacturing or production costs and any related deferred costs (e.g., initial tooling costs) which exceeds the aggregate estimated cost of all in-process and delivered units on the basis of the estimated average cost of all units expected to be produced

statement: One listed note item is the aggregate amount representing claims or other similar items subject to uncertainty concerning their determination or ultimate realization, with a description of the nature and status of the principal items comprising it.
quote: (ii) The aggregate amount representing claims or other similar items subject to uncertainty concerning their determination or ultimate realization, and include a description of the nature and status of the principal items comprising such aggregate amount.

statement: One listed note item is the amount of progress payments netted against inventory at the date of the balance sheet.
quote: (iii) The amount of progress payments netted against inventory at the date of the balance sheet.

statement: If income is derived from more than one of the subcaptions of the net sales and revenues caption, each class that is not more than 10 percent of the sum of the items may be combined with another class.
quote: If income is derived from more than one of the subcaptions described under § 210.5-03.1, each class which is not more than 10 percent of the sum of the items may be combined with another class.

statement: If classes of income are combined under the 10 percent rule, the related costs and expenses described under the costs and expenses caption shall be combined in the same manner.
quote: each class which is not more than 10 percent of the sum of the items may be combined with another class. If these items are combined, related costs and expenses as described under § 210.5-03.2 shall be combined in the same manner.

statement: The net sales and gross revenues caption requires net sales of tangible products, operating revenues of public utilities or others, income from rentals, revenues from services and other revenues to be stated separately.
quote: 1. Net sales and gross revenues. State separately: (a) Net sales of tangible products (gross sales less discounts, returns and allowances), (b) operating revenues of public utilities or others; (c) income from rentals; (d) revenues from services; and (e) other revenues.

statement: The costs and expenses applicable to sales and revenues caption requires cost of tangible goods sold, operating expenses of public utilities or others, expenses applicable to rental income, cost of services and expenses applicable to other revenues to be stated separately.
quote: 2. Costs and expenses applicable to sales and revenues. State separately the amount of (a) cost of tangible goods sold, (b) operating expenses of public utilities or others, (c) expenses applicable to rental income, (d) cost of services, and (e) expenses applicable to other revenues.

statement: Amounts earned from transactions with related parties shall be disclosed as required under section 210.4-08(k).
quote: Amounts earned from transactions with related parties shall be disclosed as required under § 210.4-08(k).

statement: The caption list includes selling, general and administrative expenses as its own caption, and other general expenses are items not normally included in that caption, with any material item stated separately.
quote: 4. Selling, general and administrative expenses. 5. Provision for doubtful accounts and notes. 6. Other general expenses. Include items not normally included in caption 4 above. State separately any material item.

statement: The registrant shall describe the most significant restrictions on the payment of dividends by the registrant, indicating their sources, their pertinent provisions, and the amount of retained earnings or net income restricted or free of restrictions.
quote: (1) Describe the most significant restrictions on the payment of dividends by the registrant, indicating their sources, their pertinent provisions, and the amount of retained earnings or net income restricted or free of restrictions.

statement: When material, the registrant shall describe the nature of any restrictions on the ability of consolidated subsidiaries and unconsolidated subsidiaries to transfer funds to the registrant in the form of cash dividends, loans or advances.
quote: disclosures in paragraphs (e)(3)(i) and (ii) of this section shall be provided when material. (i) Describe the nature of any restrictions on the ability of consolidated subsidiaries and unconsolidated subsidiaries to transfer funds to the registrant in the form of cash dividends, loans or advances

statement: Summarized information as to assets, liabilities and results of operations, as detailed in section 210.1-02(bb), shall be presented in notes to the financial statements on an individual or group basis for subsidiaries not consolidated, which is one of two listed groups.
quote: (1) The summarized information as to assets, liabilities and results of operations as detailed in § 210.1-02(bb) shall be presented in notes to the financial statements on an individual or group basis for: (i) Subsidiaries not consolidated;

statement: Summarized information is presented on an individual or group basis for subsidiaries not consolidated or, if the criteria in section 210.1-02(w) for a significant subsidiary are met, for 50 percent or less owned persons accounted for by the equity method by the registrant or by a subsidiary of the registrant.
quote: on an individual or group basis for: (i) Subsidiaries not consolidated; or (ii) For 50 percent or less owned persons accounted for by the equity method by the registrant or by a subsidiary of the registrant, if the criteria in § 210.1-02(w) for a significant subsidiary are met

statement: Amounts of related party transactions should be stated on the face of the balance sheet, statement of comprehensive income, or statement of cash flows.
quote: (1) Amounts of related party transactions should be stated on the face of the balance sheet, statement of comprehensive income, or statement of cash flows.

statement: Where separate financial statements are presented for the registrant, certain investees, or subsidiaries, any intercompany profits or losses resulting from transactions with related parties and the effects thereof shall be disclosed.
quote: (2) In cases where separate financial statements are presented for the registrant, certain investees, or subsidiaries, any intercompany profits or losses resulting from transactions with related parties and the effects thereof shall be disclosed.

statement: Separate financial statements must be filed for a majority-owned subsidiary not consolidated by the registrant or by a subsidiary of the registrant when the conditions are met, substituting 20 percent for 10 percent in the tests used to determine a significant subsidiary.
quote: substituting 20 percent for 10 percent in the tests used therein to determine a significant subsidiary, are met for a majority-owned subsidiary not consolidated by the registrant or by a subsidiary of the registrant, separate financial statements of such subsidiary must be filed

statement: The article containing the form rule, and other articles of Regulation S-X, clarify certain disclosures that must be included in any event in financial statements filed with the Commission.
quote: This article and other articles of Regulation S-X provide clarification of certain disclosures which must be included in any event, in financial statements filed with the Commission.

statement: The list in paragraph (i)(1) sets the number of days at 60 days (75 days for fiscal years ending before December 15, 2006) for large accelerated filers, 75 days for accelerated filers and 90 days for all other registrants.
quote: the number of days shall be: (i) 60 days (75 days for fiscal years ending before December 15, 2006) for large accelerated filers (as defined in § 240.12b-2 of this chapter); (ii) 75 days for accelerated filers (as defined in § 240.12b-2 of this chapter); and (iii) 90 days for all other registrants.

statement: Subject to the points stated in the next sentences (CL-CLS-1572, CL-CLS-1573 and CL-CLS-1574), the notes listed in the general notes rule are to be set forth, if applicable to the person for which the financial statements are filed, on the face of the appropriate statement or in appropriately captioned notes.
quote: If applicable to the person for which the financial statements are filed, the following shall be set forth on the face of the appropriate statement or in appropriately captioned notes.

statement: Summarized information of subsidiaries not consolidated shall not be combined for disclosure purposes with the summarized information of 50 percent or less owned persons.
quote: Summarized information of subsidiaries not consolidated shall not be combined for disclosure purposes with the summarized information of 50 percent or less owned persons.

statement: Contracts or programs of shorter duration may also be included in the long-term contracts or programs definition, if deemed appropriate.
quote: Contracts or programs of shorter duration may also be included, if deemed appropriate.

statement: The separate statements rule looks to any of the conditions set forth in section 210.1-02(w), tested with 20 percent substituted for 10 percent, being met for a majority-owned subsidiary; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CLS-0849.
quote: If any of the conditions set forth in § 210.1-02(w), substituting 20 percent for 10 percent in the tests used therein to determine a significant subsidiary, are met for a majority-owned subsidiary

statement: One condition for the paragraph (c) extension is that the registrant files annual, quarterly and other reports pursuant to section 13 or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and all reports due have been filed.
quote: (1) The registrant files annual, quarterly and other reports pursuant to section 13 or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and all reports due have been filed;

statement: A second condition for the paragraph (c) extension is that, for the most recent fiscal year for which audited financial statements are not yet available, the registrant reasonably and in good faith expects to report income attributable to the registrant, after taxes; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CLS-0858.
quote: (2) For the most recent fiscal year for which audited financial statements are not yet available the registrant reasonably and in good faith expects to report income attributable to the registrant, after taxes; and

statement: A third condition for the paragraph (c) extension is that for at least one of the two fiscal years immediately preceding the most recent fiscal year the registrant reported income attributable to the registrant, after taxes.
quote: (3) For at least one of the two fiscal years immediately preceding the most recent fiscal year the registrant reported income attributable to the registrant, after taxes.

statement: Article 8 of Regulation S-X applies to financial statements filed for smaller reporting companies.
quote: Sections 210.8-01 through 210.8-08 (Article 8) shall be applicable to financial statements filed for smaller reporting companies.

statement: A smaller reporting company that elects the Article 8 form and content need not apply the other Regulation S-X form and content requirements, except for listed ones.
quote: (b) Smaller reporting companies electing to prepare their financial statements with the form and content required in Article 8 need not apply the other form and content requirements in Regulation S-X with the exception of the following:

statement: Under Article 8, a smaller reporting company files audited statements of comprehensive income, cash flows and changes in stockholders' equity for each of the two fiscal years preceding the most recent audited balance sheet, or a shorter period in business.
quote: audited statements of comprehensive income, cash flows and changes in stockholders' equity for each of the two fiscal years preceding the date of the most recent audited balance sheet (or such shorter period as the registrant has been in business)

statement: The contracting officer shall terminate contracts, whether for default or convenience, only when it is in the Government's interest.
quote: The contracting officer shall terminate contracts, whether for default or convenience, only when it is in the Government's interest.

statement: After the contracting officer issues a notice of termination, the termination contracting officer (TCO) is responsible for negotiating any settlement with the contractor, including a no-cost settlement if appropriate.
quote: After the contracting officer issues a notice of termination, the termination contracting officer (TCO) is responsible for negotiating any settlement with the contractor, including a no-cost settlement if appropriate.

statement: The notice of termination shall state, among its listed items, that the contract is being terminated for the convenience of the Government (or for default) under the contract clause authorizing the termination, the effective date of termination, the extent of termination, and any special instructions.
quote: The notice shall state— (1) That the contract is being terminated for the convenience of the Government (or for default) under the contract clause authorizing the termination; (2) The effective date of termination; (3) The extent of termination; (4) Any special instructions;

statement: One listed item of the notice of termination is the steps the contractor should take to minimize the impact on personnel if the termination, together with all other outstanding terminations, will result in a significant reduction in the contractor's work force.
quote: (5) The steps the contractor should take to minimize the impact on personnel if the termination, together with all other outstanding terminations, will result in a significant reduction in the contractor's work force

statement: Consistent with the termination clause and the notice of termination, the TCO shall direct the action required of the prime contractor.
quote: Consistent with the termination clause and the notice of termination, the TCO shall— (1) Direct the action required of the prime contractor;

statement: One listed duty of the TCO is to examine the settlement proposal of the prime contractor and, when appropriate, the settlement proposals of subcontractors.
quote: (2) Examine the settlement proposal of the prime contractor and, when appropriate, the settlement proposals of subcontractors;

statement: One listed pair of TCO duties is to promptly negotiate settlement with the contractor and enter into a settlement agreement and, if unable to negotiate a complete settlement, to promptly settle the contractor's settlement proposal by determination for the elements that cannot be agreed on.
quote: (3) Promptly negotiate settlement with the contractor and enter into a settlement agreement; and (4) Promptly settle the contractor's settlement proposal by determination for the elements that cannot be agreed on, if unable to negotiate a complete settlement.

statement: After receipt of the notice of termination, the contractor shall comply with the notice and the termination clause of the contract, except as otherwise directed by the TCO, and the notice and clause applicable to convenience terminations generally require the listed duties; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CLS-0908.
quote: After receipt of the notice of termination, the contractor shall comply with the notice and the termination clause of the contract, except as otherwise directed by the TCO. The notice and clause applicable to convenience terminations generally require that the contractor—

statement: One listed group of duties is to stop work immediately on the terminated portion of the contract and stop placing subcontracts under it, to terminate all subcontracts related to the terminated portion of the prime contract, and to immediately advise the TCO of any special circumstances precluding the stoppage of work.
quote: (a) Stop work immediately on the terminated portion of the contract and stop placing subcontracts thereunder; (b) Terminate all subcontracts related to the terminated portion of the prime contract; (c) Immediately advise the TCO of any special circumstances precluding the stoppage of work;

statement: One listed duty is to perform the continued portion of the contract and submit promptly any request for an equitable adjustment of price for the continued portion, supported by evidence of any increase in the cost, if the termination is partial.
quote: (d) Perform the continued portion of the contract and submit promptly any request for an equitable adjustment of price for the continued portion, supported by evidence of any increase in the cost, if the termination is partial;

statement: One listed duty is to take necessary or directed action to protect and preserve property in the contractor's possession in which the Government has or may acquire an interest and, as directed by the TCO, to deliver the property to the Government.
quote: (e) Take necessary or directed action to protect and preserve property in the contractor's possession in which the Government has or may acquire an interest and, as directed by the TCO, deliver the property to the Government;

statement: One listed duty is to promptly notify the TCO in writing of any legal proceedings growing out of any subcontract or other commitment related to the terminated portion of the contract.
quote: (f) Promptly notify the TCO in writing of any legal proceedings growing out of any subcontract or other commitment related to the terminated portion of the contract;

statement: One listed duty is to settle outstanding liabilities and proposals arising out of termination of subcontracts, obtaining any approvals or ratifications required by the TCO.
quote: (g) Settle outstanding liabilities and proposals arising out of termination of subcontracts, obtaining any approvals or ratifications required by the TCO;

statement: One listed pair of duties is to dispose of termination inventory, as directed or authorized by the TCO, and to promptly submit the contractor's own settlement proposal, supported by appropriate schedules.
quote: (h) Promptly submit the contractor's own settlement proposal, supported by appropriate schedules; and (i) Dispose of termination inventory, as directed or authorized by the TCO.

statement: The TCO shall refer each prime contractor settlement proposal valued at or above the threshold for obtaining certified cost or pricing data set forth in FAR 15.403-4(a)(1) to the appropriate audit agency for review and recommendations.

statement: In the basic cost-reimbursement changes clause, the Contracting Officer may at any time, by written order and without notice to the sureties, if any, make changes within the general scope of the contract in any one or more of the areas the clause then lists.
