quote: The 30-day period may be varied according to agency procedures.

quote: the estimated cost of this contract and, if this contract is incrementally funded, the funds allotted for the performance of this contract, shall not be increased or considered to be increased except by specific written modification of the contract

However, if the Contracting Officer decides that the facts justify it, the Contracting Officer may receive and act upon a proposal submitted before final payment of the contract.

quote: The Contracting Officer may, at any time, without notice to the sureties, if any, by written order designated or indicated to be a change order, make changes in the work within the general scope of the contract, including changes—

quote: the notice shall state— (1) The date, nature, and circumstances of the conduct regarded as a change; (2) The name, function, and activity of each Government individual and Contractor official or employee involved in or knowledgeable about such conduct;

statement: The Contracting Officer shall promptly, within a number of calendar days left blank in the printed clause to be negotiated, after receipt of the notice, respond to the notice in writing.
quote: The Contracting Officer shall promptly, within ___ (to be negotiated) calendar days after receipt of notice, respond to the notice in writing.

statement: In responding, the Contracting Officer shall either take one of the listed responses, which include confirming that the conduct constitutes a change and, when necessary, directing the mode of further performance, and countermanding any communication regarded as a change.

statement: The equitable adjustment provision of the notification clause applies where the Contracting Officer confirms that Government conduct effected a change as alleged by the Contractor and the conduct causes an increase or decrease in the Contractor's cost of, or the time required for, performance of any part of the work.
quote: If the Contracting Officer confirms that Government conduct effected a change as alleged by the Contractor, and the conduct causes an increase or decrease in the Contractor's cost of, or the time required for, performance of any part of the work under this contract

statement: Under the notification clause, an equitable adjustment shall be made in the contract price or delivery schedule or both, and in such other provisions of the contract as may be affected.
quote: an equitable adjustment shall be made— (i) In the contract price or delivery schedule or both; and (ii) In such other provisions of the contract as may be affected.

statement: The equitable adjustment under the notification clause shall not include increased costs or time extensions for delay resulting from the Contractor's failure to provide notice or to continue performance as the clause provides.
quote: The equitable adjustment shall not include increased costs or time extensions for delay resulting from the Contractor's failure to provide notice or to continue performance as provided, respectively, in (b) and (c) above.

statement: In the disputes clause, a claim means a written demand or written assertion by one of the contracting parties seeking, as a matter of right, the payment of money in a sum certain, the adjustment or interpretation of contract terms, or other relief arising under or relating to the contract.
quote: Claim, as used in this clause, means a written demand or written assertion by one of the contracting parties seeking, as a matter of right, the payment of money in a sum certain, the adjustment or interpretation of contract terms, or other relief arising under or relating to this contract.

statement: The Contractor shall provide the specified certification when submitting any claim exceeding $100,000.

quote: that the amount requested accurately reflects the contract adjustment for which the Contractor believes the Government is liable; and that I am authorized to certify the claim on behalf of the Contractor.”

quote: A claim by the Contractor shall be made in writing and, unless otherwise stated in this contract, submitted within 6 years after accrual of the claim to the Contracting Officer for a written decision.

statement: For Contractor-certified claims over $100,000, the Contracting Officer must, within 60 days, decide the claim or notify the Contractor of the date by which the decision will be made.
quote: For Contractor-certified claims over $100,000, the Contracting Officer must, within 60 days, decide the claim or notify the Contractor of the date by which the decision will be made.

statement: The Contracting Officer's decision shall be final unless the Contractor appeals or files a suit as provided in the Contract Disputes statute.
quote: The Contracting Officer's decision shall be final unless the Contractor appeals or files a suit as provided in 41 U.S.C. chapter 71.

statement: The Government shall pay interest on the amount found due and unpaid from the date that the Contracting Officer receives the claim (certified, if required) or from the date that payment otherwise would be due if that date is later, until the date of payment.
quote: The Government shall pay interest on the amount found due and unpaid from (1) the date that the Contracting Officer receives the claim (certified, if required); or (2) the date that payment otherwise would be due, if that date is later, until the date of payment.

statement: Under the basic disputes clause, the Contractor shall proceed diligently with performance of the contract, pending final resolution of any request for relief, claim, appeal, or action arising under the contract, and comply with any decision of the Contracting Officer.
quote: The Contractor shall proceed diligently with performance of this contract, pending final resolution of any request for relief, claim, appeal, or action arising under the contract, and comply with any decision of the Contracting Officer.

quote: Upon receipt of the order, the Contractor shall immediately comply with its terms and take all reasonable steps to minimize the incurrence of costs allocable to the work covered by the order during the period of work stoppage.

quote: Upon receipt of the final decision in the protest, the Contracting Officer shall either— (1) Cancel the stop-work order; or (2) Terminate the work covered by the order as provided in the Default, or the Termination for Convenience of the Government, clause of this contract.

statement: If a stop-work order issued under the protest clause is canceled either before or after a final decision in the protest, the Contractor shall resume work.
quote: If a stop-work order issued under this clause is canceled either before or after a final decision in the protest, the Contractor shall resume work.

quote: The Contracting Officer shall make an equitable adjustment in the delivery schedule or contract price, or both, and the contract shall be modified, in writing, accordingly, if—

statement: The contractor shall submit a final settlement proposal covering unvouchered costs and any proposed fee to the TCO within 1 year from the effective date of termination, unless the period is extended by the TCO.
quote: The contractor shall submit a final settlement proposal covering unvouchered costs and any proposed fee to the TCO within 1 year from the effective date of termination, unless the period is extended by the TCO.

statement: The contractor shall use the form prescribed in 49.602-1, unless the TCO authorizes otherwise.
quote: The contractor shall use the form prescribed in 49.602-1, unless the TCO authorizes otherwise.

statement: The settlement proposal shall not include costs that have been finally disallowed by the contracting officer, or costs previously vouchered and formally questioned by the Government but not yet decided as to allowability.
quote: The proposal shall not include costs that have been— (a) Finally disallowed by the contracting officer; or (b) Previously vouchered and formally questioned by the Government but not yet decided as to allowability.

statement: The inventory disposal schedules shall be submitted within 120 days from the effective date of termination unless otherwise extended by the TCO based on a written justification to support the extension.
quote: The inventory disposal schedules shall be submitted within 120 days from the effective date of termination unless otherwise extended by the TCO based on a written justification to support the extension.

statement: The inventory disposal schedules shall be prepared on Standard Form 1428, Inventory Disposal Schedule.
quote: The inventory disposal schedules shall be prepared on Standard Form 1428, Inventory Disposal Schedule.

statement: The TCO shall submit the settlement proposal to the appropriate audit agency for review, but no referral is required if the settlement proposal is limited to an adjustment of fee.
quote: The TCO shall submit the settlement proposal to the appropriate audit agency for review (see 49.107). However, if the settlement proposal is limited to an adjustment of fee, no referral to the audit agency is required.

statement: In a partial termination, the TCO shall limit the settlement to an adjustment of the fee, if any, and, with the concurrence of the contracting office, to a reduction in the estimated cost.
quote: In a partial termination, the TCO shall limit the settlement to an adjustment of the fee, if any, and with the concurrence of the contracting office, to a reduction in the estimated cost.

statement: In a partial termination, the TCO shall adjust the fee as provided in 49.304-2 and 49.305 unless the terminated portion is clearly severable from the balance of the contract; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CLS-1314.
quote: The TCO shall adjust the fee as provided in 49.304-2 and 49.305, unless— (1) The terminated portion is clearly severable from the balance of the contract

statement: The second exception to the TCO's duty to adjust the fee as provided in 49.304-2 and 49.305 (the unless-clause quoted in CL-CLS-1313) is that performance of the contract is virtually complete, or performance of any continued portion is only on subsidiary items or spare parts, or is otherwise not substantial.
quote: or (2) Performance of the contract is virtually complete, or performance of any continued portion is only on subsidiary items or spare parts, or is otherwise not substantial.

statement: In the case of the exceptions in paragraph (a) of the partial-termination section, the procedures in 49.302 and 49.303 apply.
quote: In the case of the exceptions in paragraph (a), the procedures in 49.302 and 49.303 apply.

statement: The contractor shall limit the settlement proposal to a proposed reduction in the amount of fee.
quote: The contractor shall limit the settlement proposal to a proposed reduction in the amount of fee.

statement: The final settlement proposal shall be submitted to the TCO within one year from the effective date of termination, unless the period is extended by the TCO.
quote: The final settlement proposal shall be submitted to the TCO within one year from the effective date of termination, unless the period is extended by the TCO.

statement: The proposal may be submitted in the form prescribed in 49.602-1 or by letter appropriately certified.
quote: The proposal may be submitted in the form prescribed in 49.602-1 or by letter appropriately certified.

statement: The contractor shall substantiate the amount of fee claimed.
quote: The contractor shall substantiate the amount of fee claimed (see 49.305).

statement: When a partial termination settlement is limited to an adjustment of fee, the contractor shall continue to submit the SF 1034 public voucher for costs reimbursable under the contract.
quote: When a partial termination settlement is limited to adjustment of fee, the contractor shall continue to submit the SF 1034, Public Voucher for Purchases and Services Other than Personal, for costs reimbursable under the contract.

statement: The contractor shall not be reimbursed for costs of settlements with subcontractors unless the required approvals or ratifications have been obtained.
quote: The contractor shall not be reimbursed for costs of settlements with subcontractors unless required approvals or ratifications have been obtained (see 49.108).

statement: When a contract is terminated for default, or a procedure authorized by 49.402-4 is followed, the contracting officer shall prepare a memorandum for the contract file explaining the reasons for the action taken.
quote: When a contract is terminated for default or a procedure authorized by 49.402-4 is followed, the contracting officer shall prepare a memorandum for the contract file explaining the reasons for the action taken.

statement: The contracting officer, in accordance with agency procedures, shall ensure that information relating to the termination for default notice and a subsequent withdrawal or a conversion to a termination for convenience is reported in accordance with 42.1503(h).
quote: The contracting officer, in accordance with agency procedures, shall ensure that information relating to the termination for default notice and a subsequent withdrawal or a conversion to a termination for convenience is reported in accordance with 42.1503(h).

statement: If the surety does not arrange for completion of the contract, the contracting officer normally will arrange for completion of the work by awarding a new contract based on the same plans and specifications.
quote: If the surety does not arrange for completion of the contract, the contracting officer normally will arrange for completion of the work by awarding a new contract based on the same plans and specifications.

statement: The new completion contract may be the result of sealed bidding or any other appropriate contracting method or procedure.
quote: The new contract may be the result of sealed bidding or any other appropriate contracting method or procedure.

statement: The contracting officer shall exercise reasonable diligence to obtain the lowest price available for completion.
quote: The contracting officer shall exercise reasonable diligence to obtain the lowest price available for completion.

statement: The contract provides that the contractor and the surety are liable to the Government for resultant damages.
quote: The contract provides that the contractor and the surety are liable to the Government for resultant damages.

statement: The contracting officer shall use all retained percentages of progress payments previously made and any progress payments due for work completed before the termination to liquidate the liability of the contractor and the surety to the Government.
quote: The contracting officer shall use all retained percentages of progress payments previously made to the contractor and any progress payments due for work completed before the termination to liquidate the contractor's and the surety's liability to the Government.

statement: If the retained and unpaid amounts are insufficient, the contracting officer shall take steps to recover the additional sum from the contractor and the surety.
quote: If the retained and unpaid amounts are insufficient, the contracting officer shall take steps to recover the additional sum from the contractor and the surety.

statement: Subject to the terms of the termination clause, and whenever termination inventory is involved, the contractor shall submit complete inventory disposal schedules to the TCO reflecting inventory that is allocable to the terminated portion of the contract.
quote: Subject to the terms of the termination clause, and whenever termination inventory is involved, the contractor shall submit complete inventory disposal schedules to the TCO reflecting inventory that is allocable to the terminated portion of the contract.

statement: The TCO shall execute a no-cost settlement agreement, as 49.603-6 or 49.603-7 applies, if the conditions in the rest of the sentence hold; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CLS-1301.
quote: The TCO shall execute a no-cost settlement agreement (see 49.603-6 or 49.603-7, as applicable) if

statement: FAR subpart 49.3 is headed Additional Principles for Cost-Reimbursement Contracts Terminated for Convenience; the quote is a complete heading, and CL-CLS-1333 gives the heading of 49.303.
quote: Subpart 49.3—Additional Principles for Cost-Reimbursement Contracts Terminated for Convenience
note: The subpart heading is printed at the end of the text of the preceding section in the stored original.

statement: FAR 49.303 is headed Procedure after discontinuing vouchers.
quote: 49.303 Procedure after discontinuing vouchers.

statement: FAR 49.304 is headed Procedure for partial termination.
quote: 49.304 Procedure for partial termination.

statement: FAR 49.402 is headed Termination of fixed-price contracts for default.
quote: 49.402 Termination of fixed-price contracts for default.
note: The quoted heading is the whole text printed at the section number; its sub-sections, such as 49.402-5 and 49.402-8, follow under it.

statement: The subpart prescribes the principal contract termination clauses. It does not apply to contracts that use the clause at 52.213-4, Terms and Conditions—Simplified Acquisitions (Other Than Commercial Products and Commercial Services).
quote: This subpart prescribes the principal contract termination clauses. This subpart does not apply to contracts that use the clause at 52.213-4, Terms and Conditions—Simplified Acquisitions (Other Than Commercial Products and Commercial Services).

statement: Agencies may, in appropriate cases, authorize the use of special purpose clauses when those clauses are consistent with the chapter.
quote: In appropriate cases, agencies may authorize the use of special purpose clauses, if consistent with this chapter.

statement: The standard forms listed below in that section shall be used for settling terminated prime contracts.
quote: The standard forms listed below shall be used for settling terminated prime contracts.

statement: The forms at 49.602-1 and 49.602-2 may also be used for settling terminated subcontracts.
quote: The forms at 49.602-1 and 49.602-2 may also be used for settling terminated subcontracts.

statement: Standard Form 1428, Inventory Disposal Schedule, and Standard Form 1429, its continuation sheet, shall be used to support settlement proposals submitted on the forms specified in 49.602-1(b) and (d).
quote: Standard Form (SF) 1428, Inventory Disposal Schedule, and SF 1429, Inventory Disposal Schedule—Continuation Sheet, shall be used to support settlement proposals submitted on the forms specified in 49.602-1(b) and (d).

statement: Standard Form 1439, Schedule of Accounting Information, shall be filed in support of a settlement proposal unless the proposal is filed on Standard Form 1438, Settlement Proposal (Short Form).
quote: Standard Form 1439, Schedule of Accounting Information, shall be filed in support of a settlement proposal unless the proposal is filed on Standard Form 1438, Settlement Proposal (Short Form) (see 49.206-1(e)).

statement: Standard Form 1440, Application for Partial Payment, shall be used to apply for partial payments.
quote: Standard Form 1440, Application for Partial Payment, shall be used to apply for partial payments (see 49.112-1).

statement: Standard Form 30, Amendment of Solicitation/Modification of Contract, shall be used to execute a settlement agreement.
quote: Standard Form 30 (SF 30), Amendment of Solicitation/Modification of Contract, shall be used to execute a settlement agreement (see 49.109-1).

statement: The formats to be used for termination for convenience settlement agreements should be substantially as shown in the section that contains this sentence.
quote: The formats to be used for termination for convenience settlement agreements should be substantially as shown in this section (see 49.109).

statement: A termination contracting officer may modify the contents of these settlement agreements to conform with special termination clauses prescribed or authorized by the officer's agency. The sentence cites 49.501 and 49.505(c) as examples to see.
quote: Termination contracting officers (TCO's) may, however, modify the contents of these agreements to conform with special termination clauses prescribed or authorized by their agencies (e.g., see 49.501 and 49.505(c)).
note: This is a permission held by the termination contracting officer, not a duty.

statement: Congressional notification is required for any termination involving a reduction in employment of 100 or more contractor employees.
quote: Congressional notification is required for any termination involving a reduction in employment of 100 or more contractor employees.
note: The quoted sentence does not say who gives the notification or when.

statement: Proposed terminations must be cleared through department or agency liaison offices before the termination notice, or any information on the proposed termination, is released to the contractor.
quote: Proposed terminations must be cleared through department/agency liaison offices before release of the termination notice, or any information on the proposed termination, to the contractor.

statement: The procedures at PGI 249.7001 are to be followed for congressional notification and release of information.
quote: Follow the procedures at PGI 249.7001 for congressional notification and release of information.

statement: The clause at 252.249-7002, Notification of Anticipated Contract Termination or Reduction, shall be used in all contracts under a major defense program.
quote: Use the clause at 252.249-7002, Notification of Anticipated Contract Termination or Reduction, in all contracts under a major defense program.

statement: A listing of the Standard forms is located in subpart 53.3.
quote: A listing of the Standard forms is located in subpart 53.3.

statement: FAR section 45.602 applies to the reutilization, including transfer and donation, of Government property that is not required for continued performance of a Government contract.
quote: This section is applicable to the reutilization, including transfer and donation, of Government property that is not required for continued performance of a Government contract.

statement: Except for 45.602-1, section 45.602 does not apply to scrap other than scrap aircraft parts.
quote: Except for 45.602-1, this section does not apply to scrap other than scrap aircraft parts.
note: The excepted section is 45.602-1, which the printed text carves out of the scrap exclusion. The text does not say what happens to scrap that the exclusion leaves out.

statement: Surplus personal property that has completed screening in accordance with 45.602-3(a) shall be sold in accordance with the Federal Management Regulation policy for the sale of surplus personal property, at 41 CFR part 102-38.
quote: Surplus personal property that has completed screening in accordance with 45.602-3(a) shall be sold in accordance with the policy for the sale of surplus personal property contained in the Federal Management Regulation, at part 102-38 (41 CFR part 102-38).
note: The sentence is in the passive and does not name who sells the property.

statement: Agencies may specify implementing procedures.
quote: Agencies may specify implementing procedures.
note: A permission, not a duty; the sentence follows the requirement that screened surplus personal property be sold under the Federal Management Regulation policy.

statement: Under the section titled Use of GSA sponsored sales centers, agencies may use sales center services.
quote: Use of GSA sponsored sales centers. Agencies may use sales center services.
note: The quote includes the section title, which names the centers as GSA sponsored. The sentence does not make their use a duty.

statement: Use of such sales centers for the sale of surplus property is authorized when it is in the best interest of the Government and consistent with contract terms and conditions.
quote: Use of such centers for sale of surplus property is authorized when in the best interest of the Government, consistent with contract terms and conditions.
note: The section title names the centers as GSA sponsored. The sentence does not say who decides whether the best-interest and consistency conditions are met.

statement: Under the section titled Proceeds from sales of surplus property, proceeds of any sale are to be credited to the Treasury of the United States as miscellaneous receipts, unless otherwise authorized by statute or the contract or any subcontract thereunder authorizes the proceeds to be credited to the price or cost of the work.
quote: Proceeds of any sale are to be credited to the Treasury of the United States as miscellaneous receipts, unless otherwise authorized by statute or the contract or any subcontract thereunder authorizes the proceeds to be credited to the price or cost of the work (40 U.S.C. 571 and 574).
note: The section heading limits the paragraph to sales of surplus property. The sentence is passive and does not name who credits the proceeds. The statute locations the paragraph cites are not restated here.

statement: Agencies should consider the sale of property pursuant to the exchange/sale authority in FMR 102-39 (41 CFR part 102-39) when agencies are acquiring or plan to acquire similar products and other requirements of the authority are satisfied.
quote: Agencies should consider the sale of property pursuant to the exchange/sale authority in FMR 102-39 (41 CFR part 102-39) when agencies are acquiring or plan to acquire similar products and other requirements of the authority are satisfied.
note: The verb is should, so this is a consideration rather than a duty.

statement: The subpart on reporting, reutilization and disposal establishes policies and procedures for the reporting, reutilization and disposal of contractor inventory excess to contracts and of property that forms the basis of a claim against the Government, for example termination inventory under fixed-price contracts.
quote: This subpart establishes policies and procedures for the reporting, reutilization, and disposal of contractor inventory excess to contracts and of property that forms the basis of a claim against the Government (e.g., termination inventory under fixed-price contracts).

statement: The subpart on reporting, reutilization and disposal does not apply to the disposal of real property or to property for which the Government has a lien or title solely as a result of advance, progress, or performance-based payments that have been liquidated.
quote: This subpart does not apply to the disposal of real property or to property for which the Government has a lien or title solely as a result of advance, progress, or performance-based payments that have been liquidated.

statement: The paragraph on proceeds ends with a parenthetical citing sections 571 and 574 of title 40 of the United States Code.
note: The quote is the citation printed at the end of the proceeds sentence; the section does not say what the cited sections provide.

statement: The condition for that examination is that public financial statements of the governmental agency are customarily examined by that auditing staff.
quote: if public financial statements of such governmental agency are customarily examined by such auditing staff.
note: Completes the sentence begun in CL-CLS-1238.

statement: If a registrant is required to file financial statements of any other person, those statements need not be examined if examination of them would not be required were that person itself a registrant.
quote: If a registrant is required to file financial statements of any other person, such statements need not be examined if examination of such statements would not be required if such person were itself a registrant.

statement: No caption should be shown in any financial statement as to which the items and conditions are not present.
quote: No caption should be shown in any financial statement as to which the items and conditions are not present.
note: Paragraph (a) of the section.

statement: Financial statements that are not required, or that are inapplicable because the required matter is not present, need not be filed.
quote: Financial statements not required or inapplicable because the required matter is not present need not be filed.
note: Paragraph (b) of the section.

statement: The reasons for the omission of any required financial statements shall be indicated.
quote: The reasons for the omission of any required financial statements shall be indicated.
note: Paragraph (c) of the section. The text names no one who indicates the reasons and does not say where they are indicated.

statement: If a note covering substantially the same subject matter is required for two or more financial statements relating to the same or affiliated persons, for which separate sets of notes are presented, the required information may be shown in a note to only one of those statements; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CLS-1454.
quote: If a note covering substantially the same subject matter is required with respect to two or more financial statements relating to the same or affiliated persons, for which separate sets of notes are presented, the required information may be shown in a note to only one of such statements

statement: The required information may be shown in a note to only one of the statements provided that a clear and specific reference to it is made in each of the other statements for which the note is required.
quote: Provided, That a clear and specific reference thereto is made in each of the other statements with respect to which the note is required.
note: Completes the sentence begun in CL-CLS-1453.

statement: Discount on shares, or any unamortized balance of it, shall be shown separately as a deduction from the applicable account or accounts as circumstances require.
quote: Discount on shares, or any unamortized balance thereof, shall be shown separately as a deduction from the applicable account(s) as circumstances require.

statement: FAR part 49 establishes policies and procedures relating to the complete or partial termination of contracts for the convenience of the Government or for default.
quote: This part establishes policies and procedures relating to the complete or partial termination of contracts for the convenience of the Government or for default.

statement: FAR part 49 prescribes contract clauses relating to termination and excusable delay and includes instructions for using termination and settlement forms.
quote: It prescribes contract clauses relating to termination and excusable delay and includes instructions for using termination and settlement forms.

statement: The section on notice of termination for convenience refers readers to 49.402-3(g) for notice of termination for default.
quote: (See 49.402-3(g) for notice of termination for default.)

statement: The section says to use the clause at 252.244-7000, Subcontracts for Commercial Products and Commercial Services, in solicitations and contracts, including solicitations and contracts using FAR part 12 procedures for the acquisition of commercial products and commercial services.
quote: Use the clause at 252.244-7000, Subcontracts for Commercial Products and Commercial Services, in solicitations and contracts, including solicitations and contracts using FAR part 12 procedures for the acquisition of commercial products and commercial services.

statement: Change order means a written order, signed by the contracting officer, directing the contractor to make a change that the Changes clause authorizes the contracting officer to order without the contractor's consent.
quote: Change order means a written order, signed by the contracting officer, directing the contractor to make a change that the Changes clause authorizes the contracting officer to order without the contractor's consent.

statement: Continued portion of the contract means the portion of a contract that the contractor must continue to perform following a partial termination.
quote: Continued portion of the contract means the portion of a contract that the contractor must continue to perform following a partial termination.

statement: Contract modification means any written change in the terms of a contract, and the definition points to 43.103.
quote: Contract modification means any written change in the terms of a contract (see 43.103).

statement: A partial termination is the termination of a part, but not all, of the work that has not been completed and accepted under a contract.
quote: Partial termination means the termination of a part, but not all, of the work that has not been completed and accepted under a contract.

statement: The terminated portion of the contract is the portion of a contract that the contractor is not to perform following a partial termination.
quote: Terminated portion of the contract means the portion of a contract that the contractor is not to perform following a partial termination.

statement: Termination inventory is any property purchased, supplied, manufactured, furnished, or otherwise acquired for the performance of a contract subsequently terminated and properly allocable to the terminated portion of the contract.
quote: Termination inventory means any property purchased, supplied, manufactured, furnished, or otherwise acquired for the performance of a contract subsequently terminated and properly allocable to the terminated portion of the contract.

quote: It includes Government-furnished property. It does not include any facilities, material, special test equipment, or special tooling that are subject to a separate contract or to a special contract requirement governing their use or disposition.

quote: Termination for convenience means the exercise of the Government's right to completely or partially terminate performance of work under a contract when it is in the Government's interest.

quote: Termination for default means the exercise of the Government's right to completely or partially terminate a contract because of the contractor's actual or anticipated failure to perform its contractual obligations.

statement: A cost is allowable only when it complies with all of the following: reasonableness, allocability, standards promulgated by the CAS Board if applicable (otherwise generally accepted accounting principles and practices appropriate to the circumstances), the terms of the contract, and any limitations set forth in FAR subpart 31.2.
quote: A cost is allowable only when the cost complies with all of the following requirements: (1) Reasonableness. (2) Allocability.
note: RFO FAR 31.201-2(a) retains the same allowability requirements.

statement: The contracting officer may disallow all or part of a claimed cost that is inadequately supported by the contractor's records.
quote: The contracting officer may disallow all or part of a claimed cost that is inadequately supported.
note: Renumbered to paragraph (d)(2) in RFO FAR 31.201-2.

statement: A cost is reasonable if, in its nature and amount, it does not exceed that which would be incurred by a prudent person in the conduct of competitive business.
quote: A cost is reasonable if, in its nature and amount, it does not exceed that which would be incurred by a prudent person in the conduct of competitive business.
note: RFO FAR 31.201-3(a) defines reasonableness using reasonable person instead of prudent person.

statement: No presumption of reasonableness attaches to the incurrence of costs by a contractor.
quote: No presumption of reasonableness shall be attached to the incurrence of costs by a contractor.
note: In RFO FAR 31.201-3(a)(1), this rule is set forth in a separate subparagraph.

statement: A cost is allocable if it is assignable or chargeable to one or more cost objectives on the basis of relative benefits received or other equitable relationship.
quote: A cost is allocable if it is assignable or chargeable to one or more cost objectives on the basis of relative benefits received or other equitable relationship.
note: In RFO FAR 31.201-4, this fundamental requirement is designated paragraph (a).

statement: Subject to the general allocability definition (assignable or chargeable to cost objectives on the basis of relative benefits received or other equitable relationship), a cost is allocable to a Government contract if it is necessary to the overall operation of the business, although a direct relationship to any particular cost objective cannot be shown.
quote: Is necessary to the overall operation of the business, although a direct relationship to any particular cost objective cannot be shown.
note: In RFO FAR 31.201-4, this base category is renumbered from paragraph (c) to paragraph (d).

statement: Costs of amusement, diversions, social activities, and directly associated costs are unallowable.
quote: Costs of amusement, diversions, social activities, and any directly associated costs such as tickets to shows or sports events, meals, lodging, rentals, transportation, and gratuities are unallowable.
note: RFO FAR 31.205-14(a) structures the principle into lettered paragraphs and references sporting events.

statement: Costs made specifically unallowable under the entertainment cost principle are not allowable under any other cost principle.
quote: Costs made specifically unallowable under this cost principle are not allowable under any other cost principle.
note: RFO FAR 31.205-14(c) contains the same rule.

statement: Travel costs incurred by contractor personnel on official company business are allowable, subject to the limitations in the travel cost principle.
quote: Costs incurred by contractor personnel on official company business are allowable, subject to the limitations contained in this subsection.

note: RFO FAR 31.205-46(a)(3)(iv) retains the $75 receipt threshold for actual expense method claims.

quote: Airfare costs in excess of the lowest priced airfare available to the contractor during normal business hours are unallowable except when such accommodations require circuitous routing, require travel during unreasonable hours, excessively prolong travel
note: RFO FAR 31.205-46(b) structures the excess airfare restrictions and exceptions under subsection (b)(1).

quote: Except as provided in paragraphs (d) and (e) of this subsection, or as provided in agency regulations, costs for IR&D and B&P are allowable as indirect expenses on contracts to the extent that those costs are allocable and reasonable.
note: Under FAR 31.205-18(c), IR&D and B&P costs are allowable as indirect expenses subject to allocability and reasonableness.

statement: Under DFARS 231.205-18(a), a major contractor is any contractor whose covered segments allocated a total of more than $11 million in IR&D and B&P costs to covered contracts during the preceding fiscal year; the exclusion of smaller segments from that total is stated in CL-CMP-0880.
quote: Major contractor means any contractor whose covered segments allocated a total of more than $11 million in IR&D costs and B&P costs to covered contracts during the preceding fiscal year.
note: Major contractors are subject to the DTIC reporting and allowability requirements in DFARS 231.205-18(c).

statement: Under DFARS 231.205-18(a), a covered segment is a product division of the contractor that allocated more than $1,100,000 in IR&D and B&P costs to covered contracts during the preceding fiscal year; a contractor with no product divisions is itself the covered segment as a whole.
quote: Covered segment means a product division of the contractor that allocated more than $1,100,000 in independent research and development (IR&D) costs and bid and proposal (B&P) costs to covered contracts during the preceding fiscal year.
note: Segments allocating less than $1,100,000 are not subject to the allowability limitations in DFARS 231.205-18(c).

statement: The three primary contractor business systems audited by the Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) are the Accounting System, the Material Management and Accounting System (MMAS), and the Cost Estimating System.
quote: This chapter provides a general overview of the three primary contractor business systems audited by the Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA): the Accounting System, the Material Management and Accounting System (MMAS), and the Cost Estimating System.

statement: Fundamental requirements for contractor business system audits apply to each contractor business system used to propose, charge, or bill significant costs to Government contracts.
quote: These fundamental requirements apply to audits of each of the contractor's business systems that are used to propose, charge, or bill significant costs to Government contracts.

statement: After audit or review of a business system, the contracting officer is responsible for determining if the system is acceptable.
quote: After audit or review of a business system, the contracting officer is responsible for determining if the system is acceptable.

statement: The objective of each business system audit is to gather sufficient appropriate evidence to express an opinion on the contractor's compliance with applicable business system criteria during the audit period.
quote: The objective of each business system audit is to gather sufficient appropriate evidence to express an opinion on the contractor's compliance with the applicable business system criteria (e.g., DFARS, FAR, applicable laws and regulations, and contract terms) during the audit period.

statement: When the auditor can rely on the contractor's business system to record, process, summarize, and report in a manner consistent with the applicable DFARS and Government contract laws and regulations, control risk would be considered low.
quote: In those cases where the auditor can rely on the contractor's business system to record, process, summarize, and report in a manner consistent with the applicable DFARS and Government contract laws and regulations, control risk would be considered low.

statement: For contractors with outstanding business system deficiencies, the auditor should recommend actions to the ACO to encourage correction, such as suspension of costs, disapproval of the system, or penalties.
quote: At those contractors with outstanding business system deficiencies, the auditor should recommend actions to the ACO to encourage the contractor to correct the deficiencies (e.g., suspension of costs, disapproval of system, penalties).

statement: Smaller contractors may have less formal internal controls that accomplish business system control objectives.
quote: Smaller contractors may have less formal internal controls that accomplish these control objectives.

statement: Once a full business system audit has been performed, it should serve as a baseline for establishing the scope of subsequent audits of that system.
quote: Once a full business system audit has been performed, it should serve as a baseline for establishing the scope of subsequent audits of that system.

statement: Subsequent audits should cover major system changes, including procedures to validate that changes have controls in place to comply with applicable DFARS business system criteria; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-8124.
quote: In addition, subsequent audits should cover major system changes. This should include audit procedures to validate that the business system changes have controls in place to comply with the applicable DFARS business system (i.e., accounting, MMAS and estimating systems) criteria

statement: For key internal controls that have changed, the auditor should request a contractor walk-through and demonstration to gain an understanding, while leveraging information from the prior audit where possible.
quote: For key internal controls that have changed, the auditor should request a contractor walk-through and demonstration to gain an understanding. The auditor should leverage information from the prior audit where possible to prevent duplication and increase efficiency.

statement: The auditor should identify control objectives associated with the contractor's compliance with DFARS business systems requirements, applicable laws and regulations, and contract terms.
quote: The auditor should identify those control objectives associated with the contractor’s compliance with the DFARS business systems requirements, applicable laws and regulations, and contract terms.

statement: While DCAA auditors do not express an opinion on internal controls, they test key internal controls that are related to DFARS compliance.
quote: While we do not express an opinion on internal controls, we do test the key internal controls that are related to DFARS compliance.

statement: To obtain evidence of the effectiveness of internal control activities, the auditor should perform physical observations, inquiries of appropriate personnel, or inspection of relevant documents.
quote: To obtain evidence of the effectiveness of internal control activities, the auditor should perform physical observations, inquiries of appropriate personnel, or inspection of relevant documents.

statement: No single specific test of controls is always necessary, applicable, or equally effective in every circumstance, and a combination of tests is often required to provide necessary assurance that controls operate effectively.
quote: No one specific test is always necessary, applicable, or equally effective in every circumstance. In fact, a combination of these types of tests is often required to provide the necessary level of assurance that controls are working effectively.

statement: Timing of an audit procedure refers to when it is performed or the period or date to which the audit evidence applies.
quote: Timing of an audit procedure refers to when it is performed or the period or date to which the audit evidence applies.

statement: When evidence relates only to a specific point in time, such as from physical observation, the auditor should obtain additional evidence that the control was effective during the entire audit period.
quote: When the evidence relates only to a specific point in time, such as evidence obtained from physical observation, the auditor should obtain additional evidence that the control was effective during the entire audit period.

statement: The extent of testing of business system controls is significantly impacted by the audit office's total audit experience with the contractor.
quote: The extent of testing is also significantly impacted by the office's total audit experience with the contractor.

statement: Control risk is the likelihood that a material misstatement or noncompliance in an account or area subject to audit will not be prevented or detected and corrected on a timely basis by the contractor’s internal controls.
quote: Control risk is the likelihood that a material misstatement or noncompliance in an account or area subject to audit will not be prevented or detected and corrected on a timely basis by the contractor’s internal controls.

statement: In assessing control risk, the auditor considers the effectiveness of established control activities to accomplish stated control objectives, where more effective control activities result in lower control risk.
quote: In assessing control risk, the auditor considers the effectiveness of established control activities to accomplish stated control objectives. The more effective the control activities are, the lower the control risk.

statement: Only when internal controls have been tested and determined to be effective can the auditor rely on them and reduce the amount of substantive testing in the applicable audit area.
quote: Only when the internal controls have been tested and determined to be effective, can the auditor rely on them and reduce the amount of substantive testing in the applicable audit area.

statement: If internal controls are found not to be operating effectively, the auditor cannot rely on them when performing other than business system audits, and will need to design substantive audit procedures to account for the lack of effective internal controls in the applicable audit area.
quote: If the internal controls are found not to be operating effectively, the auditor cannot rely on them (when performing other than business system audits) and will need to design substantive audit procedures to account for the lack of effective internal controls in the applicable audit area.

statement: Assessments of low risk for specific control objectives mean the auditor can rely on internal controls and reduce testing in other related audits to analytical procedures or a combination of tests of details.
quote: Assessments of low risk for specific control objectives mean the auditor can rely on the contractor’s internal controls and can reduce testing in other related audits to analytical procedures and/or a combination of tests of details.

statement: A material weakness is a deficiency or combination of deficiencies in internal control over business system information such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement will not be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis.
quote: Weakness means a deficiency or combination of deficiencies in the internal control over information in contractor business systems, such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of such information will not be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis.

statement: A reasonable possibility exists when the likelihood of an event occurring is either probable or more than remote but less than likely.
quote: A reasonable possibility exists when the likelihood of an event occurring is — (1) probable; or (2) more than remote but less than likely.

statement: A system deficiency is a deficiency or combination of deficiencies in internal control over information in contractor business systems that does not rise to the level of a material weakness.
quote: A system deficiency is a deficiency or combination of deficiencies in the internal control over information in contractor business systems that does not rise to the level of a material weakness.

statement: A less than material noncompliance that warrants attention of governance is a noncompliance that does not have a material impact on the acceptability of the business system but is important enough to be communicated.
quote: A less than material noncompliance that warrants attention of those charged with governance (the contractor and contracting officer) is a noncompliance that does not have a material impact on the acceptability of the business system but is important enough to be communicated.

statement: Incurred cost audits are usually performed on a contractor-wide basis by first evaluating management and financial systems and controls combined with transaction testing across all business activities.
quote: Incurred cost audits are usually performed on a contractor-wide basis. This approach recognizes the efficiency of first gaining an understanding of the adequacy of management and financial systems and controls combined with transaction testing across all business activities

statement: Periodic audits of relevant business systems establish an understanding of internal systems and controls to determine the nature and extent of transaction testing on incurred cost audits.
quote: Periodic audits of relevant business systems serve to develop an appropriate understanding of systems and controls necessary to determine the nature and extent of transaction testing needed on individual incurred cost audits.

statement: Separate audits of individual business systems may not be required for smaller contractors, whose internal controls may instead be evaluated during the final indirect cost audit or other contract audits.
quote: For smaller contractors, separate audits of individual contractor business systems may not be necessary. An understanding of the contractor's relevant internal controls may be gained at the time of the final indirect cost audit or during other contract audits.

statement: Auditors must design and perform procedures on all material balances to support the audit opinion, regardless of assessed risk.

statement: Qualitative risks may justify auditing amounts that fall below the quantitative materiality threshold.

statement: A cost impact proposal audit tests the contractor's proposed estimate of the cost impact to Government contracts of a practice change or a material noncompliance, expressed as a general dollar magnitude or a detailed cost impact.

statement: Contractors with fully CAS-covered contracts must complete, submit and maintain a Disclosure Statement.

quote: that the business unit of the contractor or subcontractor that will perform the work— (1) Is primarily engaged in the sale of commercial items; and (2) Would not otherwise be subject to the Cost Accounting Standards under this Chapter.

statement: The head of an executive agency may waive the applicability of the Cost Accounting Standards for a contract or subcontract under exceptional circumstances when necessary to meet the needs of the agency.
quote: The head of an executive agency may waive the applicability of the Cost Accounting Standards for a contract or subcontract under exceptional circumstances when necessary to meet the needs of the agency.

statement: A determination to waive the applicability of the Cost Accounting Standards by the agency head must be set forth in writing and must include a statement of the circumstances justifying the waiver.
quote: A determination to waive the applicability of the Cost Accounting Standards by the agency head shall be set forth in writing, and shall include a statement of the circumstances justifying the waiver.

statement: The head of an executive agency may not delegate the waiver authority under paragraphs (a) and (b) of the section to any official below the senior policymaking level in the agency.
quote: The head of an executive agency may not delegate the authority under paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section, to any official below the senior policymaking level in the agency.

statement: The head of each executive agency must report the waivers granted under paragraphs (a) and (b) to the Cost Accounting Standards Board on an annual basis, not later than 90 days after the close of the Government's fiscal year.
quote: The head of each executive agency shall report the waivers granted under paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section, for that agency, to the Cost Accounting Standards Board, on an annual basis, not later than 90 days after the close of the Government's fiscal year.

statement: Upon request of an agency head or his designee, the Cost Accounting Standards Board may waive all or any part of the Cost Accounting Standards clause requirements, or of the disclosure and consistency of cost accounting practices requirements.
quote: Upon request of an agency head or his designee, the Cost Accounting Standards Board may waive all or any part of the requirements of 9903.201-4(a), Cost Accounting Standards, or 9903.201-4(c), Disclosure and Consistency of Cost Accounting Practices

statement: The requirements of part 9903 shall, to the maximum extent practicable, be administered by the cognizant Federal agency responsible for a particular contractor organization or location, usually the Federal agency responsible for negotiating indirect cost rates on behalf of the Government.
quote: The requirements of part 9903 shall, to the maximum extent practicable, be administered by the cognizant Federal agency responsible for a particular contractor organization or location, usually the Federal agency responsible for negotiating indirect cost rates on behalf of the Government.

statement: The cognizant Federal agency should take the lead role in administering the requirements of part 9903 and in coordinating CAS administrative actions with all affected Federal agencies.
quote: The cognizant Federal agency should take the lead role in administering the requirements of part 9903 and coordinating CAS administrative actions with all affected Federal agencies.

statement: When multiple CAS-covered contracts or more than one Federal agency are involved, agencies should discourage Contracting Officers from individually administering CAS on a contract-by-contract basis.
quote: When multiple CAS-covered contracts or more than one Federal agency are involved, agencies should discourage Contracting Officers from individually administering CAS on a contract-by-contract basis.

statement: Federal agencies shall prescribe regulations and establish internal policies and procedures governing how they will administer the requirements of CAS-covered contracts, with particular emphasis on inter-agency coordination activities.
quote: Federal agencies shall prescribe regulations and establish internal policies and procedures governing how agencies will administer the requirements of CAS-covered contracts, with particular emphasis on inter-agency coordination activities.

statement: Internal agency policies and procedures must provide for the designation of the agency office or officials responsible for administering CAS at each contractor business unit and for the delegation of the necessary contracting authority; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-8047.
quote: Internal agency policies and procedures shall provide for the designation of the agency office(s) or officials responsible for administering CAS under the agency's CAS-covered contracts at each contractor business unit and the delegation of necessary contracting authority

statement: A cost accounting practice is any disclosed or established accounting method or technique used for allocation of cost to cost objectives, assignment of cost to cost accounting periods, or measurement of cost.
quote: Cost accounting practice, as used in this part, means any disclosed or established accounting method or technique which is used for allocation of cost to cost objectives, assignment of cost to cost accounting periods, or measurement of cost.

statement: The determination of the amount paid, or of a change in the amount paid, for a unit of goods and services is not a cost accounting practice.
quote: The determination of the amount paid or a change in the amount paid for a unit of goods and services is not a cost accounting practice.

statement: Allocation of cost to cost objectives includes both direct and indirect allocation of cost.
quote: Allocation of cost to cost objectives, as used in this part, includes both direct and indirect allocation of cost.

statement: A change to a cost accounting practice is any alteration in a cost accounting practice, whether or not the practices are covered by a Disclosure Statement, apart from the exclusions that follow in the section.
quote: any alteration in a cost accounting practice, as defined in 9903.302-1, whether or not such practices are covered by a Disclosure Statement, except for the following

statement: The initial adoption of a cost accounting practice for the first time a cost is incurred, or a function is created, is not a change in cost accounting practice.
quote: The initial adoption of a cost accounting practice for the first time a cost is incurred, or a function is created, is not a change in cost accounting practice.

statement: The partial or total elimination of a cost, or of the cost of a function, is not a change in cost accounting practice.
quote: The partial or total elimination of a cost or the cost of a function is not a change in cost accounting practice.

statement: The revision of a cost accounting practice for a cost which previously had been immaterial is not a change in cost accounting practice.
quote: The revision of a cost accounting practice for a cost which previously had been immaterial is not a change in cost accounting practice.

statement: In determining whether amounts of cost are material or immaterial, the listed criteria shall be considered where appropriate, and no one criterion is necessarily determinative.
quote: In determining whether amounts of cost are material or immaterial, the following criteria shall be considered where appropriate; no one criterion is necessarily determinative

statement: The absolute dollar amount involved is a materiality criterion: the larger the dollar amount, the more likely it is that the amount is material.
quote: (a) The absolute dollar amount involved. The larger the dollar amount, the more likely that it will be material.

statement: The amount of contract cost compared with the amount under consideration is a materiality criterion: the larger the proportion of the amount under consideration to contract cost, the more likely it is to be material.
quote: (b) The amount of contract cost compared with the amount under consideration. The larger the proportion of the amount under consideration to contract cost, the more likely it is to be material.

statement: Direct cost items, especially where the amounts are themselves part of a base for allocation of indirect costs, normally have more impact on materiality than the same amount of indirect costs.
quote: (c) The relationship between a cost item and a cost objective. Direct cost items, especially if the amounts are themselves part of a base for allocation of indirect costs, will normally have more impact than the same amount of indirect costs.

statement: In judging cumulative impact, it is appropriate to consider whether individually immaterial items tend to offset one another or tend to be in the same direction and so accumulate into a material amount.
quote: (e) The cumulative impact of individually immaterial items. It is appropriate to consider whether such impacts: (1) Tend to offset one another, or (2) Tend to be in the same direction and hence to accumulate into a material amount.

statement: The cost of administrative processing of the price adjustment modification is a materiality criterion; if the cost to process exceeds the amount to be recovered, the amount is less likely to be material.
quote: (f) The cost of administrative processing of the price adjustment modification shall be considered. If the cost to process exceeds the amount to be recovered, it is less likely the amount will be material.

statement: The amount of insurance cost to be assigned to a cost accounting period is the projected average loss for that period plus insurance administration expenses in that period.
quote: The amount of insurance cost to be assigned to a cost accounting period is the projected average loss for that period plus insurance administration expenses in that period.

statement: The allocation of insurance costs to cost objectives shall be based on the beneficial or causal relationship between the insurance costs and the benefiting or causing cost objectives.
quote: The allocation of insurance costs to cost objectives shall be based on the beneficial or casual relationship between the insurance costs and the benefiting or causing cost objectives.

quote: The premium cost applicable to a given policy term shall be assigned pro rata among the cost accounting periods covered by the policy term, except as provided in subdivisions (a)(1) (ii) through (vi) of this subsection.

statement: Where insurance is purchased specifically for, and directly allocated to, a single final cost objective, the premium need not be prorated among cost accounting periods.
quote: Where insurance is purchased specifically for, and directly allocated to, a single final cost objective, the premium need not be prorated among cost accounting periods.

statement: Except as provided in the two listed subdivisions, actual losses shall not become a part of insurance costs.
quote: Except as provided in subdivisions (a)(2)(ii) and (iii) of this subsection, actual losses shall not become a part of insurance costs.

statement: The self-insurance charge that the contractor makes for each period for each type of self-insured risk shall represent the projected average loss for that period.
quote: the contractor shall make a self-insurance charge for each period for each type of self-insured risk which shall represent the projected average loss for that period

statement: Insurance costs shall be allocated on the basis of the factors used to determine the premium, assessment, refund, dividend or self-insurance charge, subject to an exception stated in the same sentence.

statement: Insurance administration expenses which are material in relation to total insurance costs shall be allocated on the same basis as the related premium costs or self-insurance charge.
quote: Insurance administration expenses which are material in relation to total insurance costs shall be allocated on the same basis as the related premium costs or self-insurance charge.

statement: The contractor shall maintain records necessary to substantiate the amounts of premiums, refunds, dividends, losses and self-insurance charges paid or accrued, and the measurement and allocation of insurance costs.

statement: The cost of money applicable to the investment in tangible and intangible capital assets being constructed, fabricated or developed for a contractor's own use shall be included in the capitalized acquisition cost of such assets.

statement: A representative investment amount shall be determined each cost accounting period for each capital asset being constructed, fabricated or developed, giving appropriate consideration to the rate at which costs of construction are incurred.

statement: Other methods for calculating the cost of money to be capitalized may be used, provided the resulting amount does not differ materially from the amount calculated by use of the prescribed rate and investment amount paragraphs.

statement: The FAR System is established for the codification and publication of uniform policies and procedures for acquisition by all executive agencies.
quote: The Federal Acquisition Regulations System is established for the codification and publication of uniform policies and procedures for acquisition by all executive agencies.

statement: The FAR System consists of the FAR, which is the primary document, and agency acquisition regulations that implement or supplement the FAR.
quote: The Federal Acquisition Regulations System consists of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), which is the primary document, and agency acquisition regulations that implement or supplement the FAR.

statement: The FAR System does not include internal agency guidance of the type described in paragraph (a)(2) of FAR 1.301.
quote: The FAR System does not include internal agency guidance of the type described in 1.301(a)(2).

statement: The FAR applies to all acquisitions as defined in part 2 of the FAR, except where expressly excluded.
quote: The FAR applies to all acquisitions as defined in part 2 of the FAR, except where expressly excluded.

statement: Subject to the authorities in paragraph (c) of FAR 1.301 and other statutory authority, an agency head may issue or authorize the issuance of agency acquisition regulations that implement or supplement the FAR.
quote: Subject to the authorities in paragraph (c) below and other statutory authority, an agency head may issue or authorize the issuance of agency acquisition regulations that implement or supplement the FAR

statement: When adopting acquisition regulations, agencies shall ensure that they comply with the Paperwork Reduction Act and the Regulatory Flexibility Act.
quote: When adopting acquisition regulations, agencies shall ensure that they comply with the Paperwork Reduction Act (44 U.S.C. 3501, et seq.) as implemented in 5 CFR part 1320 (see 1.105) and the Regulatory Flexibility Act (5 U.S.C. 601, et seq.).

statement: Agency acquisition regulations implementing or supplementing the FAR for the military departments and defense agencies are issued subject to the authority of the Secretary of Defense.
quote: Agency acquisition regulations implementing or supplementing the FAR are, for— (1) The military departments and defense agencies, issued subject to the authority of the Secretary of Defense;

statement: Issuances under paragraph (a)(2) of FAR 1.301 need not be publicized for public comment.
quote: Issuances under 1.301(a)(2) need not be publicized for public comment.

quote: (b) Written justification for such certification is provided to the Administrator for Federal Procurement Policy by the Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council, and the Administrator approves in writing the inclusion of such certification requirement.

statement: Under a statute, the FAR Council must periodically adjust all statutory acquisition-related dollar thresholds in the FAR for inflation, except as provided in paragraph (c) of FAR 1.109.

statement: The inflation adjustment is calculated every 5 years using the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers.
quote: This adjustment is calculated every 5 years, starting in October 2005, using the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U)

statement: The statute does not permit escalation of acquisition-related dollar thresholds established by the bonds subchapter or the construction wage rate requirements subchapter of 40 U.S.C. chapter 31.

statement: If a threshold is adjusted for inflation, the changed threshold applies throughout the remaining term of the contract, unless there is a subsequent threshold adjustment.
