statement: The statutes cited in FAR 3.402 require in every negotiated contract a warranty by the contractor against contingent fees and permit, as an exception to the warranty, contingent fee arrangements between contractors and bona fide employees or bona fide agencies.
quote: These statutes— (a) Require in every negotiated contract a warranty by the contractor against contingent fees; (b) Permit, as an exception to the warranty, contingent fee arrangements between contractors and bona fide employees or bona fide agencies;

statement: One listed provision of the statutes cited in FAR 3.402 is that, for breach or violation of the warranty by the contractor, the Government may annul the contract without liability or deduct from the contract price or consideration, or otherwise recover, the full amount of the contingent fee.
quote: (c) Provide that, for breach or violation of the warranty by the contractor, the Government may annul the contract without liability or deduct from the contract price or consideration, or otherwise recover, the full amount of the contingent fee.

statement: The contracting officer shall insert the Covenant Against Contingent Fees clause in all solicitations and contracts exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold, other than those for commercial products or commercial services.
quote: The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.203-5, Covenant Against Contingent Fees, in all solicitations and contracts exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold, other than those for commercial products or commercial services (see parts 2 and 12).

statement: When there is specific evidence or other reasonable basis to suspect one or more of the violations described in paragraph (a) of FAR 3.405, the chief of the contracting office shall review the facts and, if appropriate, take or direct one or more of the listed or other actions.
quote: When there is specific evidence or other reasonable basis to suspect one or more of the violations in paragraph (a) of this section, the chief of the contracting office shall review the facts and, if appropriate, take or direct one or more of the following, or other, actions:

statement: One listed action, if before award, is to reject the bid or proposal.
quote: (1) If before award, reject the bid or proposal.

statement: One listed action, if after award, is to enforce the Government's right to annul the contract or to recover the fee.
quote: (2) If after award, enforce the Government's right to annul the contract or to recover the fee.

statement: A kickback is any money, fee, commission, credit, gift, gratuity, thing of value, or compensation of any kind provided to any prime contractor, prime contractor employee, subcontractor, or subcontractor employee for the purpose of improperly obtaining or rewarding favorable treatment; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-2038.
quote: Kickback, means any money, fee, commission, credit, gift, gratuity, thing of value, or compensation of any kind which is provided to any prime contractor, prime contractor employee, subcontractor, or subcontractor employee for the purpose of improperly obtaining or rewarding favorable treatment

statement: The favorable treatment in the kickback definition is treatment in connection with a prime contract or in connection with a subcontract relating to a prime contract.
quote: in connection with a prime contract or in connection with a subcontract relating to a prime contract

statement: The Kickbacks statute prohibits any person from providing, attempting to provide, or offering to provide any kickback, and from soliciting, accepting, or attempting to accept any kickbacks.
quote: The Kickbacks statute— (a) Prohibits any person from— (1) Providing, attempting to provide, or offering to provide any kickback; (2) Soliciting, accepting, or attempting to accept any kickbacks;

statement: One listed prohibition is including, directly or indirectly, the amount of any kickback in the contract price charged by a subcontractor to a prime contractor or a higher tier subcontractor or in the contract price charged by a prime contractor to the United States.
quote: (3) Including, directly or indirectly, the amount of any kickback in the contract price charged by a subcontractor to a prime contractor or a higher tier subcontractor or in the contract price charged by a prime contractor to the United States.

statement: The Kickbacks statute provides that the contracting officer may offset the amount of a kickback against monies owed by the United States to the prime contractor under the prime contract to which the kickback relates.
quote: (d) Provides that— (1) The contracting officer may offset the amount of a kickback against monies owed by the United States to the prime contractor under the prime contract to which such kickback relates;

statement: One listed provision is that the contracting officer may direct a prime contractor to withhold from any sums owed to a subcontractor under a subcontract of the prime contract the amount of any kickback which was or may be offset against the prime contractor under paragraph (d)(1).
quote: (2) The contracting officer may direct a prime contractor to withhold from any sums owed to a subcontractor under a subcontract of the prime contract the amount of any kickback which was or may be offset against the prime contractor under paragraph (d)(1) of this section;

statement: The contracting officer shall insert the Anti-Kickback Procedures clause in solicitations and contracts exceeding $200,000, other than those for commercial products or commercial services.
quote: The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.203-7, Anti-Kickback Procedures, in solicitations and contracts exceeding $200,000, other than those for commercial products or commercial services (see part 12).

statement: The Kickbacks statute requires each contracting agency to include in each prime contract, other than for commercial products or commercial services, exceeding $200,000, a requirement that the prime contractor shall have in place and follow reasonable procedures designed to prevent and detect violations, among other listed requirements; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-2103.
quote: Requires each contracting agency to include in each prime contract, other than for commercial products or commercial services, exceeding $200,000, a requirement that the prime contractor shall— (1) Have in place and follow reasonable procedures designed to prevent and detect violations

statement: One listed requirement is that the prime contractor cooperate fully with any Federal agency investigating a possible violation of the Kickbacks statute.
quote: (2) Cooperate fully with any Federal agency investigating a possible violation of the Kickbacks statute.

statement: The written report of a possible violation of the Kickbacks statute by a prime contractor or subcontractor goes to the inspector general of the contracting agency, to the head of the contracting agency if the agency does not have an inspector general, or to the Attorney General; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-2047.
quote: Requires a prime contractor or subcontractor to report in writing to the inspector general of the contracting agency, the head of the contracting agency if the agency does not have an inspector general, or the Attorney General any possible violation of the Kickbacks statute

statement: The duty to report any possible violation of the Kickbacks statute applies when the prime contractor or subcontractor has reasonable grounds to believe such violation may have occurred.
quote: any possible violation of the Kickbacks statute when the prime contractor or subcontractor has reasonable grounds to believe such violation may have occurred

statement: Buying-in may decrease competition or result in poor contract performance, and the contracting officer must take appropriate action to ensure buying-in losses are not recovered by the contractor through the pricing of change orders or follow-on contracts subject to cost analysis.
quote: Buying-in may decrease competition or result in poor contract performance. The contracting officer must take appropriate action to ensure buying-in losses are not recovered by the contractor through the pricing of— (1) Change orders; or (2) Follow-on contracts subject to cost analysis.

statement: FAR 3.503-1 states a requirement that subcontractors not be unreasonably precluded from making direct sales to the Government of any supplies or services made or furnished under a contract, but this does not preclude contractors from asserting rights that are otherwise authorized by law or regulation.
quote: require that subcontractors not be unreasonably precluded from making direct sales to the Government of any supplies or services made or furnished under a contract. However, this does not preclude contractors from asserting rights that are otherwise authorized by law or regulation.

statement: The CMMC rule in 32 CFR part 170 applies to, among others, all DoD contract and subcontract awardees that will process, store, or transmit information meeting the standards for FCI or CUI on contractor information systems in performance of the DoD contract.
quote: (a) The requirements of this part apply to: (1) All DoD contract and subcontract awardees that will process, store, or transmit information, in performance of the DoD contract, that meets the standards for FCI or CUI on contractor information systems;

statement: One listed group the rule applies to is the private-sector businesses or other entities comprising the CMMC Assessment and Certification Ecosystem.
quote: (2) Private-sector businesses or other entities comprising the CMMC Assessment and Certification Ecosystem, as specified in subpart C of this part.

statement: The requirements of the part do not apply to Federal information systems operated by contractors or subcontractors on behalf of the Government.
quote: (b) The requirements of this part do not apply to Federal information systems operated by contractors or subcontractors on behalf of the Government.

statement: The program requirements include acquisitions of commercial items, other than those exclusively for COTS items, valued at greater than the micro-purchase threshold, except under the circumstances the paragraph lists.
quote: including those for the acquisition of commercial items (except those exclusively for COTS items) valued at greater than the micro-purchase threshold except under the following circumstances:

statement: DoD Program Managers or requiring activities are responsible for selecting the CMMC Status that applies to a particular procurement or contract, based on whether FCI or CUI will be processed on, stored on, or transmitted through a contractor information system.
quote: (d) DoD Program Managers or requiring activities are responsible for selecting the CMMC Status that will apply for a particular procurement or contract based upon the type of information, FCI or CUI, that will be processed on, stored on, or transmitted through a contractor information system.

statement: Phase 1 begins on the effective date of the complementary 48 CFR part 204 CMMC Acquisition final rule, and DoD intends to require Level 1 (Self) or Level 2 (Self) status for all applicable DoD solicitations and contracts as a condition of contract award.
quote: (1) Phase 1. Begins on the effective date of the complementary 48 CFR part 204 CMMC Acquisition final rule. DoD intends to include the requirement for CMMC Statuses of Level 1 (Self) or Level 2 (Self) for all applicable DoD solicitations and contracts as a condition of contract award.

statement: Phase 2 begins one calendar year after the start of Phase 1, and DoD intends then to add a requirement for Level 2 (C3PAO) status for applicable DoD solicitations and contracts as a condition of contract award.
quote: (2) Phase 2. Begins one calendar year following the start date of Phase 1. In addition to Phase 1 requirements, DoD intends to include the requirement for CMMC Status of Level 2 (C3PAO) for applicable DoD solicitations and contracts as a condition of contract award.

statement: Phase 3 begins one calendar year after the start of Phase 2, and DoD intends then to require Level 2 (C3PAO) status for all applicable DoD solicitations and contracts as a condition of contract award; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-2136.
quote: (3) Phase 3. Begins one calendar year following the start date of Phase 2. In addition to Phase 1 and 2 requirements, DoD intends to include the requirement for CMMC Status of Level 2 (C3PAO) for all applicable DoD solicitations and contracts as a condition of contract award

statement: Phase 4, full implementation, begins one calendar year after the start of Phase 3, and DoD will include the program requirements in all applicable DoD solicitations and contracts, including option periods on contracts awarded before Phase 4 begins.
quote: (4) Phase 4, full implementation. Begins one calendar year following the start date of Phase 3. DoD will include CMMC Program requirements in all applicable DoD solicitations and contracts including option periods on contracts awarded prior to the beginning of Phase 4.

statement: The safeguarding and security requirements specified for Level 1 are those in 48 CFR 52.204-21, for Level 2 are those in NIST SP 800-171 R2, and for Level 3 are selected requirements from NIST SP 800-172 Feb2021.
quote: the safeguarding requirements and security requirements specified in 48 CFR 52.204-21 (for Level 1), NIST SP 800-171 R2 (incorporated by reference, see § 170.2) (for Level 2), and selected security requirements from NIST SP 800-172 Feb2021 (incorporated by reference, see § 170.2) (for Level 3).

statement: The CMMC Assessment Scope is the set of all assets in the OSA's environment that will be assessed against CMMC security requirements, and it must be specified before the assessment.
quote: (1) The CMMC Assessment Scope must be specified prior to assessment in accordance with the requirements of this section. The CMMC Assessment Scope is the set of all assets in the OSA's environment that will be assessed against CMMC security requirements.

statement: OSA information systems that process, store, or transmit FCI are in scope for Level 1 and must be self-assessed against the applicable CMMC security requirements.
quote: OSA information systems which process, store, or transmit FCI are in scope for CMMC Level 1 and must be self-assessed against applicable CMMC security requirements.

statement: Assets that process, store, or transmit CUI are in the Level 2 assessment scope as CUI Assets, which the OSA must document in the asset inventory and whose treatment it must document in the SSP.
quote: Assets that are in the Level 2 CMMC Assessment Scope Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) Assets • Assets that process, store, or transmit CUI • Document in the asset inventory • Document asset treatment in the System Security Plan (SSP).

statement: Out-of-Scope Assets for Level 2 are assets that cannot process, store, or transmit CUI and do not provide security protections for CUI Assets.
quote: Assets that are not in the Level 2 CMMC Assessment Scope Out-of-Scope Assets • Assets that cannot process, store, or transmit CUI; and do not provide security protections for CUI Assets

statement: The Level 3 assessment scope must be equal to or a subset of the Level 2 assessment scope.
quote: Relationship between Level 2 and Level 3 CMMC Assessment Scope. The Level 3 CMMC Assessment Scope must be equal to or a subset of the Level 2 CMMC Assessment Scope

statement: To maintain Final Level 1 (Self) status, the OSA must conduct a Level 1 self-assessment on an annual basis and submit the results in SPRS or its successor capability.
quote: To maintain compliance with the requirements for the CMMC Status of Final Level 1 (Self), the OSA must conduct a Level 1 self-assessment on an annual basis and submit the results in SPRS, or its successor capability.

statement: To achieve Final Level 1 (Self) status the OSA must achieve a MET result for all security requirements specified in 32 CFR 170.14(c)(2), and no POA&Ms are permitted for Level 1.
quote: The OSA must complete and achieve a MET result for all security requirements specified in § 170.14(c)(2) to achieve the CMMC Status of Final Level 1 (Self). No POA&Ms are permitted for CMMC Level 1.

statement: Affirmation of the Level 1 (Self) status is required for all Level 1 self-assessments.
quote: (2) Affirmation. Affirmation of the Level 1 (Self) CMMC Status is required for all Level 1 self-assessments.

statement: Before award of any contract or subcontract that requires Level 1 (Self) status, the OSA must both achieve that status and have submitted an affirmation of compliance into SPRS for all information systems within the assessment scope.
quote: Prior to award of any contract or subcontract with a requirement for the CMMC Status of Level 1 (Self), OSAs must both achieve a CMMC Status of Level 1 (Self) and have submitted an affirmation of compliance into SPRS for all information systems within the CMMC Assessment Scope.

statement: To maintain Level 2 (Self) status, the OSA must conduct a Level 2 self-assessment every three years and submit the results in SPRS within three years of the status date of the Conditional Level 2 (Self) status.
quote: To maintain compliance with the requirements for a CMMC Status of Level 2 (Self), the OSA must conduct a Level 2 self-assessment every three years and submit the results in SPRS, within three years of the CMMC Status Date associated with the Conditional Level 2 (Self).

statement: The OSA achieves Conditional Level 2 (Self) status if its Level 2 self-assessment results in a POA&M that meets all the Level 2 POA&M requirements in the POA&M section of the part.
quote: The OSA has achieved the CMMC Status of Conditional Level 2 (Self) if the Level 2 self-assessment results in a POA&M and the POA&M meets all the CMMC Level 2 POA&M requirements listed in § 170.21(a)(2).

statement: For a Conditional Level 2 (Self) status the OSA must remediate any NOT MET requirements, perform a POA&M closeout self-assessment and post compliance results to SPRS within 180 days of the status date.
quote: The OSA must remediate any NOT MET requirements, must perform a POA&M closeout self-assessment, and must post compliance results to SPRS within 180 days of the CMMC Status Date associated with the Conditional Level 2 (Self).

statement: If a Conditional Level 2 (Self) status expires within the period of performance of a contract, standard contractual remedies apply; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-2077.
quote: If Conditional Level 2 (Self) CMMC Status expires within the period of performance of a contract, standard contractual remedies will apply,

statement: The OSA achieves Final Level 2 (Self) status if its Level 2 self-assessment results in a passing score, whether upon initial self-assessment or as the result of a POA&M closeout self-assessment.
quote: The OSA has achieved the CMMC Status of Final Level 2 (Self) if the Level 2 self-assessment results in a passing score as defined in § 170.24. This score may be achieved upon initial self-assessment or as the result of a POA&M closeout self-assessment, as applicable.

statement: To achieve Level 2 (C3PAO) status the OSC must achieve a MET result for all security requirements specified in 32 CFR 170.14(c)(3) and must obtain a Level 2 certification assessment from an authorized or accredited C3PAO.
quote: The OSC must complete and achieve a MET result for all security requirements specified in § 170.14(c)(3) to achieve the CMMC Status of Level 2 (C3PAO). The OSC must obtain a Level 2 certification assessment from an authorized or accredited C3PAO

statement: To maintain Level 2 (C3PAO) status, the Level 2 certification assessment must be completed within three years of the status date of the Conditional Level 2 (C3PAO) status.
quote: To maintain compliance with the requirements for a CMMC Status of Level 2 (C3PAO), the Level 2 certification assessment must be completed within three years of the CMMC Status Date associated with the Conditional Level 2 (C3PAO).

statement: For a Conditional Level 2 (C3PAO) status the OSC must remediate any NOT MET requirements and undergo a POA&M closeout certification assessment from a C3PAO, which must post compliance results into eMASS within 180 days of the status date.
quote: The OSC must remediate any NOT MET requirements, must undergo a POA&M closeout certification assessment from a C3PAO, and the C3PAO must post compliance results into the CMMC instantiation of eMASS within 180 days of the CMMC Status Date associated with the Conditional Level 2 (C3PAO).

statement: The same sentence that sets standard contractual remedies for an expired Conditional Level 2 (Self) status also makes the OSA ineligible for additional awards requiring Level 2 (Self) or higher for the information system within the assessment scope until a new status is achieved.
quote: and the OSA will be ineligible for additional awards with a requirement for the CMMC Status of Level 2 (Self), or higher requirement, for the information system within the CMMC Assessment Scope until such time as a new CMMC Status is achieved.

statement: A Final Level 2 (C3PAO) status for the information systems within the Level 3 assessment scope is a prerequisite to undergo a Level 3 certification assessment, and Level 3 recertification also has a prerequisite of a new Level 2 assessment.
quote: A CMMC Status of Final Level 2 (C3PAO) for information systems within the Level 3 CMMC Assessment Scope is a prerequisite to undergo a Level 3 certification assessment. CMMC Level 3 recertification also has a prerequisite for a new CMMC Level 2 assessment.

statement: A Level 3 certification assessment is performed by DCMA DIBCAC on behalf of DoD, after the OSC has achieved Final Level 2 (C3PAO) status on the Level 3 assessment scope.
quote: The OSC must achieve a CMMC Status of Final Level 2 (C3PAO) on the Level 3 CMMC Assessment Scope, as defined in § 170.19(d), prior to initiating a Level 3 certification assessment, which will be performed by DCMA DIBCAC (www.dcma.mil/DIBCAC) on behalf of the DoD.

statement: To maintain Level 3 (DIBCAC) status, the Level 3 certification assessment must be performed every three years for all information systems within the Level 3 assessment scope.
quote: To maintain compliance with the requirements for a CMMC Status of Level 3 (DIBCAC), the Level 3 certification assessment must be performed every three years for all information systems within the Level 3 CMMC Assessment Scope.

statement: An OSA may achieve Conditional Level 2 (Self) or Conditional Level 2 (C3PAO) status only if, among the listed conditions, the assessment score divided by the total number of Level 2 security requirements is greater than or equal to 0.8.
quote: An OSA is only permitted to achieve the CMMC Status of Conditional Level 2 (Self) or Conditional Level 2 (C3PAO), as appropriate, if all the following conditions are met: (i) The assessment score divided by the total number of CMMC Level 2 security requirements is greater than or equal to 0.8;

statement: Another listed condition for Conditional Level 2 status is that no requirement on the POA&M has a point value greater than 1, except that CUI encryption may be included if encryption is employed but is not FIPS-validated.
quote: None of the security requirements included in the POA&M have a point value of greater than 1 as specified in the CMMC Scoring Methodology set forth in § 170.24, except SC.L2-3.13.11 CUI Encryption may be included on a POA&M if encryption is employed but it is not FIPS-validated

statement: Among the requirements that may not be on a Level 2 POA&M are external connections, control of public information and the system security plan.
quote: None of the following security requirements are included in the POA&M: (A) AC.L2-3.1.20 External Connections (CUI Data). (B) AC.L2-3.1.22 Control Public Information (CUI Data). (C) CA.L2-3.12.4 System Security Plan.

statement: One listed group of requirements, escort visitors, physical access logs and manage physical access, is among those that may not be on a Level 2 POA&M.
quote: (D) PE.L2-3.10.3 Escort Visitors (CUI Data). (E) PE.L2-3.10.4 Physical Access Logs (CUI Data). (F) PE.L2-3.10.5 Manage Physical Access (CUI Data).

statement: An OSC may achieve Conditional Level 3 (DIBCAC) status only if, among the listed conditions, the assessment score divided by the total number of Level 3 security requirements is greater than or equal to 0.8.
quote: An OSC is only permitted to achieve the CMMC Status of Conditional Level 3 (DIBCAC) if all the following conditions are met: (i) The assessment score divided by the total number of CMMC Level 3 security requirements is greater than or equal to 0.8; and

statement: Among the requirements that may not be on a Level 3 POA&M are the security operations center, the cyber incident response team, threat-informed risk assessment and supply chain risk response.
quote: The POA&M does not include any of following security requirements: (A) IR.L3-3.6.1e Security Operations Center. (B) IR.L3-3.6.2e Cyber Incident Response Team. (C) RA.L3-3.11.1e Threat-Informed Risk Assessment. (D) RA.L3-3.11.6e Supply Chain Risk Response.

statement: The closing of a POA&M must be confirmed by a closeout assessment within 180 days of the Conditional status date, and if it is not, the Conditional status for the information system will expire.
quote: The closing of a POA&M must be confirmed by a POA&M closeout assessment within 180-days of the Conditional CMMC Status Date. If the POA&M is not successfully closed out within the 180-day timeframe, the Conditional CMMC Status for the information system will expire.

statement: Under the Level 2 scoring method an OSA with all Level 2 requirements MET is awarded the maximum score, and for each requirement NOT MET the associated value is subtracted from the maximum score, which may result in a negative score.
quote: If all CMMC Level 2 security requirements are MET, OSAs are awarded the maximum score. For each requirement NOT MET, the associated value of the security requirement is subtracted from the maximum score, which may result in a negative score.

statement: Five points are subtracted for a basic or derived NIST SP 800-171 R2 requirement that, if not implemented, could lead to significant exploitation of the network or exfiltration of CUI.
quote: (1) For NIST SP 800-171 R2 basic and derived security requirements that, if not implemented, could lead to significant exploitation of the network, or exfiltration of CUI, five (5) points are subtracted from the maximum score.

statement: Three points are subtracted for a basic or derived requirement that, if not implemented, has a specific and confined effect on the security of the network and its data.
quote: (2) For basic and derived security requirements that, if not implemented, have a specific and confined effect on the security of the network and its data, three (3) points are subtracted from the maximum score.

statement: One point is subtracted for each remaining derived requirement, other than the noted exceptions, that if not implemented has a limited or indirect effect on the security of the network and its data.
quote: (3) All remaining derived security requirements, other than the exceptions noted, if not implemented, have a limited or indirect effect on the security of the network and its data. For these, 1 point is subtracted from the maximum score.

statement: The Level 3 certification assessment score equals the number of Level 3 security requirements that are assessed as MET.
quote: The Level 3 certification assessment score is equal to the number of CMMC Level 3 security requirements that are assessed as MET.

statement: The Affirming Official is the senior level representative within each OSA who is responsible for ensuring the OSA's compliance with the CMMC Program requirements and has the authority to affirm its continuing compliance; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-8128.
quote: The Affirming Official is the senior level representative from within each Organization Seeking Assessment (OSA) who is responsible for ensuring the OSA's compliance with the CMMC Program requirements and has the authority to affirm the OSA's continuing compliance

statement: An Affirming Official from each OSA, whether prime or subcontractor, must affirm continuing compliance after every assessment, including POA&M closeout, and annually thereafter.
quote: An Affirming Official from each OSA, whether a prime or subcontractor, must affirm the continuing compliance of their respective organizations with the specified security requirement after every assessment, including POA&M closeout, and annually thereafter.

statement: CMMC requirements apply to prime contractors and to subcontractors at all tiers of the supply chain that will process, store, or transmit any FCI or CUI on contractor information systems in performance of the DoD contract or subcontract.
quote: (a) CMMC requirements apply to prime contractors and subcontractors throughout the supply chain at all tiers that will process, store, or transmit any FCI or CUI on contractor information systems in the performance of the DoD contract or subcontract.

statement: A subcontractor that will only process, store, or transmit FCI and not CUI in performance of the subcontract must have Level 1 (Self) status.
quote: (1) If a subcontractor will only process, store, or transmit FCI (and not CUI) in performance of the subcontract, then a CMMC Status of Level 1 (Self) is required for the subcontractor.

statement: A subcontractor that will process, store, or transmit CUI in performance of the subcontract must have at least Level 2 (Self) status.
quote: (2) If a subcontractor will process, store, or transmit CUI in performance of the subcontract, then a CMMC Status of Level 2 (Self) is the minimum requirement for the subcontractor.

statement: A subcontractor that will process, store, or transmit CUI, under a prime contract that requires Level 2 (C3PAO) status, must have at least Level 2 (C3PAO) status.
quote: (3) If a subcontractor will process, store, or transmit CUI in performance of the subcontract and the associated prime contract has a requirement for a CMMC Status of Level 2 (C3PAO), then the CMMC Status of Level 2 (C3PAO) is the minimum requirement for the subcontractor.

statement: A subcontractor that will process, store, or transmit CUI, under a prime contract that requires Level 3 (DIBCAC) status, must have at least Level 2 (C3PAO) status.
quote: (4) If a subcontractor will process, store, or transmit CUI in performance of the subcontract and the associated prime contract has a requirement for the CMMC Status of Level 3 (DIBCAC), then the CMMC Status of Level 2 (C3PAO) is the minimum requirement for the subcontractor.

statement: Where the final anticipated dollar value must be the highest final priced alternative to the Government, that alternative includes the dollar value of all options.
quote: the final anticipated dollar value must be the highest final priced alternative to the Government, including the dollar value of all options.

statement: Buying-in means submitting an offer below anticipated costs, expecting to increase the contract amount after award or to achieve the other result listed in the definition; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-2102.
quote: Buying-in as used in this section, means submitting an offer below anticipated costs, expecting to— (1) Increase the contract amount after award (e.g., through unnecessary or excessively priced change orders); or

statement: One listed expectation in the definition of buying-in is to receive follow-on contracts at artificially high prices to recover losses incurred on the buy-in contract.
quote: (2) Receive follow-on contracts at artificially high prices to recover losses incurred on the buy-in contract.

statement: One listed requirement is that the prime contractor have in place and follow reasonable procedures designed to prevent and detect violations of the Kickbacks statute in its own operations and direct business relationships, for example company ethics rules prohibiting kickbacks by employees, agents, or subcontractors.
quote: (1) Have in place and follow reasonable procedures designed to prevent and detect violations of the Kickbacks statute in its own operations and direct business relationships (e.g., company ethics rules prohibiting kickbacks by employees, agents, or subcontractors;

statement: Two statutes cited in FAR 3.503-1 require that subcontractors not be unreasonably precluded from making direct sales to the Government of any supplies or services made or furnished under a contract.
quote: 10 U.S.C. 4655 and 41 U.S.C. 4704 require that subcontractors not be unreasonably precluded from making direct sales to the Government of any supplies or services made or furnished under a contract.

statement: A contingent fee means any commission, percentage, brokerage, or other fee that is contingent upon the success that a person or concern has in securing a Government contract.
quote: Contingent fee, means any commission, percentage, brokerage, or other fee that is contingent upon the success that a person or concern has in securing a Government contract.

statement: The contingent fees subpart applies to all contracts.
quote: This subpart applies to all contracts.

statement: Statutory requirements for negotiated contracts are, as a matter of policy, extended to sealed bid contracts.
quote: Statutory requirements for negotiated contracts are, as a matter of policy, extended to sealed bid contracts.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.107(a), the contracting officer shall insert the provision at 52.252-1, Solicitation Provisions Incorporated by Reference, in solicitations in order to incorporate provisions by reference.
quote: (a) The contracting officer shall insert the provision at 52.252-1, Solicitation Provisions Incorporated by Reference, in solicitations in order to incorporate provisions by reference.
note: The RFO section heading prints no edition date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The paragraph reads the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.107(b), the contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.252-2, Clauses Incorporated by Reference, in solicitations and contracts in order to incorporate clauses by reference.
quote: (b) The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.252-2, Clauses Incorporated by Reference, in solicitations and contracts in order to incorporate clauses by reference.
note: The RFO section heading prints no edition date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The paragraph reads the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.107(c), the contracting officer shall insert the provision at 52.252-3, Alterations in Solicitation, in solicitations in order to revise or supplement, as necessary, other parts of the solicitation that apply to the solicitation phase only, except for any provision authorized for use with a deviation.
quote: (c) The contracting officer shall insert the provision at 52.252-3, Alterations in Solicitation, in solicitations in order to revise or supplement, as necessary, other parts of the solicitation that apply to the solicitation phase only, except for any provision authorized for use with a deviation.

quote: (1) The services to be furnished under the proposed contract will be substantially the same as services being furnished by an incumbent contractor whose contract the proposed contract will succeed. (2) The services will be performed in the same locality.

quote: a revised prevailing wage determination received by the contracting agency after award of a new contract or a modification as specified in 22.1007(b) shall not be effective provided that the start of performance is within 30 days of the award or the specified modification

quote: If the contracting officer is aware that contract performance involves classes of service employees not included in the wage determination, the contracting officer shall require the contractor to classify the unlisted classes so as to provide a reasonable relationship

quote: The contractor shall initiate the conforming procedure before unlisted classes of employees perform contract work. The contractor shall submit Standard Form (SF) 1444, Request For Authorization of Additional Classification and Rate.

quote: Within 30 days of receipt of the request, the Wage and Hour Division will (1) approve, modify, or disapprove the request when the parties are in agreement or (2) render a final determination in the event of disagreement among the parties.

statement: Under the Executive Order minimum wage enforcement section, contracting officers shall withhold payment at the direction of the Administrator.
quote: Contracting officers shall withhold payment at the direction of the Administrator.

quote: If the contractor does not remedy the violation, the Administrator may direct withholding of payments due on the contract or any other contract between the contractor and the Federal Government.

quote: Provide suitable remedies, including termination, to be imposed on contractors that fail to comply with the requirements of paragraphs (a) through (d) of this section.

quote: SAFETY Act designation means a determination by DHS pursuant to 6 U.S.C. 441(b) and 6 U.S.C. 443(a), as further delineated in 6 CFR 25.4, that a particular Anti-Terrorism Technology constitutes a QATT under the SAFETY Act.
note: The RFO clause prints the edition date (Feb 2009), recorded as edition_date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.250-3(c)(2)(i)-(ii), the block designation or block certification contains a detailed description of and specification for the technology it covers, and a listing of those portions of the SAFETY Act application kit that applicants must complete and submit.
quote: (i) A detailed description of and specification for the technology covered by the block designation or block certification; (ii) A listing of those portions of the SAFETY Act application kit that must be completed and submitted by applicants;

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.250-3(c)(2)(iii)-(iv), (c)(3), the block designation or block certification states its expiration date and any other terms and conditions, and offerors should read it carefully to make sure they comply with its terms if they plan to take advantage of SAFETY Act coverage for their technology or technologies.
quote: (iii) The date of its expiration; and (iv) Any other terms and conditions. (3) Offerors should read this block designation or block certification carefully to make sure they comply with its terms if they plan to take advantage of SAFETY Act coverage for their technology(ies).
note: The RFO clause prints the edition date (Feb 2009), recorded as edition_date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.250-3(d), a determination by DHS to issue, or not to issue, a SAFETY Act designation for a particular technology as a qualified anti-terrorism technology is not a determination that the technology meets, or fails to meet, the requirements of any solicitation issued by any Federal, State, local or tribal governments.
quote: A determination by DHS to issue a SAFETY Act designation, or not to issue a SAFETY Act designation for a particular technology as a QATT is not a determination that the technology meets, or fails to meet, the requirements of any solicitation issued by any Federal, State, local or tribal governments.
note: The RFO clause prints the edition date (Feb 2009), recorded as edition_date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.250-3(e), neither SAFETY Act designation nor certification is a requirement of the action, and whether to seek the benefits of the SAFETY Act for a proposed product or service is entirely up to the offeror.
quote: (e) Neither SAFETY Act designation nor certification is in any way a requirement of this action. Whether to seek the benefits of the SAFETY Act for a proposed product or service is entirely up to the offeror.
note: The RFO clause prints the edition date (Feb 2009), recorded as edition_date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.250-3(f), in the basic block provision, a proposal in which pricing or any other terms or conditions are offered contingent on SAFETY Act designation or certification of the proposed product or service will not be considered for award.
quote: (f) Proposals in which pricing or any other terms or conditions are offered contingent upon SAFETY Act designation or SAFETY Act certification of the proposed product(s) or service(s) will not be considered for award.
note: The RFO clause prints the edition date (Feb 2009), recorded as edition_date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.250-3 Alt I(f)(1), the first alternate, prescribed in 50.206(b)(2), substitutes a paragraph (f) that authorizes offerors to submit proposals made contingent on SAFETY Act designation, or on certification where a block certification exists, before award.
quote: Alternate I (Feb 2009). As prescribed in 50.206 (b)(2), substitute the following paragraph (f): (f)(1) Offerors are authorized to submit proposals made contingent upon SAFETY Act designation (or SAFETY Act certification, if a block certification exists) before award.
note: The RFO alternate prints the edition date (Feb 2009), recorded as edition_date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.250-3 Alt I(f)(1), under the first alternate, an offeror whose offer is contingent on SAFETY Act designation or certification also may submit an alternate offer without the contingency.
quote: When an offer is made contingent upon SAFETY Act designation or certification, the offeror also may submit an alternate offer without the contingency.
note: The RFO alternate prints the edition date (Feb 2009), recorded as edition_date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: Agencies shall avoid duplicate audits, reviews, inspections and examinations of contractors or subcontractors by more than one agency through the use of interagency agreements.
quote: Agencies shall avoid duplicate audits, reviews, inspections, and examinations of contractors or subcontractors, by more than one agency, through the use of interagency agreements.

statement: Subject to the fiscal regulations of the agencies and applicable interagency agreements, the requesting agency shall reimburse the servicing agency for rendered services in accordance with the Economy Act.
quote: Subject to the fiscal regulations of the agencies and applicable interagency agreements, the requesting agency shall reimburse the servicing agency for rendered services in accordance with the Economy Act (31 U.S.C. 1535).

statement: DoD requires reimbursement from non-DoD organizations at a rate set by the Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller/Chief Financial Officer), except for listed cases; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-2553.
quote: DoD requires reimbursement, at a rate set by the Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller/Chief Financial Officer), from non-DoD organizations, except for—
note: The listed exceptions follow in the next printed items.

statement: Two listed exceptions to the DoD reimbursement requirement are quality assurance, contract administration and audit services provided under a no-charge reciprocal agreement, and services performed under subcontracts awarded by the Small Business Administration under the small business subpart of the FAR.
quote: (A) Quality assurance, contract administration, and audit services provided under a no-charge reciprocal agreement; (B) Services performed under subcontracts awarded by the Small Business Administration under FAR subpart 19.8;

statement: One listed exception to the DoD reimbursement requirement covers quality assurance requests performed for the Canadian Department of National Defence and pricing services performed for Public Works and Government Services Canada.
quote: (C) Quality assurance requests performed for the Canadian Department of National Defence and pricing services performed for Public Works and Government Services Canada (PWGSC), operating as Public Services and Procurment Canada (PSPC).
note: The quote keeps the source spelling.

statement: Departments and agencies may request an exception from the DoD reimbursement policy from the Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller/Chief Financial Officer), and the request must show that an exception is in the best interest of the Government.
quote: Departments and agencies may request an exception from the reimbursement policy in paragraph (b)(i) of this section from the Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller/Chief Financial Officer). A request must show that an exception is in the best interest of the Government.

statement: Departments and agencies must pay for services performed by non-DoD activities, foreign governments or international organizations, unless reciprocal agreements provide otherwise.
quote: Departments and agencies must pay for services performed by non-DoD activities, foreign governments, or international organizations, unless otherwise provided by reciprocal agreements.

statement: Foreign governments and international organizations may request contract administration services on their direct purchases from U.S. producers.
quote: Foreign governments and international organizations may request contract administration services on their direct purchases from U.S. producers.

statement: Other foreign governments, including Canadian government organizations other than PSPC, and international organizations send their requests for contract administration services to the DoD Central Control Point at the Headquarters, Defense Contract Management Agency.
quote: Other foreign governments (including Canadian government organizations other than PSPC) and international organizations send their requests for contract administration services to the DoD Central Control Point (CCP) at the Headquarters, Defense Contract Management Agency
note: The preceding printed paragraph lets PWGSC, operating as PSPC, submit its requests directly to the cognizant contract administration office.

statement: As provided in agency procedures, contracting officers may delegate contract administration or specialized support services, either through interagency agreements or by direct request to the cognizant CAO listed in the Federal Directory of Contract Administration Services Components.
quote: As provided in agency procedures, contracting officers may delegate contract administration or specialized support services, either through interagency agreements or by direct request to the cognizant CAO listed in the Federal Directory of Contract Administration Services Components.

statement: The delegation should include, among other items, the name and address of the CAO designated to perform the administration, which also shall be entered in the contract, and any special instructions, including any functions withheld or any specific authorization to perform functions listed in 42.302(b).
quote: The delegation should include— (1) The name and address of the CAO designated to perform the administration (this information also shall be entered in the contract); (2) Any special instructions, including any functions withheld or any specific authorization to perform functions listed in 42.302(b);
note: The delegation list continues with further items that this claim does not cover.

statement: For individual contracts or groups of contracts, the contracting office may delegate to the CAO functions not listed in 42.302, provided that listed conditions are met, one being prior coordination with the CAO to ensure the availability of required resources.
quote: For individual contracts or groups of contracts, the contracting office may delegate to the CAO functions not listed in 42.302: Provided that— (1) Prior coordination with the CAO ensures the availability of required resources;

statement: The contracting officer at the requesting agency may rescind or recall a delegation to administer a contract or perform a contract administration function, except for functions pertaining to cost accounting standards and negotiation of forward pricing rates and indirect cost rates.
quote: The contracting officer at the requesting agency may rescind or recall a delegation to administer a contract or perform a contract administration function, except for functions pertaining to cost accounting standards and negotiation of forward pricing rates and indirect cost rates

statement: The requesting agency must coordinate with the CAO to establish a reasonable transition period before rescinding or recalling a delegation.
quote: The requesting agency must coordinate with the CAO to establish a reasonable transition period prior to rescinding or recalling the delegation.

statement: Supporting contract administration shall not be used for subcontracts unless the Government otherwise would incur undue cost, successful completion of the prime contract is threatened, or it is authorized under paragraph (f) of the section or elsewhere in the regulation.
quote: supporting contract administration shall not be used for subcontracts unless— (i) The Government otherwise would incur undue cost; (ii) Successful completion of the prime contract is threatened; or (iii) It is authorized under paragraph (f) of this section or elsewhere in this regulation.

statement: An agency may decline a request for contract administration services on a case-by-case basis if its resources are inadequate to accomplish the tasks, and a declination shall be in writing.
quote: An agency may decline a request for contract administration services on a case-by-case basis if resources of the agency are inadequate to accomplish the tasks. Declinations shall be in writing.

statement: The Defense Contract Management Agency maintains the Federal Directory of Contract Administration Services Components.
quote: The Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) maintains the Federal Directory of Contract Administration Services Components.

statement: DoD activities shall not retain for administration any contract that requires performance of any contract administration function at or near contractor facilities, except listed categories of contract, which include contracts for the National Security Agency and research and development with universities.
quote: DoD activities shall not retain any contract for administration that requires performance of any contract administration function at or near contractor facilities, except contracts for— (A) The National Security Agency; (B) Research and development with universities;
note: The printed exception list continues with further categories.

statement: Contract administration functions for base, post, camp and station contracts on a military installation are normally the responsibility of the installation or tenant commander.
quote: Contract administration functions for base, post, camp, and station contracts on a military installation are normally the responsibility of the installation or tenant commander.

statement: Production surveillance is a function of contract administration used to determine contractor progress and to identify any factors that may delay performance.
quote: Production surveillance is a function of contract administration used to determine contractor progress and to identify any factors that may delay performance.

statement: Production surveillance involves Government review and analysis of the contractor's performance plans, schedules, controls and industrial processes, and of the contractor's actual performance under them.
quote: Production surveillance involves Government review and analysis of (a) contractor performance plans, schedules, controls, and industrial processes and (b) the contractor's actual performance under them.

statement: The production surveillance and reporting subpart applies to all contracts for supplies or services other than construction contracts, and Federal Supply Schedule contracts.
quote: This subpart applies to all contracts for supplies or services other than construction contracts, and Federal Supply Schedule contracts.

statement: The contracting officer shall insert the Production Progress Reports clause in solicitations and contracts when production progress reporting is required, unless a construction contract or a Federal Supply Schedule contract is contemplated.
quote: The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.242-2, Production Progress Reports, in solicitations and contracts when production progress reporting is required; unless a construction contract, or a Federal Supply Schedule contract is contemplated.

statement: When the Production Progress Reports clause is used, the contracting officer shall specify appropriate reporting instructions in the Schedule.
quote: When the clause at 52.242-2 is used, the contracting officer shall specify appropriate reporting instructions in the Schedule (see 42.1106(a)).

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.250-3 Alt I(f)(2), under the first alternate, the Government may not award a contract based on a contingent offer unless the offeror demonstrates before award that DHS has issued a SAFETY Act designation, or a certification where a block certification exists, for the offeror's technology.
quote: then the Government may not award a contract based on such offer unless the offeror demonstrates prior to award that DHS has issued a SAFETY Act designation (or SAFETY Act certification, if a block certification exists) for the offeror’s technology.
note: The RFO alternate prints the edition date (Feb 2009), recorded as edition_date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.250-3 Alt I(f)(3), under the first alternate, the Government reserves the right to award the contract based on a noncontingent offer before DHS resolves the offeror's application for designation, or for certification where a block certification exists.
quote: (3) The Government reserves the right to award the contract based on a noncontingent offer, prior to DHS resolution of the offeror’s application for SAFETY Act designation (or SAFETY Act certification, if a block certification exists).
note: The RFO alternate prints the edition date (Feb 2009), recorded as edition_date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: If the contractor disagrees with a notice of intent to disallow costs it may submit a written response, which shall be answered by withdrawal of the notice or by a written decision within 60 days.
quote: In the event of disagreement, the contractor may submit to the contracting officer a written response. Any such response shall be answered by withdrawal of the notice or by making a written decision within 60 days.

statement: As a minimum, the notice shall, among other listed items, refer to the contract's Notice of Intent to Disallow Costs clause and state the contractor's name and list the numbers of the affected contracts.
quote: As a minimum, the notice shall— (1) Refer to the contract's Notice of Intent to Disallow Costs clause; (2) State the contractor's name and list the numbers of the affected contracts;

statement: Two listed items of the notice are a description of the costs to be disallowed, with estimated dollar value by item, applicable time periods and reasons, and a description of the potential impact on billing rates and forward pricing rate agreements.
quote: (3) Describe the costs to be disallowed, including estimated dollar value by item and applicable time periods, and state the reasons for the intended disallowance; (4) Describe the potential impact on billing rates and forward pricing rate agreements;
note: These items are listed under the minimum-content lead-in in the same paragraph.

statement: A notice that involves elements of indirect cost shall not be issued without coordination with the contracting officer or auditor having authority for final indirect cost settlement.
quote: If the notice involves elements of indirect cost, it shall not be issued without coordination with the contracting officer or auditor having authority for final indirect cost settlement (see 42.705).

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.250-3 Alt II(f)(1), the second alternate, prescribed in 50.206(b)(3), substitutes a paragraph (f) that authorizes offerors to submit offers presuming that designation, or certification where a block certification exists, will be obtained before or after award.
quote: Alternate II ( Feb 2009). As prescribed in 50.206 (b)(3), substitute the following paragraph (f): (f)(1) Offerors are authorized to submit offers presuming that SAFETY Act designation (or SAFETY Act certification, if a block certification exists) will be obtained before or after award.
note: The RFO alternate prints the edition date (Feb 2009), recorded as edition_date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: The contracting officer shall insert the Notice of Intent to Disallow Costs clause in solicitations and contracts when a cost-reimbursement contract, a fixed-price incentive contract, or a contract providing for price redetermination is contemplated.
quote: The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.242-1, Notice of Intent to Disallow Costs, in solicitations and contracts when a cost-reimbursement contract, a fixed-price incentive contract, or a contract providing for price redetermination is contemplated.

statement: The contract auditor is the authorized representative of the contracting officer for, among listed duties, receiving vouchers from contractors electronically or by other delivery methods as directed by the terms of the contract.
quote: The contract auditor is the authorized representative of the contracting officer for— (A) Receiving vouchers from contractors electronically or by other delivery methods as directed by the terms of the contract;

statement: One listed duty of the contract auditor as the contracting officer's authorized representative is issuing DCAA Forms 1, Notice of Contract Costs Suspended and/or Disapproved, to deduct costs where allowability is questionable.
quote: (D) Issuing DCAA Forms 1, Notice of Contract Costs Suspended and/or Disapproved, to deduct costs where allowability is questionable.

statement: The administrative contracting officer approves all completion and final vouchers and sends them to the disbursing officer, and may issue or direct the issuance of DCAA Form 1 on any cost when there is reason to believe it should be suspended or disallowed.
quote: The administrative contracting officer— (A) Approves all completion/final vouchers and sends them to the disbursing officer; and (B) May issue or direct the issuance of DCAA Form 1 on any cost when there is reason to believe it should be suspended or disallowed.

statement: When notified of bankruptcy proceedings, agencies shall, as a minimum, furnish the notice of bankruptcy to legal counsel and other appropriate agency offices and affected buying activities, among other listed actions.
quote: When notified of bankruptcy proceedings, agencies shall, as a minimum— (1) Furnish the notice of bankruptcy to legal counsel and other appropriate agency offices (e.g., contracting, financial, property) and affected buying activities;

statement: One listed minimum action on notice of bankruptcy is to determine the amount of the Government's potential claim against the contractor, identifying and reviewing any contracts that have not been closed out.
quote: (2) Determine the amount of the Government's potential claim against the contractor (in assessing this impact, identify and review any contracts that have not been closed out, including those physically completed or terminated);

statement: Two further listed minimum actions on notice of bankruptcy are to take actions necessary to protect the Government's financial interests and safeguard Government property, and to furnish pertinent contract information to the legal counsel representing the Government.
quote: (3) Take actions necessary to protect the Government's financial interests and safeguard Government property; and (4) Furnish pertinent contract information to the legal counsel representing the Government.

statement: The contracting officer shall consult the legal counsel, whenever possible, before taking any action regarding the contractor's bankruptcy proceedings.
quote: The contracting officer shall consult the legal counsel, whenever possible, prior to taking any action regarding the contractor's bankruptcy proceedings.

statement: The contracting officer shall insert the Bankruptcy clause in all solicitations and contracts exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold.
quote: The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.242-13, Bankruptcy, in all solicitations and contracts exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold.

statement: A suspension of work under a construction or architect-engineer contract may be ordered by the contracting officer for a reasonable period of time, and if the suspension is unreasonable the contractor may submit a written claim for increases in the cost of performance, excluding profit.
quote: A suspension of work under a construction or architect-engineer contract may be ordered by the contracting officer for a reasonable period of time. If the suspension is unreasonable, the contractor may submit a written claim for increases in the cost of performance, excluding profit.

statement: The Government Delay of Work clause provides for the administrative settlement of contractor claims that arise from delays and interruptions in the contract work caused by the acts, or failures to act, of the contracting officer.
quote: The clause at 52.242-17, Government Delay of Work, provides for the administrative settlement of contractor claims that arise from delays and interruptions in the contract work caused by the acts, or failures to act, of the contracting officer.

statement: The Government Delay of Work clause is not applicable if the contract otherwise specifically provides for an equitable adjustment because of the delay or interruption, for example when the Changes clause is applicable.
quote: This clause is not applicable if the contract otherwise specifically provides for an equitable adjustment because of the delay or interruption; e.g., when the Changes clause is applicable.
note: The quote begins with the words this clause, which refer to the clause named in the preceding printed sentence.

statement: The Government Delay of Work clause does not authorize the contracting officer to order a suspension, delay or interruption of the contract work and shall not be used as the basis or justification of such an order.
quote: The clause does not authorize the contracting officer to order a suspension, delay, or interruption of the contract work and it shall not be used as the basis or justification of such an order.

statement: If the contracting officer has notice of an unordered delay or interruption covered by the clause, the contracting officer shall act to end the delay or take other appropriate action as soon as practicable.
quote: If the contracting officer has notice of an unordered delay or interruption covered by the clause, the contracting officer shall act to end the delay or take other appropriate action as soon as practicable.

statement: The contracting officer shall retain in the file a record of all negotiations leading to any adjustment made under the Government Delay of Work clause, and related certified cost or pricing data, or data other than certified cost or pricing data.
quote: The contracting officer shall retain in the file a record of all negotiations leading to any adjustment made under the clause, and related certified cost or pricing data, or data other than certified cost or pricing data.

statement: Past performance information, including the ratings and supporting narratives, is relevant information, for future source selection purposes, regarding a contractor's actions under previously awarded contracts or orders.
quote: Past performance information (including the ratings and supporting narratives) is relevant information, for future source selection purposes, regarding a contractor's actions under previously awarded contracts or orders.

statement: Past performance information includes, for example, the contractor's record of conforming to requirements and to standards of good workmanship, forecasting and controlling costs, and adherence to schedules, including the administrative aspects of performance.
quote: It includes, for example, the contractor's record of— (1) Conforming to requirements and to standards of good workmanship; (2) Forecasting and controlling costs; (3) Adherence to schedules, including the administrative aspects of performance;
note: The printed list continues with further items.

statement: Agencies shall monitor their compliance with the past performance evaluation requirements and use the Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System metric tools to measure the quality and timely reporting of past performance information.
quote: Agencies shall monitor their compliance with the past performance evaluation requirements (see 42.1502), and use the Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS) metric tools to measure the quality and timely reporting of past performance information.

statement: The Payments to Small Business Subcontractors clause is inserted in all solicitations and contracts containing the Small Business Subcontracting Plan clause.
quote: Insert the clause at 52.242-5, Payments to Small Business Subcontractors, in all solicitations and contracts containing the clause at 52.219-9, Small Business Subcontracting Plan.

statement: The Certificate of Independent Price Determination provision is to be inserted as prescribed in FAR 3.103-1.
quote: As prescribed in 3.103-1, insert the following provision.

statement: Paragraph (a) of the provision lists matters that the offeror certifies.
quote: (a) The offeror certifies that—

statement: One listed certification in the provision is that the prices in the offer were arrived at independently, without, for the purpose of restricting competition, any consultation, communication, or agreement with any other offeror or competitor relating to those prices, the intention to submit an offer, or the methods or factors used to calculate the prices offered.
quote: arrived at independently, without, for the purpose of restricting competition, any consultation, communication, or agreement with any other offeror or competitor relating to (i) those prices, (ii) the intention to submit an offer, or (iii) the methods or factors used to calculate the prices offered;

statement: One listed certification in the provision is that the prices in the offer have not been and will not be knowingly disclosed by the offeror, directly or indirectly, to any other offeror or competitor before bid opening for a sealed bid solicitation or before contract award for a negotiated solicitation, unless otherwise required by law.
quote: have not been and will not be knowingly disclosed by the offeror, directly or indirectly, to any other offeror or competitor before bid opening (in the case of a sealed bid solicitation) or contract award (in the case of a negotiated solicitation) unless otherwise required by law;

statement: One listed certification in the provision is that no attempt has been made or will be made by the offeror to induce any other concern to submit or not to submit an offer for the purpose of restricting competition.
quote: No attempt has been made or will be made by the offeror to induce any other concern to submit or not to submit an offer for the purpose of restricting competition.

statement: The Covenant Against Contingent Fees clause is to be inserted as prescribed in FAR 3.404.
quote: As prescribed in 3.404, insert the following clause:

statement: In the covenant clause the Contractor warrants that no person or agency has been employed or retained to solicit or obtain the contract upon an agreement or understanding for a contingent fee, except a bona fide employee or agency.
quote: (a) The Contractor warrants that no person or agency has been employed or retained to solicit or obtain this contract upon an agreement or understanding for a contingent fee, except a bona fide employee or agency.

statement: For breach or violation of the covenant warranty, the Government shall have the right to annul the contract without liability or to deduct from the contract price or consideration, or otherwise recover, the full amount of the contingent fee.
quote: For breach or violation of this warranty, the Government shall have the right to annul this contract without liability or to deduct from the contract price or consideration, or otherwise recover, the full amount of the contingent fee.

statement: The Anti-Kickback Procedures clause is to be inserted as prescribed in FAR 3.502-3.
