statement: Government members of the Team must be empowered to make acquisition decisions within their areas of responsibility, including selection, negotiation, and administration of contracts consistent with the Guiding Principles.
quote: Government members of the Team must be empowered to make acquisition decisions within their areas of responsibility, including selection, negotiation, and administration of contracts consistent with the Guiding Principles.

statement: In particular, the contracting officer must have the authority, to the maximum extent practicable and consistent with law, to determine the application of rules, regulations, and policies on a specific contract.
quote: In particular, the contracting officer must have the authority to the maximum extent practicable and consistent with law, to determine the application of rules, regulations, and policies, on a specific contract.

statement: The authority to make decisions and the accountability for the decision made will be delegated to the lowest level within the System, consistent with law.
quote: (b) The authority to make decisions and the accountability for the decision made will be delegated to the lowest level within the System, consistent with law.

statement: The System will foster cooperative relationships between the Government and its contractors, consistent with its overriding responsibility to the taxpayers.
quote: (d) The System will foster cooperative relationships between the Government and its contractors consistent with its overriding responsibility to the taxpayers.

statement: If a contract contains the clause at 52.222-1, Notice to the Government of Labor Disputes, the contractor also must report any actual or potential dispute that may delay contract performance.
quote: If a contract contains the clause at 52.222-1, Notice to the Government of Labor Disputes, the contractor also must report any actual or potential dispute that may delay contract performance.

statement: The Acquisition Team consists of all participants in Government acquisition, including the technical, supply, and procurement communities, the customers they serve, and the contractors who provide the products and services.
quote: The Acquisition Team consists of all participants in Government acquisition including not only representatives of the technical, supply, and procurement communities but also the customers they serve, and the contractors who provide the products and services.

statement: Contracting officers have authority to enter into, administer, or terminate contracts and make related determinations and findings, but may bind the Government only to the extent of the authority delegated to them.
quote: Contracting officers have authority to enter into, administer, or terminate contracts and make related determinations and findings. Contracting officers may bind the Government only to the extent of the authority delegated to them.

statement: A contracting officer's representative has no authority to make any commitments or changes that affect price, quality, quantity, delivery, or other terms and conditions of the contract, nor in any way to direct the contractor or its subcontractors to operate in conflict with the contract terms and conditions.
quote: (5) Has no authority to make any commitments or changes that affect price, quality, quantity, delivery, or other terms and conditions of the contract nor in any way direct the contractor or its subcontractors to operate in conflict with the contract terms and conditions;

statement: The Government must not hesitate to communicate with industry as early as possible in the acquisition cycle to help the Government determine the capabilities available in the marketplace.
quote: The Government must not hesitate to communicate with industry as early as possible in the acquisition cycle to help the Government determine the capabilities available in the marketplace.

statement: The Government will maximize its use of commercial products and commercial services in meeting Government requirements.
quote: (5) The Government will maximize its use of commercial products and commercial services in meeting Government requirements.

statement: It is the policy of the System to promote competition in the acquisition process.
quote: (6) It is the policy of the System to promote competition in the acquisition process.

statement: All members of the Team are required to employ planning as an integral part of the overall process of acquiring products or services, and although advance planning is required, each member of the Team must be flexible in order to accommodate changing or unforeseen mission needs.
quote: (8) All members of the Team are required to employ planning as an integral part of the overall process of acquiring products or services. Although advance planning is required, each member of the Team must be flexible in order to accommodate changing or unforeseen mission needs.

statement: Not only must the System have integrity, but the actions of each member of the Team must reflect integrity, fairness, and openness.
quote: Not only must the System have integrity, but the actions of each member of the Team must reflect integrity, fairness, and openness.

statement: Fairness and openness require open communication among team members, internal and external customers, and the public.
quote: Fairness and openness require open communication among team members, internal and external customers, and the public.

statement: The Government must exercise discretion, use sound business judgment, and comply with applicable laws and regulations in dealing with contractors and prospective contractors.
quote: The Government shall exercise discretion, use sound business judgment, and comply with applicable laws and regulations in dealing with contractors and prospective contractors.

statement: The System must support the attainment of public policy goals adopted by the Congress and the President.
quote: (d) Fulfill public policy objectives. The System must support the attainment of public policy goals adopted by the Congress and the President.

statement: Agencies are encouraged to develop internal procedures seeking voluntary feedback from interested parties in an acquisition to assess process strengths and weaknesses and improve effectiveness and efficiency of the acquisition process.
quote: (a) Agencies are encouraged to develop internal procedures seeking voluntary feedback from interested parties in an acquisition to assess process strengths and weaknesses and improve effectiveness and efficiency of the acquisition process.

statement: Agencies may utilize a variety of feedback mechanisms available to the public, such as surveys, in-person exchanges, and group exchanges.
quote: Agencies may— (1) Utilize a variety of feedback mechanisms available to the public (e.g., surveys, in-person, and/or group exchanges);

statement: Agencies shall cooperate, and encourage contractors to cooperate, with Federal and State agencies responsible for enforcing labor requirements such as safety, health and sanitation, maximum hours and minimum wages, and equal employment opportunity, and the list continues in CL-CMP-7178.
quote: Agencies shall cooperate, and encourage contractors to cooperate with Federal and State agencies responsible for enforcing labor requirements such as— (a) Safety; (b) Health and sanitation; (c) Maximum hours and minimum wages; (d) Equal employment opportunity;

statement: The list of labor requirements that agencies shall cooperate on, begun in CL-CMP-7177, continues with child and convict labor, age discrimination, disabled and Vietnam veteran employment, employment of workers with disabilities, and eligibility for employment under United States immigration laws.
quote: (e) Child and convict labor; (f) Age discrimination; (g) Disabled and Vietnam veteran employment; (h) Employment of workers with disabilities; and (i) Eligibility for employment under United States immigration laws.

statement: Executive Order 13706 establishes paid sick leave for employees of certain Federal contractors, and the section points to subpart 22.21 and the clause at 52.222-62, Paid Sick Leave under Executive Order 13706.
quote: Executive Order 13706 establishes paid sick leave for employees of certain Federal contractors. See subpart 22.21 and the clause at 52.222-62, Paid Sick Leave under Executive Order 13706.

statement: Purchases must be made from, and contracts awarded to, responsible prospective contractors only, and no purchase or award may be made unless the contracting officer makes an affirmative determination of responsibility.
quote: (a) Purchases shall be made from, and contracts shall be awarded to, responsible prospective contractors only. (b) No purchase or award shall be made unless the contracting officer makes an affirmative determination of responsibility.

statement: Where the information does not clearly indicate that the prospective contractor is responsible, the contracting officer must make a determination of nonresponsibility.
quote: In the absence of information clearly indicating that the prospective contractor is responsible, the contracting officer shall make a determination of nonresponsibility.

statement: For a small business concern the contracting officer must follow the Certificate of Competency and determinations of responsibility rules, and where Section 8(a) of the Small Business Act applies the contracting officer is pointed to the 8(a) subpart.
quote: If the prospective contractor is a small business concern, the contracting officer shall comply with subpart 19.6, Certificates of Competency and Determinations of Responsibility. (If Section 8(a) of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 637) applies, see subpart 19.8.)

statement: An award to a supplier based on lowest evaluated price alone can be false economy if there is subsequent default, late deliveries or other unsatisfactory performance resulting in additional contractual or administrative costs.
quote: The award of a contract to a supplier based on lowest evaluated price alone can be false economy if there is subsequent default, late deliveries, or other unsatisfactory performance resulting in additional contractual or administrative costs.

statement: It is important that Government purchases be made at the lowest price, but that does not require an award to a supplier solely because it submits the lowest offer.
quote: While it is important that Government purchases be made at the lowest price, this does not require an award to a supplier solely because that supplier submits the lowest offer.

statement: A prospective contractor must affirmatively demonstrate its responsibility, including the responsibility of its proposed subcontractors when necessary.
quote: A prospective contractor must affirmatively demonstrate its responsibility, including, when necessary, the responsibility of its proposed subcontractors.

statement: A preaward survey is normally required only when the information on hand or readily available to the contracting officer, including information from commercial sources, is not sufficient to make a determination regarding responsibility.
quote: A preaward survey is normally required only when the information on hand or readily available to the contracting officer, including information from commercial sources, is not sufficient to make a determination regarding responsibility.

statement: Where the contemplated contract will have a fixed price at or below the simplified acquisition threshold, or will involve the acquisition of commercial products or commercial services, the contracting officer should not request a preaward survey unless circumstances justify its cost.
quote: if the contemplated contract will have a fixed price at or below the simplified acquisition threshold or will involve the acquisition of commercial products or commercial services (see part 12), the contracting officer should not request a preaward survey unless circumstances justify its cost.

statement: When a cognizant contract administration office becomes aware of a prospective award to a contractor about which unfavorable information exists and no preaward survey has been requested, it must promptly obtain and transmit the details to the contracting officer.
quote: When a cognizant contract administration office becomes aware of a prospective award to a contractor about which unfavorable information exists and no preaward survey has been requested, it shall promptly obtain and transmit details to the contracting officer.

statement: If the prospective contractor is debarred, suspended or ineligible, the surveying activity must advise the contracting officer promptly and must not proceed with the preaward survey unless the contracting officer specifically requests it to do so.
quote: If the prospective contractor is debarred, suspended, or ineligible, the surveying activity shall advise the contracting officer promptly and not proceed with the preaward survey unless specifically requested to do so by the contracting officer.

statement: Except as provided in the Freedom of Information Act subpart, information accumulated to determine the responsibility of a prospective contractor, including the preaward survey report, must not be released or disclosed outside the Government.
quote: Except as provided in subpart 24.2, Freedom of Information Act, information (including the preaward survey report) accumulated for purposes of determining the responsibility of a prospective contractor shall not be released or disclosed outside the Government.

statement: On a Governmentwide basis, appropriated or otherwise made available funds are prohibited from use for contracts with either an inverted domestic corporation or a subsidiary of such a corporation, except as provided in the exception paragraph and the waiver section.
quote: prohibit, on a Governmentwide basis, the use of appropriated (or otherwise made available) funds for contracts with either an inverted domestic corporation, or a subsidiary of such a corporation, except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section and in 9.108-4 Waiver.

statement: The prohibition does not apply to a Federal Government contract entered into before the date of enactment of the Act, or to any task order issued under such a contract.
quote: This section shall not apply to any Federal Government contract entered into before the date of the enactment of this Act, or to any task order issued pursuant to such contract.

statement: Contracting officers should consult legal counsel if, during the performance of a contract, a contractor becomes an inverted domestic corporation or a subsidiary of one.
quote: contracting officers should consult with legal counsel if, during the performance of a contract, a contractor becomes an inverted domestic corporation or a subsidiary of one.

statement: If the Secretary of Defense determines, under the procedures at 32 CFR part 216, that an institution of higher education is ineligible to receive funds from a covered agency because of a policy or practice described in 9.110-3 (CL-CMP-7304), the Secretary of Defense will create an active exclusion record for the institution in the System for Award Management, and a covered agency may not solicit offers from, award contracts to, or consent to subcontracts with the institution.
quote: The Secretary of Defense will create an active exclusion record for the institution in the System for Award Management; and (b) A covered agency shall not solicit offers from, award contracts to, or consent to subcontracts with the institution.

statement: The bar on soliciting offers, awarding contracts and consenting to subcontracts does not apply to acquisitions at or below the simplified acquisition threshold or to acquisitions of commercial products and commercial services, including commercially available off-the-shelf items.
quote: The prohibition in this paragraph (b) does not apply to acquisitions at or below the simplified acquisition threshold or to acquisitions of commercial products and commercial services, including commercially available off-the-shelf items.

statement: A suspension is for a temporary period pending the completion of an investigation and any ensuing legal proceedings, unless the suspending and debarring official terminates it sooner or it ends as otherwise provided in the section.
quote: Suspension shall be for a temporary period pending the completion of an investigation and any ensuing legal proceedings, unless sooner terminated by the suspending and debarring official or as provided in this section.

statement: If legal proceedings are not initiated within 12 months after the date of the suspension notice, the suspension must be terminated unless an office of a United States Assistant Attorney General, a United States Attorney or another responsible prosecuting official requests its extension.
quote: If legal proceedings are not initiated within 12 months after the date of the suspension notice, the suspension shall be terminated unless an office of a U.S. Assistant Attorney General, U.S. Attorney, or other responsible prosecuting official requests its extension

statement: On such a request the suspension may be extended for an additional 6 months, and a suspension may never extend beyond 18 months unless legal proceedings have been initiated within that period.
quote: in which case it may be extended for an additional 6 months. In no event may a suspension extend beyond 18 months, unless legal proceedings have been initiated within that period.

statement: The suspending and debarring official must notify the Department of Justice or other responsible prosecuting official of the proposed termination at least 30 days before the 12-month period expires, to give that official an opportunity to request an extension.
quote: The suspending and debarring official shall notify the Department of Justice or other responsible prosecuting official of the proposed termination of the suspension, at least 30 days before the 12-month period expires, to give that official an opportunity to request an extension

statement: A contractor that provides systems engineering and technical direction for a system but does not have overall contractual responsibility for its development, integration, assembly and checkout, or its production may not be awarded a contract to supply the system; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-7201.
quote: A contractor that provides systems engineering and technical direction for a system but does not have overall contractual responsibility for its development, its integration, assembly, and checkout, or its production shall not— (1) Be awarded a contract to supply the system
note: Companion claim CL-CMP-7201 covers the major components and the subcontractor or consultant side of the same bar.

statement: The bar covers the system's major components as well, and the contractor may not be a subcontractor or consultant to a supplier of the system or any of its major components.
quote: supply the system or any of its major components; or (2) Be a subcontractor or consultant to a supplier of the system or any of its major components.

statement: Systems engineering includes a combination of substantially all of these activities: determining specifications, identifying and resolving interface problems, developing test requirements, evaluating test data and supervising design.
quote: Systems engineering includes a combination of substantially all of the following activities: determining specifications, identifying and resolving interface problems, developing test requirements, evaluating test data, and supervising design.

statement: Technical direction includes a combination of substantially all of these activities: developing work statements, determining parameters, directing other contractors' operations and resolving technical controversies.
quote: Technical direction includes a combination of substantially all of the following activities: developing work statements, determining parameters, directing other contractors' operations, and resolving technical controversies.

statement: A contractor performing these activities occupies a highly influential and responsible position in determining a system's basic concepts and supervising their execution by other contractors, so it should not be in a position to make decisions favoring its own products or capabilities.
quote: occupies a highly influential and responsible position in determining a system's basic concepts and supervising their execution by other contractors. Therefore this contractor should not be in a position to make decisions favoring its own products or capabilities.

statement: An affected solicitation must contain a provision that invites offerors' attention to the subpart, states the nature of the potential conflict as seen by the contracting officer and states the nature of the proposed restraint upon future contractor activities; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-7206.
quote: affected solicitations shall contain a provision that— (a) Invites offerors' attention to this subpart; (b) States the nature of the potential conflict as seen by the contracting officer; (c) States the nature of the proposed restraint upon future contractor activities

statement: Depending on the nature of the acquisition, that provision must also state whether the terms of any proposed clause and the application of the subpart to the contract are subject to negotiation.
quote: (d) Depending on the nature of the acquisition, states whether or not the terms of any proposed clause and the application of this subpart to the contract are subject to negotiation.

statement: Where eligibility for future prime contract or subcontract awards will be restricted as a condition of award, or the contractor must agree to some other restraint, the solicitation must contain a proposed clause that specifies both the nature and the duration of the proposed restraint.
quote: If, as a condition of award, the contractor's eligibility for future prime contract or subcontract awards will be restricted or the contractor must agree to some other restraint, the solicitation shall contain a proposed clause that specifies both the nature and duration of the proposed restraint.

statement: The restraint must be limited to a fixed term of reasonable duration, sufficient to avoid the circumstance of unfair competitive advantage or potential bias.
quote: The restraint imposed by a clause shall be limited to a fixed term of reasonable duration, sufficient to avoid the circumstance of unfair competitive advantage or potential bias.

statement: Except as the subpart specifies, a pool is treated the same as any other prospective or actual contractor.
quote: Except as specified in this subpart, a pool shall be treated the same as any other prospective or actual contractor.

statement: The contracting officer may not award a contract to a pool unless the offer leading to the contract is submitted by the pool in its own name or by an individual pool member expressly stating that the offer is on behalf of the pool.
quote: The contracting officer shall not award a contract to a pool unless the offer leading to the contract is submitted by the pool in its own name or by an individual pool member expressly stating that the offer is on behalf of the pool.

statement: On receipt of an offer submitted by a group representing that it is a pool, the contracting officer must verify its approved status with the SBA District Office Director or other approving agency and document in the contract file that the verification was made.
quote: Upon receipt of an offer submitted by a group representing that it is a pool, the contracting officer shall verify its approved status with the SBA District Office Director or other approving agency and document the contract file that the verification was made.

statement: Pools approved by the SBA under the Small Business Act are entitled to the preferences and privileges accorded to small business concerns, and approval under the Defense Production Act does not confer those preferences and privileges.
quote: Pools approved by the SBA under the Small Business Act are entitled to the preferences and privileges accorded to small business concerns. Approval under the Defense Production Act does not confer these preferences and privileges.

statement: Before awarding a contract to an unincorporated pool, the contracting officer must require each pool member participating in the contract to furnish a certified copy of a power of attorney identifying the agent authorized to sign the offer or contract on that member's behalf.
quote: Before awarding a contract to an unincorporated pool, the contracting officer shall require each pool member participating in the contract to furnish a certified copy of a power of attorney identifying the agent authorized to sign the offer or contract on that member's behalf.

statement: The contracting officer must insert the Security Requirements clause in solicitations and contracts when the contract may require access to classified information, unless the conditions specified in the exception paragraph apply.
quote: The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.204-2, Security Requirements, in solicitations and contracts when the contract may require access to classified information, unless the conditions specified in paragraph (d) of this section apply.

statement: For a contemplated cost contract for research and development with an educational institution, the contracting officer must use the clause with its Alternate I.
quote: If a cost contract (see 16.302) for research and development with an educational institution is contemplated, the contracting officer shall use the clause with its Alternate I.

statement: For a contemplated construction or architect-engineer contract where employee identification is required for security reasons, the contracting officer must use the clause with its Alternate II.
quote: If a construction or architect-engineer contract where employee identification is required for security reasons is contemplated, the contracting officer shall use the clause with its Alternate II.

statement: Where the contracting agency is not covered by the NISP and has prescribed a clause and alternates substantially the same as the standard clause, the contracting officer must use the agency-prescribed clause as required by agency procedures.
quote: If the contracting agency is not covered by the NISP and has prescribed a clause and alternates that are substantially the same as those at 52.204-2, the contracting officer shall use the agency-prescribed clause as required by agency procedures.

statement: Agencies must follow FIPS publication 201 and the associated OMB implementation guidance for personal identity verification for all affected contractor and subcontractor personnel; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-7311.
quote: Agencies must follow FIPS PUB Number 201 and the associated OMB implementation guidance for personal identity verification for all affected contractor and subcontractor personnel

statement: Agencies must include their implementation of that guidance in solicitations and contracts that require the contractor to have routine physical access to a Federally-controlled facility and/or routine access to a Federally-controlled information system.
quote: Agencies must include their implementation of FIPS PUB 201 and OMB Guidance M-05-24 in solicitations and contracts that require the contractor to have routine physical access to a Federally-controlled facility and/or routine access to a Federally-controlled information system.

statement: Agency procedures must ensure that contractors return such identification to the issuing agency as soon as any of the listed events occurs, unless the agency determines otherwise.
quote: shall ensure that contractors return such identification to the issuing agency as soon as any of the following occurs, unless otherwise determined by the agency:

statement: The women-owned business representation provision goes in all solicitations that are not set aside for small business concerns, exceed the simplified acquisition threshold and are for contracts to be performed in the United States or its outlying areas.
quote: the provision at 52.204-5, Women-Owned Business (Other Than Small Business), in all solicitations that— (1) Are not set aside for small business concerns; (2) Exceed the simplified acquisition threshold; and (3) Are for contracts that will be performed in the United States or its outlying areas.

statement: The unique entity identifier provision goes in solicitations that do not contain the System for Award Management provision or that meet a condition at 4.605(c)(2).
quote: Insert the provision at 52.204-6, Unique Entity Identifier, in solicitations that do not contain the provision at 52.204-7, System for Award Management, or meet a condition at 4.605(c)(2).
note: The next paragraph places the unique entity identifier maintenance clause in solicitations and resulting contracts that contain that provision.

statement: An offeror must give the contracting officer the CAGE code assigned to that offeror's location before award of a contract action above the micro-purchase threshold when there is a requirement to be registered in the System for Award Management.
quote: Offerors shall provide the contracting officer the CAGE code assigned to that offeror's location prior to the award of a contract action above the micro-purchase threshold, when there is a requirement to be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM)
note: The printed text states the same duty where the solicitation requires a unique entity identifier, and requires the contracting officer to carry the code into the contract and electronic transmissions of contract data.

statement: An offeror that is owned or controlled by another entity must give the contracting officer that entity's CAGE code and legal name before award of a contract action above the micro-purchase threshold when there is a requirement to be registered in SAM; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-7330.
quote: Offerors, if owned or controlled by another entity, shall provide the contracting officer with the CAGE code and legal name of that entity prior to the award of a contract action above the micro-purchase threshold, when there is a requirement to be registered in SAM
note: The paragraph repeats the registration condition stated for the offeror's own code.

statement: The contracting officer must insert the provision at 52.204-24, Representation Regarding Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Services or Equipment, in all solicitations for contracts; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-7321.
quote: The contracting officer shall insert the provision at 52.204-24, Representation Regarding Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Services or Equipment— (1) In all solicitations for contracts
note: The printed paragraph also covers solicitations for an order under an indefinite delivery contract.

statement: The covered telecommunications prohibition clause goes in all solicitations and contracts.
quote: The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.204-25, Prohibition on Contracting for Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Services or Equipment, in all solicitations and contracts.
note: The next paragraph places the covered telecommunications representation provision in all solicitations.

statement: File documentation must be sufficient to constitute a complete history of the transaction, providing a complete background as a basis for informed decisions at each step in the acquisition process and supporting the actions taken.
quote: The documentation in the files (see 4.803) shall be sufficient to constitute a complete history of the transaction for the purpose of— (1) Providing a complete background as a basis for informed decisions at each step in the acquisition process; (2) Supporting actions taken

statement: All contract files other than files for contracts using simplified acquisition procedures must be closed as soon as practicable after the contracting officer receives a contract completion statement from the contract administration office.
quote: All other contract files shall be closed as soon as practicable after the contracting officer receives a contract completion statement from the contract administration office.

statement: The contracting officer must ensure that all required contractual actions have been completed and prepare a statement to that effect; that statement is authority to close the contract file and must be made part of the official contract file.
quote: The contracting officer shall ensure that all contractual actions required have been completed and shall prepare a statement to that effect. This statement is authority to close the contract file and shall be made a part of the official contract file.

statement: The contracting officer must verify the summary level score of a current NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment, and a current assessment is one not more than 3 years old unless the solicitation specifies a lesser time.
quote: The contracting officer shall verify that the summary level score of a current NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment (i.e., not more than 3 years old, unless a lesser time is specified in the solicitation)

statement: The summary level score must be posted in the Supplier Performance Risk System for each covered contractor information system that is relevant to an offer, contract, task order or delivery order.
quote: for each covered contractor information system that is relevant to an offer, contract, task order, or delivery order are posted in Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS)

statement: The verification is required before awarding a contract, task order or delivery order to an offeror or contractor required to implement NIST SP 800-171 in accordance with the clause at DFARS 252.204-7012.
quote: prior to— (1) Awarding a contract, task order, or delivery order to an offeror or contractor that is required to implement NIST SP 800-171 in accordance with the clause at 252.204-7012

statement: The verification is also required before exercising an option period or extending the period of performance on a contract, task order or delivery order with a contractor required to implement NIST SP 800-171 under that clause.
quote: (2) Exercising an option period or extending the period of performance on a contract, task order, or delivery order with a contractor that is that is required to implement the NIST SP 800-171 in accordance with the clause at 252.204-7012.

statement: The contracting officer must include the CMMC level required by the program office or requiring activity in the solicitation provision and the contract clause prescribed for it.
quote: The contracting officer shall include the CMMC level (see 32 CFR 170.19) required by the program office or requiring activity in the solicitation provision and contract clause prescribed at 204.7504.

statement: Before award the contracting officer checks SPRS and does not award to an offeror without a current CMMC status posted there at the level the solicitation requires or higher, for each CMMC UID the offeror provides.
quote: Contracting officers shall check SPRS and not award a contract, task order, or delivery order to an offeror that does not have a current CMMC status posted in SPRS at the CMMC level (see 32 CFR 170.15 through 170.18) required by the solicitation, or higher, for each CMMC UID provided by the offeror.

statement: The contracting officer must check SPRS and must not exercise an option or extend the period of performance on a contract, task order or delivery order unless the contractor has a current CMMC status posted in SPRS; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-7406.
quote: Contracting officers shall check SPRS and not exercise an option or extend the period of performance on a contract, task order, or delivery order, unless the contractor has a current CMMC status posted in SPRS

statement: If the contractor provides new CMMC UIDs during performance, the contracting officer checks SPRS, using the UIDs assigned there, that the contractor has a current CMMC status at the required level or higher; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-7408.
quote: If the contractor provides new CMMC UIDs during performance of the contract, task order, or delivery order, the contracting officer shall check in SPRS, using the CMMC UIDs assigned by SPRS, that the contractor has a current CMMC status at the required CMMC level, or higher

statement: At time of award the contractor must hold a CMMC status at the level the solicitation specifies or higher for all information systems used in performance that will process, store or transmit FCI or CUI.
quote: Contractors are required to achieve, at time of award, a CMMC status at the CMMC level specified in the solicitation, or higher, for all information systems used in the performance of the contract, task order, or delivery order that will process, store, or transmit FCI or CUI.

statement: The contractor must maintain a current CMMC status at the specified level or higher throughout the life of the contract, task order or delivery order where the contract requires it.
quote: Contractors are required to maintain a current CMMC status at the specified CMMC level or higher, if required by the contract, task order, or delivery order, throughout the life of the contract, task order, or delivery order.

statement: CMMC levels 2 and 3 may sit at a conditional level for up to 180 days from the status date and award may occur with a conditional level, while level 1 requires a final level for award.
quote: CMMC levels 2 and 3 can be in a conditional level for a period not to exceed 180 days from the CMMC status date (32 CFR 170.21), and award can occur with a conditional CMMC level. CMMC level 1 requires a final CMMC level for award.

statement: The contracting officer may rely on a “does not” answer to the provision at DFARS 252.204-7016 unless there is an independent reason to question the representation.
quote: If the offeror selects “does not” in response to the provision at DFARS 252.204-7016, the contracting officer may rely on the representation, unless the contracting officer has an independent reason to question the representation.

statement: The contracting officer may rely on a “will not” answer under the provision at DFARS 252.204-7017 unless there is an independent reason to question the representation.
quote: If the offeror selects “will not” in paragraph (d) of the provision at DFARS 252.204-7017, the contracting officer may rely on the representation, unless the contracting officer has an independent reason to question the representation.

statement: If the contracting officer has a reason to question the “does not” representation in FAR 52.204-26, FAR 52.212-3(v) or DFARS 252.204-7016, the contracting officer must consult with the requiring activity and legal counsel.
quote: If the contracting officer has a reason to question the “does not” representation in FAR 52.204-26, FAR 52.212-3(v), or 252.204-7016, then the contracting officer shall consult with the requiring activity and legal counsel.

statement: An offeror that answers “does” in that provision must complete the representation at DFARS 252.204-7017.
quote: If the offeror selects “does” in paragraph (c) of the provision at DFARS 252.204-7016, the offeror must complete the representation at DFARS 252.204-7017.

statement: An offeror that answers “will” in the DFARS 252.204-7017 provision must provide the information required by paragraph (e) of that provision.
quote: If an offeror selects “will” in paragraph (d) of the provision at DFARS 252.204-7017, the offeror must provide the information required by paragraph (e) of the provision.

statement: When an offeror completes paragraph (e) of either of the provisions at FAR 52.204-24 or DFARS 252.204-7017, the contracting officer has the duties that the following paragraphs set out; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-7422.
quote: When an offeror completes paragraph (e) of either of the provisions at FAR 52.204-24 or DFARS 252.204-7017, the contracting officer shall—

quote: For equipment, systems, or services that use covered telecommunications equipment or services as a substantial or essential component of any system, or as critical technology as part of any system, that a waiver as described at FAR 4.2104 has been granted; or

quote: The findings are statements of fact or rationale essential to support the determination and must cover each requirement of the statute or regulation.

quote: A class D&F shall be for a specified period, with the expiration date stated in the document.

quote: The contracting officer shall ensure that individual actions taken pursuant to the authority of a class D&F are within the scope of the D&F.

note: No RFO text for this section is printed in this packet, so this card carries no RFO citation.

The lead-in that makes them things the agreement must do is quoted in CL-CMP-9342 and CL-CMP-9343; the two items read the same as the codified items.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.222-34 Alternates I and II (c)(5) and (c)(6), the listed items of the project labor agreement paragraph include other mechanisms for labor-management cooperation on matters of mutual interest and concern, including productivity, quality of work, safety, and health, and full conformity to all statutes, regulations, Executive orders, and agency requirements.
quote: (5) Provide other mechanisms for labor-management cooperation on matters of mutual interest and concern, including productivity, quality of work, safety, and health; and (6) Fully conform to all statutes, regulations, Executive orders, and agency requirements.
citation_codified: FAR 52.222-34 Alternate I(c)(5) and (6); Alternate II(c)(5) and (6)
citation_rfo: RFO FAR 52.222-34 Alternate I(c)(5) and (6); Alternate II(c)(5) and (6)

The lead-in that makes them things the agreement must do is quoted in CL-CMP-9342 and CL-CMP-9343; the two items read the same as the codified items.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.222-34 Alternates I and II (d), any project labor agreement reached pursuant to the clause does not change the terms of the contract or provide for any price adjustment by the Government.
quote: (d) Any project labor agreement reached pursuant to this clause does not change the terms of this contract or provide for any price adjustment by the Government.
citation_rfo: RFO FAR 52.222-34 Alternate I(d); Alternate II(d)
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The same paragraph (d) prints in Alternate I and in Alternate II, so the quote matches in both places; it is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.222-34 Alternate I(f), the contractor must also include the substance of paragraphs (d) through (f) of the clause in subcontracts with subcontractors engaged in construction on the construction project.
quote: and must include the substance of paragraphs (d) through (f) of this clause in subcontracts with subcontractors engaged in construction on the construction project.
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). This is the second half of the Alternate I paragraph (f) sentence; its first half is quoted in CL-CMP-1995. It differs from the codified half only in using "must" where the codified text has "shall".

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.222-34 Alternate II(f), for each order that uses a project labor agreement, the contractor must require subcontractors engaged in construction on the construction project to agree to any project labor agreement negotiated by the prime contractor pursuant to the clause; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-9349.
quote: (f) Subcontracts. For each order that uses a project labor agreement, the Contractor must— (1) Require subcontractors engaged in construction on the construction project to agree to any project labor agreement negotiated by the prime contractor pursuant to this clause; and
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). Alternate II paragraph (f) and item (1) differ from the codified text only in using "must" where the codified text has "shall". Item (2) is quoted in CL-CMP-9349.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.222-34 Alternate II(f)(2), the contractor must include the substance of paragraphs (d) through (f) of the clause in subcontracts with subcontractors engaged in construction on the construction project.
quote: (2) Include the substance of paragraphs (d) through (f) of this clause in subcontracts with subcontractors engaged in construction on the construction project.
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The quoted item follows the lead-in quoted in CL-CMP-9348, "For each order that uses a project labor agreement, the Contractor must-", which uses "must" where the codified text has "shall"; the item itself is the same as the codified item.

statement: DoD contracting officers must use the FAR part 31 text published on the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul web page in place of the FAR part 31 text codified at 48 CFR chapter 1.
quote: Contracting officers must use— • The FAR part 31, Contract Cost Principles and Procedures, published on the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul web page at https://www.acquisition.gov/faroverhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-31 in lieu of the text codified at 48 CFR chapter 1
note: The same memo directs use of its attached DFARS part 231 in place of 48 CFR chapter 2. Effective date is the memo's signature date; it says effective immediately. Rev 1 supersedes 2026-O0032 of 2025-12-19, not stored, so whether DoD used the RFO text from that earlier date is unconfirmed.

statement: Revision 1 of the DoD part 31 class deviation took effect immediately and supersedes Class Deviation 2026-O0032 issued on December 19, 2025.
quote: Effective immediately, this class deviation revises and supersedes Class Deviation 2026O0032, issued on December 19, 2025.
note: The memo was signed on 2026-08-04 (p. 2). The extracted text drops the hyphen in 2026-O0032.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.201-6(a), expressly unallowable costs, and costs mutually agreed to be unallowable (including mutually agreed to be unallowable directly associated costs), must be identified and excluded from any billing, claim, or proposal applicable to a Government contract.
quote: Expressly unallowable costs or mutually agreed to be unallowable costs (including mutually agreed to be unallowable directly associated costs) must be identified and excluded from any billing, claim, or proposal applicable to a Government contract.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph has the same rule as the codified paragraph, with 'must' in place of 'shall' and the definition of a directly associated cost moved to a numbered subparagraph.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.201-6(b)(1), costs that become designated as unallowable, or as unallowable directly associated costs of unallowable costs, as a result of a written decision furnished by a contracting officer must be identified if included in or used in computing any billing, claim, or proposal applicable to a Government contract.
quote: become designated as unallowable or as unallowable directly associated costs of unallowable costs as a result of a written decision furnished by a contracting officer must be identified if included in or used in computing any billing, claim, or proposal applicable to a Government contract.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph has the same rule as the codified paragraph, with 'must' in place of 'shall'.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.201-6(c)(2), statistical sampling is an acceptable practice for contractors to follow in accounting for and presenting unallowable costs provided the listed criteria are met, the first being that the sampling results in an unbiased sample that is a reasonable representation of the sampling universe.
quote: Statistical sampling is an acceptable practice for contractors to follow in accounting for and presenting unallowable costs, provided the following criteria are met: (i) The statistical sampling results in an unbiased sample that is a reasonable representation of the sampling universe.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The first criterion is the same as the codified one; the RFO lead-in says 'provided the following criteria are met' without naming the paragraphs.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.201-6(c)(2)(ii) and (iii), two more of the listed criteria for acceptable statistical sampling are that any large dollar value or high risk transaction is separately reviewed for unallowable costs and excluded from the sampling process and that the statistical sampling permits audit verification.
quote: (ii) Any large dollar value or high risk transaction is separately reviewed for unallowable costs and excluded from the sampling process. (iii) The statistical sampling permits audit verification.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The second and third criteria are the same as the codified ones.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.201-6(c)(4), use of statistical sampling methods for identifying and segregating unallowable costs should be the subject of an advance agreement (see 31.110).
quote: Use of statistical sampling methods for identifying and segregating unallowable costs should be the subject of an advance agreement (see 31.110).
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph points to 31.110 for advance agreements where the codified paragraph cites 31.109, and it no longer says the agreement is between the contractor and the cognizant administrative contracting officer or Federal official.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.201-6(c)(4)(ii), the cognizant administrative contracting officer (ACO) or Federal official must request input from the cognizant auditor before entering into any such agreements.
quote: (ii) The cognizant administrative contracting officer (ACO) or Federal official must request input from the cognizant auditor before entering into any such agreements.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph has the same duty as the codified paragraph, with 'must' in place of 'shall', now printed as its own subparagraph.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.201-6(c)(5), in the absence of an advance agreement, if an initial review of the facts results in a challenge of the statistical sampling methods by the contracting officer or the contracting officer's representative, the burden of proof must be on the contractor; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-9359.
quote: In the absence of an advance agreement, if an initial review of the facts results in a challenge of the statistical sampling methods by the contracting officer or the contracting officer’s representative, the burden of proof must be on the contractor
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph has the same rule as the codified paragraph, with 'must' in place of 'shall'.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.201-6(c)(5), where the burden of proof is on the contractor, it is a burden to establish that such a method meets the criteria in paragraph (c)(2) of the section.
quote: to establish that such a method meets the criteria in paragraph (c)(2) of this section.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph has the same burden as the codified paragraph.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.201-6(d), if a directly associated cost is included in a cost pool that is allocated over a base that includes the unallowable cost with which it is associated, the directly associated cost must remain in the cost pool.
quote: If a directly associated cost is included in a cost pool that is allocated over a base that includes the unallowable cost with which it is associated, the directly associated cost must remain in the cost pool.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph has the same rule as the codified paragraph, with 'must' in place of 'shall'.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.201-6(d)(2), in all other cases the directly associated costs, if material in amount, must be purged from the cost pool as unallowable costs.
quote: In all other cases, the directly associated costs, if material in amount, must be purged from the cost pool as unallowable costs.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph has the same rule as the codified paragraph, now printed as its own subparagraph.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-4(a), bonding costs arise when the Government requires assurance against financial loss to itself or others by reason of the act or default of the contractor or where the contractor requires similar assurance.
quote: Bonding costs arise when the Government requires assurance against financial loss to itself or others by reason of the act or default of the contractor or where the contractor requires similar assurance.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph has the same substance as codified paragraph (a); the list of bonds is split off into a new paragraph (b).

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-4(b), Government and contractor assurance includes such bonds as bid, performance, payment, advance payment, infringement, and fidelity bonds.
quote: Government and contractor assurance includes such bonds as bid, performance, payment, advance payment, infringement, and fidelity bonds.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph has the same list as the last sentence of codified paragraph (a), printed as its own paragraph (b).

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-4(c), costs of bonding required pursuant to the terms of the contract are allowable.
quote: Costs of bonding required pursuant to the terms of the contract are allowable.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph has the same rule as codified paragraph (b), renumbered from (b) to (c).

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-4(d), costs of bonding required by the contractor in the general conduct of its business are allowable to the extent that such bonding is in accordance with sound business practice and the rates and premiums are reasonable under the circumstances.
quote: Costs of bonding required by the contractor in the general conduct of its business are allowable to the extent that such bonding is in accordance with sound business practice and the rates and premiums are reasonable under the circumstances.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph has the same rule as codified paragraph (c), renumbered from (c) to (d).

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-12(a), economic planning costs are the costs of general long-range management planning that is concerned with the future overall development of the contractor's business; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CMP-9368.
quote: Economic planning costs are the costs of general long-range management planning that is concerned with the future overall development of the contractor's business
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph has the same definition as the first sentence of the codified section, which is now printed as paragraph (a); the quote stops before the clause about economic dislocations, which CL-CMP-9368 carries.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-12(b) and (c), economic planning costs do not include organization or reorganization costs covered by 31.205-27, the text refers to 31.205-38 for market planning costs other than economic planning costs, and economic planning costs are allowable.
quote: Economic planning costs do not include organization or reorganization costs covered by 31.205-27. (See 31.205-38 for market planning costs other than economic planning costs.) (c) Economic planning costs are allowable.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO text has the same exclusion, cross-reference and allowability rule as the codified section, now printed as paragraphs (b) and (c); the codified section prints the allowability sentence second, before the exclusion.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-12(a), the long-range management planning that makes up economic planning costs may take into account the eventual possibility of economic dislocations or fundamental alterations in those markets in which the contractor currently does business.
quote: and that may take into account the eventual possibility of economic dislocations or fundamental alterations in those markets in which the contractor currently does business.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph keeps this clause of the codified definition, now in paragraph (a); it is the second half of the sentence that CL-CMP-9366 quotes in part.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-31(a), plant reconversion costs are those incurred in restoring or rehabilitating the contractor's facilities to approximately the same condition that existed immediately prior to the start of the Government contract, with the exception of reasonable wear and tear.
quote: Plant reconversion costs are those incurred in restoring or rehabilitating the contractor's facilities to approximately the same condition that existed immediately prior to the start of the Government contract, with the exception of reasonable wear and tear.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph excepts 'reasonable wear and tear' where the codified section says 'fair wear and tear excepted'; otherwise the definition is the same.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-31(b), reconversion costs are unallowable except for the cost of removing Government property and the restoration or rehabilitation costs caused by such removal.
quote: Reconversion costs are unallowable except for the cost of removing Government property and the restoration or rehabilitation costs caused by such removal.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph has the same rule as the second sentence of the codified section, now printed as paragraph (b).

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-31(c), in circumstances where equity so dictates, additional costs may be allowed to the extent agreed upon before costs are incurred.
quote: In circumstances, where equity so dictates, additional costs may be allowed to the extent agreed upon before costs are incurred.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph says 'in circumstances, where equity so dictates' where the codified section says 'in special circumstances where equity so dictates'; the word 'special' is gone.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-31(c), care should be exercised to avoid duplication of costs through allowance as contingencies, additional profit or fee, or in other contracts.
quote: Care should be exercised to avoid duplication of costs through allowance as contingencies, additional profit or fee, or in other contracts.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO sentence has the same caution as the last sentence of the codified section, with the words 'of costs' added after 'duplication'.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.201-1(a)(1), the total cost of a contract, including standard costs properly adjusted for applicable variances, is the sum of the direct and indirect costs allocable to the contract, incurred or to be incurred, plus any allocable cost of money pursuant to 31.205-10, less any allocable credits.
quote: The total cost, including standard costs properly adjusted for applicable variances, of a contract is the sum of the direct and indirect costs allocable to the contract, incurred or to be incurred, plus any allocable cost of money pursuant to 31.205-10, less any allocable credits.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph has the same formula as the first sentence of codified paragraph (a), now printed as subparagraph (a)(1).

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.201-1(a)(2), in determining what constitutes a cost, any generally accepted method of determining or estimating costs that is equitable and consistently applied may be used.
quote: In determining what constitutes a cost, any generally accepted method of determining or estimating costs that is equitable and consistently applied may be used.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph has the same rule as the second sentence of codified paragraph (a), with 'determining' in place of 'ascertaining'.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.201-1(b), while the total cost of a contract includes all costs properly allocable to the contract, the allowable costs to the Government are limited to those allocable costs that are allowable pursuant to this part.
quote: While the total cost of a contract includes all costs properly allocable to the contract, the allowable costs to the Government are limited to those allocable costs that are allowable pursuant to this part.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph limits allowable costs to those allowable 'pursuant to this part'; the codified paragraph says 'pursuant to Part 31 and applicable agency supplements', so the reference to agency supplements is gone.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.201-5(a), a credit (for example income, a rebate, or an allowance) relating to an allowable cost under a cost contract, received by or accruing to the contractor, must be credited to the Government.
quote: A credit (e.g., income, rebate, or allowance) relating to an allowable cost under a cost contract, received by or accruing to the contractor, must be credited to the Government.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph limits the credit rule to an allowable cost 'under a cost contract' and no longer speaks of 'the applicable portion' of 'any' credit; the codified section has neither limit.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.201-5(b), the credit must be a cost reduction to the contract or a cash refund, and the text refers to 31.105-6(i)(3) for pension adjustments and asset reversions.
quote: The credit must be a cost reduction to the contract or a cash refund. (See 31.105-6(i)(3) for pension adjustments and asset reversions).
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph refers to 31.105-6(i)(3) for pension adjustments and asset reversions where the codified section refers to 31.205-6(j)(3).

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-7(a), contingency, as used in the subpart, means a possible future event or condition arising from presently known or unknown causes, the outcome of which is indeterminable at the present time.
quote: Contingency, as used in this subpart, means a possible future event or condition arising from presently known or unknown causes, the outcome of which is indeterminable at the present time.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph has the same definition as the codified paragraph, with a 'Definition' heading added.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-7(b)(1), costs for contingencies are generally unallowable for historical costing purposes because such costing deals with costs incurred and recorded on the contractor's books.
quote: Costs for contingencies are generally unallowable for historical costing purposes because such costing deals with costs incurred and recorded on the contractor's books.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO subparagraph has the same rule as the first sentence of codified paragraph (b).

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-7(b)(2), a contingency factor may be recognized when it is applicable to a past period to give recognition to minor unsettled factors in the interest of expediting settlement (for example terminations).
quote: A contingency factor may be recognized when it is applicable to a past period to give recognition to minor unsettled factors in the interest of expediting settlement (e.g., terminations).
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The codified sentence opens 'However, in some cases, as for example, terminations'; the RFO subparagraph drops the words 'in some cases' and treats terminations only as an example.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-7(c)(1), the first category of contingencies in estimates of future costs is those that may arise from presently known and existing conditions, the effects of which are foreseeable within reasonable limits of accuracy.
quote: Those that may arise from presently known and existing conditions, the effects of which are foreseeable within reasonable limits of accuracy;
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO subparagraph has the same category description as the codified one; the quote stops before the example.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-7(c)(1), contingencies of the first category are to be included in the estimates of future costs so as to provide the best estimate of performance cost.
quote: Contingencies of this category are to be included in the estimates of future costs so as to provide the best estimate of performance cost.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO sentence has the same rule as the codified one.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-7(c)(2), the second category of contingencies in estimates of future costs is those that may arise from presently known or unknown conditions, the effect of which cannot be measured so precisely as to provide equitable results to the contractor and to the Government.
quote: Those that may arise from presently known or unknown conditions, the effect of which cannot be measured so precisely as to provide equitable results to the contractor and to the Government
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO subparagraph has the same category description as the codified one; the quote stops before the example.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-7(c)(2), contingencies of the second category are to be excluded from cost estimates under the several items of cost but should be disclosed separately (including the basis upon which the contingency is computed) to facilitate the negotiation of appropriate contractual coverage.
quote: Contingencies of this category are to be excluded from cost estimates under the several items of cost but should be disclosed separately (including the basis upon which the contingency is computed) to facilitate the negotiation of appropriate contractual coverage.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO sentence has the same rule as the codified one.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-10(a)(1), cost of money is an imputed cost that is not a form of interest on borrowings (see 31.205-20).
quote: Is an imputed cost that is not a form of interest on borrowings (see 31.205-20);
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph has the same rule as the codified paragraph.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-10(a)(2), cost of money is an incurred cost for cost-reimbursement purposes under applicable cost-reimbursement contracts and for progress payment purposes under fixed-price contracts.
quote: Is an incurred cost for— (i) Cost-reimbursement purposes under applicable cost-reimbursement contracts; and (ii) Progress payment purposes under fixed-price contracts;
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph has the same rule as the codified paragraph, with the two purposes listed as subparagraphs (i) and (ii) and the quotation marks around 'incurred cost' dropped.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-10(a)(3), cost of money refers to facilities capital cost of money (see 48 CFR 9904.414) and to cost of money as an element of the cost of capital assets under construction (see 48 CFR 9904.417).
quote: Refers to— (i) Facilities capital cost of money (see 48 CFR 9904.414); and (ii) Cost of money as an element of the cost of capital assets under construction (see 48 CFR 9904.417).
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph has the same two references as the codified paragraph.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-10(b)(1), cost of money is allowable when it is measured, assigned, and allocated to contracts in accordance with 48 CFR 9904.414 or measured and added to the cost of capital assets under construction in accordance with 48 CFR 9904.417, as applicable.
quote: Cost of money is allowable when— (1) It is measured, assigned, and allocated to contracts in accordance with 48 CFR 9904.414 or measured and added to the cost of capital assets under construction in accordance with 48 CFR 9904.417, as applicable;
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph states the allowability condition with 'when' where the codified paragraph says 'provided'; the measurement, assignment and allocation condition itself is the same.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 31.205-10(b)(2), one of the conditions listed for cost of money to be allowable is that the requirements of 31.205-52, which limit the allowability of cost of money, are followed.
quote: The requirements of 31.205-52, which limit the allowability of cost of money, are followed;
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO paragraph has the same condition as the codified paragraph. It is one of the conditions listed after 'allowable when'.

note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0032 Rev 1 directs its use (CL-CMP-9351). The RFO wording is the same as codified paragraph (c)(3); only the paragraph letter changes.

statement: The Contractor must notify the Contracting Officer if scheduled rates of pay for labor or unit prices for material increase or decrease during contract performance.
quote: (a) The Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer if, at any time during contract performance, the rates of pay for labor (including fringe benefits) or the unit prices for material shown in the Schedule either increase or decrease.

statement: The Contractor must furnish the notice within 60 days after the increase or decrease, or within any additional period the Contracting Officer approves in writing, but not later than the date of final payment.
quote: The Contractor shall furnish this notice within 60 days after the increase or decrease, or within any additional period that the Contracting Officer may approve in writing, but not later than the date of final payment under this contract.

statement: Subject to the exception stated in the next sentence (CL-CTF-9494), after receiving the notice and data, the Contracting Officer and the Contractor negotiate a price adjustment in the contract unit prices and its effective date.

statement: The Contractor must continue performance pending agreement on, or determination of, any adjustment and its effective date.
quote: The Contractor shall continue performance pending agreement on, or determination of, any adjustment and its effective date.

statement: There is no adjustment for any change in labor rates or material unit prices that would not result in a net change of at least 3 percent of the then-current total contract price.
quote: There shall be no adjustment for any change in rates of pay for labor (including fringe benefits) or unit prices for material which would not result in a net change of at least 3 percent of the then-current total contract price.

statement: The net-change limitation does not apply if, after final delivery of all line items, either party requests an adjustment.
quote: This limitation shall not apply, however, if, after final delivery of all line items, either party requests an adjustment under paragraph (b) above.

statement: The aggregate of increases in any contract unit price under the clause will not exceed 10 percent of the original unit price, and there is no percentage limitation on decreases.
quote: (4) The aggregate of the increases in any contract unit price made under this clause shall not exceed 10 percent of the original unit price. There is no percentage limitation on the amount of decreases that may be made under this clause.

statement: The Contracting Officer may examine the Contractor's books, records, and other supporting data relevant to the cost of labor and material during all reasonable times; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-0310.

statement: The Contracting Officer may examine the books, records, and supporting data until the end of 3 years after final payment, or the periods in FAR subpart 4.7, whichever is earlier.
quote: until the end of 3 years after the date of final payment under this contract or the time periods specified in subpart 4.7 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), whichever is earlier.

statement: Selecting the contract type is generally a matter for negotiation that requires sound judgment, and it should be considered together with price negotiation.

statement: FAR 32.1108 says a Governmentwide commercial purchase card charge authorizes the third party that issued the card to make immediate payment to the contractor, and that the Government reimburses the third party at a later date.
