statement: FAR 32.1108 says the contracting officer shall not authorize the Governmentwide commercial purchase card as a method of payment during any period the SAM indicates that the contractor has delinquent debt subject to collection under the TOP.
quote: (ii) The contracting officer shall not authorize the Governmentwide commercial purchase card as a method of payment during any period the SAM indicates that the contractor has delinquent debt subject to collection under the TOP.

statement: FAR 32.1110 says the contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.232-33, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer—System for Award Management, in solicitations and contracts that include the provision at 52.204-7, System for Award Management; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-1542.
quote: (a) The contracting officer shall insert the clause at— (1) 52.232-33, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer—System for Award Management, in solicitations and contracts that include the provision at 52.204-7, System for Award Management,
note: The same paragraph continues with an alternative trigger and exceptions, which are stated in the next claim.

statement: The same paragraph also names an agency clause that requires a contractor to be registered in SAM and maintain registration until final payment as a trigger, and closes with two exceptions, which are payment through a third party arrangement and an exception listed in 32.1103(a) through (i).
quote: or an agency clause that requires a contractor to be registered in SAM and maintain registration until final payment, unless— (i) Payment will be made through a third party arrangement (see 13.301 and paragraph (d) of this section); or (ii) An exception listed in 32.1103(a) through (i) applies.

statement: FAR 32.1110(a)(2)(i) lists the clause at 52.232-34, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer—Other than System for Award Management, for solicitations and contracts that require EFT as the method for payment; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-1544.
quote: (2) (i) 52.232-34, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer—Other than System for Award Management, in solicitations and contracts that require EFT as the method for payment

statement: FAR 32.1110(a)(2)(i) describes the solicitations and contracts that require EFT as the method for payment as ones that do not include the provision at 52.204-7, System for Award Management, or a similar agency clause that requires the contractor to be registered in SAM.
quote: but do not include the provision at 52.204-7, System for Award Management, or a similar agency clause that requires the contractor to be registered in SAM.

statement: FAR 32.1110 says that if EFT information is to be submitted to other than the payment office in accordance with agency procedures, the contracting officer shall insert in solicitations and contracts the clause at 52.232-35, Designation of Office for Government Receipt of Electronic Funds Transfer Information; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-1573.
quote: (c) If EFT information is to be submitted to other than the payment office in accordance with agency procedures, the contracting officer shall insert in solicitations and contracts the clause at 52.232-35, Designation of Office for Government Receipt of Electronic Funds Transfer Information,
note: The printed paragraph continues with an alternative clause substantially the same as 52.232-35, which a later claim states.

statement: FAR 32.1110 says that if payment under a written contract will be made by a charge to a Government account with a third party such as a Governmentwide commercial purchase card, the contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.232-36, Payment by Third Party, in solicitations and contracts.
quote: (d) If payment under a written contract will be made by a charge to a Government account with a third party such as a Governmentwide commercial purchase card, then the contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.232-36, Payment by Third Party, in solicitations and contracts.

statement: FAR 32.1110 says that if the contract or agreement provides for the use of delivery orders and provides that the ordering office designate the method of payment for individual orders, the contracting officer shall insert in the solicitation and contract or agreement the clause at 52.232-37.
quote: (e) If the contract or agreement provides for the use of delivery orders, and provides that the ordering office designate the method of payment for individual orders, the contracting officer shall insert, in the solicitation and contract or agreement, the clause at 52.232-37,
note: The printed paragraph continues with the applicable EFT and third party clauses to be inserted as well.

statement: FAR 32.1110(g) applies if the solicitation contains the clause at 52.232-34, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer—Other Than System for Award Management, and an offeror is required to submit EFT information prior to award; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-1549.
quote: (g) If the solicitation contains the clause at 52.232-34, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer—Other than System for Award Management, and an offeror is required to submit EFT information prior to award—

statement: One listed action under FAR 32.1110(g) is that the contracting officer shall insert in the solicitation the provision at 52.232-38, Submission of Electronic Funds Transfer Information with Offer, or a provision substantially the same.
quote: (1) The contracting officer shall insert in the solicitation the provision at 52.232-38, Submission of Electronic Funds Transfer Information with Offer, or a provision substantially the same;

statement: FAR 32.001 defines a delivery payment as a payment for accepted supplies or services, including accepted partial deliveries, says commercial financing payments are liquidated by deduction from delivery payments, and says delivery payments are invoice payments for prompt payment purposes.
quote: Delivery payment means a payment for accepted supplies or services, including payments for accepted partial deliveries. Commercial financing payments are liquidated by deduction from these payments. Delivery payments are invoice payments for prompt payment purposes.

statement: FAR 32.001 defines an invoice payment as a Government disbursement of monies to a contractor under a contract or other authorization for supplies or services accepted by the Government.
quote: Invoice payment means a Government disbursement of monies to a contractor under a contract or other authorization for supplies or services accepted by the Government.

statement: FAR 32.001 lists payments for accepted partial deliveries and final cost or fee payments where amounts owed have been settled among the invoice payments.
quote: (1) Invoice payments include— (i) Payments for partial deliveries that have been accepted by the Government; (ii) Final cost or fee payments where amounts owed have been settled between the Government and the contractor;

statement: FAR 32.001 lists, for purposes of subpart 32.9 only, all payments made under the Payments Under Fixed-Price Construction Contracts clause and the Payments Under Fixed-Price Architect-Engineer Contracts clause among the invoice payments.
quote: (iii) For purposes of subpart 32.9 only, all payments made under the clause at 52.232-5, Payments Under Fixed-Price Construction Contracts, and the clause at 52.232-10, Payments Under Fixed-Price Architect-Engineer Contracts;

statement: FAR 32.001 lists interim payments under a cost-reimbursement contract for services, when Alternate I of the Prompt Payment clause is used, among the invoice payments, and says invoice payments do not include contract financing payments.
quote: (iv) Interim payments under a cost-reimbursement contract for services when Alternate I of the clause at 52.232-25, Prompt Payment, is used. (2) Invoice payments do not include contract financing payments.

statement: FAR 32.001 lists progress payments based on a percentage or stage of completion among the contract financing payments, except those made under the Fixed-Price Construction Contracts clause or the Fixed-Price Architect-Engineer Contracts clause.
quote: (v) Progress payments based on a percentage or stage of completion (see 32.102(e)), except those made under the clause at 52.232-5, Payments Under Fixed-Price Construction Contracts, or the clause at 52.232-10, Payments Under Fixed-Price Architect-Engineer Contracts;

statement: FAR 32.001 lists interim payments under a cost reimbursement contract among the contract financing payments, except for a cost reimbursement contract for services when Alternate I of the Prompt Payment clause is used.
quote: (vi) Interim payments under a cost reimbursement contract, except for a cost reimbursement contract for services when Alternate I of the clause at 52.232-25, Prompt Payment, is used.

statement: FAR 32.001 defines a commercial interim payment as any payment that is not a commercial advance payment or a delivery payment, and says these payments are contract financing payments for prompt payment purposes.
quote: Commercial interim payment means any payment that is not a commercial advance payment or a delivery payment. These payments are contract financing payments for prompt payment purposes

statement: FAR 32.001 defines the designated billing office as the office or person, governmental or nongovernmental, designated in the contract where the contractor first submits invoices and contract financing requests.
quote: Designated billing office means the office or person (governmental or nongovernmental) designated in the contract where the contractor first submits invoices and contract financing requests.

statement: FAR 32.007 says agency heads may prescribe shorter periods for payment of contract financing based on contract pricing or administrative considerations.
quote: (3) Agency heads may prescribe shorter periods for payment based on contract pricing or administrative considerations.

statement: FAR 32.007 says a proper contract financing request must comply with the terms and conditions specified by the contract, and that the contractor must correct any defects in requests submitted in the manner specified in the contract or as directed by the contracting officer.
quote: (c) A proper contract financing request must comply with the terms and conditions specified by the contract. The contractor must correct any defects in requests submitted in the manner specified in the contract or as directed by the contracting officer.

statement: FAR 32.007 says the designated billing office and designated payment office must annotate each contract financing request with the date their respective offices received the request.
quote: (d) The designated billing office and designated payment office must annotate each contract financing request with the date their respective offices received the request.

statement: FAR 32.111(b) says the contracting officer shall insert the clauses listed in that paragraph, appropriately modified with respect to payment due dates in accordance with agency regulations.
quote: (b) The contracting officer shall insert the following clauses, appropriately modified with respect to payment due dates in accordance with agency regulations:

statement: FAR 32.111(b) lists the clause at 52.232-8, Discounts for Prompt Payment, for solicitations and contracts when a fixed-price supply contract or fixed-price service contract is contemplated.
quote: (1) The clause at 52.232-8, Discounts for Prompt Payment, in solicitations and contracts when a fixed-price supply contract or fixed-price service contract is contemplated.

statement: FAR 32.111(b) lists a clause substantially the same as the clause at 52.232-9, Limitation on Withholding of Payments, for solicitations and contracts when a supply, research and development, service, time-and-materials, or labor-hour contract is contemplated; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-1565.
quote: (2) A clause, substantially the same as the clause at 52.232-9, Limitation on Withholding of Payments, in solicitations and contracts when a supply contract, research and development contract, service contract, time-and-materials contract, or labor-hour contract is contemplated

statement: FAR 32.111(b)(2) describes the contract contemplated as one that includes two or more terms authorizing the temporary withholding of amounts otherwise payable to the contractor for supplies delivered or services performed.
quote: or labor-hour contract is contemplated that includes two or more terms authorizing the temporary withholding of amounts otherwise payable to the contractor for supplies delivered or services performed.

statement: FAR 32.111(a)(7), in the prescription for the clause at 52.232-7 for time-and-materials and labor-hour contracts, says that, if the contracting officer determines it is necessary to withhold payment to protect the Government interests, paragraph (a)(7) of that clause permits the contracting officer to unilaterally issue a modification requiring the contractor to withhold 5 percent of amounts due; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-1567.
quote: If the contracting officer determines that it is necessary to withhold payment to protect the Government's interests, paragraph (a)(7) of the clause permits the contracting officer to unilaterally issue a modification requiring the contractor to withhold 5 percent of amounts due

statement: FAR 32.111(a)(7), in the prescription for the clause at 52.232-7, says the withholding of 5 percent of amounts due that the modification requires is up to a maximum of $50,000 under the contract.
quote: requiring the contractor to withhold 5 percent of amounts due, up to a maximum of $50,000 under the contract.

statement: FAR 32.502-4 says that, if advance agency approval has been given in accordance with 32.501-1, the contracting officer may substitute a different customary rate for other than small business concerns for the progress payment and liquidation rate indicated.
quote: (2) If advance agency approval has been given in accordance with 32.501-1, the contracting officer may substitute a different customary rate for other than small business concerns for the progress payment and liquidation rate indicated.

statement: FAR 32.502-4 says that, if an unusual progress payment rate is approved for the prime contractor, the approved rate is substituted for the customary rate in paragraphs (a)(1), (a)(6), and (b) of the clause.
quote: (3) If an unusual progress payment rate is approved for the prime contractor (see 32.501-2), substitute the approved rate for the customary rate in paragraphs (a)(1), (a)(6), and (b) of the clause.

statement: FAR 32.502-4 says that, if the liquidation rate is changed from the customary progress payment rate, the new rate is substituted for the rate in paragraphs (a)(1), (a)(6), and (b) of the clause.
quote: (4) If the liquidation rate is changed from the customary progress payment rate (see 32.503-8 and 32.503-9), substitute the new rate for the rate in paragraphs (a)(1), (a)(6), and (b) of the clause.

statement: FAR 32.1110 says that, when the clause at 52.232-36 is included in a solicitation or contract, the contracting officer shall also insert the clause at 52.232-33 or the clause at 52.232-34; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-1572.
quote: When the clause at 52.232-36 is included in a solicitation or contract, the contracting officer shall also insert the clause at 52.232-33, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer—System for Award Management, or 52.232-34

statement: FAR 32.1110(d) leaves the choice between the clause at 52.232-33 and the clause at 52.232-34 to be made as appropriate.
quote: or 52.232-34, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer—Other Than System for Award Management, as appropriate.

statement: FAR 32.1110(c) allows, in place of the clause at 52.232-35, a clause substantially the same as 52.232-35 that clearly informs the contractor where to send the EFT information.
quote: or a clause substantially the same as 52.232-35 that clearly informs the contractor where to send the EFT information.

statement: FAR 32.304-5 says the contractor shall also execute an assignment of claims if requested to do so by the guarantor or the financing institution.
quote: (b) The contractor shall also execute an assignment of claims if requested to do so by the guarantor or the financing institution.

statement: DFARS 204.7103-1 says contracts shall identify the items or services to be acquired as separate contract line items unless it is not feasible to do so.
quote: Contracts shall identify the items or services to be acquired as separate contract line items unless it is not feasible to do so.

statement: Contract line items shall have all four listed characteristics, although exceptions within the characteristics may make a separate contract line item appropriate even though one characteristic appears to be missing.
quote: (a) Contract line items shall have all four of the following characteristics; however, there are exceptions within the characteristics, which may make establishing a separate contract line item appropriate even though one of the characteristics appears to be missing—

statement: The first characteristic is that the item shall have a single unit price or a single total price, subject to the listed exceptions.
quote: (1) Single unit price. The item shall have a single unit price or a single total price, except—

statement: The single unit price characteristic has an exception when the item is not separately priced but the price is included in the unit price of another contract line item, in which case NSP is entered instead of the unit price.
quote: (1) Single unit price. The item shall have a single unit price or a single total price, except— (i) If the item is not separately priced (NSP) but the price is included in the unit price of another contract line item, enter NSP instead of the unit price;

statement: Subparagraph (iii) of the single unit price paragraph lists the situation when the items or services are being acquired on a cost-reimbursement contract.
quote: (iii) When the items or services are being acquired on a cost-reimbursement contract;

statement: Subparagraph (v) of the single unit price paragraph lists the situation when the contract line item is established to refer to an exhibit or an attachment, and if management needs dictate that a unit price be entered, the price shall be set forth in the item description block and enclosed in parentheses.
quote: (v) When the contract line item is established to refer to an exhibit or an attachment (if management needs dictate that a unit price be entered, the price shall be set forth in the item description block and enclosed in parentheses);

statement: Supplies are separately identifiable if they have no more than one national stock number, item description or manufacturer's part number, and services if they have no more than one scope of work or description of services.
quote: (i) Supplies are separately identifiable if they have no more than one— (A) National stock number (NSN); (B) Item description; or (C) Manufacturer's part number. (ii) Services are separately identifiable if they have no more than one— (A) Scope of work; or (B) Description of services.

statement: Each contract line item or service shall have its own delivery schedule, period of performance, or completion date expressly stated, and the words as required count as an expressly stated delivery term.
quote: (3) Separate delivery schedule. Each contract line item or service shall have its own delivery schedule, period of performance, or completion date expressly stated (“as required” constitutes an expressly stated delivery term).

statement: Each contract line item shall reference a single accounting classification citation, except as provided in the paragraph that authorizes multiple citations.
quote: (i) Each contract line item shall reference a single accounting classification citation except as provided in paragraph (a)(4)(ii) of this subsection.

statement: One listed situation in which a contract line item may use multiple accounting classification citations is a single, nonseverable deliverable to be paid for with R&D or other funds properly incrementally obligated over several fiscal years in accordance with DoD policy.
quote: (ii) The use of multiple accounting classification citations for a contract line item is authorized in the following situations: (A) A single, nonseverable deliverable to be paid for with R&D or other funds properly incrementally obligated over several fiscal years in accordance with DoD policy;

statement: When multiple accounting classification citations are authorized for a single contract line item, informational subline items are established for each accounting classification citation.
quote: (iii) When the use of multiple accounting classification citations is authorized for a single contract line item, establish informational subline items for each accounting classification citation in accordance with 204.7104-1(a).

statement: For a contract that combines fixed-price, time-and-materials or labor-hour, and cost-reimbursement line items, the contract type of each contract line item is identified in Section B to facilitate appropriate payment.
quote: (c) For a contract that contains a combination of fixed-price line items, time-and-materials/labor-hour line items, and/or cost-reimbursement line items, identify the contract type for each contract line item in Section B, Supplies or Services and Prices/Costs, to facilitate appropriate payment.

statement: There are only two kinds of subline items, informational ones and ones that consist of more than one item requiring separate identification.
quote: There are only two kinds of subline items: those which are informational in nature and those which consist of more than one item that requires separate identification.

statement: Subline items that identify information relating directly to the contract line item and integral to it, such as parts of an assembly or kit, shall not be scheduled separately for delivery, identified separately for shipment or performance, or priced separately for payment purposes.
quote: information that relates directly to the contract line item and is an integral part of it (e.g., parts of an assembly or parts of a kit). These subline items shall not be scheduled separately for delivery, identified separately for shipment or performance, or priced separately for payment purposes.

statement: Subline items will be used instead of contract line items to facilitate payment, delivery tracking, contract funds accounting, or other management purposes, and shall be used in the listed situations.
quote: (b) Separately identified subline items. (1) Subline items will be used instead of contract line items to facilitate payment, delivery tracking, contract funds accounting, or other management purposes. Such subline items shall be used when items bought under one contract line item number—

statement: Subline items used instead of contract line items shall be used when items bought under one contract line item number are to be paid for from more than one accounting classification, and a subline item shall be established for the quantity associated with the single accounting classification citation.
quote: Such subline items shall be used when items bought under one contract line item number— (i) Are to be paid for from more than one accounting classification. A subline item shall be established for the quantity associated with the single accounting classification citation.

statement: When the price of items not separately priced is included in the price of another contract line or subline item, it may be necessary to withhold payment on the priced line or subline item until the included items not separately priced have been delivered.
quote: (iv) When the price for items not separately priced is included in the price of another contract line or subline item, it may be necessary to withhold payment on the priced contract line or subline item until the included line or subline items that are not separately priced have been delivered.

statement: DFARS 204.7103-2 says to follow the procedures at PGI 204.7103-2 for numbering contract line items.
quote: Follow the procedures at PGI 204.7103-2 for numbering contract line items.

statement: DFARS 204.7104-2 says to follow the procedures at PGI 204.7104-2 for numbering contract subline items.
quote: Follow the procedures at PGI 204.7104-2 for numbering contract subline items.

statement: DFARS 204.7105 says to follow the procedures at PGI 204.7105 for use and numbering of contract exhibits and attachments.
quote: Follow the procedures at PGI 204.7105 for use and numbering of contract exhibits and attachments.

statement: Exhibits may be used as an alternative to putting a long list of contract line items in the schedule, and if exhibits are used a contract line item is created citing the exhibit's identifier.
quote: (d) Exhibits may be used as an alternative to putting a long list of contract line items in the schedule. If exhibits are used, create a contract line item citing the exhibit's identifier. See 204.7105.

statement: DFARS 204.7106(a) says that if new items are added, new contract line or subline item numbers or exhibit line item numbers are assigned in accordance with the procedures established at 204.7103, 204.7104, and 204.7105.
quote: (a) If new items are added, assign new contract line or subline item numbers or exhibit line item numbers, in accordance with the procedures established at 204.7103, 204.7104, and 204.7105.

statement: If a modification relates to existing contract line items or exhibit line items, the modification shall refer to those item numbers.
quote: (1) If the modification relates to existing contract line items or exhibit line items, the modification shall refer to those item numbers.

statement: If the contracting officer decides to assign new identifications to existing contract or exhibit line items, the listed rules apply.
quote: (2) If the contracting officer decides to assign new identifications to existing contract or exhibit line items, the following rules apply—

statement: Paragraph (b)(2)(i)(A) of DFARS 204.7106 says the original line item or subline item number may be used if the modification applies to the total quantity of the original line item or subline.
quote: (A) The original line item or subline item number may be used if the modification applies to the total quantity of the original line item or subline.

statement: Under paragraph (b)(2)(i)(C) of DFARS 204.7106, the original contract line item or subline item or exhibit line item number shall remain with the unchanged quantity, and the changed quantity is assigned the next available number.
quote: the original contract line item or subline item or exhibit line item number shall remain with the unchanged quantity. Assign the changed quantity the next available number.

statement: If a modification will decrease the amount obligated, there shall be coordination between the administrative and procuring contracting offices before issuance of the modification.
quote: (3) If the modification will decrease the amount obligated— (i) There shall be coordination between the administrative and procuring contracting offices before issuance of the modification;

statement: One listed requirement for a modification that decreases the amount obligated is that the contracting officer shall not issue it unless sufficient unliquidated obligation exists or the purpose is to recover monies owed to the Government.
quote: (ii) The contracting officer shall not issue the modification unless sufficient unliquidated obligation exists or the purpose is to recover monies owed to the Government.

statement: In determining the sequence of modifications to a contract or order, modifications are applied first in order of the effective date on the modification.
quote: (b) In order to determine the sequence of modifications to a contract or order, the modifications will be applied in the following order— (1) Modifications will be applied in order of the effective date on the modification;

statement: When two or more modifications have the same effective date, the modifications are applied in signature date order.
quote: (2) In the event of two or more modifications with the same effective date, modifications will be applied in signature date order;

statement: When two or more modifications have the same effective date and the same signature date, procuring contracting office modifications are applied in numeric order, followed by contract administration office modifications in numeric order.
quote: (3) In the event of two or more modifications with the same effective date and the same signature date, procuring contracting office modifications will be applied in numeric order, followed by contract administration office modifications in numeric order.

statement: DFARS 204.1601(a) says not to reuse a PIID once it has been assigned and not to assign the same PIID to more than one task or delivery order, even if they are issued under different base contracts or agreements.
quote: (a) Establishment of a Procurement Instrument Identifier (PIID). Do not reuse a PIID once it has been assigned. Do not assign the same PIID to more than one task or delivery order, even if they are issued under different base contracts or agreements.

statement: DoD-issued PIIDs are thirteen characters in length, use only alpha-numeric characters, and do not use the letter I or O in any part of the PIID.
quote: (a) Elements of a PIID. DoD-issued PIIDs are thirteen characters in length. Use only alpha-numeric characters, as prescribed in FAR 4.1603 and this subpart. Do not use the letter I or O in any part of the PIID.

statement: When a PIID is changed after contract award the new PIID is known as a continued contract, which does not constitute a new procurement.
quote: (c) Change in the PIID after its assignment. When a PIID is changed after contract award, the new PIID is known as a continued contract. (i) A continued contract— (A) Does not constitute a new procurement;

statement: When issuing a continued contract, the contracting officer shall issue an administrative modification to the predecessor contract to clearly state the listed matters; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-1636 and CL-CTF-1610.
quote: (ii) When issuing a continued contract, the contracting officer shall— (A) Issue an administrative modification to the predecessor contract to clearly state that—

statement: One listed matter in the administrative modification is that supplies and services already acquired under the predecessor contract shall remain solely under that contract for purposes of Government inspection, acceptance, payment, and closeout.
quote: (2) Supplies and services already acquired under the predecessor contract shall remain solely under that contract for purposes of Government inspection, acceptance, payment, and closeout; and

statement: Except as provided in paragraph (3) of DFARS 204.804, contracting officers shall close out contracts in accordance with the procedures at PGI 204.804, and the procuring contracting officer determines and documents the closeout date for file purposes.
quote: (1) Except as provided in paragraph (3) of this section, contracting officers shall close out contracts in accordance with the procedures at PGI 204.804. The closeout date for file purposes shall be determined and documented by the procuring contracting officer.

statement: Contracting officers may close out contracts or groups of contracts through modifications without completing a reconciliation audit or other corrective action under FAR 4.804-5(a)(3) through (15), as appropriate, if each contract meets the listed conditions; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-1613.
quote: contracting officers may close out contracts or groups of contracts through issuance of one or more modifications to such contracts without completing a reconciliation audit or other corrective action in accordance with FAR 4.804-5(a)(3) through (15), as appropriate, if each contract—

statement: One listed condition is that the contract was awarded at least 10 fiscal years before the current fiscal year for military construction or shipbuilding, or at least 7 fiscal years before the current fiscal year for all other contracts.
quote: (A) (1) For military construction (as defined at 10 U.S.C. 2801) or shipbuilding, was awarded at least 10 fiscal years before the current fiscal year; or (2) For all other contracts, was awarded at least 7 fiscal years before the current fiscal year;

statement: One listed condition is that the performance or delivery was completed at least 4 years prior to the current fiscal year; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-1615.
quote: (B) The performance or delivery was completed at least 4 years prior to the current fiscal year; and

statement: One listed condition is that a contracting official at least one level above the contracting officer has determined the contract to be not otherwise reconcilable because, as one of the alternatives, the contract or related payment records have been destroyed or lost.
quote: (C) Has been determined by a contracting official, at least one level above the contracting officer, to be not otherwise reconcilable, because— (1) The contract or related payment records have been destroyed or lost; or

statement: Subject to the condition stated in the next sentence (CL-CTF-9522), completed contract files are held in the office responsible for maintaining them for 12 months after completion and are then sent to the local records holding or staging area until they are eligible for destruction.
quote: (3) Hold completed contract files in the office responsible for maintaining them for a period of 12 months after completion. After the initial 12 month period, send the records to the local records holding or staging area until they are eligible for destruction.

statement: Pricing review files, containing documents related to reviews of the contractor's price proposals subject to certified cost or pricing data, are retained for six years.
quote: Retain pricing review files, containing documents related to reviews of the contractor's price proposals, subject to certified cost or pricing data (see FAR 15.403-4), for six years.

statement: When making a determination to exercise an option, or at any other time before issuing a modification other than a unilateral modification making an administrative change, one listed check is that the contractor's record is active in the SAM database; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-1619.
quote: (2) When making a determination to exercise an option, or at any other time before issuing a modification other than a unilateral modification making an administrative change, ensure that— (i) The contractor's record is active in the SAM database; and

statement: One listed check is that the contractor's unique entity identifier number, Commercial and Government Entity code, name, and physical address are accurately reflected in the contract document.
quote: (ii) The contractor's unique entity identifier (UEI) number, Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code, name, and physical address are accurately reflected in the contract document.

statement: If the UEI number, CAGE code, contractor name, or physical address on a contract no longer matches the contractor's record in the SAM database, the contracting officer shall process a novation or change-of-name agreement, or an address change, as appropriate.
quote: (3) At any time, if the UEI number, CAGE code, contractor name, or physical address on a contract no longer matches the information on the contractor's record in the SAM database, the contracting officer shall process a novation or change-of-name agreement, or an address change, as appropriate.

statement: On contractual documents transmitted to the payment office, the CAGE code is provided instead of the UEI, in accordance with agency procedures.
quote: (5) On contractual documents transmitted to the payment office, provide the CAGE code, instead of the UEI, in accordance with agency procedures.

statement: When using the provision at FAR 52.204-8, Annual Representations and Certifications, the provision is used with DFARS 252.204-7007, Alternate A; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-1648.
quote: When using the provision at FAR 52.204-8, Annual Representations and Certifications— (1) Use the provision with 252.204-7007, Alternate A, Annual Representations and Certifications; and

statement: Traceability of funds from accounting systems to contract actions is accomplished using ACRNs and AAIs, and the procedures at PGI 204.7107 govern their use.
quote: Traceability of funds from accounting systems to contract actions is accomplished using ACRNs and AAIs. Follow the procedures at PGI 204.7107 for use of ACRNs and AAIs.

statement: DFARS 204.7108 says to follow the procedures at PGI 204.7108 for inclusion of payment instructions in contracts.
quote: Follow the procedures at PGI 204.7108 for inclusion of payment instructions in contracts.

statement: A change order is not an authorization to exceed the estimated cost to the Government in the Schedule unless the change order contains a statement increasing the estimated cost.

statement: If the contract is terminated or the estimated cost is not increased, the Government and the Contractor must negotiate an equitable distribution of all property produced or purchased under the contract, based on the share of costs each incurred.

statement: The Government pays invoices based on the Contractor's delivery to a post office or common carrier or, where shipment is by other means, to the point of first receipt by the Government.
quote: The Government will pay invoices based on the Contractor's delivery to a post office or common carrier (or, if shipped by other means, to the point of first receipt by the Government).

statement: On that delivery the Contractor must prepare an invoice as the contract, order or blanket purchase agreement provides and display FAST PAY prominently on it.
quote: Upon delivery to a post office or common carrier (or, if shipped by other means, the point of first receipt by the Government), the Contractor shall— (i) Prepare an invoice as provided in this contract, order, or blanket purchase agreement; and (ii) Display prominently on the invoice “FAST PAY.”

statement: Invoices not prominently marked FAST PAY via manual or electronic means may be accepted by the payment office for fast payment.
quote: Invoices not prominently marked “FAST PAY” via manual or electronic means may be accepted by the payment office for fast payment.

statement: Where the purchase price excludes transportation, the Contractor must enter the prepaid shipping cost on the invoice as a separate item and must not include the cost of parcel post insurance.
quote: If the purchase price excludes the cost of transportation, the Contractor shall enter the prepaid shipping cost on the invoice as a separate item. The Contractor shall not include the cost of parcel post insurance.

statement: Where transportation charges are stated separately on the invoice, the Contractor must retain related paid freight bills or other separately paid transportation billings for 3 years and furnish them to the Government on request.

statement: Where a receiving report is required, the Contractor must either submit the report on the prescribed form with the invoice or include the listed information on the invoice.

statement: The listed information is the shipment number, the mode of shipment and, at line item level, the national stock number and/or manufacturer's part number, the unit of measure, the ship-to point, the mark-for point if in the contract and the FEDSTRIP/MILSTRIP document number if in the contract.

statement: Where the contract, order or blanket purchase agreement does not require a receiving report on a prescribed form, the Contractor must include the listed information on the invoice at the line item level, in addition to what paragraph (c)(1) requires.

statement: That line item information is the ship-to point, the mark-for point and, if in the contract, the FEDSTRIP/MILSTRIP document number.
quote: (i) Ship-To Point. (ii) Mark-For Point. (iii) FEDSTRIP/MILSTRIP document number, if in the contract.

statement: Where a receiving report is not required, the Contractor must include a copy of the invoice in each shipment.

quote: and that the supplies are in the quantity and of the quality designated by the contract, order, or blanket purchase agreement.

quote: The Contractor shall mark all outer shipping containers “FAST PAY.” When outer shipping containers are not marked “FAST PAY,” the payment office may make fast payment.

statement: A decision to retain part of a construction progress payment, and the amount withheld, is made by the contracting officer case by case, based on the assessment of past performance and the likelihood that performance will continue.
quote: Determinations to retain and the specific amount to be withheld shall be made by the contracting officer on a case-by-case basis. Such decisions will be based on the contracting officer's assessment of past performance and the likelihood that such performance will continue.

statement: Retainage is not a substitute for good contract management, and the contracting officer should not withhold funds without cause.
quote: Retainage should not be used as a substitute for good contract management, and the contracting officer should not withhold funds without cause.

statement: The amount of retainage withheld may not exceed 10 percent of the approved estimated amount under the terms of the contract, and may be adjusted as the contract approaches completion to recognize better than expected performance, the ability to rely on alternative safeguards, and other factors.
quote: retainage withheld shall not exceed 10 percent of the approved estimated amount in accordance with the terms of the contract and may be adjusted as the contract approaches completion to recognize better than expected performance, the ability to rely on alternative safeguards, and other factors.

statement: Retained amounts are paid promptly once all contract requirements are complete.
quote: Upon completion of all contract requirements, retained amounts shall be paid promptly.

statement: Contract financing methods are intended to be self-liquidating through contract performance, so agencies use them only to finance contractor working capital and not to expand contractor-owned facilities or acquire fixed assets.
quote: Contract financing methods covered in this part are intended to be self-liquidating through contract performance. Consequently, agencies shall only use the methods for financing of contractor working capital, not for the expansion of contractor-owned facilities or the acquisition of fixed assets.

statement: Under loan guarantees, an exception may be made for facilities expansion of a minor or incidental nature where a relatively small part of the guaranteed loan is used for the expansion and the contractor's repayment would not be delayed or impaired; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-3157.
quote: However, under loan guarantees, exceptions may be made for— (1) Facilities expansion of a minor or incidental nature, if a relatively small part of the guaranteed loan is used for the expansion and the contractor's repayment would not be delayed or impaired; or

statement: The limitations in this section on the use of contract financing do not apply to contracts under which facilities are being acquired for Government ownership.
quote: The limitations in this section do not apply to contracts under which facilities are being acquired for Government ownership.

statement: Performance-based payments are the preferred Government financing method when the contracting officer finds them practical and the contractor agrees to their use.
quote: (a) Performance-based payments are the preferred Government financing method when the contracting officer finds them practical, and the contractor agrees to their use.

statement: Performance-based payments are contract financing payments and are not payment for accepted items, and they are fully recoverable in the same manner as progress payments if the contractor defaults.
quote: (b) Performance-based payments are contract financing payments that are not payment for accepted items. (c) Performance-based payments are fully recoverable, in the same manner as progress payments, in the event of default.

statement: Performance-based payments are contract financing payments and therefore are not subject to the prompt payment interest-penalty provisions.
quote: (d) Performance-based payments are contract financing payments and, therefore, are not subject to the interest-penalty provisions of prompt payment (see Subpart 32.9).

statement: Performance-based payments may not be used for payments under cost-reimbursement line items.
quote: (e) Performance-based payments shall not be used for— (1) Payments under cost-reimbursement line items;
note: The same prohibition head carries the later list items; this claim quotes the first only.

statement: As used in FAR 32.202-2, a commercial advance payment is a payment made before any performance of work under the contract, and the aggregate of these payments may not exceed 15 percent of the contract price.
quote: Commercial advance payment, as used in this section, means a payment made before any performance of work under the contract. The aggregate of these payments shall not exceed 15 percent of the contract price.

statement: Commercial advance payments are contract financing payments for prompt payment purposes and so fall outside the Prompt Payment Act interest penalty, and they are not subject to the subpart on advance payments for other than commercial acquisitions.
quote: These payments are contract financing payments for prompt payment purposes (i.e., not subject to the interest penalty provisions of the Prompt Payment Act in accordance with subpart 32.9). These payments are not subject to subpart 32.4, Advance Payments for Other Than Commercial Acquisitions.

statement: The financing terms are included in the solicitation, contract financing is not a factor in evaluating the resulting proposals, and proposals of alternative financing terms are not accepted, with the text referring to FAR 14.208 and FAR 15.206 for amendments of solicitations.
quote: The financing terms shall be included in the solicitation. Contract financing shall not be a factor in the evaluation of resulting proposals, and proposals of alternative financing terms shall not be accepted (but see 14.208 and 15.206 concerning amendments of solicitations).

statement: Where award goes to an offeror that declined the proposed contract financing, the contract financing provisions are not included in the resulting contract.
quote: In the event of award to an offeror who declined the proposed contract financing, the contract financing provisions shall not be included in the resulting contract.

statement: Contract financing is not a basis for adjusting offerors' proposed prices, because the effect of contract financing is already reflected in each offeror's proposed prices.
quote: Contract financing shall not be a basis for adjusting offerors' proposed prices, because the effect of contract financing is reflected in each offeror's proposed prices.

statement: Subject to the lead-in to paragraph (b), each approval of a contract financing request specifies the amount to be paid, the necessary contractual information, and the accounts to be charged for the payment.
quote: (2) Each approval shall specify the amount to be paid, necessary contractual information, and the account(s) (see 32.206(d)) to be charged for the payment.
note: The duties of the contracting officer who receives, approves and transmits the requests are in the same paragraph.

statement: A contractor, subcontractor or supplier that needs operating funds to perform a contract related to national defense may apply to a financing institution for a loan.
quote: A contractor, subcontractor, or supplier that needs operating funds to perform a contract related to national defense may apply to a financing institution for a loan.

statement: The Federal Reserve Board transmits the application and the list of defense contracts to the interested guaranteeing agency, so that the agency can determine the contractor's eligibility.
quote: The Board will transmit the application and the list of contracts to the interested guaranteeing agency, so that the agency can determine the eligibility of the contractor.

statement: Under guaranteed loans made primarily for working capital, the agency normally limits the guarantee by an asset formula to a specified percentage of the contractor's investment in defense production contracts, the percentage being 90 percent or less, with payrolls and inventories given as examples.
quote: the agency shall normally limit the guarantee, by use of an asset formula, to an amount that does not exceed a specified percentage (90 percent or less) of the contractor's investment (e.g., payrolls and inventories) in defense production contracts.

statement: The asset formula excludes amounts for which the contractor has done no work or made no expenditure, amounts that would become due from later performance, and cash collateral or bank deposit balances.
quote: The formula shall exclude— (1) Amounts for which the contractor has not done any work or made any expenditure; (2) Amounts that would become due as the result of later performance under the contracts; and (3) Cash collateral or bank deposit balances.

statement: Progress payments are deducted from the asset formula.
quote: (b) Progress payments are deducted from the asset formula.

statement: Where the contractor enters into additional defense production contracts after the application but before authorization of a guarantee, the agency may adjust the guarantee amount or maturity date to meet a significant increase in financing need.
quote: If the contractor enters into additional defense production contracts after the application for, but before authorization of, a guarantee, the agency may adjust the loan guarantee amount or maturity date to meet any significant increase in financing need.

statement: Where the contractor enters into defense production contracts during the term of the guaranteed loan, the parties may adjust the existing guarantee agreement to provide for financing the new contracts.
quote: If the contractor enters into defense production contracts during the term of the guaranteed loan, the parties may adjust the existing guarantee agreement to provide for financing the new contracts.

statement: Contract surety bonds are incompatible with the Government's interests under guaranteed loans unless the interests of the surety are subordinated to the guaranteed loan.
quote: Contract surety bonds are incompatible with the Government's interests under guaranteed loans, unless the interests of the surety are subordinated to the guaranteed loan.

statement: Where a substantial share of the contractor's defense contracts are covered by surety bonds, or the amount of the bond is substantial in relation to the contractor's net worth, the agency shall not authorize the guarantee of a loan on a bonded contract unless the surety enters into an agreement; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-3176.
quote: If a substantial share of the contractor's defense contracts are covered by surety bonds, or the amount of the bond is substantial in relation to the contractor's net worth, the agency shall not authorize the guarantee of a loan on a bonded contract unless the surety enters into an agreement

statement: Agency approval of a guarantee for a loan involving relatively substantial subcontracts covered by surety bonds also depends on a reasonable allocation agreement between the sureties and the financing institution.
quote: The agency approval of a guarantee for a loan involving relatively substantial subcontracts covered by surety bonds shall also depend on the establishment of a reasonable allocation agreement between the sureties and the financing institution.

statement: The Federal Acquisition Regulation recognizes that prohibiting borrowings outside the guaranteed loan is preferable when practicable in a given guaranteed loan case, but that such other borrowings should be permitted when necessary.
quote: It has been recognized in practice that, while prohibition of borrowings outside the guaranteed loan is preferable when practicable in a given V-loan case, such other borrowings should be permitted when necessary.

statement: One restriction on consented other borrowing requires the contractor to provide documentation to the guaranteeing agency, at intervals not longer than 30 days, disclosing outstanding unguaranteed borrowings.
quote: A requirement that the contractor provide appropriate documentation to the guaranteeing agency, at intervals not longer than 30 days, to disclose outstanding unguaranteed borrowings.

statement: Guaranteed loans may also apply to contracts that have been terminated, partially or totally, for the convenience of the Government.
quote: The purpose of guaranteed loans; i.e., to provide for financing based on the borrower's recoverable investment in defense production contracts, may also apply to contracts that have been terminated (partially or totally) for the convenience of the Government.

statement: The procedure for a terminated-contract guarantee is substantially the same as the ordinary guarantee, except that certificates of eligibility are not required for contracts that have been totally terminated or for the terminated portion of contracts that have been partially terminated.
quote: The procedure for such guarantees is substantially the same as that outlined in 32.304, except that certificates of eligibility are not required for (1) contracts that have been totally terminated or (2) the terminated portion of contracts that have been partially terminated.

statement: Advance payments may be made at or after award of sealed bid contracts as well as negotiated contracts.
quote: These advance payments may be made at or after award of sealed bid contracts as well as negotiated contracts.

statement: Bidders may request advance payments before or after award even if the invitation for bids contains no advance payment provision.
quote: Bidders may request advance payments before or after award, even if the invitation for bids does not contain an advance payment provision.

statement: The contracting officer rejects any bid requiring that advance payments be provided as a basis for acceptance.
quote: However, the contracting officer shall reject any bid requiring that advance payments be provided as a basis for acceptance.

statement: Where advance payments are requested, the agency may enter into the contract and provide for conforming advance payments, or enter into the contract without providing for advance payments if the contractor does not actually need them; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-3185.
quote: When advance payments are requested, the agency may— (1) Enter into the contract and provide for advance payments conforming to this part 32; (2) Enter into the contract without providing for advance payments if the contractor does not actually need advance payments; or
note: A third option, denying award where the request was disapproved and adequate funds are not otherwise available, follows in the same list.

statement: The contracting officer inserts the clause at FAR 52.232-12, Advance Payments, in solicitations and contracts under which the Government will provide advance payments, except as provided in FAR 32.412(b).
quote: The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.232-12, Advance Payments, in solicitations and contracts under which the Government will provide advance payments, except as provided in 32.412(b).

statement: Where the requirement for a special account is eliminated under the paragraphs cited in the text, the contracting officer inserts the Alternate V version of the advance payments clause instead of the basic clause.
quote: If the requirement for a special account is eliminated in accordance with 32.409-3 (e) or (g), the contracting officer shall insert in the solicitation or contract the clause set forth in Alternate V of 52.232-12, Advance Payments, instead of the basic clause.

statement: Where invitations for bids and requests for proposals include a Progress Payments clause, the contracting officer inserts the provision at FAR 52.232-13, Notice of Progress Payments.
quote: The contracting officer shall insert the provision at 52.232-13, Notice of Progress Payments, in invitations for bids and requests for proposals that include a Progress Payments clause.

statement: Under the authority of the statutes cited in FAR 32.101, an invitation for bids may restrict the availability of progress payments to small business concerns only.
quote: Under the authority of the statutes cited in 32.101, an invitation for bids may restrict the availability of progress payments to small business concerns only.

statement: The contracting officer inserts the exclusive small business provision in invitations for bids if it is anticipated that both small business concerns and others may submit bids in response to the same invitation and only the small business bidders would need progress payments.
quote: in invitations for bids if it is anticipated that (1) both small business concerns and others may submit bids in response to the same invitation and (2) only the small business bidders would need progress payments.
note: The provision itself and the officer who inserts it are in the claim on paragraph (b)(2).

statement: Where the solicitation will not contain one of the provisions prescribed in the earlier paragraphs, the contracting officer inserts the provision at FAR 52.232-15, Progress Payments Not Included, in invitations for bids.
quote: The contracting officer shall insert the provision at 52.232-15, Progress Payments Not Included, in invitations for bids if the solicitation will not contain one of the provisions prescribed in paragraphs (a) and (b) above.

statement: Absent reason to believe otherwise, the administrative contracting officer may ordinarily rely on the contractor's certification in the progress payment request.
quote: Ordinarily, the ACO, in the absence of reason to believe otherwise, may rely upon the contractor's certification contained in the progress payment request.

statement: If the administrative contracting officer becomes aware of an arrangement or condition that would impair the Government's title to property affected by progress payments, the officer must require additional protective provisions.
quote: If the ACO becomes aware of any arrangement or condition that would impair the Government's title to the property affected by progress payment, the ACO shall require additional protective provisions (see 32.501-5) to establish and protect the Government's title.

statement: If the contractor fails to disclose an existing encumbrance in the progress payments certification, the administrative contracting officer should consult legal counsel about a possible False Claims Act violation.
quote: In addition, if the contractor fails to disclose an existing encumbrance in the progress payments certification, the ACO should consult with legal counsel concerning possible violation of 31 U.S.C. 3729, the False Claims Act.

statement: The contracting officer shall issue a final decision as required by FAR 33.211 if the contracting officer and the contractor are unable to reach agreement on the existence or amount of a debt in a timely manner.
quote: (a) The contracting officer shall issue a final decision as required by 33.211 if— (1) The contracting officer and the contractor are unable to reach agreement on the existence or amount of a debt in a timely manner;
note: The same paragraph also requires a final decision where a demanded debt is not liquidated or a deferment of collection is requested.

statement: Where a demand for payment was previously issued, the demand for payment included in the final decision must identify the same due date as the original demand.
quote: If a demand for payment was previously issued for the debt, the demand for payment included in the final decision shall identify the same due date as the original demand for payment.

statement: If the contractor has not liquidated the debt within 30 days of the date due and has not requested installment payments or deferment of collection, the payment office initiates withholding of principal, interest, penalties and administrative charges.
quote: If the contractor has not liquidated the debt within 30 days of the date due or requested installment payments or deferment of collection, the payment office shall initiate withholding of principal, interest, penalties, and administrative charges.

statement: Payment offices must transfer any debt that is delinquent more than 180 days to the Department of the Treasury for collection.
quote: (b) As provided for in the Debt Collection Improvement Act of 1996 (31 U.S.C. 3711(g)(1)), payment offices are required to transfer any debt that is delinquent more than 180 days to the Department of Treasury for collection.

statement: The final decision is furnished to the contractor by certified mail, return receipt requested, or by any other method that provides evidence of receipt; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-3196.
quote: (c) The contracting officer shall— (1) Furnish the decision to the contractor by certified mail, return receipt requested, or by any other method that provides evidence of receipt; and

statement: The contracting officer inserts the clause at FAR 52.232-17, Interest, in solicitations and contracts unless it is contemplated that the contract will be in one or more of the categories listed in FAR 32.611(a).
quote: The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.232—17, Interest, in solicitations and contracts unless it is contemplated that the contract will be in one or more of the following categories:

statement: The termination for convenience clauses provide that, after receipt of a termination notice, the prime contractor shall, unless the termination contracting officer directs otherwise, terminate all subcontracts to the extent they relate to performance of the terminated prime work.
quote: Termination for convenience clauses provide that after receipt of a termination notice the prime contractor shall, unless directed otherwise by the TCO, terminate all subcontracts to the extent that they relate to the performance of prime work terminated

statement: A prime contractor's failure to include an appropriate termination clause in a subcontract, or to exercise the clause rights, does not affect the Government's right to require the termination of the subcontract.
quote: The failure of a prime contractor to include an appropriate termination clause in any subcontract, or to exercise the clause rights, shall not— (1) Affect the Government's right to require the termination of the subcontract

statement: The reasonableness of the prime contractor's settlement with a subcontractor should normally be measured by the aggregate amount due under paragraph (f) of the subcontract termination clause suggested in FAR 49.502(e).
quote: In any case, the reasonableness of the prime contractor's settlement with the subcontractor should normally be measured by the aggregate amount due under paragraph (f) of the subcontract termination clause suggested in 49.502(e)

statement: The termination contracting officer allows reimbursement above the aggregate amount due under that paragraph only in unusual cases, and then only to the extent that the terms of the subcontract did not unreasonably increase the rights of the subcontractor.
quote: The TCO shall allow reimbursement in excess of that amount only in unusual cases and then only to the extent that the terms of the subcontract did not unreasonably increase the rights of the subcontractor

statement: The termination for convenience clauses in FAR 52.249, except the short-form clauses, obligate the prime contractor to assign to the Government, as directed by the termination contracting officer, all rights, titles and interest under any subcontract terminated because of termination of the prime contract.
quote: The termination for convenience clauses in 52.249, except the short-form clauses, obligate the prime contractor to assign to the Government, as directed by the TCO, all rights, titles, and interest under any subcontract terminated because of termination of the prime contract.

statement: As a general rule, the prime contractor is obligated to settle and pay subcontractors' settlement proposals arising out of the termination of subcontracts.
quote: As a general rule, the prime contractor is obligated to settle and pay these proposals.

statement: An example in which the Government's interest would be served is a sole-source subcontractor whose financial position a delay by the prime contractor in settlement or payment of its proposal would jeopardize.
quote: An example in which the Government's interest would be served is when a subcontractor is a sole source and it appears that a delay by the prime contractor in settlement or payment of the subcontractor's proposal will jeopardize the financial position of the subcontractor

statement: The termination contracting officer estimates the funds required to settle the termination and, within 30 days after receipt of the termination notice, recommends release of excess funds to the contracting officer.
quote: The TCO shall estimate the funds required to settle the termination, and within 30 days after the receipt of the termination notice, recommend the release of excess funds to the contracting officer

statement: The termination contracting officer does not recommend release of amounts under $1,000 unless requested by the contracting officer.
quote: The TCO shall not recommend the release of amounts under $1,000, unless requested by the contracting officer.

statement: If previous releases of excess funds result in a shortage of the amount required for settlement, the termination contracting officer promptly informs the contracting officer, who reinstates the funds within 30 days.
quote: If previous releases of excess funds result in a shortage of the amount required for settlement, the TCO shall promptly inform the contracting officer, who shall reinstate the funds within 30 days

statement: The format states the best estimate of the gross settlement cost and the amount available for release as excess to the contract.
quote: Based on the best information available, it is estimated that the gross settlement cost will be $____________. The amount available for release as excess to the contract is $____________.

statement: The termination contracting officer reserves in the settlement agreement any rights or demands of the parties that are excepted from the settlement and ensures that the wording of the reservation does not create any rights for the parties beyond those in existence before execution of the settlement agreement.
quote: The TCO shall— (1) Reserve in the settlement agreement any rights or demands of the parties that are excepted from the settlement; (2) Ensure that the wording of the reservation does not create any rights for the parties beyond those in existence before execution of the settlement agreement

statement: Each applicable settlement agreement is to be marked with the words "This settlement agreement contains a reservation" and the contract file is to be retained until the reservation is removed.
quote: (3) Mark each applicable settlement agreement with “This settlement agreement contains a reservation” and retain the contract file until the reservation is removed

statement: Sufficient funds are to be retained to cover complete settlement of the reserved items, and at the appropriate time a separate settlement of the reserved items is to be prepared and included in a separate settlement agreement.
quote: (4) Ensure that sufficient funds are retained to cover complete settlement of the reserved items; and (5) At the appropriate time, prepare a separate settlement of reserved items and include it in a separate settlement agreement

statement: With the consent of the contractor, the TCO or TCOs concerned may negotiate jointly two or more termination settlement proposals of the same contractor under different contracts, even though the contracts are with different contracting offices or agencies.
quote: With the consent of the contractor, the TCO or TCO's concerned may negotiate jointly two or more termination settlement proposals of the same contractor under different contracts, even though the contracts are with different contracting offices or agencies

statement: When a settlement agreement covers more than one contract, it clearly identifies the contracts involved, assigns an amendment modification number to each contract and apportions the total amount of the settlement among the several contracts on some reasonable basis; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-3253.
quote: When the settlement agreement covers more than one contract, it shall (1) clearly identify the contracts involved, (2) assign an amendment modification number to each contract, (3) apportion the total amount of the settlement among the several contracts on some reasonable basis

statement: If the settlement was negotiated on the basis of individual items, the termination contracting officer specifies the factors considered for each item.
quote: If the settlement was negotiated on the basis of individual items, the TCO shall specify the factors considered for each item.

statement: If the settlement was negotiated on an overall lump-sum basis, the termination contracting officer need not evaluate each item or group of items individually but supports the total amount of the recommended settlement in reasonable detail.
quote: If the settlement was negotiated on an overall lump-sum basis, the TCO need not evaluate each item or group of items individually, but shall support the total amount of the recommended settlement in reasonable detail

statement: The memorandum includes explanations of matters involving differences and doubtful questions settled by agreement, and the factors considered.
quote: The memorandum shall include explanations of matters involving differences and doubtful questions settled by agreement, and the factors considered.

statement: When the contract has been completely terminated, the contractor does not use Standard Form 1034 after the last day of the sixth month following the month in which the termination is effective.
quote: When the contract has been completely terminated, the contractor shall not use Standard Form 1034 (Public Voucher for Purchases and Services Other than Personal) after the last day of the sixth month following the month in which the termination is effective.

statement: When the contractor has vouchered out all costs within the 6-month period, a proposal for fee, if any, may be submitted on Standard Form 1437 or by letter appropriately certified.
quote: When the contractor has vouchered out all costs within the 6-month period, a proposal for fee, if any, may be submitted on SF 1437 (see 49.602-1) or by letter appropriately certified.

statement: The adjusted fee determination is generally based on a percentage of completion of the contract or of the terminated portion, using factors such as the extent and difficulty of the work performed by the contractor; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-3262 and CL-CTF-3128.
quote: The determination is generally based on a percentage of completion of the contract or of the terminated portion. When this basis is used, factors such as the extent and difficulty of the work performed by the contractor

statement: The factors considered under the percentage of completion basis are compared with the total work required by the contract or by the terminated portion.
quote: shall be compared with the total work required by the contract or by the terminated portion.

statement: Generally, the effort of a contractor under a cost-reimbursement construction or professional services contract can be segregated into factors such as mobilization including organization, use of finances, and contracting for and receipt of materials; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-3267.
quote: Generally, the effort of a contractor under a cost-reimbursement construction or professional services contract can be segregated into factors such as (1) mobilization including organization, (2) use of finances, (3) contracting for and receipt of materials

statement: Each applicable factor is assigned a weighted value depending on its importance and difficulty, and the total weight value of all factors should be easily divisible so that percentages can be determined.
quote: Each of the applicable factors in paragraph (a) above shall be assigned a weighted value depending on its importance and difficulty. The total weight value of all factors should be easily divisible (e.g., by 100) to determine percentages.

statement: That net sum, with sums previously paid, constitutes payment in full and complete settlement of the amount due the contractor on account of its fee under the contract.
quote: This sum, with sums previously paid, constitutes payment in full and complete settlement of the amount due the Contractor on account of its fee under the contract.

statement: The format reserves all rights and liabilities, if any, of the parties as to matters covered by any renegotiation authority.
quote: (i) All rights and liabilities, if any, of the parties, as to matters covered by any renegotiation authority.

statement: The format reserves all rights and liabilities of the parties arising under the contract and relating to reproduction rights, patent infringements, inventions or applications for patents; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-3284.
quote: (iii) All rights and liabilities of the parties arising under the contract and relating to reproduction rights, patent infringements, inventions, or applications for patents,

quote: (iv) All rights and liabilities of the parties, arising under the contract or otherwise, and concerning defects, guarantees, or warranties relating to any articles or component parts furnished to the Government by the Contractor under the contract or this agreement

statement: The format reserves all rights and liabilities of the parties under agreements relating to the future care and disposition by the contractor of Government-owned property remaining in the contractor's custody.
quote: (v) All rights and liabilities of the parties under agreements relating to the future care and disposition by the Contractor of Government-owned property remaining in the Contractor's custody

statement: The format reserves all rights and liabilities of the parties relating to Government property furnished to, or acquired by, the contractor for the performance of the contract.
quote: (vi) All rights and liabilities of the parties relating to Government property furnished to, or acquired by, the Contractor for the performance of the contract

statement: The format reserves all rights and liabilities of the parties under the contract relating to options other than options to continue or increase the work under the contract, covenants not to compete, and covenants of indemnity.
quote: (vii) All rights and liabilities of the parties under the contract relating to options (except options to continue or increase the work under the contract), covenants not to compete, and covenants of indemnity

statement: The format reserves all rights and liabilities, if any, of the parties under those clauses of the contract relating to price reductions for defective certified cost or pricing data.
quote: (viii) All rights and liabilities, if any, of the parties under those clauses of the contract relating to price reductions for defective certified cost or pricing data

statement: The agreement decreases the fee stated in the contract and, if appropriate, the estimated cost of the contract.

quote: (c) The Contractor's allowable costs and earned fee, if any, for the terminated portion of the contract will continue to be reimbursed on SF 1034, Public Voucher for Purchase and Services Other Than Personal, under the applicable provisions of the contract and part 31

statement: Termination for default is generally the exercise of the Government's contractual right to terminate a contract completely or partially because of the contractor's actual or anticipated failure to perform its contractual obligations.
quote: Termination for default is generally the exercise of the Government's contractual right to completely or partially terminate a contract because of the contractor's actual or anticipated failure to perform its contractual obligations.

quote: If the contractor can establish, or it is otherwise determined that the contractor was not in default or that the failure to perform is excusable; i.e., arose out of causes beyond the control and without the fault or negligence of the contractor

statement: The contracting officer may, with the written consent of the contractor, reinstate the terminated contract by amending the notice of termination, after a written determination is made that the supplies or services are still required and reinstatement is advantageous to the Government.
quote: the contracting officer may, with the written consent of the contractor, reinstate the terminated contract by amending the notice of termination, after a written determination is made that the supplies or services are still required and reinstatement is advantageous to the Government
