quote: If the contracting officer terminates a contract for default or follows a course of action instead of termination for default (see 49.402-4), the contracting officer promptly must assess and demand any liquidated damages to which the Government is entitled under the contract.

statement: The right to terminate a cost-reimbursement contract for default is provided for in the Termination for Default or for Convenience of the Government clause at FAR 52.249-6, which requires a 10-day notice to the contractor before termination for default in every case.
quote: The right to terminate a cost-reimbursement contract for default is provided for in the Termination for Default or for Convenience of the Government clause at 52.249-6. A 10-day notice to the contractor before termination for default is required in every case by the clause.

statement: Settlement of a cost-reimbursement contract terminated for default is subject to the principles in FAR subparts 49.1 and 49.3 as for a convenience termination, except that the costs of preparing the contractor's settlement proposal are not allowable; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-3295.

quote: However, a cost-reimbursement contract does not contain any provision for recovery of excess repurchase costs after termination for default (but see paragraph (g) of the clause at 52.246-3 with respect to failure of the contractor to replace or correct defective supplies).

statement: Standard Form 1435, Settlement Proposal (Inventory Basis), is used to submit settlement proposals resulting from the termination of fixed-price contracts if the proposals are computed on an inventory basis.
quote: Standard Form 1435, Settlement Proposal (Inventory Basis), shall be used to submit settlement proposals resulting from the termination of fixed-price contracts if the proposals are computed on an inventory basis

statement: Standard Form 1436, Settlement Proposal (Total Cost Basis), is used to submit settlement proposals resulting from the termination of fixed-price contracts if the proposals are computed on a total cost basis.
quote: Standard Form 1436, Settlement Proposal (Total Cost Basis), shall be used to submit settlement proposals resulting from the termination of fixed-price contracts if the proposals are computed on a total cost basis

statement: Standard Form 1437, Settlement Proposal for Cost-Reimbursement Type Contracts, is used to submit settlement proposals resulting from the termination of cost-reimbursement contracts.
quote: Standard Form 1437, Settlement Proposal for Cost-Reimbursement Type Contracts, shall be used to submit settlement proposals resulting from the termination of cost-reimbursement contracts

statement: Standard Form 1438, Settlement Proposal (Short Form), is used to submit settlement proposals resulting from the termination of fixed-price contracts if the total proposal is less than $10,000.
quote: Standard Form 1438, Settlement Proposal (Short Form), shall be used to submit settlement proposals resulting from the termination of fixed-price contracts if the total proposal is less than $10,000

statement: Contractors requesting authority to settle subcontractor settlement proposals furnish applicable information from the list in FAR 49.605 and any additional information required by the contracting officer.
quote: Contractors requesting authority to settle subcontractor settlement proposals shall furnish applicable information from the list below and any additional information required by the contracting officer:

statement: The contracting officer inserts the clause at FAR 52.249-12, Termination (Personal Services), in solicitations and contracts for personal services.
quote: The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.249-12, Termination (Personal Services), in solicitations and contracts for personal services (see Part 37).

statement: The contracting officer inserts the clause at FAR 52.249-14, Excusable Delays, in solicitations and contracts for supplies, services, construction, and research and development on a fee basis, when a cost-reimbursement contract is contemplated.
quote: The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.249-14, Excusable Delays, in solicitations and contracts for supplies, services, construction, and research and development on a fee basis, when a cost-reimbursement contract is contemplated.

statement: The FAR does not prescribe a clause for the cancellation or termination of orders under communication service contracts with common carriers because of special agency requirements that apply to these services.
quote: This regulation does not prescribe a clause for the cancellation or termination of orders under communication service contracts with common carriers because of special agency requirements that apply to these services.

statement: On a construction contract, when satisfactory progress has not been achieved by the contractor during a period for which a progress payment is to be made, a percentage of the progress payment may be retained.
quote: When satisfactory progress has not been achieved by a contractor during any period for which a progress payment is to be made, a percentage of the progress payment may be retained.

statement: Under loan guarantees, an exception may also be made for other instances of facilities expansion for which contract financing is appropriate under agency procedures.
quote: (2) Other instances of facilities expansion for which contract financing is appropriate under agency procedures.

statement: Performance-based payments are made in accordance with agency policy.
quote: These payments shall be made in accordance with agency policy.

quote: (2) Contracts for architect-engineer services or construction, or for shipbuilding or ship conversion, alteration, or repair, when the contracts provide for progress payments based upon a percentage or stage of completion;

statement: Performance-based payments may not be used for contracts awarded through sealed bid procedures.
quote: (3) Contracts awarded through sealed bid procedures.

statement: FAR 32.202-2 refers to FAR 32.001 for the meaning of commercial interim payment and of delivery payment.
quote: Commercial interim payment (See 32.001.) Delivery payment (See 32.001).

statement: An offer stating that the offeror will not use the contracting officer-specified contract financing terms does not alter the evaluation of the offer and does not render the offer nonresponsive or otherwise unacceptable.
quote: However, an offer stating that the contracting officer-specified contract financing terms will not be used by the offeror does not alter the evaluation of the offer, nor does it render the offer nonresponsive or otherwise unacceptable.

statement: The contracting officer responsible for administration of the contract is responsible for review and approval of contract financing requests.
quote: (a) Responsibility. The contracting officer responsible for administration of the contract shall be responsible for review and approval of contract financing requests.

statement: Unless agency regulations or an agreement with the appropriate payment official provide otherwise, the contracting officer is responsible for receiving, approving, and transmitting all contract financing requests to the appropriate payment office; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-3072.
quote: Unless otherwise provided in agency regulations, or by agreement with the appropriate payment official— (1) The contracting officer shall be responsible for receiving, approving, and transmitting all contract financing requests to the appropriate payment office; and

statement: After contract award, the contracting officer responsible for approving requests for financing payments is responsible for determining that the security continues to be adequate.
quote: (c) Management of security. After contract award, the contracting officer responsible for approving requests for financing payments shall be responsible for determining that the security continues to be adequate.

statement: If the contractor's financial condition is the Government's security, the contracting officer responsible for approving requests for financing payments is also responsible for monitoring the contractor's financial condition.
quote: If the contractor's financial condition is the Government's security, this contracting officer is also responsible for monitoring the contractor's financial condition.
note: The second sentence of paragraph (c) refers to this contracting officer, meaning the officer named in the first sentence.

statement: A financing institution that is willing to extend credit but considers a Government guarantee necessary may apply to the Federal Reserve Bank of its district for the guarantee, and application forms and guidance are available at all Federal Reserve Banks.
quote: If the financing institution is willing to extend credit, but considers a Government guarantee necessary, the institution may apply to the Federal Reserve Bank of its district for the guarantee. Application forms and guidance are available at all Federal Reserve Banks.

statement: The Federal Reserve Bank promptly sends a copy of the application, including a list of the relevant defense contracts held by the contractor, to the Federal Reserve Board.
quote: The Federal Reserve Bank will promptly send a copy of the application, including a list of the relevant defense contracts held by the contractor, to the Federal Reserve Board.

quote: (c) To expedite the process, the Federal Reserve Bank may, pursuant to instructions of a guaranteeing agency, submit lists of the defense contracts to the interested contracting officers.

quote: While eligibility is being determined, the Federal Reserve Bank will make any necessary credit investigations to supplement the information furnished by the applicant financing institution in order to— (1) Expedite necessary defense financing; and (2) Protect the Government against monetary loss.

statement: The Federal Reserve Bank sends its report and recommendation to the Federal Reserve Board, which transmits them to the interested guaranteeing agency.
quote: (e) The Federal Reserve Bank will send its report and recommendation to the Federal Reserve Board. The Board will transmit them to the interested guaranteeing agency.

statement: The asset formula may include all items under defense contracts for which the contractor would be entitled to payment on performance or termination.
quote: The asset formula may include all items under defense contracts for which the contractor would be entitled to payment on performance or termination.

quote: (c) The agency may relax the asset formula to an appropriate extent for the time actually necessary for contract performance, if the contractor's working capital and credit are inadequate.

statement: The agency may change the guarantee amount or maturity date, within the limitations at FAR 32.304-3, in the cases that follow in FAR 32.304-4.
quote: The agency may change the guarantee amount or maturity date, within the limitations at 32.304-3, as follows:

quote: Pertinent information and the Federal Reserve Bank reports will be submitted to the guaranteeing agency under the procedures for the original guarantee application, described in 32.304-1. Normally, a new certificate of eligibility is required.

quote: The agreement should give the financing institution the benefit, with regard to payments to be made on the contract, of the portion of its loans fairly attributable to expenditures made under the bonded subcontracts before notice of default.

quote: (b) If the agency consents to the contractor obtaining other borrowing during the guaranteed loan period, the agency shall apply the following restrictions: (1) A reasonable limit on the amount of other borrowing.

quote: (2) If guaranteed and unguaranteed loans are made by the same financing institution, a requirement that any collateral security requested by the institution under the unguaranteed loan is also to be secondary collateral for the guaranteed loan.

quote: Guaranteed loans also may be made before such termination if it is known that termination of particular contracts for the convenience of the Government is about to occur. These loans are expected to provide necessary financing pending termination settlements and payments.

quote: They may also finance continuing performance of defense production contracts that are eligible for guaranteed loans.
note: The quote refers to the loans described in the preceding sentences of paragraph (a).

statement: The agency shall take precautions necessary to avoid Government losses and to ensure that guaranteed loans for terminated contracts will be self-liquidating from the proceeds of defense production contracts.
quote: The agency shall take precautions necessary to avoid Government losses and to ensure the loans will be self-liquidating from the proceeds of defense production contracts.

statement: Loan guarantees for contract termination financing shall not be provided before specific contract terminations are certain.
quote: (c) Loan guarantees for contract termination financing shall not be provided before specific contract terminations are certain.

statement: Actions that designated agencies may take to facilitate the national defense without regard to other provisions of law relating to contracts, as explained in FAR 50.101-1(a), also include making advance payments.
quote: (a) Actions that designated agencies may take to facilitate the national defense without regard to other provisions of law relating to contracts, as explained in 50.101-1(a), also include making advance payments.

quote: The ratio of costs incurred to the total estimated cost of performing the contract or the terminated portion is only one factor in computing the percentage of completion.

quote: When totaled, the percentage of completion of each factor applied to the weighted value of each factor results in the overall percentage of contract completion.

statement: The percentage of completion is then applied to the total contract fee, or to the fee applicable to the terminated portion of the contract, to arrive at an equitable adjustment.
quote: The percentage of completion is then applied to the total contract fee or to the fee applicable to the terminated portion of the contract to arrive at an equitable adjustment.

statement: If the contractor or offeror meets the standards prescribed for responsible prospective contractors, the contracting officer shall not treat the contractor's need for contract financing as a handicap for a contract award, for example as a responsibility factor or evaluation criterion.
quote: (a) If the contractor or offeror meets the standards prescribed for responsible prospective contractors at 9.104, the contracting officer shall not treat the contractor's need for contract financing as a handicap for a contract award; e.g., as a responsibility factor or evaluation criterion.

statement: The contractor should not be disqualified from contract financing solely because the contractor failed to indicate a need for contract financing before the contract was awarded.
quote: (b) The contractor should not be disqualified from contract financing solely because the contractor failed to indicate a need for contract financing before the contract was awarded.

statement: Each contracting office should have available and use the services of contract financing personnel competent to evaluate credit and financial problems.
quote: Each contracting office should have available and use the services of contract financing personnel competent to evaluate credit and financial problems.

statement: In resolving any questions about the financial capability of an offeror or contractor to perform a contract, or about what form of contract financing is appropriate in a given case, the contracting officer should consult the appropriate contract financing office.
quote: In resolving any questions concerning (a) the financial capability of an offeror or contractor to perform a contract or (b) what form of contract financing is appropriate in a given case, the contracting officer should consult the appropriate contract financing office.

statement: If the contractor makes financing payments to a subcontractor under a cost-reimbursement prime contract, the contracting officer should accept the financing payments as reimbursable costs of the prime contract only under the conditions listed in the section.
quote: If the contractor makes financing payments to a subcontractor under a cost-reimbursement prime contract, the contracting officer should accept the financing payments as reimbursable costs of the prime contract only under the following conditions:

statement: One listed condition is that the payments are made under the criteria in subpart 32.5 for customary progress payments based on costs, 32.202-1 for commercial product or commercial service purchase financing, or 32.1003 for performance-based payments, as applicable.
quote: (a) The payments are made under the criteria in subpart 32.5 for customary progress payments based on costs, 32.202-1 for commercial product or commercial service purchase financing, or 32.1003 for performance-based payments, as applicable.

statement: If customary progress payments are made, a listed condition is that the payments do not exceed the progress payment rate in 32.501-1, unless unusual progress payments to the subcontractor have been approved in accordance with 32.501-2.
quote: (b) If customary progress payments are made, the payments do not exceed the progress payment rate in 32.501-1, unless unusual progress payments to the subcontractor have been approved in accordance with 32.501-2.

statement: If customary progress payments are made, a listed condition is that the subcontractor complies with the liquidation principles of 32.503-8, 32.503-9, and 32.503-10.
quote: (c) If customary progress payments are made, the subcontractor complies with the liquidation principles of 32.503-8, 32.503-9, and 32.503-10.

statement: If performance-based payments are made, a listed condition is that the subcontractor complies with the liquidation principles of 32.1004(d).
quote: (d) If performance-based payments are made, the subcontractor complies with the liquidation principles of 32.1004(d).

statement: A listed condition is that the subcontract contains financing payments terms as prescribed in the part.
quote: (e) The subcontract contains financing payments terms as prescribed in this part.

statement: The statutes provide that payment for commercial products or commercial services may be made under such terms and conditions as the head of the agency determines are appropriate or customary in the commercial marketplace and are in the best interest of the United States.
quote: 10 U.S.C. 3805 and 41 U.S.C. 4505 provide that payment for commercial products or commercial services may be made under such terms and conditions as the head of the agency determines are appropriate or customary in the commercial marketplace and are in the best interest of the United States.

statement: Contract financing may be a subject included in the market research conducted in accordance with part 10.
quote: Contract financing may be a subject included in the market research conducted in accordance with part 10.

statement: If market research for contract financing is conducted, the contracting officer should consider the extent to which other buyers provide contract financing for purchases in that market and the overall level of financing normally provided.
quote: If market research for contract financing is conducted, the contracting officer should consider— (a) The extent to which other buyers provide contract financing for purchases in that market; (b) The overall level of financing normally provided;

statement: The matters listed for the contracting officer's consideration also include the amount or percentages of any payments equivalent to commercial advance payments and the basis for any payments equivalent to commercial interim payments, with their frequency and amounts or percentages; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-3609.
quote: (c) The amount or percentages of any payments equivalent to commercial advance payments (see 32.202-2); (d) The basis for any payments equivalent to commercial interim payments (see 32.001), as well as the frequency, and amounts or percentages; and

statement: When the criteria in 32.202-1(b) are met, the contracting officer may either specify the financing terms in the solicitation or permit each offeror to propose its own customary financing terms.
quote: When the criteria in 32.202-1(b) are met, the contracting officer may either specify the financing terms in the solicitation (see 32.204) or permit each offeror to propose its own customary financing terms (see 32.205).

statement: When the contracting officer has sufficient information on financing terms that are customary in the commercial marketplace for the item, those terms may be specified in the solicitation.
quote: When the contracting officer has sufficient information on financing terms that are customary in the commercial marketplace for the item, those terms may be specified in the solicitation.

statement: As used in the subpart, a borrower is a contractor, subcontractor at any tier, or other supplier who receives a guaranteed loan.
quote: As used in this subpart— Borrower means a contractor, subcontractor (at any tier), or other supplier who receives a guaranteed loan.

statement: A guaranteed loan, or V loan, is a loan, revolving credit fund, or other financial arrangement made pursuant to Regulation V of the Federal Reserve Board, under which the guaranteeing agency is obligated, on demand of the lender, to purchase a stated percentage of the loan; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-3611.
quote: Guaranteed loan or V loan means a loan, revolving credit fund, or other financial arrangement made pursuant to Regulation V of the Federal Reserve Board, under which the guaranteeing agency is obligated, on demand of the lender, to purchase a stated percentage of the loan

statement: A guaranteeing agency is any agency that the President has authorized to guarantee loans, through Federal Reserve Banks, for expediting national defense production.
quote: Guaranteeing agency means any agency that the President has authorized to guarantee loans, through Federal Reserve Banks, for expediting national defense production.

statement: Congress has authorized Federal Reserve Banks to act, on behalf of guaranteeing agencies, as fiscal agents of the United States in the making of loan guarantees for defense production.
quote: Congress has authorized Federal Reserve Banks to act, on behalf of guaranteeing agencies, as fiscal agents of the United States in the making of loan guarantees for defense production

statement: The President has designated as guaranteeing agencies the Departments of Defense, Energy, Commerce, the Interior and Agriculture, the General Services Administration and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration.
quote: designated the following agencies as guaranteeing agencies: (a) Department of Defense. (b) Department of Energy. (c) Department of Commerce. (d) Department of the Interior. (e) Department of Agriculture. (f) General Services Administration. (g) National Aeronautics and Space Administration.

statement: If the request for a loan guarantee concerns a subcontractor that is financially weak in comparison with its contractor, the Government's interests may be fostered by the contractor making progress payments to the subcontractor.
quote: If the request for a loan guarantee concerns a subcontractor that is financially weak in comparison with its contractor, the Government's interests may be fostered by the contractor making progress payments to the subcontractor.

statement: In that case the agency shall try to arrange for the contractor to provide the progress payments, and as a result the need for the loan guarantee may be reduced or eliminated and the contractor would bear part or all of the risk of loss arising from the selection of the subcontractor.
quote: If so, the agency shall try to arrange for the contractor to provide the progress payments. As a result, the need for the loan guarantee may be reduced or eliminated and the contractor would bear part or all of the risk of loss arising from the selection of the subcontractor.

statement: Progress payments may be customary or unusual, and customary progress payments are those made under the general guidance in the subpart, using the customary progress payment rate, the cost base, and frequency of payment established in the Progress Payments clause; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-3549.
quote: Progress payments may be customary or unusual. Customary progress payments are those made under the general guidance in this subpart, using the customary progress payment rate, the cost base, and frequency of payment established in the Progress Payments clause

statement: Customary progress payments also use either the ordinary liquidation method or the alternate method as provided in subsections 32.503-8 and 32.503-9.
quote: and either the ordinary liquidation method or the alternate method as provided in subsections 32.503-8 and 32.503-9.

statement: If the contracting officer considers it necessary for protection of the Government's interest, protective terms such as the listed ones may be used in addition to the Progress Payments clause of the contract.
quote: If the contracting officer considers it necessary for protection of the Government's interest, protective terms such as the following may be used in addition to the Progress Payments clause of the contract:

statement: The listed protective terms include personal or corporate guarantees, subordinations or standbys of indebtedness, special bank accounts, and protective covenants of the kinds in paragraph (p) of the clause at 52.232-12, Advance Payments.
quote: (a) Personal or corporate guarantees. (b) Subordinations or standbys of indebtedness. (c) Special bank accounts. (d) Protective covenants of the kinds in paragraph (p) of the clause at 52.232-12, Advance Payments.

statement: A listed protective term is a provision, included in the solicitation and resultant contract when first article testing is required, limiting progress payments on first article work by a stated amount or percentage.
quote: (e) A provision, included in the solicitation and resultant contract when first article testing is required (see subpart 9.3), limiting progress payments on first article work by a stated amount or percentage.

statement: The contracting officer shall obtain the approval of the contract finance office or other offices designated under agency procedures before taking any of the actions listed in the section.
quote: The contracting officer shall obtain the approval of the contract finance office or other offices designated under agency procedures before taking any of the following actions:

statement: The listed actions include providing a progress payment rate higher than the customary rate and deviating from the progress payments terms prescribed in the part.
quote: (a) Providing a progress payment rate higher than the customary rate (see 32.501-1). (b) Deviating from the progress payments terms prescribed in this part.

statement: The listed actions also include providing progress payments to a contractor whose financial condition is in doubt, or who has had an advance payment request or loan guarantee denied for financial reasons (or approved but withdrawn or lapsed) within the previous 12 months; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-3613.
quote: (c) Providing progress payments to a contractor— (1) Whose financial condition is in doubt; (2) Who has had an advance payment request or loan guarantee denied for financial reasons (or approved but withdrawn or lapsed) within the previous 12 months; or

statement: The advance payment subpart provides policies and procedures for advance payments on prime contracts and subcontracts.
quote: This subpart provides policies and procedures for advance payments on prime contracts and subcontracts.

statement: The advance payment subpart does not include policies and procedures for advance payments for the types of transactions listed in 32.404.
quote: It does not include policies and procedures for advance payments for the types of transactions listed in 32.404.

statement: The advance payment subpart does not apply to commercial advance payments, which are subject to subpart 32.2.
quote: This subpart does not apply to commercial advance payments, which are subject to subpart 32.2.

statement: The agency may authorize advance payments in negotiated and sealed bid contracts if the action is appropriate under chapter 45 of title 41 of the United States Code, chapter 277 of title 10 of the United States Code, or Public Law 85-804 and Executive Order 10789.
quote: The agency may authorize advance payments in negotiated and sealed bid contracts if the action is appropriate under (a) 41 U.S.C. chapter 45; (b) 10 U.S.C. chapter 277; or (c) Pub. L. 85-804 (50 U.S.C. 1431-1435) and Executive Order 10789, November 14, 1958

statement: The section refers to Subpart 50.1 for other applications of Public Law 85-804.
quote: (see Subpart 50.1 for other applications of this statute)

statement: The contracting officer may use performance-based payments for individual orders and contracts provided that the contracting officer and the offeror agree on the performance-based payment terms.
quote: The contracting officer may use performance-based payments for individual orders and contracts provided— (a) The contracting officer and offeror agree on the performance-based payment terms;

statement: A condition for using performance-based payments is that the contract, individual order or line item is a fixed-price type.
quote: (b) The contract, individual order, or line item is a fixed-price type;

statement: For an indefinite delivery contract the individual order must not provide for progress payments, and for other than an indefinite delivery contract the contract must not provide for progress payments.
quote: (c) For indefinite delivery contracts, the individual order does not provide for progress payments; and (d) For other than indefinite delivery contracts, the contract does not provide for progress payments.

statement: The clause at 52.232-32, Performance-Based Payments, must be inserted in solicitations that may result in contracts providing for performance-based payments and in fixed-price contracts under which the Government will provide them.
quote: Insert the clause at 52.232-32, Performance-Based Payments, in— (1) Solicitations that may result in contracts providing for performance-based payments; and (2) Fixed-price contracts under which the Government will provide performance-based payments.

statement: The solicitation provision at 52.232-28, Invitation to Propose Performance-Based Payments, must be inserted in negotiated solicitations that invite offerors to propose performance-based payments.
quote: Insert the solicitation provision at 52.232-28, Invitation to Propose Performance-Based Payments, in negotiated solicitations that invite offerors to propose performance-based payments.

statement: The provision must be used with Alternate I in competitive negotiated solicitations if the Government intends to adjust proposed prices for proposal evaluation purposes.
quote: Use the provision with its Alternate I in competitive negotiated solicitations if the Government intends to adjust proposed prices for proposal evaluation purposes (see 32.1004(e)).

statement: The contracting officer has primary responsibility for identifying and demanding payment of contract debts, except those resulting from errors made by the payment office.
quote: The contracting officer has primary responsibility for identifying and demanding payment of contract debts except those resulting from errors made by the payment office.

statement: The contracting officer shall not collect contract debts or otherwise agree to liquidate them, for example by offsetting a debt against unpaid bills due the contractor or by allowing the contractor to retain a debt to cover amounts that may become payable in future periods.
quote: The contracting officer shall not collect contract debts or otherwise agree to liquidate contract debts (e.g., offset the amount of the debt against existing unpaid bills due the contractor, or allow contractors to retain contract debts to cover amounts that may become payable in future periods).

statement: The payment office has primary responsibility for collecting the contract debts identified by contracting officers.
quote: The payment office has primary responsibility for— (1) Collecting contract debts identified by contracting officers;

statement: The payment office has primary responsibility for identifying and collecting duplicate and erroneous payments and for authorizing the liquidation of contract debts in accordance with agency procedures.
quote: (2) Identifying and collecting duplicate and erroneous payments; and (3) Authorizing the liquidation of contract debts in accordance with agency procedures.

statement: If the contracting officer has any indication that a contractor owes money to the Government under a contract, the contracting officer shall determine promptly whether an actual debt is due and its amount.
quote: If the contracting officer has any indication that a contractor owes money to the Government under a contract, the contracting officer shall determine promptly whether an actual debt is due and the amount.

statement: Unnecessary delay in determining whether a debt is due may contribute to loss of timely availability of the funds to the program for which they were provided, increased difficulty in collecting the debt, or actual monetary loss to the Government.
quote: Any unnecessary delay may contribute to— (1) Loss of timely availability of the funds to the program for which the funds were initially provided; (2) Increased difficulty in collecting the debt; or (3) Actual monetary loss to the Government.

statement: The amount of indebtedness determined by the contracting officer shall be based on the merits of the case and consistent with the contract terms.
quote: The amount of indebtedness determined by the contracting officer shall be an amount that— (1) Is based on the merits of the case; and (2) Is consistent with the contract terms.

statement: In the assignment of claims subpart, designated agency means any department or agency of the executive branch of the United States Government.
quote: Designated agency, as used in this subpart, means any department or agency of the executive branch of the United States Government (see 32.803(d)).

statement: In the assignment of claims subpart, a no-setoff commitment means a contractual undertaking that, to the extent the Act permits, payments by the designated agency to the assignee under an assignment of claims will not be reduced to liquidate the indebtedness of the contractor to the Government.
quote: No-setoff commitment, as used in this subpart, means a contractual undertaking that, to the extent permitted by the Act, payments by the designated agency to the assignee under an assignment of claims will not be reduced to liquidate the indebtedness of the contractor to the Government.

statement: No payment the Government makes to the assignee under a contract assigned in accordance with the Act may be recovered on account of any liability of the contractor to the Government.
quote: No payments made by the Government to the assignee under any contract assigned in accordance with the Act may be recovered on account of any liability of the contractor to the Government.

statement: That immunity of the assignee applies whether the liability of the contractor arises from the assigned contract or independently of it.
quote: This immunity of the assignee is effective whether the contractor's liability arises from or independently of the assigned contract.

statement: Except as provided in paragraph (c), a no-setoff commitment in an assigned contract entitles the assignee to receive contract payments free of reduction or setoff for any liability of the contractor to the Government arising independently of the contract.
quote: Except as provided in paragraph (c) below, the inclusion of a no-setoff commitment in an assigned contract entitles the assignee to receive contract payments free of reduction or setoff for— (1) Any liability of the contractor to the Government arising independently of the contract;

statement: A no-setoff commitment's protection also covers liabilities of the contractor to the Government arising from the assigned contract for renegotiation under any statute or contract clause and for fines.
quote: (2) Any of the following liabilities of the contractor to the Government arising from the assigned contract: (i) Renegotiation under any statute or contract clause. (ii) Fines.

statement: The protection for liabilities arising from the assigned contract also covers penalties, exclusive of amounts that may be collected or withheld from the contractor under, or for failure to comply with, the terms of the contract.
quote: (iii) Penalties, exclusive of amounts that may be collected or witheld from the contractor under, or for failure to comply with, the terms of the contract.

statement: The protection for liabilities arising from the assigned contract also covers taxes or social security contributions, and the withholding or nonwithholding of them.
quote: (iv) Taxes or social security contributions. (v) Withholding or nonwithholding of taxes or social security contributions.

statement: A setoff may be appropriate in some circumstances even though the assigned contract includes a no-setoff commitment, for example when the assignee has neither made a loan under the assignment nor made a commitment to do so.
quote: (c) In some circumstances, a setoff may be appropriate even though the assigned contract includes a no-setoff commitment, e.g.— (1) When the assignee has neither made a loan under the assignment nor made a commitment to do so;

statement: A setoff may also be appropriate to the extent that the amount due on the contract exceeds the amount of any loans made or expected to be made under a firm commitment for financing.
quote: (2) To the extent that the amount due on the contract exceeds the amount of any loans made or expected to be made under a firm commitment for financing.

statement: In the prompt payment subpart, a discount for prompt payment means an invoice payment reduction offered by the contractor for payment before the due date.
quote: Discount for prompt payment means an invoice payment reduction offered by the contractor for payment prior to the due date.

statement: In the prompt payment subpart, a mixed invoice means an invoice that contains items with different payment due dates.
quote: Mixed invoice means an invoice that contains items with different payment due dates.

statement: In the prompt payment subpart, payment date means the date on which a check for payment is dated or, for an electronic funds transfer, the settlement date.
quote: Payment date means the date on which a check for payment is dated or, for an electronic funds transfer (EFT), the settlement date.

statement: In the prompt payment subpart, settlement date means the date on which an electronic funds transfer payment is credited to the financial institution of the contractor.
quote: Settlement date, as it applies to electronic funds transfer, means the date on which an electronic funds transfer payment is credited to the contractor's financial institution.

statement: Questions about delinquent payments are directed to the designated billing office or the designated payment office.
quote: Direct questions involving— (1) Delinquent payments to the designated billing office or designated payment office; and

statement: Disagreements in payment amount or timing are directed to the contracting officer for resolution, and the contracting officer must coordinate within appropriate contracting channels and seek the advice of other offices as necessary to resolve them.
quote: (2) Disagreements in payment amount or timing to the contracting officer for resolution. The contracting officer must coordinate within appropriate contracting channels and seek the advice of other offices as necessary to resolve disagreements.

statement: Small business concerns may contact the local small business specialist at the agency or a representative from the Office of Small and Disadvantaged Business Utilization for additional assistance related to payment issues, late payment interest penalties and information on the Prompt Payment Act.
quote: Small business concerns may contact the agency's local small business specialist or representative from the Office of Small and Disadvantaged Business Utilization to obtain additional assistance related to payment issues, late payment interest penalties, and information on the Prompt Payment Act.

statement: In the electronic funds transfer subpart, EFT information means the information necessary for making a payment by electronic funds transfer through specified EFT mechanisms.
quote: means information necessary for making a payment by EFT through specified EFT mechanisms.

statement: In the electronic funds transfer subpart, a Governmentwide commercial purchase card means a card that is similar in nature to a commercial credit card and is used to make financing and delivery payments for supplies and services.
quote: Governmentwide commercial purchase card means a card that is similar in nature to a commercial credit card that is used to make financing and delivery payments for supplies and services.

statement: In the electronic funds transfer subpart, the purchase card is an EFT method and may be used to meet the requirement to pay by EFT to the extent that purchase card limits do not preclude such payments.
quote: The purchase card is an EFT method and it may be used as a means to meet the requirement to pay by EFT, to the extent that purchase card limits do not preclude such payments.

statement: In the electronic funds transfer subpart, payment information means the payment advice provided by the Government to the contractor that identifies what the payment is for, any computations or adjustments made by the Government, and any information required by the Prompt Payment Act.
quote: Payment information means the payment advice provided by the Government to the contractor that identifies what the payment is for, any computations or adjustments made by the Government, and any information required by the Prompt Payment Act.

statement: Use of EFT payment methods is not a substitute for a properly executed assignment of claims in accordance with Subpart 32.8.
quote: The use of EFT payment methods is not a substitute for a properly executed assignment of claims in accordance with Subpart 32.8.

statement: EFT information that shows the ultimate recipient of the transfer to be other than the contractor, in the absence of a proper assignment of claims, is considered incorrect EFT information within the meaning of the Suspension of Payment paragraphs of the EFT clauses at 52.232-33 and 52.232-34.
quote: EFT information that shows the ultimate recipient of the transfer to be other than the contractor, in the absence of a proper assignment of claims, is considered to be incorrect EFT information within the meaning of the “Suspension of Payment” paragraphs of the EFT clauses at 52.232-33 and 52.232-34

statement: Where offerors must submit EFT information before award, the successful offeror is not responsible for resubmitting it after award of the contract except to make changes, or to place the information on invoices if agency procedures require that.
quote: If offerors are required to submit EFT information prior to award, the successful offeror is not responsible for resubmitting this information after award of the contract except to make changes, or to place the information on invoices if required by agency procedures.

statement: Where the successful offeror is not responsible for resubmitting EFT information after award, contracting officers shall forward the EFT information provided by the successful offeror to the appropriate office.
quote: Therefore, contracting officers shall forward EFT information provided by the successful offeror to the appropriate office.

statement: The part also addresses assignment of claims to aid in private financing, selected payment clauses, financing of purchases of commercial products and commercial services, performance-based payments and electronic funds transfer payments.
quote: (e) Assignment of claims to aid in private financing; (f) Selected payment clauses; (g) Financing of purchases of commercial products and commercial services; (h) Performance-based payments; and (i) Electronic funds transfer payments.

statement: The enforceability of contract provisions for security of Government financing in a foreign jurisdiction is dependent upon local law and procedure.
quote: The enforceability of contract provisions for security of Government financing in a foreign jurisdiction is dependent upon local law and procedure.

statement: Authority to reduce or suspend payments under these statutes is in addition to other Government rights, remedies, and procedures.
quote: (d) Authority to reduce or suspend payments under these statutes is in addition to other Government rights, remedies, and procedures.

statement: The matters listed for the contracting officer's consideration also include methods of liquidation of contract financing payments and any special or unusual payment terms applicable to delivery payments.
quote: (e) Methods of liquidation of contract financing payments and any special or unusual payment terms applicable to delivery payments (see 32.001).

statement: As used in the subpart, the Federal Reserve Board is the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System.
quote: Federal Reserve Board means the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System.

statement: Under a guaranteed loan, the guaranteeing agency is obligated, on demand of the lender, to purchase a stated percentage of the loan and to share any losses in the amount of the guaranteed percentage.
quote: the guaranteeing agency is obligated, on demand of the lender, to purchase a stated percentage of the loan and to share any losses in the amount of the guaranteed percentage.

statement: Any other progress payments are considered unusual, and may be used only in exceptional cases when authorized in accordance with subsection 32.501-2.
quote: Any other progress payments are considered unusual, and may be used only in exceptional cases when authorized in accordance with subsection 32.501-2.

statement: The listed actions also include providing progress payments to a contractor who is named in the consolidated list of contractors indebted to the United States, known commonly as the Hold-up List.
quote: (3) Who is named in the consolidated list of contractors indebted to the United States (known commonly as the Hold-up List).

statement: Any contract financing arrangement not in accord with the requirements of agency regulations or the part is unusual contract financing and requires advance approval in accordance with agency procedures.
quote: Any contract financing arrangement not in accord with the requirements of agency regulations or this part is unusual contract financing and requires advance approval in accordance with agency procedures.

statement: If not otherwise specified, unusual contract financing for a commercial purchase shall be approved by the head of the contracting activity.
quote: If not otherwise specified, such unusual contract financing shall be approved by the head of the contracting activity.

statement: When a contractor requests an installment payment agreement, the contracting officer must notify the contractor to send a written request for installment payments to the office designated in agency procedures.
quote: If a contractor requests an installment payment agreement, the contracting officer shall notify the contractor to send a written request for installment payments to the office designated in agency procedures.

statement: Unless the Interest clause specifies otherwise, interest charges apply to any contract debt unpaid after 30 days from the issuance of a demand; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-3618, which holds the exceptions.
quote: Unless specified otherwise in the clause at 52.232-17, Interest, interest charges shall apply to any contract debt unpaid after 30 days from the issuance of a demand

statement: Interest charges do not apply when the contract is a kind excluded under 32.611 or when the contract or debt has been exempted from interest charges under agency procedures.
quote: unless— (a) The contract is a kind excluded under 32.611; or (b) The contract or debt has been exempted from interest charges under agency procedures.

statement: The rule in this section applies if interest is accrued based on the date of the demand letter and the Government delays delivery of the demand letter, for example by undue delay after dating at the originating office or by delays in the mail; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-CTF-3632.
quote: If interest is accrued based on the date of the demand letter and delivery of the demand letter is delayed by the Government (e.g., undue delay after dating at the originating office or delays in the mail),

statement: For debts under $100,000, excluding interest, the designated agency official may compromise the debt pursuant to the Federal Claims Collection Standards (31 CFR part 902) and agency regulations.
quote: For debts under $100,000, excluding interest, the designated agency official may compromise the debt pursuant to the Federal Claims Collection Standards (31 CFR part 902) and agency regulations.

statement: Unless specifically authorized by agency procedures, contracting officers cannot compromise debts.
quote: Unless specifically authorized by agency procedures, contracting officers cannot compromise debts.

statement: The DFARS section headed Debt determination says that, when transferring a case to the contract financing office, the procedures at PGI 232.603 must be followed.
quote: Debt determination. When transferring a case to the contract financing office, follow the procedures at PGI 232.603.

statement: When issuing a demand for payment of a contract debt, the procedures at PGI 232.604 must be followed.
quote: When issuing a demand for payment of a contract debt, follow the procedures at PGI 232.604.

statement: Only the department or agency contract financing offices are authorized to compromise debts covered by this subpart.
quote: Only the department/agency contract financing offices (see PGI 232.070(c)) are authorized to compromise debts covered by this subpart.
note: In this section, this subpart is the DFARS contract debts subpart. The sentence points to PGI 232.070(c) for the offices.

statement: Transferring responsibility for debt collection must follow the procedures at PGI 232.670.
quote: Follow the procedures at PGI 232.670 for transferring responsibility for debt collection.

statement: Bankruptcy reporting must follow the procedures at PGI 232.671.
quote: Follow the procedures at PGI 232.671 for bankruptcy reporting.

statement: The requirements of FAR subpart 32.4 do not apply to advertisements in high school and college publications for military recruitment efforts under section 503 of title 10, United States Code, when the contract cost does not exceed the micro-purchase threshold.
quote: The requirements of FAR subpart 32.4 do not apply to advertisements in high school and college publications for military recruitment efforts under 10 U.S.C. 503 when the contract cost does not exceed the micro-purchase threshold.

statement: The DFARS section headed Recommendation for approval says to follow the procedures at PGI 232.409-1 for preparation of the documents required by FAR 32.409-1(e) and (f).
quote: Recommendation for approval. Follow the procedures at PGI 232.409-1 for preparation of the documents required by FAR 32.409-1(e) and (f).

statement: The DFARS section headed Findings, determination, and authorization says that, if an advance payment procedure is used without a special bank account, the procedures at PGI 232.410 must be followed.
quote: Findings, determination, and authorization. If an advance payment procedure is used without a special bank account, follow the procedures at PGI 232.410.

statement: The scope section of the FAR contract debts subpart says the subpart prescribes policies and procedures for identifying, collecting, and deferring collection of contract debts, including interest if applicable.
quote: This subpart prescribes policies and procedures for identifying, collecting, and deferring collection of contract debts (including interest, if applicable).

statement: Sections 32.607, 32.608 and 32.610 of the FAR contract debts subpart do not apply to claims against common carriers for transportation overcharges and freight and cargo losses (section 3726 of title 31, United States Code).
quote: Sections 32.607, 32.608, and 32.610 of this subpart do not apply to claims against common carriers for transportation overcharges and freight and cargo losses (31 U.S.C. 3726).

statement: In that case the date of the debt and accrual of interest must be extended to a time that is fair and reasonable under the particular circumstances; the condition that comes before this clause is in CL-CTF-3619.
quote: the date of the debt and accrual of interest shall be extended to a time that is fair and reasonable under the particular circumstances.

statement: FAR 32.409-1 lists, as paragraph (e), proposed advance payment contract terms, including proposed security requirements, and, as paragraph (f), the findings, determination, and authorization (see FAR 32.410).

note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0022 directs its use (CL-CTF-4046). The RFO wording is the same in substance as the codified paragraph; only "shall" becomes "must".

note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0022 directs its use (CL-CTF-4046). The RFO wording is the same in substance as the codified text.

quote: (4) Contracts with a foreign government or instrumentality. (5) Contracts without any provision for profit or fee with a nonprofit organization.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0022 directs its use (CL-CTF-4046). The RFO wording is the same in substance as the codified text.

quote: The contracting officer must not collect contract debts or otherwise agree to liquidate contract debts (e.g., offset the amount of the debt against existing unpaid bills due the contractor, or allow contractors to retain contract debts to cover amounts that may become payable in future periods).
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0022 directs its use (CL-CTF-4046). The RFO wording is the same in substance as the codified paragraph; only "shall" becomes "must".

statement: Under RFO FAR 32.602(b)(1), the payment office has primary responsibility for collecting contract debts identified by contracting officers.

quote: (b) The payment office has primary responsibility for— (1) Collecting contract debts identified by contracting officers; (2) Identifying and collecting duplicate and erroneous payments; and (3) Authorizing the liquidation of contract debts in accordance with agency procedures.
