note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.215-20(a)(1)(i) calls for identification of the law or regulation establishing the price offered, and, if the price is controlled under law by periodic rulings, reviews, or similar actions of a governmental body, a copy of the controlling document, unless it was previously submitted to the contracting office.
quote: (i) Identification of the law or regulation establishing the price offered. If the price is controlled under law by periodic rulings, reviews, or similar actions of a governmental body, attach a copy of the controlling document, unless it was previously submitted to the contracting office.
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.215-20(a)(1)(ii) says that for a commercial product and commercial service exception the offeror shall submit, at a minimum, information on prices at which the same item or similar items have previously been sold in the commercial market that is adequate for evaluating the reasonableness of the price for the acquisition.
quote: For a commercial product and commercial service exception, the offeror shall submit, at a minimum, information on prices at which the same item or similar items have previously been sold in the commercial market that is adequate for evaluating the reasonableness of the price for this acquisition.
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.215-20(a)(2) says the offeror grants the Contracting Officer or an authorized representative the right to examine, at any time before award, books, records, documents, or other directly pertinent records to verify any request for an exception under the provision, and the reasonableness of price.
quote: (2) The offeror grants the Contracting Officer or an authorized representative the right to examine, at any time before award, books, records, documents, or other directly pertinent records to verify any request for an exception under this provision, and the reasonableness of price.
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.215-20(a)(2) says that, for items priced using catalog or market prices, or law or regulation, access does not extend to cost or profit information or other data relevant solely to the offeror's determination of the prices to be offered in the catalog or marketplace.
quote: For items priced using catalog or market prices, or law or regulation, access does not extend to cost or profit information or other data relevant solely to the offeror’s determination of the prices to be offered in the catalog or marketplace.
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.215-20(b)(1) says the offeror shall prepare and submit certified cost or pricing data, data other than certified cost or pricing data, and supporting attachments in accordance with the instructions contained in Table 15-1 of FAR 15.408-2; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-9067.
quote: The offeror shall prepare and submit certified cost or pricing data, data other than certified cost or pricing data, and supporting attachments in accordance with the instructions contained in Table 15-1 of FAR 15.408-2,
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The codified paragraph cites Table 15-2 of FAR 15.408 and the RFO paragraph cites Table 15-1 of FAR 15.408-2. The words that incorporate the table by reference are quoted in CL-EST-9067.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.215-20(b)(1) says the instructions in Table 15-1 are incorporated as a mandatory format to be used in the contract, unless the Contracting Officer and the Contractor agree to a different format and change the clause to use Alternate I.
quote: The instructions in Table 15-1 are incorporated as a mandatory format to be used in this contract, unless the Contracting Officer and the Contractor agree to a different format and change this clause to use Alternate I.
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The codified paragraph names Table 15-2 and the RFO paragraph names Table 15-1. The mandatory-format rule and the Alternate I exception are otherwise the same.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.215-20(b)(2) says that, as soon as practicable after agreement on price, but before contract award (except for unpriced actions such as letter contracts), the offeror shall submit a Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data, as prescribed by FAR 15.403-4.
quote: (2) As soon as practicable after agreement on price, but before contract award (except for unpriced actions such as letter contracts), the offeror shall submit a Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data, as prescribed by FAR 15.403-4.
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The timing and the exception for unpriced actions are the same as in the codified paragraph. The codified paragraph cites FAR 15.406-2 for the certificate and the RFO paragraph cites FAR 15.403-4.

statement: The RFO text of Alternate II to FAR 52.215-20 says, as prescribed in 15.110(t)(2), to add a paragraph (c) to the provision requiring that, when the proposal is submitted, the offeror also submit one copy each to the Administrative Contracting Officer and the Contract Auditor.
quote: Alternate II (Oct 1997). As prescribed in 15.110(t)(2), add the following paragraph (c) to the provision: (c) When the proposal is submitted, also submit one copy each to: (1) the Administrative Contracting Officer, and (2) the Contract Auditor.
note: The RFO clause prints the edition date (Oct 1997), recorded as edition_date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The added paragraph (c) reads the same as the codified Alternate II paragraph. The RFO Alternate II is prescribed in FAR 15.110(t)(2), where the codified Alternate II is prescribed in FAR 15.408(l), and it adds the paragraph to the provision where the codified text says the basic provision.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.215-21(a)(1) says that, for modifications under the contract with price adjustments expected to exceed the threshold set forth in FAR 15.403-3(a) on the date of the agreement on price or the date of the award, whichever is later, the Contractor may submit a written request for exception.
quote: for modifications under this contract, for price adjustments expected to exceed the threshold set forth in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.403-3(a) on the date of the agreement on price or the date of the award, whichever is later, the Contractor may submit a written request for exception
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The codified clause refers to the threshold in FAR 15.403-4(a)(1) and the RFO clause refers to it in FAR 15.403-3(a). The sentence continues with the information described in paragraphs (a)(1)(i) and (ii) of the clause, which reads the same in both texts. The timing and the written request for exception are otherwise the same.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.215-21(a)(1) says that if the threshold for submission of certified cost or pricing data specified in FAR 15.403-3(a) is adjusted for inflation as set forth in FAR part 1, the changed threshold applies throughout the remaining term of the contract, unless there is a subsequent threshold adjustment.
quote: If the threshold for submission of certified cost or pricing data specified in FAR 15.403-3(a) is adjusted for inflation as set forth in FAR part 1, the changed threshold applies throughout the remaining term of the contract, unless there is a subsequent threshold adjustment.
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The codified clause cites FAR 15.403-4(a)(1), FAR 1.109(a) and FAR 1.109(d). The RFO clause cites FAR 15.403-3(a) and FAR part 1. The rule that the changed threshold applies through the remaining term is otherwise the same.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.215-21(a)(2) says the Contractor grants the Contracting Officer or an authorized representative the right to examine, at any time before award, books, records, documents, or other directly pertinent records to verify any request for an exception under the clause, and the reasonableness of price.
quote: (2) The Contractor grants the Contracting Officer or an authorized representative the right to examine, at any time before award, books, records, documents, or other directly pertinent records to verify any request for an exception under this clause, and the reasonableness of price.
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.215-21(a)(2) says that, for items priced using catalog or market prices, or law or regulation, access does not extend to cost or profit information or other data relevant solely to the Contractor's determination of the prices to be offered in the catalog or marketplace.
quote: For items priced using catalog or market prices, or law or regulation, access does not extend to cost or profit information or other data relevant solely to the Contractor’s determination of the prices to be offered in the catalog or marketplace.
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.212-2(a) says the Government will award a contract resulting from the solicitation to the responsible Offeror whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered.
quote: (a) Evaluation factors. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible Offeror whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered.
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The wording is the same as the codified paragraph, apart from the added heading and the capital letter on Offeror.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.212-2(a) says the following factors will be used to evaluate offers and tells the contracting officer to insert the evaluation factors in the relative order of importance.
quote: The following factors will be used to evaluate offers: [Insert evaluation factors in the relative order of importance.
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The codified paragraph says the factors shall be used and gives examples of factors to insert. The RFO paragraph says the factors will be used and gives no examples.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.212-2(a) says that for requests for proposals the contracting officer states that evaluation factors other than price when combined are significantly more important than price, approximately equal to price, or significantly less important than price.
quote: For requests for proposals, state: Evaluation factors other than price when combined are [significantly more important than price/approximately equal to price/significantly less important] than price.
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The codified paragraph asks for the relative importance of technical and past performance combined compared to price, with a second instruction on all other factors. The RFO paragraph compares all evaluation factors other than price, combined, with price and offers three choices.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.212-2(b) says the Government will evaluate offers for award purposes by adding the total price for all options to the total price for the basic requirement, and may determine that an offer is unacceptable if the option prices are significantly unbalanced.
quote: (b) Options (if applicable). The Government will evaluate offers for award purposes by adding the total price for all options to the total price for the basic requirement. The Government may determine that an offer is unacceptable if the option prices are significantly unbalanced.
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The wording is the same as the codified paragraph, apart from the added words (if applicable) in the heading.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.212-2(b) says the evaluation of options does not obligate the Government to exercise the option(s).
quote: The evaluation of options does not obligate the Government to exercise the option(s).
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The codified paragraph says evaluation of options shall not obligate the Government. The meaning is the same.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.212-2(c) says a written notice of award or acceptance of an offer furnished to the successful Offeror within the time for acceptance specified in the offer shall result in a binding contract without further action by either party.
quote: (c) Notice of award. A written notice of award or acceptance of an offer furnished to the successful Offeror within the time for acceptance specified in the offer, shall result in a binding contract without further action by either party.
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The codified paragraph says the notice is mailed or otherwise furnished to the successful offeror. The RFO paragraph says only that it is furnished.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.212-2(c) says that, before the offer's specified expiration time, the Government may accept an offer (or part of an offer), whether or not there are negotiations after its receipt, unless a written notice of withdrawal is received before award.
quote: Before the offer’s specified expiration time, the Government may accept an offer (or part of an offer), whether or not there are negotiations after its receipt, unless a written notice of withdrawal is received before award.
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.212-2 says that, as prescribed in 12.205(a)(2), the contracting officer is to insert a provision substantially as follows.
quote: As prescribed in 12.205(a)(2), insert a provision substantially as follows:
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The codified prescription cites FAR 12.301(c) and says the contracting officer may insert a provision substantially as follows. The RFO prescription cites FAR 12.205(a)(2) and says to insert it.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.212-1 says that, as prescribed in 12.205(a)(1), the contracting officer is to insert a clause substantially as follows.
quote: As prescribed in 12.205(a)(1), insert a clause substantially as follows:
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The codified prescription cites FAR 12.301(b)(1) and says to insert the following provision. The RFO prescription cites FAR 12.205(a)(1) and says to insert a clause substantially as follows.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.212-1(a) says offers are submitted signed and dated to the office specified in the solicitation at or before the exact time specified in the solicitation, and that as a minimum offers shall include the items listed; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-0099.
quote: (a) Submission of offers. Submit signed and dated offers to the office specified in this solicitation at or before the exact time specified in this solicitation. As a minimum, offers shall include—
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). Codified paragraph (b) becomes RFO paragraph (a). The RFO paragraph does not repeat the codified sentence on the SF 1449 and letterhead stationery. The submission rule and the words as a minimum are otherwise the same.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.212-1(a)(1) to (3) lists as minimum contents of an offer the solicitation number, the name, address and telephone number of the Offeror, and the Offeror's Unique Entity Identifier and, if applicable, Electronic Funds Transfer indicator.
quote: (1) The solicitation number; (2) The name, address, telephone number of the Offeror; (3) The Offeror’s Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and, if applicable, Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) indicator;
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The codified list also has an item for the time specified for receipt of offers, and the unique entity identifier is in a separate codified paragraph (j). The RFO list has the unique entity identifier as item (3).

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.212-1(a)(4) lists as a minimum content of an offer the information necessary to evaluate the factors contained in the provision at 52.212-2 or as described in the solicitation.
quote: (4) Information necessary to evaluate the factors contained in the provision at 52.212-2 or as described in the solicitation;
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The codified list has separate items for a technical description of the items offered, express warranty terms, price and discount terms, a remit-to address, the FAR 52.212-3 representations and certifications, acknowledgment of amendments and past performance information. The RFO item (4) uses different wording.

statement: Before agreement on price, a contracting officer who learns that certified cost or pricing data are inaccurate, incomplete or noncurrent must immediately bring the matter to the prospective contractor's attention, whether the defective data increase or decrease the price.
quote: the contracting officer shall immediately bring the matter to the attention of the prospective contractor, whether the defective data increase or decrease the contract price

statement: After award, if certified cost or pricing data are found inaccurate, incomplete or noncurrent as of the date of final agreement on price or an earlier date agreed by the parties on the Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data, the Government is entitled to a price adjustment, including profit or fee, of any significant amount by which the price was increased because of the defective data.
quote: the Government is entitled to a price adjustment, including profit or fee, of any significant amount by which the price was increased because of the defective data

statement: Subject to the conditions in (b)(5) and (b)(6), the contracting officer allows an offset for understated certified cost or pricing data submitted in support of price negotiations, up to the amount of the Government's claim for overstated data arising out of the same pricing action.
quote: the contracting officer shall allow an offset for any understated certified cost or pricing data submitted in support of price negotiations, up to the amount of the Government's claim for overstated pricing data

statement: The Government's right to a price adjustment is not affected by the contractor or subcontractor having been a sole source supplier or otherwise being in a superior bargaining position.
quote: The contractor or subcontractor was a sole source supplier or otherwise was in a superior bargaining position

statement: An overpayment for defective pricing purposes occurs only when payment is made for supplies or services accepted by the Government, and amounts paid as contract financing do not create an overpayment.
quote: Overpayment occurs only when payment is made for supplies or services accepted by the Government. Overpayments do not result from amounts paid for contract financing

statement: Where the submission of defective certified cost or pricing data was a knowing submission, the contracting officer obtains a penalty equal to the amount of the overpayment, and must obtain the advice of counsel before taking contractual action concerning penalties.
quote: the contracting officer shall obtain an amount equal to the amount of overpayment made. Before taking any contractual actions concerning penalties, the contracting officer shall obtain the advice of counsel

statement: The contracting officer may not reprice a contract solely because the profit was greater than forecast or because a contingency specified in the submission failed to materialize.
quote: The contracting officer shall not reprice the contract solely because the profit was greater than forecast or because a contingency specified in the submission failed to materialize.

statement: For each advisory audit received based on a postaward review that indicates defective pricing, the contracting officer determines whether the data submitted were defective and relied upon, and should first give the contractor an opportunity to support the accuracy, completeness and currency of the data.
quote: the contracting officer shall make a determination as to whether or not the data submitted were defective and relied upon

statement: When a prime contractor priced its proposal with defective subcontract data but later awards the subcontract at a lower price or does not subcontract the work, the prime contract price adjustment is limited to the difference, plus applicable indirect cost and profit markups, between the subcontract price used for pricing the prime contract and the amount stated in the next claim; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-0245.
quote: any adjustment in the prime contract price due to defective subcontract data is limited to the difference (plus applicable indirect cost and profit markups) between the subcontract price used for pricing the prime contract

statement: The objective of proposal analysis is to ensure that the final agreed-to price is fair and reasonable.
quote: The objective of proposal analysis is to ensure that the final agreed-to price is fair and reasonable.

statement: Price analysis is used when certified cost or pricing data are not required.
quote: Price analysis shall be used when certified cost or pricing data are not required

statement: Cost analysis is used to evaluate the reasonableness of individual cost elements when certified cost or pricing data are required.
quote: Cost analysis shall be used to evaluate the reasonableness of individual cost elements when certified cost or pricing data are required.

statement: Cost analysis may also be used on data other than certified cost or pricing data to determine cost reasonableness or cost realism when a fair and reasonable price cannot be determined through price analysis alone.
quote: Cost analysis may also be used to evaluate data other than certified cost or pricing data to determine cost reasonableness or cost realism when a fair and reasonable price cannot be determined through price analysis alone.

statement: Under FAR 15.404-1(b)(3), if information on competitive proposed prices or previous contract prices is not available or is insufficient to determine that the price is fair and reasonable, the contracting officer may use any of the remaining techniques as appropriate to the circumstances applicable to the acquisition; the sentence begins in CL-EST-9542, which carries the contracting officer's determination.
quote: information on competitive proposed prices or previous contract prices is not available or is insufficient to determine that the price is fair and reasonable, the contracting officer may use any of the remaining techniques as appropriate to the circumstances applicable to the acquisition.

statement: Cost realism analyses are performed on cost-reimbursement contracts to determine the probable cost of performance for each offeror.
quote: Cost realism analyses shall be performed on cost-reimbursement contracts to determine the probable cost of performance for each offeror.

statement: The probable cost produced by cost realism analysis is used for purposes of evaluation to determine the best value.
quote: The probable cost shall be used for purposes of evaluation to determine the best value.

statement: Where cost realism analysis is used on competitive fixed-price incentive contracts or on other competitive fixed-price-type contracts, the proposals are still evaluated using the criteria in the solicitation and the offered prices are not adjusted as a result of the analysis.
quote: proposals shall be evaluated using the criteria in the solicitation, and the offered prices shall not be adjusted as a result of the analysis

statement: Recommendations or conclusions about the Government's review of a proposal are not disclosed to the offeror or contractor without the concurrence of the contracting officer.
quote: Recommendations or conclusions regarding the Government's review or analysis of an offeror's or contractor's proposal shall not be disclosed to the offeror or contractor without the concurrence of the contracting officer

statement: Normally, adequate price competition establishes a fair and reasonable price.
quote: Normally, adequate price competition establishes a fair and reasonable price

statement: An offer may be rejected if the contracting officer determines that the lack of price balance poses an unacceptable risk to the Government.
quote: An offer may be rejected if the contracting officer determines that the lack of balance poses an unacceptable risk to the Government.

statement: An acceptable estimating system must produce verifiable, supportable, documented and timely cost estimates that are an acceptable basis for negotiation of fair and reasonable prices, in addition to being maintained, reliable and consistently applied.
quote: (1) Is maintained, reliable, and consistently applied; (2) Produces verifiable, supportable, documented, and timely cost estimates that are an acceptable basis for negotiation of fair and reasonable prices

statement: An estimating system is the contractor's policies, procedures and practices for budgeting and planning controls and for generating estimates of costs and other data included in proposals submitted in the expectation of receiving contract awards.
quote: the Contractor's policies, procedures, and practices for budgeting and planning controls, and generating estimates of costs and other data included in proposals submitted to customers in the expectation of receiving contract awards.

statement: The contractor must establish, maintain and comply with an acceptable estimating system.
quote: The Contractor shall establish, maintain, and comply with an acceptable estimating system.

statement: One condition under which paragraphs (d) and (e) apply to a large business is that, in its fiscal year preceding award, it received Department of Defense prime contracts or subcontracts totaling $50 million or more for which certified cost or pricing data were required.
quote: In its fiscal year preceding award of this contract, received Department of Defense (DoD) prime contracts or subcontracts, totaling $50 million or more for which certified cost or pricing data were required

statement: The second of the two conditions in DFARS 252.215-7002(c)(2), which must both be met in the contractor's fiscal year preceding award of the contract (CL-EST-9437), is that the contracting officer notified the contractor in writing that paragraphs (d) and (e) of the clause apply (the first condition, a contract volume band, is in CL-EST-9436).
quote: Was notified, in writing, by the Contracting Officer that paragraphs (d) and (e) of this clause apply

statement: The contractor discloses its estimating system to the administrative contracting officer in writing.
quote: The Contractor shall disclose its estimating system to the Administrative Contracting Officer (ACO), in writing

statement: One requirement for an acceptable estimating system disclosure is that the documentation accurately describes the policies, procedures and practices the contractor currently uses in preparing cost proposals; the second requirement is in CL-EST-9442.
quote: Accurately describes those policies, procedures, and practices that the Contractor currently uses in preparing cost proposals

statement: The contractor must disclose significant changes to its cost estimating system to the administrative contracting officer on a timely basis.
quote: Disclose significant changes to the cost estimating system to the ACO on a timely basis

statement: An acceptable estimating system establishes clear responsibility for preparation, review and approval of cost estimates and budgets.
quote: Establish clear responsibility for preparation, review, and approval of cost estimates and budgets

statement: The system must identify and document the sources of data and the estimating methods and rationale used in developing cost estimates and budgets.
quote: Identify and document the sources of data and the estimating methods and rationale used in developing cost estimates and budgets

statement: The system must provide for internal review of, and accountability for, the acceptability of the estimating system, including the budgetary data supporting indirect cost estimates and comparisons of projected results to actual results.
quote: Provide for internal review of, and accountability for, the acceptability of the estimating system, including the budgetary data supporting indirect cost estimates and comparisons of projected results to actual results

statement: The contractor must respond within 30 days to a written initial determination from the contracting officer that identifies material weaknesses in its estimating system.
quote: The Contractor shall respond within 30 days to a written initial determination from the Contracting Officer that identifies material weaknesses in the Contractor's estimating system.

statement: After a final determination of material weaknesses, the contractor must within 45 days of receipt either correct the weaknesses or submit an acceptable corrective action plan showing milestones and actions to eliminate them.
quote: within 45 days of receipt of the final determination, either correct the material weaknesses or submit an acceptable corrective action plan showing milestones and actions to eliminate the material weaknesses

statement: If the contracting officer makes a final determination to disapprove the contractor's estimating system and the contract includes the Contractor Business Systems clause, the contracting officer withholds payments in accordance with that clause.
quote: the Contracting Officer will withhold payments in accordance with that clause

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.212-1(a)(5) lists as a minimum content of an offer responses to provisions that require Offeror completion of information, representations, and certifications, other than those collected via the System for Award Management.
quote: (5) Responses to provisions that require Offeror completion of information, representations, and certifications (other than those collected via the System for Award Management (SAM));
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The codified item (8) calls for a completed copy of the representations and certifications at FAR 52.212-3. The RFO item (5) refers to provisions that require Offeror completion and excludes information collected via the System for Award Management.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.212-1(a)(6) says offers shall include a statement specifying the extent of agreement with all terms, conditions, and provisions included in the solicitation and any solicitation amendments.
quote: (6) A statement specifying the extent of agreement with all terms, conditions, and provisions included in the solicitation and any solicitation amendments.
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The codified item (11) requires the statement only if the offer is not submitted on the SF 1449. The RFO item (6) has no such condition and adds any solicitation amendments.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.212-1(b) says the Offeror agrees to hold the prices in its offer firm for 60 calendar days from the date specified for receipt of offers, unless another time period is specified in an addendum to the solicitation.
quote: (b) Period for acceptance of offers. The Offeror agrees to hold the prices in its offer firm for 60 calendar days from the date specified for receipt of offers, unless another time period is specified in an addendum to the solicitation.
note: The RFO title prints "(Deviation Date)" rather than a date, so edition_date is blank; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). note: The RFO clause prints the edition date (Jun 2003), recorded as edition_date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: The RFO text of FAR 52.215-16(b) says that if the prospective Contractor does not propose this cost, the resulting contract will include the clause Waiver of Facilities Capital Cost of Money.
quote: (b) If the prospective Contractor does not propose this cost, the resulting contract will include the clause Waiver of Facilities Capital Cost of Money.
note: The RFO clause prints the edition date (Jun 2003), recorded as edition_date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: A contracting officer should request field pricing assistance when the information available at the buying activity is inadequate to determine a fair and reasonable price.
quote: The contracting officer should request field pricing assistance when the information available at the buying activity is inadequate to determine a fair and reasonable price.

statement: A field pricing request must be tailored to reflect the minimum essential supplementary information needed to conduct a technical or cost or pricing analysis.
quote: The contracting officer shall tailor requests to reflect the minimum essential supplementary information needed to conduct a technical or cost or pricing analysis.

statement: The type of information and level of detail requested must be tailored in accordance with the specialized resources available at the buying activity and the magnitude and complexity of the required analysis.
quote: The contracting officer shall tailor the type of information and level of detail requested in accordance with the specialized resources available at the buying activity and the magnitude and complexity of the required analysis.

statement: Field pricing assistance is generally available to provide technical, audit, and special reports associated with the cost elements of a proposal, including subcontracts.
quote: Field pricing assistance is generally available to provide— (i) Technical, audit, and special reports associated with the cost elements of a proposal, including subcontracts;

statement: Field pricing information and other reports may include proprietary or source selection information, which must be appropriately identified and protected.
quote: Field pricing information and other reports may include proprietary or source selection information (see 2.101). This information must be appropriately identified and protected accordingly.

statement: Audit and field pricing information, whether written or reported telephonically or electronically, must be made a part of the official contract file.
quote: Audit and field pricing information, whether written or reported telephonically or electronically, shall be made a part of the official contract file

statement: The auditor must not reveal audit conclusions or recommendations to the offeror or contractor without obtaining the contracting officer's concurrence, but the auditor may discuss statements of facts with the contractor.
quote: The auditor shall not reveal the audit conclusions or recommendations to the offeror/contractor without obtaining the concurrence of the contracting officer. However, the auditor may discuss statements of facts with the contractor.

statement: The contracting officer must not request a separate preaward audit of indirect costs unless the information already available from an existing audit, completed within the preceding 12 months, is considered inadequate for determining the reasonableness of the proposed indirect costs.
quote: The contracting officer shall not request a separate preaward audit of indirect costs unless the information already available from an existing audit, completed within the preceding 12 months, is considered inadequate for determining the reasonableness of the proposed indirect costs

statement: The administrative contracting officer or the auditor, as appropriate, must notify the contracting officer immediately if the data provided for review is so deficient as to preclude review or audit.
quote: The ACO or the auditor, as appropriate, shall notify the contracting officer immediately if the data provided for review is so deficient as to preclude review or audit

statement: If the offeror or contractor again refuses to provide adequate data or access to necessary data, the contracting officer shall withhold the award or price adjustment and refer the contract action to a higher authority.
quote: Should the offeror/contractor again refuse to provide adequate data, or provide access to necessary data, the contracting officer shall withhold the award or price adjustment and refer the contract action to a higher authority

statement: When field pricing assistance is requested, contracting officers are encouraged to team with appropriate field experts throughout the acquisition process, including negotiations.
quote: When field pricing assistance is requested, contracting officers are encouraged to team with appropriate field experts throughout the acquisition process, including negotiations

statement: Identifying general market conditions affecting determinations of commerciality and a fair and reasonable price is one item in the list of information that helps contracting officers make those determinations, in the list of what field pricing assistance can provide under FAR 15.404-2(a)(2)(iii).
quote: Identifying general market conditions affecting determinations of commerciality and a fair and reasonable price

statement: The contracting officer is responsible for the determination of a fair and reasonable price for the prime contract, including subcontracting costs.
quote: The contracting officer is responsible for the determination of a fair and reasonable price for the prime contract, including subcontracting costs.

statement: The contracting officer should consider whether a contractor or subcontractor has an approved purchasing system, has performed cost or price analysis of proposed subcontractor prices, or has negotiated the subcontract prices before negotiation of the prime contract; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-0440.
quote: The contracting officer should consider whether a contractor or subcontractor has an approved purchasing system, has performed cost or price analysis of proposed subcontractor prices, or has negotiated the subcontract prices before negotiation of the prime contract

statement: Those considerations do not relieve the contracting officer from the responsibility to analyze the contractor's submission, including subcontractor's certified cost or pricing data.
quote: This does not relieve the contracting officer from the responsibility to analyze the contractor's submission, including subcontractor's certified cost or pricing data.

statement: The prime contractor or a subcontractor shall conduct appropriate cost or price analyses to establish the reasonableness of proposed subcontract prices.
quote: The prime contractor or subcontractor shall— (1) Conduct appropriate cost or price analyses to establish the reasonableness of proposed subcontract prices;

statement: The results of those analyses must be included in the price proposal.
quote: The prime contractor or subcontractor shall— (1) Conduct appropriate cost or price analyses to establish the reasonableness of proposed subcontract prices; (2) Include the results of these analyses in the price proposal;

statement: A contractor or subcontractor that is required to submit certified cost or pricing data must also obtain and analyze certified cost or pricing data before awarding any subcontract, purchase order, or modification expected to exceed the certified cost or pricing data threshold; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-0441.
quote: Any contractor or subcontractor that is required to submit certified cost or pricing data also shall obtain and analyze certified cost or pricing data before awarding any subcontract, purchase order, or modification expected to exceed the certified cost or pricing data threshold

statement: The subcontracts for which certified cost or pricing data is to be submitted to the Government are those that are the lower of either $20 million or more, or both more than the pertinent certified cost or pricing data threshold and more than 10 percent of the prime contractor's proposed price, unless the contracting officer believes such submission is unnecessary.
quote: the lower of either— (i) $20 million or more; or (ii) Both more than the pertinent certified cost or pricing data threshold and more than 10 percent of the prime contractor's proposed price, unless the contracting officer believes such submission is unnecessary.

statement: The contracting officer should require the contractor or subcontractor to submit to the Government, or cause the submission of, subcontractor certified cost or pricing data below the thresholds in paragraph (c)(1); the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-0443.
quote: The contracting officer should require the contractor or subcontractor to submit to the Government (or cause submission of) subcontractor certified cost or pricing data below the thresholds in paragraph (c)(1) of this subsection

statement: Subcontractor certified cost or pricing data shall be current, accurate, and complete as of the date of price agreement or, if applicable, an earlier date agreed upon by the parties and specified on the contractor's Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data.
quote: Subcontractor certified cost or pricing data shall be current, accurate, and complete as of the date of price agreement, or, if applicable, an earlier date agreed upon by the parties and specified on the contractor's Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data

statement: If there is more than one prospective subcontractor for any given work, the contractor need only submit certified cost or pricing data for the prospective subcontractor most likely to receive the award.
quote: If there is more than one prospective subcontractor for any given work, the contractor need only submit to the Government certified cost or pricing data for the prospective subcontractor most likely to receive the award.

statement: Should-cost reviews differ from traditional evaluation methods because they do not assume that a contractor's historical costs reflect efficient and economical operation.
quote: Should-cost reviews differ from traditional evaluation methods because they do not assume that a contractor's historical costs reflect efficient and economical operation.

statement: Should-cost reviews evaluate the economy and efficiency of the contractor's existing work force, methods, materials, equipment, real property, operating systems, and management.
quote: these reviews evaluate the economy and efficiency of the contractor's existing work force, methods, materials, equipment, real property, operating systems, and management

statement: These reviews are accomplished by a multi-functional team of Government contracting, contract administration, pricing, audit, and engineering representatives.
quote: These reviews are accomplished by a multi-functional team of Government contracting, contract administration, pricing, audit, and engineering representatives.

statement: There are two types of should-cost reviews, program should-cost review and overhead should-cost review, and these reviews may be performed together or independently.
quote: There are two types of should-cost reviews—program should-cost review (see paragraph (b) of this subsection) and overhead should-cost review (see paragraph (c) of this subsection). These should-cost reviews may be performed together or independently.

statement: When a program should-cost review is conducted relative to a contractor proposal, a separate audit report on the proposal is required.
quote: When a program should-cost review is conducted relative to a contractor proposal, a separate audit report on the proposal is required.

statement: An overhead should-cost review is used to evaluate indirect costs such as fringe benefits, shipping and receiving, real property and equipment, depreciation, plant maintenance and security, taxes, and general and administrative activities.
quote: An overhead should-cost review is used to evaluate indirect costs, such as fringe benefits, shipping and receiving, real property, and equipment, depreciation, plant maintenance and security, taxes, and general and administrative activities.

statement: An overhead should-cost review is normally used to evaluate and negotiate an FPRA with the contractor, and when such a review is conducted a separate audit report is required.
quote: It is normally used to evaluate and negotiate an FPRA with the contractor. When an overhead should-cost review is conducted, a separate audit report is required.

statement: After completing the negotiation, the contracting officer shall provide the administrative contracting officer a report of any identified uneconomical or inefficient practices, together with a report of correction or disposition agreements reached with the contractor.
quote: After completing the negotiation, the contracting officer shall provide the ACO a report of any identified uneconomical or inefficient practices, together with a report of correction or disposition agreements reached with the contractor.

statement: The contracting officer shall establish a follow-up plan to monitor the correction of the uneconomical or inefficient practices.
quote: The contracting officer shall establish a follow-up plan to monitor the correction of the uneconomical or inefficient practices.

statement: When a program should-cost review is planned, the contracting officer should state this fact in the acquisition plan or acquisition plan updates and in the solicitation.
quote: When a program should-cost review is planned, the contracting officer should state this fact in the acquisition plan or acquisition plan updates (see subpart 7.1) and in the solicitation.

statement: In lieu of submitting certified cost or pricing data, the offeror may submit a written request for exception by submitting the information described in the provision's exception paragraphs.
quote: In lieu of submitting certified cost or pricing data, the Offeror may submit a written request for exception by submitting the information described in paragraphs (b)(1)(i) and (ii) of this provision.

statement: The contracting officer may require additional supporting information, but only to the extent necessary to determine whether an exception should be granted and whether the price is fair and reasonable.
quote: The Contracting Officer may require additional supporting information, but only to the extent necessary to determine whether an exception should be granted and whether the price is fair and reasonable.

statement: Under paragraph (c)(1) of the basic provision, the offeror shall prepare and submit certified cost or pricing data and supporting attachments in accordance with the instructions contained in Table 15-2 of FAR 15.408.
quote: The Offeror shall prepare and submit certified cost or pricing data and supporting attachments in accordance with the instructions contained in Table 15-2 of FAR 15.408

statement: Under paragraph (c)(2) of the basic provision, as soon as practicable after agreement on price, but before contract award, except for unpriced actions such as letter contracts, the offeror shall submit a Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data.
quote: As soon as practicable after agreement on price, but before contract award (except for unpriced actions such as letter contracts), the Offeror shall submit a Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data

statement: The offeror is responsible for determining whether a subcontractor qualifies for an exception from the requirement for submission of certified cost or pricing data on the basis of adequate price competition.
quote: The Offeror is responsible for determining whether a subcontractor qualifies for an exception from the requirement for submission of certified cost or pricing data on the basis of adequate price competition

statement: Adequate price competition for that purpose means two or more responsible offerors, competing independently, submit priced offers that satisfy the Government's expressed requirement.
quote: i.e., two or more responsible offerors, competing independently, submit priced offers that satisfy the Government's expressed requirement

statement: Under the basic provision, data other than certified cost or pricing data submitted in accordance with the provision shall include the minimum information necessary to permit a determination that the proposed price is fair and reasonable.
quote: Data other than certified cost or pricing data submitted in accordance with this provision shall include the minimum information necessary to permit a determination that the proposed price is fair and reasonable

statement: Where uncertified cost data is required, the information shall be provided in the form in which it is regularly maintained by the offeror or prospective subcontractor in its business operations.
quote: In cases in which uncertified cost data is required, the information shall be provided in the form in which it is regularly maintained by the Offeror or prospective subcontractor in its business operations.

statement: Under the basic provision, a written request from the contracting officer for additional information starts a 10-day period for the offeror's response; what the response must contain is stated in the next claim.
quote: Within 10 days of a written request from the Contracting Officer for additional information

statement: No cost data may be required from a prospective subcontractor in any case in which there are sufficient non-Government sales of the same item to establish reasonableness of price.
quote: No cost data may be required from a prospective subcontractor in any case in which there are sufficient non-Government sales of the same item to establish reasonableness of price.

statement: The offeror shall insert the substance of the provision, including this paragraph (e), in subcontracts exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold defined in FAR part 2.
quote: The Offeror shall insert the substance of this provision, including this paragraph (e), in subcontracts exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold defined in FAR part 2.

statement: For a commercial product or commercial service exception, the offeror shall submit at a minimum information that is adequate for determining commerciality and evaluating the reasonableness of the price for the acquisition.
quote: For a commercial product or commercial service exception, the Offeror shall submit, at a minimum, information that is adequate for determining commerciality and evaluating the reasonableness of the price for this acquisition

statement: The comparison is with either the actual subcontract price or the actual cost to the contractor, if not subcontracted, provided the data on which the actual subcontract price is based are not themselves defective.
quote: , and either the actual subcontract price or the actual cost to the contractor, if not subcontracted, provided the data on which the actual subcontract price is based are not themselves defective.

statement: If the contractor wishes the Government to protect the data and information as privileged or confidential, it must mark the documents with the appropriate legends before submission.
quote: If the Contractor wishes the Government to protect the data and information as privileged or confidential, the Contractor must mark the documents with the appropriate legends before submission.

statement: A further condition is that award will be made to the offeror whose proposal represents the best value where price is a substantial factor in source selection, and a further condition is that there is no finding that the price of the otherwise successful offeror is unreasonable.
quote: (B) Award will be made to the offeror whose proposal represents the best value (see 2.101) where price is a substantial factor in source selection; and (C) There is no finding that the price of the otherwise successful offeror is unreasonable.

quote: The Contractor did not include facilities capital cost of money as a proposed cost of this contract. Therefore, it is an unallowable cost under this contract.

statement: Those agencies may prescribe specific exemptions for situations in which mandatory use of a structured approach would be clearly inappropriate.
quote: (ii) May prescribe specific exemptions for situations in which mandatory use of a structured approach would be clearly inappropriate.

quote: (2) A subcontractor or prospective subcontractor furnished the Contractor certified cost or pricing data that were not complete, accurate, and current as certified in the Contractor's Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data;

statement: The limit is the amount by which the actual subcontract, or the actual cost to the Contractor if there was no subcontract, was less than the prospective subcontract cost estimate submitted by the Contractor.

quote: provided, that the actual subcontract price was not itself affected by defective certified cost or pricing data.

quote: (i) The Contractor or subcontractor was a sole source supplier or otherwise was in a superior bargaining position and thus the price of the contract would not have been modified even if accurate, complete, and current certified cost or pricing data had been submitted.

quote: (ii) The Contracting Officer should have known that the certified cost or pricing data in issue were defective even though the Contractor or subcontractor took no affirmative action to bring the character of the data to the attention of the Contracting Officer.

quote: (iii) The contract was based on an agreement about the total cost of the contract and there was no agreement about the cost of each item procured under the contract. (iv) The Contractor or subcontractor did not submit a Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data.

statement: Under the basic provision, the response to such a request is the requested information, or a written explanation for the inability to fully comply, so that the proposed price can be adequately evaluated in accordance with FAR 15.403-3 or DFARS 234.7002(e).

statement: Auditors collaborate with and advise procurement teams, but are prohibited from acting as formal members of integrated product teams or participating in procurement decision-making.

statement: In the manual's service table, an audit of a complete proposal is an examination of the full proposal against acquisition regulations, cost principles and CAS where applicable, and its output is an audit report expressing an opinion or a disclaimer of opinion.

statement: The manual says a proposal is inadequate when the contractor fails to submit required supporting data, or when cost data is insufficient to perform the planned audit procedures.

statement: On receiving a proposal, the auditor assesses its adequacy using the standard Proposal Adequacy Checklist in DFARS, and notifies the contracting officer in writing immediately if significant inadequacies are identified.

statement: If a contractor refuses to provide required certified cost data or denies access to its books and records, the auditor notifies the contracting officer immediately to obtain their support, and follows the Agency's process for denial of access to records if necessary.

statement: The audit team should discuss potential deficiencies or noncompliances with the contractor so they can be corrected, and consider them when planning audit procedures.

quote: Negotiations are exchanges, in either a competitive or sole source environment, between the Government and offerors, that are undertaken with the intent of allowing the offeror to revise its proposal.

statement: Discussions are tailored to each offeror's proposal and must be conducted by the contracting officer with each offeror within the competitive range.
quote: (1) Discussions are tailored to each offeror's proposal, and must be conducted by the contracting officer with each offeror within the competitive range.

statement: FAR 52.216-5 is a clause on prospective price redetermination that is inserted in contracts as prescribed in FAR 16.205-4.
quote: 52.216-5 Price Redetermination—Prospective. As prescribed in 16.205-4, insert the following clause:

statement: Under the clause, prices are periodically redetermined, subject to listed exceptions that include prices for supplies delivered and services performed before the first effective date of price redetermination, which remain fixed; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-1700.
quote: unit prices and the total price stated in this contract shall be periodically redetermined in accordance with this clause, except that (1) the prices for supplies delivered and services performed before the first effective date of price redetermination (see paragraph (c) below) shall remain fixed

statement: The first period runs from the contract date to a stated point and each later period runs for a stated number of months from the end of the last, except that the parties may agree to vary the length of the final period.
quote: The first period shall extend from the date of the contract to __, [see Note (1)] and the second and each succeeding period shall extend for __ [insert appropriate number] months from the end of the last preceding period, except that the parties may agree to vary the length of the final period.

statement: The contractor submits its data within a window set by a stated maximum and a stated minimum number of days before the end of each redetermination period except the last.
quote: Not more than __ nor less than __ [see Note (2)] days before the end of each redetermination period, except the last, the Contractor shall submit—

statement: One listed submission, which the contractor makes within the window before the end of each redetermination period except the last (CL-EST-1653), is proposed prices for supplies that may be delivered or services that may be performed in the next succeeding period, with an estimate and breakdown of their costs in the Table 15-2 format of FAR 15.408 or another form the parties agree.
quote: Proposed prices for supplies that may be delivered or services that may be performed in the next succeeding period, and— (A) An estimate and breakdown of the costs of these supplies or services in the format of Table 15-2, FAR 15.408, or in any other form on which the parties may agree;

statement: Two further listed items that accompany the cost estimate are sufficient data to support its accuracy and reliability and an explanation of its differences from the original or last preceding estimate.
quote: (B) Sufficient data to support the accuracy and reliability of this estimate; and (C) An explanation of the differences between this estimate and the original (or last preceding) estimate for the same supplies or services; and

statement: One listed submission is a statement of all costs incurred in performing the contract through the end of a stated month before the proposed prices are submitted; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-9148.
quote: A statement of all costs incurred in performing this contract through the end of the ___ month (see Note (3)) before the submission of proposed prices

quote: If the Contractor fails to submit the data required by subparagraphs (1) and (2) above, within the time specified, the Contracting Officer may suspend payments under this contract until the data are furnished.

quote: 52.216-16 Incentive Price Revision—Firm Target. As prescribed in 16.406(a), insert the following clause:

statement: The clause makes the Schedule items it identifies subject to price revision, provided that in no event may their total final price exceed the stated ceiling price.
quote: are subject to price revision in accordance with this clause; provided, that in no event shall the total final price of these items exceed the ceiling price of ___ dollars ($___).

statement: The contractor submits its data within a number of days set by the contracting officer after the end of the month in which it delivered the last unit of supplies and completed the services for the items.
quote: Within __ [Contracting Officer insert number of days] days after the end of the month in which the Contractor has delivered the last unit of supplies and completed the services specified by item number in paragraph (a) of this clause, the Contractor shall submit

statement: Two listed data items are a detailed statement of all costs incurred up to the end of that month and an estimate of costs of further performance, if any, that may be necessary to complete all work under the items.
quote: (i) A detailed statement of all costs incurred up to the end of that month in performing all work under the items; (ii) An estimate of costs of further performance, if any, that may be necessary to complete performance of all work under the items;

statement: The total final price is established by applying to the total final negotiated cost an adjustment for profit or loss, and the adjustment equals the total target profit when total final negotiated cost equals total target cost.
quote: The total final price shall be established by applying to the total final negotiated cost an adjustment for profit or loss, as follows: (i) If the total final negotiated cost is equal to the total target cost, the adjustment is the total target profit.

statement: One listed case is that, when total final negotiated cost is greater than total target cost, the adjustment is the total target profit less a stated percent of the amount of the overrun.
quote: If the total final negotiated cost is greater than the total target cost, the adjustment is the total target profit, less ___ [Contracting Officer insert percent] percent of the amount by which the total final negotiated cost exceeds the total target cost.

statement: One listed case is that, when final negotiated cost is less than total target cost, the adjustment is the total target profit plus a stated percent of the amount of the underrun.
quote: If the final negotiated cost is less than the total target cost, the adjustment is the total target profit plus ___ [Contracting Officer insert percent] percent of the amount by which the total final negotiated cost is less than the total target cost.

statement: Pending the modification that sets the total final price, the contractor invoices at billing prices, and the billing prices are the target prices shown in the contract.
quote: Pending execution of the contract modification (see paragraph (e) above), the Contractor shall submit invoices or vouchers in accordance with billing prices as provided in this paragraph. The billing prices shall be the target prices shown in this contract.

statement: If it appears from the contractor's information that billing prices will be substantially greater than estimated final prices, the parties shall negotiate a reduction in billing prices.
quote: If at any time it appears from information provided by the contractor under subparagraph (g)(2) below that the then-current billing prices will be substantially greater than the estimated final prices, the parties shall negotiate a reduction in the billing prices.

statement: The parties may negotiate an increase in billing prices by any or all of the difference between target prices and the ceiling price, on the contractor's factual data showing that final cost will be substantially greater than target cost.
quote: Similarly, the parties may negotiate an increase in billing prices by any or all of the difference between the target prices and the ceiling price, upon the Contractor's submission of factual data showing that final cost under this contract will be substantially greater than the target cost.

statement: FAR 52.216-17 is a clause on incentive price revision with successive targets that is inserted in contracts as prescribed in FAR 16.406(b).

statement: Upon the contracting officer's receipt of the data (CL-EST-9514), the contracting officer and the contractor shall promptly establish either a firm fixed price or a profit adjustment formula for determining final profit, and the parties shall negotiate a total firm target cost based upon the data submitted under paragraph (c).
quote: the Contracting Officer and the Contractor shall promptly establish either a firm fixed price or a profit adjustment formula for determining final profit, as follows: (1) The parties shall negotiate a total firm target cost, based upon the data submitted under paragraph (c) above.

statement: Total initial target profit is decreased if total firm target cost is more than total initial target cost, and increased if total firm target cost is less.
quote: If the total firm target cost is more than the total initial target cost, the total initial target profit shall be decreased. If the total firm target cost is less than the total initial target cost, the total initial target profit shall be increased.

statement: The total firm target profit may in no event be less than one stated percent or more than another stated percent of the total initial target cost.
quote: provided, that in no event shall the total firm target profit be less than __ percent or more than __ percent [Contracting Officer insert percents] of the total initial target cost.

statement: If total firm target cost plus total firm target profit represent a reasonable price for the part of the contract subject to price revision, the parties may agree on a firm fixed price.
quote: If the total firm target cost plus the total firm target profit represent a reasonable price for performing that part of the contract subject to price revision under this clause, the parties may agree on a firm fixed price

statement: A failure to agree to a firm fixed price is not a dispute under the Disputes clause, and if agreement is not reached or a firm fixed price is inappropriate the parties shall establish a profit adjustment formula.
quote: Failure of the parties to agree to a firm fixed price shall not constitute a dispute under the Disputes clause. If agreement is not reached, or if establishment of a firm fixed price is inappropriate, the Contractor and the Contracting Officer shall establish a profit adjustment formula

statement: One listed case of the profit adjustment formula is that, when total final negotiated cost is greater than total firm target cost, the adjustment is the total firm target profit less a stated percent of the overrun.
quote: If the total final negotiated cost is greater than the total firm target cost, the adjustment is the total firm target profit, less __ percent of the amount by which the total final negotiated cost exceeds the total firm target cost.

statement: One listed case of the profit adjustment formula is that, when total final negotiated cost is less than total firm target cost, the adjustment is the total firm target profit plus a stated percent of the underrun.
quote: If the total final negotiated cost is less than the total firm target cost, the adjustment is the total firm target profit, plus __ percent of the amount by which the total final negotiated cost is less than the total firm target cost.

statement: Under the Order Limitations clause, when the Government requires covered supplies or services in an amount of less than a stated figure, neither the Government nor the contractor is obligated to buy or furnish them under the contract.
quote: (a) Minimum order. When the Government requires supplies or services covered by this contract in an amount of less than ___ [insert dollar figure or quantity], the Government is not obligated to purchase, nor is the Contractor obligated to furnish, those supplies or services under the contract.

statement: Under the Order Limitations clause, the contractor is not obligated to honor an order for a single item, or for a combination of items, in excess of the stated dollar figure or quantity.
quote: (b) Maximum order. The Contractor is not obligated to honor— (1) Any order for a single item in excess of ___ [insert dollar figure or quantity]; (2) Any order for a combination of items in excess of ___ [insert dollar figure or quantity];

statement: The contractor shall honor an order over the maximum order limits unless it is returned to the ordering office within a stated number of days after issuance with written notice of its intent not to ship and the reasons.

statement: Supplies or services are to be furnished when and if ordered up to the Schedule maximum, and the Government shall order at least the Schedule minimum.
quote: when and if ordered, the supplies or services specified in the Schedule up to and including the quantity designated in the Schedule as the maximum. The Government shall order at least the quantity of supplies or services designated in the Schedule as the minimum.

statement: An order issued during the effective period and not completed within that period shall be completed by the contractor within the time specified in the order.
quote: Any order issued during the effective period of this contract and not completed within that period shall be completed by the Contractor within the time specified in the order.

quote: 52.216-29 Time-and-Materials/Labor-Hour Proposal Requirements—Other Than Commercial Acquisition With Adequate Price Competition. As prescribed in 16.601(f)(1), insert the following provision:

statement: The clause's cost-distribution paragraph does not require submission of certified cost or pricing data that is not otherwise required by law or regulation.

note: Both conditions are stated as prerequisites to use, so the claim is written as a permission, not a duty.

statement: A labor-hour contract is a variation of the time-and-materials contract, differing only in that materials are not supplied by the contractor.
quote: A labor-hour contract is a variation of the time-and-materials contract, differing only in that materials are not supplied by the contractor.

statement: The section directs the reader to 12.207(b), 16.601(c) and 16.601(d) for application and limitations, for time-and-materials contracts, that also apply to labor-hour contracts.
quote: See 12.207(b), 16.601(c), and 16.601(d) for application and limitations, for time-and-materials contracts that also apply to labor-hour contracts.
note: The application and limitation rules themselves are printed in the cross-referenced sections, not in this section.

statement: The section directs the reader to 12.207(b) for the use of labor-hour contracts for certain commercial services.
quote: See 12.207(b) for the use of labor-hour contracts for certain commercial services.

statement: A letter contract is a written preliminary contractual instrument that authorizes the contractor to begin immediately manufacturing supplies or performing services.
quote: A letter contract is a written preliminary contractual instrument that authorizes the contractor to begin immediately manufacturing supplies or performing services.
note: The printed section is a description only; the operative limits on letter contracts sit in later sections of the subpart.

statement: In accordance with section 811 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2013 (Pub. L. 112-239), use of any cost-reimbursement line item for the acquisition of production of major defense acquisition programs is prohibited, unless the exception at 234.004(2)(ii) applies.
quote: In accordance with section 811 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2013 (Pub. L. 112-239), use of any cost-reimbursement line item for the acquisition of production of major defense acquisition programs is prohibited, unless the exception at 234.004(2)(ii) applies.
note: The section names no official who decides whether the exception applies and does not set out the exception.

statement: Contracting officers shall follow the principles and procedures in the Director, Defense Procurement and Acquisition Policy memorandum dated April 1, 2016; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-2987.

statement: The memorandum is entitled Guidance on Using Incentive and Other Contract Types; the quoted words complete the sentence begun in CL-EST-2986, which directs contracting officers to follow its principles and procedures when selecting and negotiating the most appropriate contract type for a given procurement.
quote: entitled “Guidance on Using Incentive and Other Contract Types,” when selecting and negotiating the most appropriate contract type for a given procurement.
note: This quote carries the rest of the sentence begun in CL-EST-2986.

statement: The section directs that the procedures at PGI 216.104-70 be followed for selecting the appropriate research and development contract type, and refers to 235.006(b) for additional approval requirements.
quote: Follow the procedures at PGI 216.104-70 for selecting the appropriate research and development contract type, and see 235.006(b) for additional approval requirements.
note: The section is an imperative that names no official, and it does not set out the additional approval requirements.

statement: The clause at 252.216-7004, Award Fee Reduction or Denial for Jeopardizing the Health or Safety of Government Personnel, is to be used in all solicitations and contracts containing award-fee provisions.
quote: Use the clause at 252.216-7004, Award Fee Reduction or Denial for Jeopardizing the Health or Safety of Government Personnel, in all solicitations and contracts containing award-fee provisions.
note: The printed text is paragraph (e) of the section.

statement: In accordance with section 3372 of title 10 of the United States Code, definitization schedules for letter contracts are to be established following the requirements at 217.7404-3(a) instead of the requirements at FAR 16.603-2(c)(3).
quote: In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 3372, establish definitization schedules for letter contracts following the requirements at 217.7404-3(a) instead of the requirements at FAR 16.603-2(c)(3).
note: The DoD rule substitutes for the FAR schedule requirement in the cited paragraph; it does not add to it. The section names no official.

statement: The period during which orders may be placed against a basic ordering agreement may not exceed 5 years.
quote: The period during which orders may be placed against a basic ordering agreement may not exceed 5 years.
note: The limit is on the period for placing orders, not on performance of the orders placed.

statement: The procedures at PGI 216.703(d) are to be followed for issuing orders under basic ordering agreements.
quote: Follow the procedures at PGI 216.703(d) for issuing orders under basic ordering agreements.
note: The section is an imperative that names no official, and it does not set out the procedures.

statement: The terms defined in section 16.501-1 are defined as used in this subpart; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-2977 and CL-EST-2978.
quote: As used in this subpart—
