quote: See PGI 216.104.
note: The section does not set out the content of PGI 216.104.

statement: Employee Stock Ownership Plans that meet the definition of a pension plan are considered a form of deferred compensation and are covered under 9904.415.
quote: Such plans are considered a form of deferred compensation and are covered under 9904.415.

statement: The definitions section defines terms that are prominent in the Standard.
quote: The following are definitions of terms which are prominent in this Standard.

statement: FAR subpart 17.1 implements title 41 of the United States Code, section 3903, and title 10, section 3501, and provides policy and procedures for the use of multi-year contracting.
quote: This subpart implements 41 U.S.C. 3903 and 10 U.S.C. 3501 and provides policy and procedures for the use of multi-year contracting.

statement: For DoD, NASA, and the Coast Guard, the authorities cited in FAR 17.101 do not apply to contracts for the purchase of supplies to which title 40 of the United States Code, section 759 applies, which the section labels information resource management supply contracts.
quote: For DoD, NASA, and the Coast Guard, the authorities cited in 17.101 do not apply to contracts for the purchase of supplies to which 40 U.S.C. 759 applies (information resource management supply contracts).

statement: Benefits may accrue by including options in a multiyear contract, and in that event contracting officers must follow the requirements of FAR subpart 17.2.
quote: Benefits may accrue by including options in a multiyear contract. In that event, contracting officers must follow the requirements of subpart 17.2.

statement: Options should not include charges for plant and equipment already amortized, or other nonrecurring charges that were included in the basic contract.
quote: Options should not include charges for plant and equipment already amortized, or other nonrecurring charges which were included in the basic contract.

statement: A management and operating contract is an agreement under which the Government contracts for the operation, maintenance, or support, on its behalf, of a Government-owned or -controlled research, development, special production, or testing establishment; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-3043.
quote: Management and operating contract means an agreement under which the Government contracts for the operation, maintenance, or support, on its behalf, of a Government-owned or -controlled research, development, special production, or testing establishment
note: The same sentence ends with the dedication test carried in CL-EST-3043.

statement: In the definition of a management and operating contract, the establishment is one wholly or principally devoted to one or more major programs of the contracting Federal agency; this completes the sentence quoted in CL-EST-3042.
quote: wholly or principally devoted to one or more major programs of the contracting Federal agency.
note: Completes the definition of management and operating contract begun in CL-EST-3042.

statement: FAR subpart 17.7 applies to all acquisitions made by nondefense agencies on behalf of DoD.
quote: This subpart applies to all acquisitions made by nondefense agencies on behalf of DoD.

statement: FAR subpart 17.7 does not apply to contracts entered into by a nondefense agency that is an element of the intelligence community for the performance of a joint program conducted to meet the needs of DoD and the nondefense agency.
quote: It does not apply to contracts entered into by a nondefense agency that is an element of the intelligence community for the performance of a joint program conducted to meet the needs of DoD and the nondefense agency.

quote: and may pay the costs of such contracts for each year from annual appropriations for that year (10 U.S.C. 2829).

statement: Under paragraph (a), headed written agreement on responsibility for management and administration, paragraph (a)(1), headed assisted acquisitions, says to follow the procedures at PGI 217.502-1(a)(1) when a contracting activity from a DoD Component provides acquisition assistance to deployed DoD units or personnel from another DoD Component.
quote: (a) Written agreement on responsibility for management and administration — (1) Assisted acquisitions. Follow the procedures at PGI 217.502-1(a)(1), when a contracting activity from a DoD Component provides acquisition assistance to deployed DoD units or personnel from another DoD Component.

statement: As used in DFARS subpart 217.75, replenishment parts means repairable or consumable parts acquired after the initial provisioning process.
quote: Replenishment parts, as used in this subpart, means repairable or consumable parts acquired after the initial provisioning process.

statement: The section headed spares acquisition integrated with production says to follow the procedures at PGI 217.7503 for acquiring spare parts concurrently with the end item.
quote: Spares acquisition integrated with production. Follow the procedures at PGI 217.7503 for acquiring spare parts concurrently with the end item.

statement: The section headed acquisition of parts when data is not available says to follow the procedures at PGI 217.7504 when acquiring parts for which the Government does not have the necessary data.
quote: Acquisition of parts when data is not available. Follow the procedures at PGI 217.7504 when acquiring parts for which the Government does not have the necessary data.

statement: The section headed provisioning says in paragraph (a) to follow the procedures at PGI 217.7601 for contracts with provisioning requirements.
quote: Provisioning. (a) Follow the procedures at PGI 217.7601 for contracts with provisioning requirements.

statement: Paragraph (b) of the provisioning section says that for technical requirements of provisioning, see DoD Manual 4140.01, Volume 2, DoD Supply Chain Materiel Management Procedures: Demand and Supply Planning.
quote: For technical requirements of provisioning, see DoD Manual 4140.01, Volume 2, DoD Supply Chain Materiel Management Procedures: Demand and Supply Planning.

statement: FAR subpart 17.6 prescribes policies and procedures for management and operating contracts for the Department of Energy and any other agency having requisite statutory authority.
quote: This subpart prescribes policies and procedures for management and operating contracts for the Department of Energy and any other agency having requisite statutory authority.

statement: Compliance with FAR subpart 17.7 is in addition to the policies and procedures for interagency acquisitions set forth in FAR subpart 17.5.
quote: Compliance with this subpart is in addition to the policies and procedures for interagency acquisitions set forth in subpart 17.5.

statement: FAR subpart 17.7 prescribes policies and procedures specific to acquisitions of supplies and services by nondefense agencies on behalf of the Department of Defense (DoD).
quote: This subpart prescribes policies and procedures specific to acquisitions of supplies and services by nondefense agencies on behalf of the Department of Defense (DoD).

statement: Before awarding a multiyear contract, the head of the agency must compare the cost of that contract to the cost of an annual procurement approach, using a present value analysis.
quote: Before awarding a multiyear contract, the head of the agency must compare the cost of that contract to the cost of an annual procurement approach, using a present value analysis.

statement: The multiyear contract is not to be awarded unless the present value analysis shows that it will result in the lower cost; the sentence also cites a statute and appropriations acts.
quote: Do not award the multiyear contract unless the analysis shows that the multiyear contract will result in the lower cost (10 U.S.C. 3501(l)(7); section 8008(a) of Pub. L. 105-56 and similar sections in subsequent DoD appropriations acts).

quote: This subpart provides guidance on additional requirements related to acquisition of replenishment parts.

statement: DoD contracting officers must use the revised FAR part 15 published on the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul web page in place of the FAR part 15 text codified at 48 CFR chapter 1.
quote: Contracting officers must use— • The revised FAR part 15, Contracting by Negotiation, published on the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul web page at https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-partdeviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-15 in lieu of the text codified at 48 CFR chapter 1
note: The same memo directs use of its attached DFARS part 215 and PGI 215 in place of the codified and published text. Effective date is the memo's signature date (2026-07-22, p. 2); it says effective immediately. Rev 1 supersedes 2026-O0048 of 2026-03-05, not stored, so whether DoD used the RFO part 15 text from that earlier date is unconfirmed.

statement: Revision 1 of the DoD part 15 class deviation took effect immediately and supersedes Class Deviation 2026-O0048 issued on March 5, 2026.
quote: Effective immediately, this class deviation revises and supersedes Class Deviation 2026O0048, issued on March 5, 2026.
note: The memo was signed on 2026-07-22. The extracted text drops the hyphen in 2026-O0048.

statement: Under RFO FAR 15.101(e)(1), agencies may publish a notice that provides a general description of the scope or purpose of the acquisition and invites potential offerors to submit information that allows the Government to advise offerors about their potential to be viable competitors.
quote: (e) Advisory multistep process. (1) Agencies may publish a notice that provides a general description of the scope or purpose of the acquisition and invites potential offerors to submit information that allows the Government to advise offerors about their potential to be viable competitors.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO paragraph says "a notice" where the codified paragraph says "a presolicitation notice (see 5.204)". The first codified sentence and the RFO paragraph agree that the agency may publish a notice inviting information that lets the Government advise offerors; the RFO paragraph has no counterpart to the four further codified sentences, which say the notice should identify the information and criteria, that information sought may be limited, that the notice shall contain sufficient information to permit an informed decision, and that the process should not be used where offerors would submit identical information twice."

statement: RFO FAR 15.101(e)(2)(iv) lists informing all respondents that, notwithstanding the advice provided by the Government in response to their submissions, they may participate in the resultant acquisition.
quote: (iv) Inform all respondents that, notwithstanding the advice provided by the Government in response to their submissions, they may participate in the resultant acquisition.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO item sits in a list that opens "agencies must" where the codified sentence says "The agency shall inform all respondents"; the rule is the same.

quote: (a) Insert the provision at 52.215-1, Instructions to Offerors—Competitive Acquisition, in all competitive RFPs where the Government intends to award a contract without negotiations.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO paragraph says "RFPs" and "without negotiations" where the codified paragraph says "solicitations" and "without discussions", and it has no "When contracting by negotiation" lead-in.

statement: RFO FAR 15.110(a)(1) says that if the Government intends to make award after negotiating with offerors within the competitive range, the provision is used with its Alternate I.
quote: (1) If the Government intends to make award after negotiating with offerors within the competitive range, use the provision with its Alternate I.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO paragraph says "after negotiating with offerors" where the codified paragraph says "after discussions with offerors"; the Alternate I instruction is otherwise the same.

statement: RFO FAR 15.110(a)(2) says that if the Government would be willing to accept alternate proposals, the clause is altered to add a paragraph (c)(9) substantially the same as Alternate II.
quote: (2) If the Government would be willing to accept alternate proposals, alter the clause to add a paragraph (c)(9) substantially the same as Alternate II.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraph in substance.

quote: (b)(1) Insert the clause at 52.215-2, Audit and Records-Negotiation (10 U.S.C. 3841, 41 U.S.C. 4706, and Audit Requirements in the OMB Uniform Guidance at 2 CFR part 200, subpart F), in RFPs and contracts except those for— (i) Acquisitions not exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold;

statement: RFO FAR 15.110(b)(2) is printed as [Reserved].
quote: (2) [Reserved]
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The codified paragraph (b)(2) holds the cross-referenced exception; the RFO paragraph with the same number is printed as reserved.

statement: RFO FAR 15.110(b)(3) says that for cost-reimbursement contracts with State and local Governments, educational institutions, and other nonprofit organizations, the clause is used with its Alternate II.
quote: (3) For cost-reimbursement contracts with State and local Governments, educational institutions, and other nonprofit organizations, use the clause with its Alternate II.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraph in substance.

statement: RFO FAR 15.110 prints paragraphs (c), (d) and (e) each as [Reserved].
quote: (c) [Reserved] (d) [Reserved] (e) [Reserved]
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). statement: RFO FAR 15.110(f) says to insert the provision at 52.215-6, Place of Performance, in RFPs, unless the place of performance is specified by the Government.
quote: (f) Insert the provision at 52.215-6, Place of Performance, in RFPs, unless the place of performance is specified by the Government.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraph in substance, with "RFPs" for "solicitations".

statement: RFO FAR 15.110(h) says to insert the clause at 52.215-8, Order of Precedence—Uniform Contract Format, in RFPs and contracts using the format at 15.108.

note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO paragraph points to the format at 15.108 where the codified paragraph points to the format at 15.204; the instruction to insert the clause is otherwise the same. The RFO section titled Uniform contract format is numbered 15.109, and the RFO section numbered 15.108 is titled Receiving proposals.

statement: RFO FAR 15.202 is titled Evaluating competitive proposals, and its paragraph (a)(1) says proposal evaluation is an assessment of the proposal and an offeror's ability to perform the prospective contract successfully.
quote: 15.202 Evaluating competitive proposals. (a) General. (1) Proposal evaluation is an assessment of the proposal and an offeror's ability to perform the prospective contract successfully.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO section with this number covers evaluating competitive proposals, not the advisory multi-step process, which the codified section with this number covers.

statement: RFO FAR 15.403-4(a) says that when certified cost or pricing data are required, contracting officers must require the contractor to execute a Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data, using the format in that paragraph, and must include the executed certificate in the contract file.
quote: (a) When certified cost or pricing data are required, contracting officers must require the contractor to execute a Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data, using the format in this paragraph, and must include the executed certificate in the contract file.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO paragraph says "contracting officers must" where the codified paragraph says "the contracting officer shall"; the rule is the same.

statement: The RFO certificate form states that the cost or pricing data are accurate, complete, and current as of the date inserted in the form.
quote: are accurate, complete, and current as of ____**.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The form wording is the same in substance; it refers to FAR subsection 15.403-3 for the data required, where the codified form refers to 15.403-4.

statement: The RFO certificate form tells the signer to insert the day, month, and year when price negotiations were concluded and price agreement was reached or, if applicable, an earlier date agreed upon between the parties that is as close as practicable to the date of agreement on price.
quote: ** Insert the day, month, and year when price negotiations were concluded and price agreement was reached or, if applicable, an earlier date agreed upon between the parties that is as close as practicable to the date of agreement on price.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO footnote is the same as the codified footnote in substance.

statement: The RFO certificate form says the certification includes the cost or pricing data supporting any advance agreements and forward pricing rate agreements between the offeror and the Government that are part of the proposal.
quote: This certification includes the cost or pricing data supporting any advance agreements and forward pricing rate agreements between the offeror and the Government that are part of the proposal.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO sentence is the same as the codified sentence.

statement: RFO FAR 15.403-4(b) says the certificate does not constitute a representation as to the accuracy of the contractor's judgment on the estimate of future costs or projections, and that it applies to the data upon which the judgment or estimate was based.
quote: (b) The certificate does not constitute a representation as to the accuracy of the contractor's judgment on the estimate of future costs or projections. It applies to the data upon which the judgment or estimate was based.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraph in substance.

statement: RFO FAR 15.403-4(d) says possession of a Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data is not a substitute for examining and analyzing the contractor's proposal.
quote: (d) Possession of a Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data is not a substitute for examining and analyzing the contractor's proposal.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: RFO FAR 15.403-3(f) says that if certified cost or pricing data are requested and submitted by an offeror, but an exception is later found to apply, the data must not be considered certified cost or pricing data and must not be certified in accordance with 15.403-4.
quote: (f) Delayed exception. If certified cost or pricing data are requested and submitted by an offeror, but an exception is later found to apply, the data must not be considered certified cost or pricing data and must not be certified in accordance with 15.403-4.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text moves this rule from the certificate section to paragraph (f) of the section on certified cost or pricing data and says "must not" where the codified paragraph says "shall not"; the RFO sentence says "requested and submitted by an offeror" where the codified sentence says "requested by the Government and submitted by an offeror". The rule is otherwise the same.

statement: RFO FAR 15.403-2(a) says certified cost or pricing data must not be obtained for acquisitions at or below the simplified acquisition threshold.
quote: (a) At or below the simplified acquisition threshold. Certified cost or pricing data must not be obtained for acquisitions at or below the simplified acquisition threshold.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraph in substance, with "must not" for "shall not".

statement: RFO FAR 15.403-2(b) says contracting officers must not require certified cost or pricing data to support any contracts, subcontracts, or modifications in the circumstances it lists; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-3199.
quote: (b) Exceptions to certified cost or pricing data requirements. Contracting officers must not require certified cost or pricing data to support any contracts, subcontracts, or modifications—
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO lead-in runs straight from "contracts, subcontracts, or modifications" to the list, without the codified parenthetical that the contracting officer may require data other than certified cost or pricing data to support a determination of a fair and reasonable price or cost realism; the RFO carries that subject in its section on data other than certified cost or pricing data, at 15.403-1(b)(1) and (b)(2).

statement: RFO FAR 15.403-2(b) lists, as circumstances in which certified cost or pricing data must not be required, when the contracting officer determines that prices agreed upon are based on adequate price competition and when the contracting officer determines that prices agreed upon are based on prices set by law or regulation.
quote: (1) When the contracting officer determines that prices agreed upon are based on adequate price competition (see standards in paragraph (c)(1) of this subsection); (2) When the contracting officer determines that prices agreed upon are based on prices set by law or regulation
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO items are the same as the codified items in substance.

statement: RFO FAR 15.403-2(b) lists, as circumstances in which certified cost or pricing data must not be required, when a commercial product or commercial service is being acquired and when a waiver has been granted.
quote: (3) When a commercial product or commercial service is being acquired (see standards in paragraph (c)(3) of this subsection); (4) When a waiver has been granted (see standards in paragraph (c)(4) of this subsection);
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO items are the same as the codified items in substance.

statement: RFO FAR 15.403-2(c)(1)(i)(A) says a price is based on adequate price competition when, among the conditions listed, two or more responsible offerors, competing independently, submit priced offers that satisfy the Government's expressed requirement.
quote: (A) Two or more responsible offerors, competing independently, submit priced offers that satisfy the Government's expressed requirement;
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: RFO FAR 15.403-2(c)(1)(i) further requires that award will be made to the offeror whose proposal represents the best value where price is a substantial factor in source selection, and that there is no finding that the price of the otherwise successful offeror is unreasonable.
quote: (B) Award will be made to the offeror whose proposal represents the best value where price is a substantial factor in source selection; and (C) There is no finding that the price of the otherwise successful offeror is unreasonable.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraphs in substance, without the codified cross-reference to the definition of best value.

statement: RFO FAR 15.403-2(c)(4)(i) says that in exceptional cases the head of the contracting activity may, without power of delegation, waive the requirement for submission of certified cost or pricing data if the price can be determined to be fair and reasonable without submission of certified cost or pricing data.
quote: (4) Waivers. (i) In exceptional cases, the HCA may, without power of delegation, waive the requirement for submission of certified cost or pricing data if the price can be determined to be fair and reasonable without submission of certified cost or pricing data.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO paragraph puts the fair-and-reasonable-price condition into the sentence that grants the waiver power, where the codified paragraph says in a later sentence that the head of the contracting activity may consider waiving if the price can be so determined.

statement: RFO FAR 15.403-1 is titled Data other than certified cost or pricing data, and its paragraph (a) says that for acquisitions that do not require certified cost or pricing data, contracting officers must generally use the order of preference that follows to determine the type of data to require.
quote: 15.403-1 Data other than certified cost or pricing data. (a) Order of preference. For acquisitions that do not require certified cost or pricing data, contracting officers must generally use the following order of preference to determine the type of data to require:
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The codified text lists steps the contracting officer shall take in paragraph (a)(1) of its section on requiring data other than certified cost or pricing data; the RFO text instead sets an order of preference that contracting officers must generally use. The codified pricing policy section at 15.402(a)(2) also states an order of preference, which this claim does not compare.

statement: The first item in the RFO order of preference is no additional data from the offeror, when adequate price competition exists.
quote: (1) No additional data from the offeror, when adequate price competition exists (see 15.403-2);
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The codified paragraph says that when adequate price competition exists, generally no additional data are necessary; the RFO text states it as the first item of an order of preference. The codified pricing policy section at 15.402(a)(2)(i) also lists no additional data from the offeror first, which this claim does not compare.

statement: RFO FAR 15.403-1(b)(1) says contracting officers must require submission of data other than certified cost or pricing data to the extent necessary to determine a fair and reasonable price.
quote: (b) Requirement. (1) Contracting officers must require submission of data other than certified cost or pricing data to the extent necessary to determine a fair and reasonable price (10 U.S.C. 3705(a) and 41 U.S.C. 3505(a)).
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO sentence has no condition that the contracting officer first determines that adequate data from sources other than the offeror are not available, which the codified paragraph states; the RFO order of preference at 15.403-1(a)(2) reaches data from the offeror last, "if necessary". For commercial products and commercial services, RFO 15.403-1(f)(2) carries a condition of that kind.

statement: RFO FAR 15.403-1(b)(1) says that, at a minimum, the data must include appropriate data on the prices at which the same item or similar items have previously been sold, adequate for determining the reasonableness of the price.
quote: At a minimum, the data must include appropriate data on the prices at which the same item or similar items have previously been sold, adequate for determining the reasonableness of the price.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO sentence is the same as the first part of the codified paragraph in substance.

statement: RFO FAR 15.403-1(b)(1) says the minimum prior-price data are not required when price reasonableness is established through adequate price competition or prices set by law or regulation, unless paragraph (e) of that subsection applies.
quote: This data is not required when price reasonableness is established through adequate price competition or prices set by law or regulation, unless paragraph (e) of this subsection applies.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO sentence makes the exception depend on paragraph (e) of its own section not applying, where the codified paragraph says unless an exception under 15.403-1(b)(1) or (2) applies.

statement: RFO FAR 15.403-1(a)(2) relies first on data available within the Government, then on data obtained from sources other than the offeror, and then, if necessary, on data obtained from the offeror.
quote: relying first on— (i) Data available within the Government; then (ii) Data obtained from sources other than the offeror; and then, if necessary, (iii) Data obtained from the offeror;
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text reaches data from the offeror last and only "if necessary", where the codified paragraph 15.403-3(a)(1)(ii) requires data from the offeror if the contracting officer determines that adequate data from other sources are not available. The codified pricing policy section at 15.402(a)(2) also lists data from the offeror last, "if necessary", which this claim does not compare.

statement: RFO FAR 15.403-1(e) says that if adequate price competition exists, but there are unusual circumstances in which additional data are necessary to determine the reasonableness of price, contracting officers must obtain the additional data from sources other than the offeror, to the maximum extent practicable.
quote: If adequate price competition exists, but there are unusual circumstances in which additional data are necessary to determine the reasonableness of price, contracting officers must obtain the additional data from sources other than the offeror, to the maximum extent practicable.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraph in substance, with "must" for "shall".

statement: RFO FAR 15.403-1(d) says an offeror who does not comply with a requirement to submit data for a contract or subcontract in accordance with paragraph (a)(1) of that subsection is ineligible for award unless the head of the contracting activity determines that it is in the best interest of the Government.
quote: an offeror who does not comply with a requirement to submit data for a contract or subcontract in accordance with paragraph (a)(1) of this subsection is ineligible for award unless the head of the contracting activity (HCA) determines that it is in the best interest of the Government
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraph in substance and keeps the cross-reference to paragraph (a)(1) of its own subsection.

statement: RFO FAR 15.403-1(d) says the head of the contracting activity bases that determination on consideration of the effort made to obtain the data, the need for the item or service, and increased cost or significant harm to the Government if award is not made.
quote: based on consideration of the following: (1) The effort made to obtain the data. (2) The need for the item or service. (3) Increased cost or significant harm to the Government if award is not made.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: RFO FAR 15.403-3 is titled Certified cost or pricing data, and its paragraph (a), Threshold, says that, unless an exception at 15.403-2 applies, contracting officers must obtain certified cost or pricing data when an action meets or exceeds the threshold of $2.5 million (for prime contracts awarded on or after July 1, 2018).
quote: 15.403-3 Certified cost or pricing data. (a) Threshold. Unless an exception at 15.403-2 applies, contracting officers must obtain certified cost or pricing data when an action meets or exceeds the threshold of $2.5 million (for prime contracts awarded on or after July 1, 2018).
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO section with this number covers certified cost or pricing data and its threshold, not data other than certified cost or pricing data, which the codified section with this number covers.

statement: RFO FAR 15.105-4(a) says that, in accordance with 15.402(a), contracting officers must state in the RFP, among listed items, whether certified cost or pricing data are required.
quote: (a) Required information. In accordance with 15.402(a), contracting officers must state in the RFP— (1) Whether certified cost or pricing data are required;
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). statement: RFO FAR 15.202(a)(2)(i) says clarifications are exchanges between the Government and offerors where offerors are given the opportunity to resolve minor or clerical errors or clarify certain aspects of their proposal.

The codified paragraph describes clarifications as limited exchanges that may occur when award without discussions is contemplated; this RFO sentence defines them by what offerors may do, which is resolve minor or clerical errors or clarify aspects of the proposal.

statement: RFO FAR 15.202(a)(2)(iv) says clarifications may occur, at the contracting officer's discretion, at any time after receipt of proposals through contract award.
quote: Clarifications may occur, at the contracting officer’s discretion, at any time after receipt of proposals through contract award.

The codified paragraph ties clarifications to when award without discussions is contemplated; this RFO sentence places them at the contracting officer's discretion at any time after receipt of proposals through contract award.

statement: RFO FAR 15.202(a)(2)(iii) says clarifications do not permit offerors to revise their proposal and cannot be used to cure proposal deficiencies or material omissions or materially alter the technical or cost elements of the proposal.
quote: Clarifications do not permit offerors to revise their proposal and cannot be used to cure proposal deficiencies or material omissions or materially alter the technical or cost elements of the proposal.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The codified limit applies to communications held before the competitive range is established; this RFO limit is written for clarifications. The next sentence of the RFO paragraph is carried by CL-EST-3344.

statement: RFO FAR 15.201(c) says contracting officers must, after release of an RFP, serve as the focal point for inquiries from actual or prospective offerors and, after receipt of proposals, control communications with offerors.
quote: (c) Contracting officers must— (1) After release of a RFP, serve as the focal point for inquiries from actual or prospective offerors; (2) After receipt of proposals, control communications with offerors;

The codified paragraph makes the contracting officer the focal point of any exchange with potential offerors after release of the solicitation; the RFO paragraph is in the section on source selection responsibilities and speaks of inquiries and of controlling communications after receipt of proposals.

statement: RFO FAR 15.201(d) says Government personnel involved in the acquisition must not engage in conduct that favors one offeror over another or that reveals an offeror's technical solution, including unique technology.
quote: (d) Limitations. Government personnel involved in the acquisition must not engage in conduct that— (1) Favors one offeror over another; (2) Reveals an offeror's technical solution, including— (i) Unique technology;

statement: RFO FAR 15.204-1(a) says a competitive range is the group of evaluated proposals that the contracting officer determines are best suited for further negotiation, and that contracting officers must establish one if negotiations will occur after evaluating competitive proposals.
quote: A competitive range is the group of evaluated proposals that the contracting officer determines are best suited for further negotiation. Contracting officers must establish a competitive range if negotiations will occur after evaluating competitive proposals.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The codified paragraph has the contracting officer establish a range of all of the most highly rated proposals, unless reduced for efficiency; this RFO paragraph defines the range as the group the contracting officer determines are best suited for further negotiation.

statement: RFO FAR 15.204-1(b) says the contracting officer may limit the number of proposals in the competitive range to the greatest number that will permit an efficient competition among the most highly evaluated proposals, and the sentence that gives this power states no condition about notice in the solicitation.
quote: The contracting officer may limit the number of proposals in the competitive range to the greatest number that will permit an efficient competition among the most highly evaluated proposals (10 U.S.C. 3303 and 41 U.S.C. 3703).
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The codified paragraph allows the limit only if the solicitation notifies offerors that the range can be limited for efficiency; the RFO sentence that grants the power contains no such condition.

statement: RFO FAR 15.204-2(b)(1) says contracting officers must negotiate with each responsible offeror within the competitive range and tailor the negotiation to the offeror's proposal but, at a minimum, indicate to, or negotiate with, each offeror any deficiencies or significant weaknesses in the proposal.
quote: (1) Contracting officers must— (i) Negotiate with each responsible offeror within the competitive range; and (ii) Tailor the negotiation to the offeror’s proposal, but at a minimum, indicate to, or negotiate with, each offeror any deficiencies or significant weaknesses in the proposal.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The codified minimum also lists adverse past performance information to which the offeror has not yet had an opportunity to respond, and speaks of discussions; the RFO paragraph speaks of negotiations with each responsible offeror and lists deficiencies and significant weaknesses.

statement: RFO FAR 15.101(a) says exchanges of information among all interested parties are encouraged and can occur at any time between the identification of a requirement through the receipt of proposals.
quote: Exchanges of information among all interested parties are encouraged and can occur at any time between the identification of a requirement through the receipt of proposals.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The wording is the same in substance as the first codified sentence on encouraging exchanges through receipt of proposals.

quote: Any exchange of information must be consistent with procurement integrity requirements in part 3 and protected in accordance with part 24.

The codified sentence requires consistency with procurement integrity requirements at 3.104; this RFO sentence cites part 3 and adds protection in accordance with part 24.

statement: RFO FAR 15.101(b) says agencies are encouraged to release draft RFPs and conduct conferences with industry before issuing competitive RFPs.
quote: Agencies are encouraged to release draft RFPs and conduct conferences with industry before issuing competitive RFPs.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). quote: Agencies are encouraged to release requests for information (RFI) when the Government does not currently intend to award a contract, but wants to obtain price, delivery, market, or capabilities information for planning purposes.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The codified paragraphs list RFIs as a technique and say they may be used for the same purpose; this RFO paragraph says agencies are encouraged to release them.

statement: RFO FAR 15.101(d) says general information on an agency's current or anticipated needs and requirements may be disclosed at any time.
quote: General information on an agency’s current or anticipated needs and requirements may be disclosed at any time.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The wording is the same in substance as the first codified sentence of paragraph (f).

quote: Insert the clause at 52.215-10, Price Reduction for Defective Certified Cost or Pricing Data, in RFPs and contracts when it is contemplated that certified cost or pricing data will be required from the contractor or any subcontractor.

statement: RFO FAR 15.103-2(a) says the lowest price technically acceptable approach is appropriate when it is in the Government's best interest to award to the offeror that submits a technically acceptable proposal with the lowest evaluated price, and that the approach does not permit tradeoffs.

statement: RFO FAR 15.103-2(b) says that, when using the approach, the RFP must identify the evaluation factors that establish the minimum requirements for acceptability and specify that award will be made on the basis of the lowest evaluated price of proposals meeting or exceeding the requirements for acceptability.
