note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The rule is the same; it is now paragraph (c)(4), with the limits as subparagraphs (i) to (iii), and uses "must not" for "shall not".

statement: RFO FAR 15.404-9(c)(4)(i) says that for experimental, developmental, or research work performed under a cost-plus-fixed-fee contract, the fee must not exceed 15 percent of the contract's estimated cost, excluding fee.
quote: (i) For experimental, developmental, or research work performed under a cost-plus-fixed-fee contract, the fee must not exceed 15 percent of the contract's estimated cost, excluding fee.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The limit is the same 15 percent; the RFO text says "must not" for "shall not".

statement: RFO FAR 15.404-9(c)(4)(ii) says that for architect-engineer services for public works or utilities, the contract price or the estimated cost and fee for production and delivery of designs, plans, drawings, and specifications must not exceed 6 percent of the estimated cost of construction of the public work or utility, excluding fees.
quote: For architect-engineer services for public works or utilities, the contract price or the estimated cost and fee for production and delivery of designs, plans, drawings, and specifications must not exceed 6 percent of the estimated cost of construction of the public work or utility, excluding fees.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The limit is the same 6 percent; the RFO text says "must not" for "shall not".

statement: RFO FAR 15.404-9(c)(4)(iii) says that for other cost-plus-fixed-fee contracts, the fee must not exceed 10 percent of the contract's estimated cost, excluding fee.
quote: (iii) For other cost-plus-fixed-fee contracts, the fee must not exceed 10 percent of the contract's estimated cost, excluding fee.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The limit is the same 10 percent; the RFO text says "must not" for "shall not".

statement: RFO FAR 15.404-9(b)(3) says that when the price negotiation is not based on cost analysis, contracting officers are not required to analyze profit.
quote: (3) When the price negotiation is not based on cost analysis, contracting officers are not required to analyze profit.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The rule is the same; it moves from codified paragraph (c)(1) to RFO paragraph (b)(3).

statement: RFO FAR 15.404-9(d)(1) says that, unless it is clearly inappropriate or not applicable, each factor outlined in paragraphs (d)(1)(i) through (vi) of that subsection must be considered by agencies in developing their structured approaches and by contracting officers in analyzing profit, whether or not using a structured approach.
quote: Unless it is clearly inappropriate or not applicable, each factor outlined in paragraphs (d)(1)(i) through (vi) of this subsection must be considered by agencies in developing their structured approaches and by contracting officers in analyzing profit, whether or not using a structured approach.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The rule is the same; the RFO text uses "must" for "shall".

statement: RFO FAR 15.404-9(b)(1)(i) says that, subject to the authorities in part 1, agencies making noncompetitive contract awards over $100,000 totaling $50 million or more a year must use a structured approach for determining the profit or fee objective in those acquisitions that require cost analysis.
quote: (1) Subject to the authorities in part 1, agencies making noncompetitive contract awards over $100,000 totaling $50 million or more a year— (i) Must use a structured approach for determining the profit or fee objective in those acquisitions that require cost analysis
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text says "Subject to the authorities in part 1" where the codified text says "Subject to the authorities in 1.301(c)", and uses "must" for "shall".

statement: RFO FAR 15.404-9(b)(1)(ii) says those agencies may prescribe specific exemptions for situations in which mandatory use of a structured approach would be clearly inappropriate.
quote: (ii) May prescribe specific exemptions for situations in which mandatory use of a structured approach would be clearly inappropriate.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The wording is the same as codified FAR 15.404-4(b)(1)(ii).

statement: RFO FAR 15.404(a) says the objective of proposal analysis is to ensure that the final agreed-to price is fair and reasonable.
quote: (a) General. The objective of proposal analysis is to ensure that the final agreed-to price is fair and reasonable.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The sentence is the same as codified FAR 15.404-1(a).

statement: RFO FAR 15.404(a)(2) says price analysis must be used when certified cost or pricing data are not required.
quote: (2) Price analysis must be used when certified cost or pricing data are not required.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The rule is the same; the RFO text uses "must" for "shall" and does not carry the codified cross-reference to paragraph (b) and 15.404-3.

statement: RFO FAR 15.404(a)(2) says that when a fair and reasonable price cannot be determined through price analysis alone, cost analysis may also be used to evaluate data other than certified cost or pricing data to determine cost reasonableness or cost realism.
quote: When a fair and reasonable price cannot be determined through price analysis alone, cost analysis may also be used to evaluate data other than certified cost or pricing data to determine cost reasonableness or cost realism.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The rule is the same; the RFO text moves it into the second sentence of paragraph (a)(2).

statement: RFO FAR 15.404(a)(3) says cost analysis must be used when certified cost or pricing data are required, and that price analysis must be used to verify that the overall price offered is fair and reasonable.
quote: (3) Cost analysis must be used when certified cost or pricing data are required. However, price analysis must be used to verify that the overall price offered is fair and reasonable.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO sentence does not carry the codified words "to evaluate the reasonableness of individual cost elements", and says price analysis "must" be used to verify the overall price where the codified text says it "should" be used.

statement: RFO FAR 15.404-2(a) says cost analysis includes the review and evaluation of any separate cost elements and profit or fee in an offeror's or contractor's proposal, as needed to determine a fair and reasonable price or to determine cost realism; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-3417.
quote: Cost analysis is the review and evaluation of any separate cost elements and profit or fee in an offeror's or contractor's proposal, as needed to determine a fair and reasonable price or to determine cost realism
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The definition of cost analysis moves from codified paragraph (c)(1) to RFO 15.404-2(a) with the same wording; the quote stops before the clause on the application of judgment, which another claim carries.

statement: RFO FAR 15.404(a)(4) says cost realism must be used when contemplating the award of a cost-reimbursement contract.
quote: (4) Cost realism must be used when contemplating the award of a cost-reimbursement contract.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). This general statement has no single codified counterpart; codified FAR 15.404-1(d)(2) says cost realism analyses shall be performed on cost-reimbursement contracts to determine the probable cost of performance for each offeror, and RFO 15.404-3(b) says the same.

statement: RFO FAR 15.404-1(c) says the techniques at 15.404-1(b)(1) and (2) are the preferred methods for price analysis.
quote: The techniques at 15.404-1(b)(1) and (2) are the preferred methods for price analysis.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The first two techniques are preferred in both texts; the RFO text sets this out in paragraph (c), whose last sentence says a price being in a catalog does not, in and of itself, make it fair and reasonable, a sentence that codified FAR 15.403-3(c)(1) has.

statement: RFO FAR 15.404-1(c) says that if the contracting officer determines that information on competitive proposed prices or previous contract prices is not available or is insufficient to determine that the price is fair and reasonable, the contracting officer may use any of the remaining techniques; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-3415.
quote: However, if the contracting officer determines that information on competitive proposed prices or previous contract prices is not available or is insufficient to determine that the price is fair and reasonable, the contracting officer may use any of the remaining techniques
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The rule is the same as codified FAR 15.404-1(b)(3); the sentence continues with the words that carry the qualification as appropriate to the circumstances applicable to the acquisition, which another claim carries.

statement: RFO FAR 15.404-3(b) says cost realism analyses must be performed on cost-reimbursement contracts to determine the probable cost of performance for each offeror.
quote: (b) Probable Cost. Cost realism analyses must be performed on cost-reimbursement contacts to determine the probable cost of performance for each offeror.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The rule is the same; the RFO text prints "contacts" for "contracts" and uses "must" for "shall".

statement: RFO FAR 15.404-3(b)(1) says the probable cost must be used for purposes of evaluation to determine the best value.
quote: The probable cost must be used for purposes of evaluation to determine the best value.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The rule is the same; the RFO text uses "must" for "shall".

statement: RFO FAR 15.404-3(c) says cost realism analyses may also be used on competitive fixed-price incentive contracts; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-3416.
quote: Cost realism analyses may also be used on competitive fixed-price incentive contracts
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The rule is the same as codified FAR 15.404-1(d)(3); the sentence continues with the exceptional cases for other competitive fixed-price-type contracts, which another claim carries.

statement: RFO FAR 15.404-3(c) says the results of the analysis may be used in performance risk assessments and responsibility determinations, but proposals must be evaluated using the criteria in the RFP and the offered prices must not be adjusted as a result of the analysis.
quote: Results of the analysis may be used in performance risk assessments and responsibility determinations. However, proposals must be evaluated using the criteria in the RFP, and the offered prices must not be adjusted as a result of the analysis.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The rule is the same; the RFO text says RFP where the codified text says solicitation and uses "must" for "shall".

statement: RFO FAR 15.404(b) says recommendations or conclusions regarding the Government's review or analysis of an offeror's or contractor's proposal must not be disclosed to the offeror or contractor without the concurrence of the contracting officer.
quote: Recommendations or conclusions regarding the Government's review or analysis of an offeror's or contractor's proposal must not be disclosed to the offeror or contractor without the concurrence of the contracting officer.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The rule is the same; the RFO text moves it to paragraph (b) and uses "must not" for "shall not".

statement: RFO FAR 15.204-2(c) says a proposal must be eliminated from consideration for award when the contracting officer determines that a proposal should no longer be included in the competitive range.
quote: (c) Elimination from the competitive range. A proposal must be eliminated from consideration for award when the contracting officer determines that a proposal should no longer be included in the competitive range.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text places the rule on elimination from the competitive range in 15.204-2(c) and states when a proposal must be eliminated, where codified FAR 15.307(a) speaks of a proposal eliminated or otherwise removed from the competitive range.

statement: RFO FAR 15.204-2(c)(1) says that when a proposal is eliminated, no further revisions to the proposal can be accepted or considered.
quote: (1) When a proposal is eliminated, no further revisions to the proposal can be accepted or considered.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text says when a proposal is eliminated where the codified text says eliminated or otherwise removed from the competitive range, and says no further revisions can be accepted or considered where the codified text says no further revisions shall be accepted or considered.

statement: RFO FAR 15.204-2(d)(1)(i) says that when negotiations with an offeror are finished, and that offeror has not been eliminated from the competitive range, contracting officers must provide the offeror with an opportunity to submit a proposal revision; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-3407.
quote: (d) Proposal revision. (1) When negotiations with an offeror are finished, and that offeror has not been eliminated from the competitive range, contracting officers must provide the offeror with— (i) An opportunity to submit a proposal revision; and
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text ties the opportunity to the point when negotiations with that offeror are finished and it has not been eliminated, and speaks of a proposal revision, where codified FAR 15.307(b) gives each offeror still in the competitive range an opportunity to submit a final proposal revision at the conclusion of discussions.

statement: RFO FAR 15.204-2(d)(1)(ii) says contracting officers must also provide the offeror a notice requiring the proposal revision in writing and stating that the Government intends to make award without obtaining further revisions.
quote: (ii) A notice requiring the proposal revision in writing and stating that the Government intends to make award without obtaining further revisions.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text speaks of a notice requiring the proposal revision where codified FAR 15.307(b) speaks of requests for final proposal revisions; the content, in writing and no further revisions, is the same.

statement: RFO FAR 15.204-2(d)(2) says each offeror with a proposal still within the competitive range must be given an equal amount of time within which to submit their proposal revision.
quote: (2) Each offeror with a proposal still within the competitive range must be given an equal amount of time within which to submit their proposal revision.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text states the timing as an equal amount of time for each offeror, where codified FAR 15.307(b) says the contracting officer is required to establish a common cut-off date only for receipt of final proposal revisions; the words common cut-off date do not appear in RFO 15.204-2.

statement: RFO FAR 15.001 defines a proposal revision as a change to material elements of a proposal made after the RFP closing date, at the request of or as allowed by a contracting officer, as the result of negotiations.
quote: Proposal revision is a change to material elements of a proposal made after the RFP closing date, at the request of or as allowed by a contracting officer, as the result of negotiations.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text defines a proposal revision as a change made at the request of or as allowed by a contracting officer as the result of negotiations, where codified FAR 15.307(b) says the contracting officer may request or allow proposal revisions to clarify and document understandings reached during negotiations.

statement: RFO FAR 15.205 says the source selection decision must represent the source selection authority's independent judgement and be based on a comparative assessment of proposals against all source selection criteria in the RFP.
quote: The source selection decision must represent the SSA’s independent judgement and be based on a comparative assessment of proposals against all source selection criteria in the RFP.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The sentence states the independent judgement and comparative assessment requirements together, and does not carry the codified clause that the source selection authority may use reports and analyses prepared by others; the RFO text uses "must" for "shall".

statement: RFO FAR 15.205 says the source selection decision must be based on a comparative assessment of proposals against all source selection criteria in the RFP.
quote: The source selection decision must represent the SSA’s independent judgement and be based on a comparative assessment of proposals against all source selection criteria in the RFP.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The requirement is the same as the first sentence of codified FAR 15.308; the quote is the whole RFO sentence, which also carries the independent judgement requirement, and the RFO text says RFP where the codified text says solicitation and uses "must" for "shall".

statement: RFO FAR 15.205 says the source selection decision must be documented and include the rationale for any business judgments and tradeoffs made or relied on by the source selection authority, including benefits associated with additional costs.
quote: The source selection decision must be documented and include the rationale for any business judgments and tradeoffs made or relied on by the SSA, including benefits associated with additional costs.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The rule is the same as the third sentence of codified FAR 15.308; the RFO text uses "must" for "shall".

statement: RFO FAR 15.205 says the documentation does not need to quantify the tradeoffs that led to the decision.
quote: The documentation does not need to quantify the tradeoffs that led to the decision.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The rule is the same as the last sentence of codified FAR 15.308.

statement: Price analysis should be used to verify that the overall price offered is fair and reasonable.
quote: Price analysis should be used to verify that the overall price offered is fair and reasonable.

statement: RFO FAR 15.404-1(c) says the contracting officer may use any of the remaining techniques as appropriate to the circumstances applicable to the acquisition.
quote: the contracting officer may use any of the remaining techniques as appropriate to the circumstances applicable to the acquisition.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The wording is the same as the end of the codified sentence at FAR 15.404-1(b)(3).

statement: RFO FAR 15.404-3(c) says cost realism analyses may also be used, in exceptional cases, on other competitive fixed-price-type contracts when new requirements may not be fully understood by competing offerors, there are quality concerns, or past experience indicates that contractors' proposed costs have resulted in quality or service shortfalls.
quote: or, in exceptional cases, on other competitive fixed-price-type contracts when new requirements may not be fully understood by competing offerors, there are quality concerns, or past experience indicates that contractors' proposed costs have resulted in quality or service shortfalls.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The wording is the same as the rest of the codified sentence at FAR 15.404-1(d)(3).

statement: RFO FAR 15.404-2(a) says cost analysis also includes the application of judgment to determine how well the proposed costs represent what the cost of the contract should be, assuming reasonable economy and efficiency.
quote: and the application of judgment to determine how well the proposed costs represent what the cost of the contract should be, assuming reasonable economy and efficiency.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The wording is the same as the end of the codified definition at FAR 15.404-1(c)(1).

statement: RFO FAR 15.107(a) says offerors are responsible for submitting proposals, and any revisions or modifications, so as to reach the Government office designated in the RFP by the time specified in the RFP.
quote: Offerors are responsible for submitting proposals, and any revisions or modifications, so as to reach the Government office designated in the RFP by the time specified in the RFP.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO paragraph says the RFP where codified FAR 15.208(a) says the solicitation; the offerors' responsibility is the same. The differences are in wording only; the text is the same in substance.

statement: RFO FAR 15.107(a)(2) says that if no time is specified in the RFP, the time for receipt is 4:30 p.m., local time, for the designated Government office on the date that proposals are due.
quote: If no time is specified in the RFP, the time for receipt is 4:30 p.m., local time, for the designated Government office on the date that proposals are due.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO paragraph says the RFP where codified FAR 15.208(a) says the solicitation; the default time of receipt is the same. The differences are in wording only; the text is the same in substance.

statement: RFO FAR 15.107(b)(1) says a proposal, modification or revision received at the designated Government office after the exact time specified for receipt of proposals is late and will not be considered, with the exception that follows in the next claim; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-3433 and CL-EST-3434.
quote: Any proposal, modification, or revision, that is received at the designated Government office after the exact time specified for receipt of proposals is “late” and will not be considered,
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO sentence adds a comma after 'will not be considered' and then states the exception; the definition of a late proposal is otherwise the same as in codified FAR 15.208(b)(1). The differences are in wording only; the text is the same in substance.

statement: RFO FAR 15.107(b)(1) says the late proposal will not be considered unless it is received before award is made, the contracting officer determines that accepting the late proposal would not unduly delay the acquisition, and the further conditions that follow the dash are met; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-3434.
quote: unless it is received before award is made, the contracting officer determines that accepting the late proposal would not unduly delay the acquisition, and—
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO sentence runs these conditions into one lead-in that ends 'and—', where codified FAR 15.208(b)(1) has a semicolon before 'and—'; the conditions are otherwise the same. The conditions that follow are quoted in separate claims. The differences are in wording only; the text is the same in substance.

statement: RFO FAR 15.107(b)(1)(i) lists as a condition that, if the proposal was transmitted through an electronic commerce method authorized by the RFP, it was received at the initial point of entry to the Government infrastructure not later than 5:00 p.m. one working day prior to the date specified for receipt of proposals.
quote: (i) If it was transmitted through an electronic commerce method authorized by the RFP, it was received at the initial point of entry to the Government infrastructure not later than 5:00 p.m. one working day prior to the date specified for receipt of proposals;
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO item says the RFP where codified FAR 15.208(b)(1)(i) says the solicitation and ends with a semicolon without 'or'; the RFO list joins its last two items with 'or', so the cutoff is the same alternative. The differences are in wording only; the text is the same in substance.

statement: RFO FAR 15.107(b)(1)(ii) and (iii) list as further conditions that there is acceptable evidence to establish that the proposal was received at the Government installation designated for receipt of proposals and was under the Government's control prior to the time set for receipt of proposals, or that it was the only proposal received.
quote: (ii) There is acceptable evidence to establish that it was received at the Government installation designated for receipt of proposals and was under the Government's control prior to the time set for receipt of proposals; or (iii) It was the only proposal received.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: RFO FAR 15.107(b)(2) says a late modification of an otherwise successful proposal, that makes its terms more favorable to the Government, will be considered at any time it is received and may be accepted by the contracting officer.
quote: A late modification of an otherwise successful proposal, that makes its terms more favorable to the Government, will be considered at any time it is received and may be accepted by the contracting officer.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO paragraph adds 'by the contracting officer' after 'may be accepted'; the late-modification exception is otherwise the same.

statement: RFO FAR 15.107(b)(3) says acceptable evidence to establish the time of receipt at the Government installation includes electronic timestamps and the time/date stamp of that installation on the proposal wrapper; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-3438.
quote: Acceptable evidence to establish the time of receipt at the Government installation includes electronic timestamps, the time/date stamp of that installation on the proposal wrapper,
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO list adds 'electronic timestamps' at the start of the examples of acceptable evidence; the time/date stamp on the proposal wrapper is the same as in codified FAR 15.208(c).

statement: RFO FAR 15.107(b)(3) continues that acceptable evidence includes other documentary evidence of receipt maintained by the installation, or oral testimony or statements of Government personnel.
quote: other documentary evidence of receipt maintained by the installation, or oral testimony or statements of Government personnel.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: RFO FAR 15.107(c) addresses the case in which proposals cannot be received at the Government office designated for receipt of proposals by the exact time specified in the RFP because an emergency or unanticipated event interrupts normal Government processes; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-3440.
quote: If proposals cannot be received at the Government office designated for receipt of proposals by the exact time specified in the RFP because an emergency or unanticipated event interrupts normal Government processes,
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO paragraph puts the interruption first and the RFP in place of the solicitation; the condition is otherwise the same as in codified FAR 15.208(d). The consequence is quoted in the next claim. The differences are in wording only; the text is the same in substance.

statement: RFO FAR 15.107(c) adds that, where urgent Government requirements preclude amendment of the RFP closing date, the time specified for RFP will be deemed to be extended to the same time of day specified in the RFP on the first work day on which normal Government processes resume.
quote: and urgent Government requirements preclude amendment of the RFP closing date, the time specified for RFP will be deemed to be extended to the same time of day specified in the RFP on the first work day on which normal Government processes resume.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text prints 'the time specified for RFP' where codified FAR 15.208(d) says 'the time specified for receipt of proposals'; the extension to the first work day on which normal processes resume is the same. The differences are in wording only; the text is the same in substance.

statement: RFO FAR 15.107(d) says proposals may be withdrawn by written notice at any time before award.
quote: Proposals may be withdrawn by written notice at any time before award.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The wording is the same as the codified paragraph.

statement: RFO FAR 15.107(d)(2) says oral proposals in response to oral RFPs may be withdrawn orally.
quote: Oral proposals in response to oral RFPs may be withdrawn orally.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO paragraph says oral RFPs where codified FAR 15.208(e) says oral solicitations; the oral withdrawal rule is the same. The differences are in wording only; the text is the same in substance.

statement: RFO FAR 15.106(a) says that when the Government changes its requirements or terms and conditions, the contracting officer must amend the RFP.
quote: When the Government changes its requirements or terms and conditions, the contracting officer must amend the RFP.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO sentence uses must where codified FAR 15.206(a) says shall, and the RFP where it says the solicitation; the RFO sentence does not repeat the words 'either before or after receipt of proposals', which RFO paragraphs (a)(1) and (a)(2) address by timing of the amendment.

statement: RFO FAR 15.106(e)(1) says contracting officers must amend the RFP if the Government is interested in a proposal that involves a departure from the stated requirements.
quote: Contracting officers must amend the RFP if the Government is interested in a proposal that involves a departure from the stated requirements.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO sentence uses must where codified FAR 15.206(d) says shall, and ties the duty to the Government being interested in a proposal that involves a departure from the stated requirements; the RFO sentence carries no 'provided' condition, and the next RFO sentence (see the next claim) addresses revealing the alternate solution.

statement: RFO FAR 15.106(e)(1) also says the amendment should not reveal the alternate solution proposed or any other information that is entitled to protection.
quote: The amendment should not reveal the alternate solution proposed or any other information that is entitled to protection.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). Codified FAR 15.206(d) makes the duty to amend subject to 'provided this can be done without revealing' the alternate solution or protected information and cites 15.207(b) and 15.306(e); the RFO text states this as a separate sentence with 'should not reveal' and no cross-reference.

statement: RFO FAR 15.106(e)(2) says contracting officers must cancel the RFP and issue a new one, regardless of the stage of the acquisition, if an amendment is proposed after offers have been received, and a further condition follows; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-3447 and CL-EST-3448.
quote: (2) Contracting officers must cancel the RFP and issue a new one, regardless of the stage of the acquisition if an amendment— (i) Is proposed after offers have been received, and
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text uses must where codified FAR 15.206(e) says shall and sets the conditions out as a list; the further condition is quoted in the next claim.

statement: RFO FAR 15.106(e)(2)(ii) makes it a condition that, in the judgment of the contracting officer, based on market research or otherwise, the amendment has a requirement change that is so substantial it exceeds what prospective offerors reasonably could have anticipated as a change to the RFP; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-EST-3448.
quote: (ii) In the judgment of the contracting officer, based on market research or otherwise, has a requirement change that is so substantial it exceeds what prospective offerors reasonably could have anticipated as a change to the RFP,
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO item words the substantial-change condition about the requirement change and 'as a change to the RFP', where codified FAR 15.206(e) says 'an amendment proposed for issuance after offers have been received is so substantial as to exceed what prospective offerors reasonably could have anticipated'; the contracting officer's judgment, based on market research or otherwise, is kept.

statement: RFO FAR 15.106(e)(2)(ii) adds the condition that additional sources likely would have submitted offers had the change been in the RFP.
quote: and additional sources likely would have submitted offers had the change been in the RFP.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO item says 'had the change been in the RFP' where codified FAR 15.206(e) says 'had the substance of the amendment been known to them'.

statement: RFO FAR 15.102(b)(3)(i) says that when the uniform contract format is not used, contracting officers must ensure competitive RFPs, at a minimum, describe the Government's requirement and any anticipated terms and conditions that will apply to the contract.
quote: When the uniform contract format is not used, contracting officers must ensure— (i) Competitive RFPs, at a minimum, describe the Government's requirement; any anticipated terms and conditions that will apply to the contract;
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.215-10(a), the price reduction rule applies if any price, including profit or fee, negotiated in connection with the contract, or any cost reimbursable under it, was increased by any significant amount because of the grounds quoted in CL-EST-9242, CL-EST-9243 and CL-EST-9244.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.215-10(a)(1), one ground is that the Contractor or a subcontractor furnished certified cost or pricing data that were not complete, accurate, and current as certified in its Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.215-10(a)(2), another ground is that a subcontractor or prospective subcontractor furnished the Contractor certified cost or pricing data that were not complete, accurate, and current as certified in the Contractor's Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data.
quote: (2) A subcontractor or prospective subcontractor furnished the Contractor certified cost or pricing data that were not complete, accurate, and current as certified in the Contractor’s Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data;
note: The RFO clause prints the edition date (Aug 2011), recorded as edition_date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The wording is the same as the codified item apart from the quotation mark style.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.215-10(a)(3), a third ground is that any of these parties furnished data of any description that were not accurate, and the price or cost shall then be reduced accordingly and the contract shall be modified to reflect the reduction.
quote: (3) Any of these parties furnished data of any description that were not accurate, the price or cost shall be reduced accordingly and the contract shall be modified to reflect the reduction.
note: The RFO clause prints the edition date (Aug 2011), recorded as edition_date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The wording is the same as the codified item.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.215-10(c)(1), if the Contracting Officer determines under paragraph (a) that a price or cost reduction should be made, the Contractor agrees not to raise the matters quoted in CL-EST-9246, CL-EST-9247 and CL-EST-9248 as a defense.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.215-10(c)(1)(i), the Contractor may not raise as a defense that the Contractor or subcontractor was a sole source supplier or otherwise was in a superior bargaining position and thus the price of the contract would not have been modified even if accurate, complete, and current certified cost or pricing data had been submitted.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.215-10(c)(1)(ii), the Contractor may not raise as a defense that the Contracting Officer should have known that the certified cost or pricing data in issue were defective even though the Contractor or subcontractor took no affirmative action to bring the character of the data to the attention of the Contracting Officer.

note: The RFO clause prints the edition date (Aug 2011), recorded as edition_date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The wording is the same as the codified item.

quote: (iii) The contract was based on an agreement about the total cost of the contract and there was no agreement about the cost of each item procured under the contract. (iv) The Contractor or subcontractor did not submit a Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data.
note: The RFO clause prints the edition date (Aug 2011), recorded as edition_date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The wording is the same as the codified items.

quote: (d) If any reduction in the contract price under this clause reduces the price of items for which payment was made prior to the date of the modification reflecting the price reduction, the Contractor shall be liable to and shall pay the United States at the time such overpayment is repaid-

note: The RFO clause prints the edition date (Aug 2011), recorded as edition_date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The wording is the same as the codified item.

quote: The OMB Uniform Guidance at 2 CFR part 200, subpart E and appendix III, provides principles for determining the costs applicable to work performed by educational institutions under contracts with the Government.

quote: (b) Any reduction in the contract price under paragraph (a) of this clause due to defective data from a prospective subcontractor that was not subsequently awarded the subcontract shall be limited to the amount, plus applicable overhead and profit markup
note: The RFO clause prints the edition date (Aug 2011), recorded as edition_date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The wording is the same as the codified paragraph. The sentence is quoted in three claims, CL-EST-9259 to CL-EST-9261.

quote: (B) The Contractor proves that the certified cost or pricing data were available before the "as of" date specified on its Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data, and that the data were not submitted before such date.
note: The RFO clause prints the edition date (Aug 2011), recorded as edition_date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0038 makes it effective (CL-CMP-9762). The wording is the same as the codified item.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.215-10(c)(2)(ii)(A), an offset shall not be allowed if the understated data were known by the Contractor to be understated before the "as of" date specified on its Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data.

statement: Under the RFO text of FAR 52.215-10(c)(2)(ii)(B), an offset shall not be allowed if the Government proves that the facts demonstrate that the contract price would not have increased in the amount to be offset even if the available data had been submitted before the "as of" date specified on the Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data.

statement: Cost realism means that the costs in an offeror's proposal are realistic for the work to be performed, reflect a clear understanding of the requirements, and are consistent with the various elements of the offeror's technical proposal.
quote: Cost realism means that the costs in an offeror's proposal— (1) Are realistic for the work to be performed; (2) Reflect a clear understanding of the requirements; and (3) Are consistent with the various elements of the offeror's technical proposal.

statement: Best value means the expected outcome of an acquisition that, in the Government's estimation, provides the greatest overall benefit in response to the requirement.
quote: Best value means the expected outcome of an acquisition that, in the Government's estimation, provides the greatest overall benefit in response to the requirement.

statement: Advisory and assistance services means those services provided under contract by nongovernmental sources to support or improve organizational policy development, decision-making, management and administration, program and/or project management and administration, or R&D activities; the definition continues in CL-EST-9409.
quote: Advisory and assistance services means those services provided under contract by nongovernmental sources to support or improve: organizational policy development; decision-making; management and administration; program and/or project management and administration; or R&D activities.

quote: Broad agency announcement means a general announcement of an agency's research interest including criteria for selecting proposals and soliciting the participation of all offerors capable of satisfying the Government's needs (see 6.102(d)(2)).

statement: Cost or pricing data means all facts that, as of the date of price agreement, or, if applicable, an earlier date agreed upon between the parties that is as close as practicable to the date of agreement on price, prudent buyers and sellers would reasonably expect to affect price negotiations significantly.
quote: means all facts that, as of the date of price agreement, or, if applicable, an earlier date agreed upon between the parties that is as close as practicable to the date of agreement on price, prudent buyers and sellers would reasonably expect to affect price negotiations significantly.

statement: Cost or pricing data are factual, not judgmental, and are verifiable; the definition continues in CL-EST-9417.
quote: Cost or pricing data are factual, not judgmental; and are verifiable.

statement: Certified cost or pricing data means cost or pricing data that were required to be submitted in accordance with FAR 15.403-4 and 15.403-5 and have been certified, or are required to be certified, in accordance with 15.406-2.
quote: Certified cost or pricing data means “cost or pricing data” that were required to be submitted in accordance with FAR 15.403-4 and 15.403-5 and have been certified, or are required to be certified, in accordance with 15.406-2.

statement: The certification of certified cost or pricing data states that, to the best of the person's knowledge and belief, the cost or pricing data are accurate, complete, and current as of a date certain before contract award; the definition continues in CL-EST-9399.
quote: This certification states that, to the best of the person's knowledge and belief, the cost or pricing data are accurate, complete, and current as of a date certain before contract award.

quote: Data other than certified cost or pricing data means pricing data, cost data, and judgmental information necessary for the contracting officer to determine a fair and reasonable price or to determine cost realism.
note: RFO 2.101 (S-0015) has the same wording.

statement: Data other than certified cost or pricing data may include the identical types of data as certified cost or pricing data, consistent with Table 15-2 of FAR 15.408, but without the certification; the definition continues in CL-EST-9400 and CL-EST-9401.
quote: Such data may include the identical types of data as certified cost or pricing data, consistent with Table 15-2 of 15.408, but without the certification.
note: RFO 2.101 (S-0015) has the same wording.

statement: Market research means collecting and analyzing information about capabilities within the market to satisfy agency needs.
quote: Market research means collecting and analyzing information about capabilities within the market to satisfy agency needs.
note: RFO 2.101 (S-0015) has the same wording.

statement: Facilities capital cost of money means cost of money as an element of the cost of facilities capital as used at 48 CFR 9904.414, titled Cost Accounting Standard, Cost of Money as an Element of the Cost of Facilities Capital.
quote: Facilities capital cost of money means “cost of money as an element of the cost of facilities capital” as used at 48 CFR 9904.414—Cost Accounting Standard—Cost of Money as an Element of the Cost of Facilities Capital.

statement: The first paragraph of the definition of nondevelopmental item covers any previously developed item of supply used exclusively for governmental purposes by a Federal agency, a State or local government, or a foreign government with which the United States has a mutual defense cooperation agreement.
quote: (1) Any previously developed item of supply used exclusively for governmental purposes by a Federal agency, a State or local government, or a foreign government with which the United States has a mutual defense cooperation agreement;

statement: Past performance means an offeror's or contractor's performance on active and physically completed contracts, with a cross-reference to 4.804-4.
quote: Past performance means an offeror's or contractor's performance on active and physically completed contracts (see 4.804-4).

statement: An unsolicited proposal is a written proposal for a new or innovative idea that is submitted to an agency on the initiative of the offeror for the purpose of obtaining a contract with the Government, and the definition continues in companion claim CL-EST-9313.
quote: Unsolicited proposal means a written proposal for a new or innovative idea that is submitted to an agency on the initiative of the offeror for the purpose of obtaining a contract with the Government,

statement: The definition of an unsolicited proposal continues that it is not in response to a request for proposals, Broad Agency Announcement, Small Business Innovation Research topic, Small Business Technology Transfer Research topic, Program Research and Development Announcement, or any other Government-initiated solicitation or program.
quote: and that is not in response to a request for proposals, Broad Agency Announcement, Small Business Innovation Research topic, Small Business Technology Transfer Research topic, Program Research and Development Announcement, or any other Government-initiated solicitation or program.

statement: A solicitation provision or provision is a term or condition used only in solicitations and applying only before contract award.
quote: Solicitation provision or provision means a term or condition used only in solicitations and applying only before contract award.
