statement: Unless otherwise agreed to by the concerned agencies, the part is not applicable to listed categories, one of which is food resources, food resource facilities, livestock resources, veterinary resources, plant health resources and the domestic distribution of farm equipment and commercial fertilizer.
quote: Unless otherwise agreed to by the concerned agencies, the provisions of this part are not applicable to: (i) Food resources, food resource facilities, livestock resources, veterinary resources, plant health resources, and the domestic distribution of farm equipment and commercial fertilizer
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.10(c)(1)(i); the section lists further excluded categories.

statement: The regulation establishes two levels of priority, identified by the rating symbols DO and DX.
quote: (1) There are two levels of priority established by this regulation, identified by the rating symbols “DO” and “DX.”
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.11(a)(1).

statement: All DO rated orders have equal priority with each other and take preference over unrated orders, and all DX rated orders have equal priority with each other and take preference over DO rated orders and unrated orders.
quote: (2) All DO rated orders have equal priority with each other and take preference over unrated orders. All DX rated orders have equal priority with each other and take preference over DO rated orders and unrated orders.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.11(a)(2).

statement: A Directive issued by Commerce takes preference over any DX rated order, DO rated order or unrated order, as stipulated in the Directive.
quote: (3) In addition, a Directive issued by Commerce takes preference over any DX rated order, DO rated order, or unrated order, as stipulated in the Directive.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.11(a)(3).

statement: Program identification symbols do not in themselves connote any priority, and a priority rating consists of the rating symbol, DO or DX, and the program identification symbol.
quote: Program identification symbols, in themselves, do not connote any priority. (c) Priority ratings. A priority rating consists of the rating symbol—DO and DX—and the program identification symbol, such as A1, A7, or N1.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.11(b) and (c).

statement: The priority rating on a rated order may be changed or cancelled by an official action of the Department of Commerce or by written notification from the person who placed the rated order, including a Delegate Agency.
quote: (a) The priority rating on a rated order may be changed or cancelled by: (1) An official action of the Department of Commerce; or (2) Written notification from the person who placed the rated order (including a Delegate Agency).
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.16(a).

statement: An amendment to a rated order that significantly alters a supplier's original production or delivery schedule constitutes a new rated order as of the date of its receipt, and the supplier must accept or reject the amended order.
quote: (c) An amendment to a rated order that significantly alters a supplier's original production or delivery schedule shall constitute a new rated order as of the date of its receipt. The supplier must accept or reject the amended order according to the provisions of § 700.13.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.16(c).

statement: A person must cancel any rated orders that the person or a predecessor in interest has placed with suppliers, or cancel the priority ratings on those orders, if the person no longer needs the items in those orders to fill a rated order.
quote: (e) A person must cancel any rated orders that the person (or a predecessor in interest) has placed with suppliers or cancel the priority ratings on those orders if the person no longer needs the items in those orders to fill a rated order.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.16(e).

statement: Among the things a person must use rated orders to obtain are items that will be physically incorporated into other items to fill rated orders, including the portion of such items normally consumed or converted into scrap or by-products in the course of processing.
quote: (a) A person must use rated orders to obtain: (1) Items which will be physically incorporated into other items to fill rated orders, including that portion of such items normally consumed, or converted into scrap or by-products, in the course of processing;
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.17(a)(1).

statement: One listed thing a person must use rated orders to obtain is MRO needed to produce the finished items to fill rated orders, and the priority rating used for MRO must contain the program identification symbol H7 along with the rating symbol on the customer's rated order.
quote: (4) MRO needed to produce the finished items to fill rated orders. However, for MRO, the priority rating used must contain the program identification symbol H7 along with the rating symbol contained on the customer's rated order.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.17(a)(4); the printed sections do not define MRO.

statement: A person may use a rated order to replace inventoried items, including finished items, that were used to fill rated orders, and one listed condition is that the order be placed within 90 days of the date of use of the inventory.
quote: (b) A person may use a rated order to replace inventoried items (including finished items) if such items were used to fill rated orders, as follows: (1) The order must be placed within ninety (90) days of the date of use of the inventory.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.17(b)(1).

statement: One listed condition for a rated order that replaces inventoried items is that it use a DO rating symbol and the program identification symbol on the customer's rated order, and a DX rating symbol may not be used even if the inventory was used to fill a DX rated order.
quote: (2) A DO rating symbol and the program identification symbol indicated on the customer's rated order must be used on the order. A DX rating symbol may not be used even if the inventory was used to fill a DX rated order.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.17(b)(2).

statement: A person may not place a rated order unless the person is in receipt of a rated order, has been explicitly authorized to do so by the Department of Commerce or a Delegate Agency, or is otherwise permitted to do so by the part.
quote: (a) General limitations. (1) A person may not place a rated order pursuant to this part unless the person is in receipt of a rated order, has been explicitly authorized to do so by the Department of Commerce or a Delegate Agency or is otherwise permitted to do so by this part.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.18(a)(1).

statement: Rated orders may not be used to obtain delivery on a date earlier than needed, or a greater quantity of the item than needed except to obtain a minimum procurable quantity.
quote: (2) Rated orders may not be used to obtain: (i) Delivery on a date earlier than needed; (ii) A greater quantity of the item than needed, except to obtain a minimum procurable quantity;
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.18(a)(2)(i) and (ii); the list continues in the same paragraph.

statement: One listed thing rated orders may not be used to obtain is items in advance of the receipt of a rated order, except as specifically authorized by the Department of Commerce.
quote: (iii) Items in advance of the receipt of a rated order, except as specifically authorized by the Department of Commerce (see § 700.51(c) for information on obtaining authorization for a priority rating in advance of a rated order);
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.18(a)(2)(iii); the quote points to § 700.51(c), which is not printed here.

statement: One listed group of items for which rated orders may not be used, unless specific priority rating authority has been obtained from a Delegate Agency or the Department of Commerce, is items for plant improvement, expansion or construction, unless they will be physically incorporated into a construction project covered by a rated order.
quote: Any of the following items unless specific priority rating authority has been obtained from a Delegate Agency or the Department of Commerce: (A) Items for plant improvement, expansion, or construction, unless they will be physically incorporated into a construction project covered by a rated order;
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.18(a)(2)(iv)(A).

statement: One listed item is production or construction equipment or items to be used for the manufacture of production equipment.
quote: (B) Production or construction equipment or items to be used for the manufacture of production equipment
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.18(a)(2)(iv)(B); it sits in the same list as the preceding claim.

statement: Notwithstanding any authorization or requirement elsewhere in the part, no person may place a rated order to obtain listed items, one of which is copper raw materials, unless such order is authorized by an official action of the Department of Commerce.
quote: Notwithstanding any authorization or requirement to place a rated order stated elsewhere in this part, no person may place a rated order to obtain the following items unless such order is authorized by an official action of the Department of Commerce. (1) Copper raw materials.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.18(b); the list continues with other items.

statement: For projects believed to maximize domestic energy supplies, a person may request priority rating authority for scarce, critical and essential supplies of materials, equipment and services; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-IND-0183.
quote: (a) For projects believed to maximize domestic energy supplies, a person may request priority rating authority for scarce, critical, and essential supplies of materials, equipment, and services
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.21(a).

statement: A person may request priority rating authority for scarce, critical and essential supplies of materials, equipment and services (related to the production of materials or equipment, or the installation, repair or maintenance of equipment) by submitting a request to the Department of Energy.
quote: a person may request priority rating authority for scarce, critical, and essential supplies of materials, equipment, and services (related to the production of materials or equipment, or the installation, repair, or maintenance of equipment) by submitting a request to the Department of Energy.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.21(a); the first part of the sentence is claim CL-IND-0182.

statement: If the Department of Energy notifies the Department of Commerce that the project maximizes domestic energy supplies and that the materials, equipment or services are critical and essential, the Department of Commerce will determine whether the items in question are scarce; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-IND-0216.
quote: (b) If the Department of Energy notifies the Department of Commerce that the project maximizes domestic energy supplies and that the materials, equipment, or services are critical and essential, the Department of Commerce will determine whether the items in question are scarce
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.21(b); the sentence goes on to a second finding about need to use the priorities authority.

statement: After its analysis, the Department of Commerce will advise the Department of Energy whether the two findings have been satisfied, and if they are satisfied it will authorize the Department of Energy to grant the use of a priority rating to the applicant.
quote: After the Department of Commerce has conducted its analysis, it will advise the Department of Energy whether the two findings have been satisfied. If the findings are satisfied, the Department of Commerce will authorize the Department of Energy to grant the use of a priority rating to the applicant.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.21(c).

statement: Before using its allocations authority to address a supply problem within its resource jurisdiction, the Department of Commerce will develop a plan with listed contents.
quote: Before the Department of Commerce uses its allocations authority to address a supply problem within its resource jurisdiction, it will develop a plan that includes:
note: Source is the lead-in of 15 CFR 700.31.

statement: Three listed contents of the plan are a statement of the specific objectives of the allocation action, a list of the materials, services or facilities to be allocated, and a list or description of the sources subject to the action.
quote: (c) A statement of the specific objective(s) of the allocation action; (d) A list of the materials, services, or facilities to be allocated; (e) A list or description of the sources of the materials, services, or facilities that will be subject to the allocation action;
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.31(c) to (e).

statement: Allocation orders may be issued directly to the affected persons, by constructive notice through publication in the Federal Register, or by publication of a temporary final rule in the Federal Register.
quote: Allocation orders may be issued directly to the affected persons, by constructive notice to the parties through publication in the Federal Register, or by the publication of a temporary final rule in the Federal Register.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.34, opening sentence.

statement: Every allocation order must include a detailed description of the required allocation action, including its relationship to previously or subsequently received DX rated orders, DO rated orders and unrated orders.
quote: Elements to be included in all allocation orders. (1) A detailed description of the required allocation action(s), including its relationship to previously or subsequently received DX rated orders, DO rated orders, and unrated orders.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.34(a)(1).

statement: One listed element of every allocation order is specific start and end calendar dates for each required allocation action.
quote: (2) Specific start and end calendar dates for each required allocation action.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.34(a)(2).

statement: An allocation order issued directly to affected persons must include a statement that reads in substance that it is an allocation order certified for national defense use.
quote: (b) Elements to be included in orders issued directly to affected persons. (1) A statement that reads in substance: “This is an allocation order certified for national defense use.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.34(b)(1).

statement: The printed section 700.34 was revised, effective August 27, 2026, through August 27, 2027.
quote: Effective Date Note: At 91 FR 50705, Aug. 6, 2026, § 700.34 was revised, effective Aug. 27, 2026, through Aug. 27, 2027.
note: Source is the effective date note after 15 CFR 700.34.

statement: Audits and investigations are official actions involving the examination of books, records, documents, other writings and information to ensure that the Defense Production Act, the Selective Service Act and related statutes, and the part have been properly followed.
quote: (a) Audits and investigations are official actions involving the examination of books, records, documents, other writings, and information to ensure that the provisions of the Defense Production Act, the Selective Service Act and related statutes, and this part have been properly followed.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.71(a).

statement: The Department of Commerce may issue administrative subpoenas, which constitute official actions.
quote: (c) In administering this part, the Department of Commerce may issue the following documents, which constitute official actions: (1) Administrative subpoenas.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.71(c)(1); the section describes the subpoena further.

statement: One listed document, a demand for information, requires a person to furnish to a duly authorized representative of the Department of Commerce any information necessary or appropriate to the enforcement or the administration of the Defense Production Act, the Selective Service Act or the part.
quote: Demand for information. A demand for information requires a person to furnish to a duly authorized representative of the Department of Commerce any information necessary or appropriate to the enforcement or the administration of the Defense Production Act, the Selective Service Act, or this part.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.71(c)(2).

statement: Willful violation of the listed provisions of the Defense Production Act, the priorities provisions of the Selective Service Act and related statutes, or the part is a crime, and upon conviction a person may be punished by fine or imprisonment, or both; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-IND-0217.
quote: (a) Willful violation of the provisions of Title I or sections 705 or 707 of the Defense Production Act, the priorities provisions of the Selective Service Act and related statutes or this part is a crime and upon conviction, a person may be punished by fine or imprisonment, or both
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.74(a).

statement: The government may also seek an injunction from a court of appropriate jurisdiction to prohibit the continuance of any violation of, or to enforce compliance with, the Defense Production Act, the part, or an official action.
quote: (b) The government may also seek an injunction from a court of appropriate jurisdiction to prohibit the continuance of any violation of, or to enforce compliance with, the Defense Production Act, this part, or an official action.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.74(b).

statement: The adjustments or exceptions process applies to the part and to official actions issued under it, except for Directive Allocation Orders issued by a temporary final rule.
quote: The adjustments or exceptions described in this section apply to this part and official actions issued under this part, except for Directive Allocation Orders issued by a temporary final rule.
note: Source is the opening of 15 CFR 700.80.

statement: A person may submit a request to the Office of Strategic Industries and Economic Security of the Department of Commerce for an adjustment or exception on listed grounds.
quote: (a) A person may submit a request to the Office of Strategic Industries and Economic Security, U.S. Department of Commerce, for an adjustment or exception on the ground that:
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.80(a), lead-in.

statement: One listed ground for an adjustment or exception is that a provision of the part or an official action results in an undue or exceptional hardship on that person not suffered generally by others in similar situations and circumstances.
quote: (1) A provision of this part or an official action results in an undue or exceptional hardship on that person not suffered generally by others in similar situations and circumstances;
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.80(a)(1).

statement: One listed ground for an adjustment or exception is that the consequence of following a provision of the part or an official action is contrary to the intent of the Defense Production Act, the Selective Service Act and related statutes, or the part.
quote: (2) The consequence of following a provision of this part or an official action is contrary to the intent of the Defense Production Act, the Selective Service Act and related statutes, or this part.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.80(a)(2).

statement: The Office of Strategic Industries and Economic Security shall respond to requests for adjustment of or exceptions to compliance within 25 days, not including Saturdays, Sundays or Government holidays, of the date of receipt.
quote: The Office of Strategic Industries and Economic Security shall respond to requests for adjustment of or exceptions to compliance with the provisions of this part or an official action within twenty-five (25) days, not including Saturdays, Sundays or Government holidays, of the date of receipt.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.80(c).

statement: A request for adjustment or exception does not relieve any person from complying with the part or official action in question while the request is being considered, unless such interim relief is granted in writing.
quote: The submission of a request for adjustment or exception shall not relieve any person from the obligation of complying with the provisions of this part or official action in question while the request is being considered unless such interim relief is granted in writing
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.80(c), first sentence.

statement: A person whose request for adjustment or exception has been denied by the Office of Strategic Industries and Economic Security may appeal to the Assistant Secretary for Export Administration, who shall review and reconsider the denial.
quote: Any person who has had a request for adjustment or exception denied by the Office of Strategic Industries and Economic Security under § 700.80, may appeal to the Assistant Secretary for Export Administration, Department of Commerce, who shall review and reconsider the denial.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.81(a).

statement: An appeal of a denied request must be received by the Assistant Secretary for Export Administration no later than 45 days after receipt of a written notice of denial; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-IND-0329.
quote: Appeals of denied requests for exceptions from or adjustments to compliance with the provisions of this part or an official action must be received by the Assistant Secretary for Export Administration no later than forty-five (45) days after receipt of a written notice of denial
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.81(b); the next sentence of the section lets the Assistant Secretary accept a later appeal at discretion.

statement: The decision of the Assistant Secretary for Export Administration shall be made within a reasonable time after receipt of the appeal and shall be the final administrative action.
quote: (h) The decision of the Assistant Secretary for Export Administration shall be made within a reasonable time after receipt of the appeal and shall be the final administrative action.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.81(h).

statement: The printed section 700.80 was amended, effective August 27, 2026, through August 27, 2027.
quote: Effective Date Note: At 91 FR 50705, Aug. 6, 2026, § 700.80 was amended, effective Aug. 27, 2026, through Aug. 27, 2027.
note: Source is the effective date note after 15 CFR 700.80.

statement: Persons are required to make and preserve for at least three years accurate and complete records of any transaction covered by the part or an official action.
quote: (a) Persons are required to make and preserve for at least three years, accurate and complete records of any transaction covered by this part (OMB control number 0694-0053) or an official action.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.91(a).

statement: Records must be maintained in sufficient detail to permit the determination, upon examination, of whether each transaction complies with the part or any official action, and the part does not specify any particular method or system to be used.
quote: (b) Records must be maintained in sufficient detail to permit the determination, upon examination, of whether each transaction complies with the provisions of this part or any official action. However, this part does not specify any particular method or system to be used.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.91(b).

statement: Records required to be maintained by the part must be made available for examination on demand by duly authorized representatives of the Department of Commerce.
quote: (c) Records required to be maintained by this part must be made available for examination on demand by duly authorized representatives of the Department of Commerce as provided in § 700.71.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.91(c).

statement: The part and all official actions, unless specifically stated otherwise, apply to transactions in any state, territory or possession of the United States and the District of Columbia.
quote: (a) This part and all official actions, unless specifically stated otherwise, apply to transactions in any state, territory, or possession of the United States and the District of Columbia.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.92(a).

statement: The part and all official actions apply not only to deliveries to other persons but also to deliveries to affiliates and subsidiaries of a person and deliveries from one branch, division or section of a single entity to another under common ownership or control.
quote: This part and all official actions apply not only to deliveries to other persons but also include deliveries to affiliates and subsidiaries of a person and deliveries from one branch, division, or section of a single entity to another branch, division, or section under common ownership or control.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.92(b).

statement: The small-order level below which a person is not required to place a priority rating on an order is $125,000 or one half of the Simplified Acquisition Threshold, whichever amount is greater; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-IND-0214.
quote: A person is not required to place a priority rating on an order for less than $125,000, or one half of the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (as established in the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR)) (see FAR section 2.101), whichever amount is greater
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.17(f); the timely-delivery proviso is the next claim.

statement: The relief from placing a priority rating on a small order applies provided that delivery can be obtained in a timely fashion without the use of the priority rating.
quote: provided that delivery can be obtained in a timely fashion without the use of the priority rating.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.17(f); the small-order level is the previous claim.

statement: The listed amendments to a rated order do not constitute a new rated order: a change in shipping destination; a reduction in the total amount of the order; and an increase in the total amount of the order which has negligible impact upon deliveries.
quote: (d) The following amendments do not constitute a new rated order: a change in shipping destination; a reduction in the total amount of the order; an increase in the total amount of the order which has negligible impact upon deliveries;

statement: The Department of Commerce will determine whether the items in question are scarce and, if they are scarce, whether there is a need to use the priorities authority.
quote: the Department of Commerce will determine whether the items in question are scarce, and, if they are scarce, whether there is a need to use the priorities authority.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.21(b); it follows the notification from the Department of Energy described in CL-IND-0184.

statement: The punishment by fine or imprisonment, or both, for a willful violation is as provided in sections 103 and 705 of the Defense Production Act and in section 468(f) of the Selective Service Act.
quote: or both as provided in sections 103 and 705 of the Defense Production Act and in section 468(f) of the Selective Service Act.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.74(a); the printed section states no fine amount or term of imprisonment.

statement: No person shall deliver any item if the person knows or has reason to believe that the item will be accepted, redelivered, held, or used in violation of the Defense Production Act, the part, or an official action.
quote: (3) No person shall deliver any item if the person knows or has reason to believe that the item will be accepted, redelivered, held, or used in violation of the Defense Production Act, this part, or an official action.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.74(c)(3).

statement: After the 45-day period, an appeal may be accepted at the discretion of the Assistant Secretary for Export Administration.
quote: After this forty-five (45) day period, an appeal may be accepted at the discretion of the Assistant Secretary for Export Administration.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.81(b).

statement: Each request for adjustment or exception must be in writing and contain a complete statement of all the facts and circumstances related to the provision of the part or official action from which adjustment is sought and a full and precise statement of the reasons why relief should be provided.
quote: (b) Each request for adjustment or exception must be in writing and contain a complete statement of all the facts and circumstances related to the provision of this part or official action from which adjustment is sought and a full and precise statement of the reasons why relief should be provided.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.80(b).

statement: Persons must also develop, maintain and submit to the Department of Commerce any other records and reports that may be required for the administration of the Defense Production Act, the Selective Service Act and related statutes, and the part.
quote: (d) In addition, persons must develop, maintain, and submit any other records and reports to the Department of Commerce that may be required for the administration of the Defense Production Act, the Selective Service Act and related statutes, and this part.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.91(d).

statement: When undertaking an audit, investigation or other inquiry, the Department of Commerce shall define the scope and purpose in the official action given to the person under investigation; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-IND-0330.
quote: (b) When undertaking an audit, investigation, or other inquiry, the Department of Commerce shall: (1) Define the scope and purpose in the official action given to the person under investigation
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.71(b)(1); the section adds a second duty on Commerce.

statement: The adjustment or exception process for Directive Allocation Orders issued by a temporary final rule is contained in each Directive Allocation Order.
quote: The adjustment or exception process for Directive Allocation Orders issued by a temporary final rule are contained in each Directive Allocation Order, see supplement no. 1 to part 700, paragraph (c).
note: Source is the second sentence of 15 CFR 700.80.

statement: The submission of an appeal does not relieve any person from the obligation of complying with the part or official action in question while the appeal is being considered, unless such relief is granted in writing.
quote: (g) The submission of an appeal under this section shall not relieve any person from the obligation of complying with the provisions of this part or official action in question while the appeal is being considered, unless such relief is granted in writing
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.81(g).

statement: A person adding a rating to an unrated order, or changing or cancelling a priority rating, must promptly notify all suppliers to whom the order was sent of the addition, change or cancellation.
quote: (f) A person adding a rating to an unrated order, or changing or cancelling a priority rating must promptly notify all suppliers to whom the order was sent of the addition, change or cancellation.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.16(f).

statement: If an unrated order is amended so as to make it a rated order, or a DO rating is changed to a DX rating, the supplier must give the appropriate preferential treatment to the order as of the date the change is received by the supplier.
quote: (b) If an unrated order is amended so as to make it a rated order, or a DO rating is changed to a DX rating, the supplier must give the appropriate preferential treatment to the order as of the date the change is received by the supplier.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.16(b).

statement: Separate rated orders may not be placed solely for obtaining minimum procurable quantities on each order if the minimum procurable quantity would be sufficient to cover more than one rated order.
quote: (3) Separate rated orders may not be placed solely for obtaining minimum procurable quantities on each order if the minimum procurable quantity would be sufficient to cover more than one rated order.
note: Source is 15 CFR 700.18(a)(3).

statement: The amendments that do not constitute a new rated order also include a minor variation in size or design before the start of production and a change agreed upon between the supplier and the customer.
quote: a minor variation in size or design (prior to the start of production); or a change which is agreed upon between the supplier and the customer.

statement: Once a priority rating has been authorized under this part, further action by the Department of Commerce generally is not needed.
quote: Once a priority rating has been authorized pursuant to this part, further action by the Department of Commerce generally is not needed.

statement: In the event that problems occur, as the preceding sentence anticipates, a person should immediately contact the appropriate contract administration officer or the Department of Commerce for guidance or assistance.
quote: In this event, a person should immediately contact the appropriate contract administration officer or the Department of Commerce for guidance or assistance.

statement: Special priorities assistance is a service provided to alleviate problems that do arise.
quote: Special priorities assistance is a service provided to alleviate problems that do arise.

statement: If additional formal aid is needed for a rated order placed by a Delegate Agency, special priorities assistance should be sought from the Delegate Agency through the contract administration officer.
quote: If additional formal aid is needed for a rated order placed by a Delegate Agency, special priorities assistance should be sought from the Delegate Agency through the contract administration officer.

statement: If the Delegate Agency is unable to resolve the problem or to authorize the use of a priority rating and believes additional assistance is warranted, the Delegate Agency may forward the request to the Department of Commerce for action.
quote: If the Delegate Agency is unable to resolve the problem or to authorize the use of a priority rating and believes additional assistance is warranted, the Delegate Agency may forward the request to the Department of Commerce for action.

statement: If additional formal aid is needed for a rated order placed by other authorized persons, special priorities assistance should be sought from the Department of Commerce.
quote: If additional formal aid is needed for a rated order placed by other authorized persons, special priorities assistance should be sought from the Department of Commerce.

statement: Special priorities assistance may be provided for any reason consistent with this part, such as assisting in obtaining timely deliveries of items needed to satisfy rated orders or authorizing the use of priority ratings on orders to obtain items not otherwise ratable under this part.
quote: Special priorities assistance may be provided for any reason consistent with this part, such as assisting in obtaining timely deliveries of items needed to satisfy rated orders or authorizing the use of priority ratings on orders to obtain items not otherwise ratable under this part.

statement: If the Department of Commerce is unable to resolve the problem or to authorize the use of a priority rating and believes additional assistance is warranted, the Department of Commerce may forward the request to another agency, identified in § 700.10(c), as appropriate, for action.
quote: If the Department of Commerce is unable to resolve the problem or to authorize the use of a priority rating and believes additional assistance is warranted, the Department of Commerce may forward the request to another agency, identified in § 700.10(c), as appropriate, for action.

statement: A request for special priorities assistance must be submitted on Form BIS-999 (OMB control number 0694-0057) to the local contract administration representative or to the Department of Commerce.
quote: A request for special priorities assistance must be submitted on Form BIS-999 (OMB control number 0694-0057) to the local contract administration representative or to the Department of Commerce.

statement: Form BIS-999 may be obtained from the Delegate Agency representative or from the Department of Commerce.
quote: Form BIS-999 may be obtained from the Delegate Agency representative or from the Department of Commerce.

statement: A sample Form BIS-999 is attached at appendix I, and a fillable Form BIS-999 may be obtained from the website the paragraph gives.
quote: A sample Form BIS-999 is attached at appendix I. A fillable Form BIS-999 may be obtained on the following website:

statement: If a rated order is likely to be delayed because a person is unable to obtain items not normally rated under this part, the person may request the authority to use a priority rating in ordering the needed items.
quote: If a rated order is likely to be delayed because a person is unable to obtain items not normally rated under this part, the person may request the authority to use a priority rating in ordering the needed items.

statement: Priority ratings may be authorized for items such as production or construction equipment, computers not used as production items, and expansion, rebuilding or replacing plant facilities.
quote: Examples of items for which priority ratings may be authorized include: (1) Production or construction equipment; (2) Computers when not used as production items; and (3) Expansion, rebuilding or replacing plant facilities.

quote: The procuring agency contracting officer, or authorized representative, designates the proper NAICS code and corresponding size standard in a solicitation, selecting the single NAICS code which best describes the principal purpose of the product or service being acquired.

quote: A procurement is generally classified according to the component which accounts for the greatest percentage of contract value.

statement: The alternative listed option is to divide the solicitation into discrete categories, such as line items or special item numbers, and assign each discrete category the single NAICS code and corresponding size standard; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MKT-1839.
quote: Multiple Award Contract; or (ii) Divide the solicitation into discrete categories (such as Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs), Special Item Numbers (SINs), Sectors, Functional Areas (FAs), or the equivalent), and assign each discrete category the single NAICS code and corresponding size standard

statement: A concern must meet the applicable size standard for each category, such as a line item or special item number, for which it seeks an award as a small business concern.
quote: A concern must meet the applicable size standard for each category (CLIN, SIN, Sector, FA or equivalent) for which it seeks an award as a small business concern.

statement: The contracting officer must assign a single NAICS code to each order issued against a Multiple Award Contract, and that code must be one included in the underlying Multiple Award Contract.
quote: The contracting officer must assign a single NAICS code for each order issued against a Multiple Award Contract. The NAICS code assigned to an order must be a NAICS code included in the underlying Multiple Award Contract.

statement: A concern, including its affiliates, must qualify as small under the NAICS code assigned to a contract as of the date the concern submits a written self-certification that it is small to the procuring activity as part of its initial offer or response that includes price.
quote: A concern, including its affiliates, must qualify as small under the NAICS code assigned to a contract as of the date the concern submits a written self-certification that it is small to the procuring activity as part of its initial offer or response which includes price.

statement: If a single NAICS code is assigned to a multiple award contract, SBA determines size status for the underlying multiple award contract as of the date a business concern submits its initial offer, which includes price.
quote: If a single NAICS code is assigned to a multiple award contract as set forth in § 121.402(c)(1)(i), SBA determines size status for the underlying multiple award contract as of the date a business concern submits its initial offer (or other formal response to a solicitation), which includes price

statement: Where an order is set aside for small business under an unrestricted multiple award contract, SBA determines size status for each order as of the date a business concern submits its initial offer or other formal response to a solicitation.
quote: Where an order is set-aside for small business under an unrestricted multiple award contract, SBA determines size status for each order placed against the multiple award contract as of the date a business concern submits its initial offer (or other formal response to a solicitation)

statement: For an order under a set-aside or reserved multiple award contract, SBA determines size status as of the date a business concern submits its initial offer, which includes price, for the set-aside or reserved multiple award contract, unless a contracting officer requests size recertification with respect to a specific order.
quote: SBA determines size status as of the date a business concern submits its initial offer, which includes price, for the set-aside or reserved multiple award contract, unless a contracting officer requests size recertification with respect to a specific order.

statement: For subcontracting purposes, a concern must qualify as small as of the date that it certifies that it is small for the subcontract.
quote: For subcontracting purposes, a concern must qualify as small as of the date that it certifies that it is small for the subcontract.

statement: A follow-on or renewal contract is a new contracting action, so size is determined as of the date the concern submits a written self-certification that it is small as part of its initial offer, including price, for that contract.
quote: A follow-on or renewal contract is a new contracting action. As such, size is determined as of the date the concern submits a written self-certification that it is small to the procuring agency as part of its initial offer including price for the follow-on or renewal contract.

statement: The section addresses how a small business concern qualifies to provide manufactured products or other supply items under a small business set-aside, service-disabled veteran-owned small business, HUBZone, WOSB or EDWOSB, or 8(a) contract.
quote: How does a small business concern qualify to provide manufactured products or other supply items under a small business set-aside, service-disabled veteran-owned small business, HUBZone, WOSB or EDWOSB, or 8(a) contract?

statement: An offeror must either be the manufacturer or producer of the end item being procured, which must be manufactured or produced in the United States, or comply with the requirements of paragraph (b), (c) or (d) of that section; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MKT-0527.
quote: an offeror must either: (1) Be the manufacturer or producer of the end item being procured (and the end item must be manufactured or produced in the United States); or (2) Comply with the requirements of paragraph (b), (c) or (d) of this section

statement: A firm may qualify as a small business concern for a requirement to provide manufactured products or other supply items as a nonmanufacturer if it meets the conditions listed after this lead-in.
quote: (b) Nonmanufacturers. (1) A firm may qualify as a small business concern for a requirement to provide manufactured products or other supply items as a nonmanufacturer if it:

statement: One listed nonmanufacturer condition is that the firm does not exceed 500 employees, or 150 employees for the Information Technology Value Added Reseller exception to NAICS code 541519.
quote: (i) Does not exceed 500 employees (or 150 employees for the Information Technology Value Added Reseller exception to NAICS Code 541519, which is found at § 121.201, footnote 18);

statement: Two further listed nonmanufacturer conditions are that the firm is primarily engaged in the retail or wholesale trade and normally sells the type of item being supplied, and that it takes ownership or possession of the items with its personnel, equipment or facilities in a manner consistent with industry practice.

statement: The last listed nonmanufacturer condition is that the firm will supply the end item of a small business manufacturer, processor or producer made in the United States, or obtains a waiver of that requirement.

quote: The nonmanufacturer rule applies only to procurements that have been assigned a manufacturing or supply NAICS code, or the Information Technology Value Added Resellers (ITVAR) exception to NAICS code 541519.

statement: In a multiple item acquisition, if at least 50 percent of the estimated contract value is composed of items manufactured by small business concerns, a waiver of the nonmanufacturer rule is not required.
quote: Multiple item acquisitions. (1) If at least 50% of the estimated contract value is composed of items that are manufactured by small business concerns, then a waiver of the nonmanufacturer rule is not required.

statement: A waiver for a class of products will be granted when there are no small business manufacturers or processors available to participate in the Federal market for that class of products.
quote: A waiver for a class of products (class waiver) will be granted when there are no small business manufacturers or processors available to participate in the Federal market for that class of products.

statement: Contractors that have been awarded or have performed a contract to supply a specific class of products to the Federal Government within 24 months from the date of the waiver request count as available to participate in the Federal market; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MKT-0529.
quote: Available to participate in the context of the Federal market means that contractors exist that have been awarded or have performed a contract to supply a specific class of products to the Federal Government within 24 months from the date of the request for waiver

statement: An individual waiver for an item in a solicitation will be approved when the SBA Director, Office of Government Contracting, reviews and accepts a contracting officer's determination that no small business manufacturer or processor can reasonably be expected to offer a product; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MKT-0549.
quote: An individual waiver for an item in a solicitation will be approved when the SBA Director, Office of Government Contracting, reviews and accepts a contracting officer's determination that no small business manufacturer or processor can reasonably be expected to offer a product
