quote: An individual waiver applies only to the contract for which it is granted and does not apply to modifications outside the scope of the contract or other procurement actions (e.g., follow-on or bridge contracts).

statement: Any interested person, business, association, or Federal agency may submit a request for a waiver for a particular class of products.
quote: Any interested person, business, association, or Federal agency may submit a request for a waiver for a particular class of products.

statement: A request for a class waiver need not be in any particular form, but should include a statement of the class of products, the applicable NAICS code, and detailed information on the efforts made to identify small business manufacturers or processors for the class.
quote: Requests for a waiver of a class of products need not be in any particular form, but should include a statement of the class of products to be waived, the applicable NAICS code, and detailed information on the efforts made to identify small business manufacturers or processors for the class.

statement: A contracting officer's request for an individual waiver need not be in any particular form but must, at a minimum, include listed items, the first of which is a definitive statement of each specific item sought to be waived and justification as to why the item is required.
quote: A contracting officer's request for a waiver of the Nonmanufacturer Rule for specific solicitations need not be in any particular form, but must, at a minimum, include: (i) A definitive statement of each specific item sought to be waived and justification as to why the specific item is required;

statement: If SBA's research verifies that no small business manufacturers or processors exist for the item, the Director, Office of Government Contracting will grant an individual, one-time waiver.
quote: If SBA's research verifies that no small business manufacturers or processors exist for the item, the Director, Office of Government Contracting will grant an individual, one-time waiver.

statement: Where a procurement or order has been restricted to or reserved for small businesses or a particular group of small businesses, the entities listed in the paragraph may file a size protest in connection with it.
quote: or any instance in which a procurement or order has been restricted to or reserved for small businesses or a particular group of small businesses (including a partial set-aside), the following entities may file a size protest

statement: The same list includes any offeror that the contracting officer has not eliminated from consideration for any procurement-related reason, such as non-responsiveness, technical unacceptability or outside of the competitive range, and the contracting officer.
quote: (i) Any offeror that the contracting officer has not eliminated from consideration for any procurement-related reason, such as non-responsiveness, technical unacceptability or outside of the competitive range; (ii) The contracting officer;

statement: The same list includes the SBA Government Contracting Area Director having responsibility for the area in which the headquarters of the protested offeror is located, regardless of the location of a parent company or affiliates, and the Director, Office of Government Contracting.
quote: (iii) The SBA Government Contracting Area Director having responsibility for the area in which the headquarters of the protested offeror is located, regardless of the location of a parent company or affiliates, the Director, Office of Government Contracting

statement: For an unrestricted Government procurement in which a business concern has represented itself as a small business concern, any offeror and the contracting officer may protest, among the listed entities.
quote: For any unrestricted Government procurement in which a business concern has represented itself as a small business concern, the following entities may protest in connection with a particular procurement: (i) Any offeror; (ii) The contracting officer;

statement: A protest keyed to bid opening must be received by the contracting officer before the close of business on the fifth day, exclusive of Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays, after bid opening for the contract.
quote: (i) A protest must be received by the contracting officer prior to the close of business on the 5th day, exclusive of Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays, after bid opening for (A) The contract;

statement: Where the contracting officer notifies the protestor of the identity of the prospective awardee, a protest must be received by the contracting officer before the close of business on the fifth day, exclusive of Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays, after that notice for the contract.
quote: A protest must be received by the contracting officer prior to the close of business on the 5th day, exclusive of Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays, after the contracting officer has notified the protestor of the identity of the prospective awardee for (i) The contract;

statement: The protest time limits do not apply to contracting officers, funding agreement officers or SBA, who may file protests before or after awards, except to the extent set forth in paragraph (e) of that section; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MKT-1840.
quote: The time limitations in paragraph (a) of this section do not apply to contracting officers, funding agreement officers or SBA, and they may file protests before or after awards, except to the extent set forth in paragraph (e) of this section

statement: When SBA receives a size protest, the SBA Area Director for Government Contracting, or designee, will notify the contracting officer, the protested concern, and the protestor that the protest has been received.
quote: When SBA receives a size protest, the SBA Area Director for Government Contracting, or designee, will notify the contracting officer, the protested concern, and the protestor that the protest has been received.

statement: The size determination will be based primarily on the information supplied by the protestor or the entity requesting the determination and the information provided by the concern whose size status is at issue.
quote: The size determination will be based primarily on the information supplied by the protestor or the entity requesting the size determination and that provided by the concern whose size status is at issue.

statement: The protested concern must return the completed SBA Form 355 and all other requested information to SBA within three working days from the date of receipt of the blank form, and SBA has discretion to grant an extension of time.
quote: The protested concern or concern whose size is at issue must return the completed SBA Form 355 and all other requested information to SBA within 3 working days from the date of receipt of the blank form from SBA. SBA has discretion to grant an extension of time to file the form.

statement: If a concern whose size status is at issue submits incomplete information, SBA may presume that disclosure of the missing information would demonstrate that the concern is other than a small business.
quote: or if it submits incomplete information, SBA may presume that disclosure of the information required by the form or other missing information would demonstrate that the concern is other than a small business

statement: If no protest is pending under FAR subpart 33.1, the SBA Area Office will issue a formal size determination within 15 business days after receipt of a protest or a request for a formal size determination, if possible.
quote: After receipt of a protest or a request for a formal size determination, if no protest is pending under FAR subpart 33.1, the SBA Area Office will issue a formal size determination within 15 business days, if possible;

statement: The concern whose size is under consideration has the burden of establishing its small business size.
quote: The concern whose size is under consideration has the burden of establishing its small business size.

statement: The presumption of loss to the United States covers every contract, subcontract, cooperative agreement, cooperative research and development agreement, or grant which is set aside, reserved, or otherwise classified as intended for award to small business concerns.
quote: (a) Presumption of Loss Based on the Total Amount Expended. In every contract, subcontract, cooperative agreement, cooperative research and development agreement, or grant which is set aside, reserved, or otherwise classified as intended for award to small business concerns

statement: Whenever it is established that a business concern other than a small business concern willfully sought and received the award by misrepresentation, the presumption of loss is based on the total amount expended.
quote: based on the total amount expended on the contract, subcontract, cooperative agreement, cooperative research and development agreement, or grant whenever it is established that a business concern other than a small business concern willfully sought and received the award by misrepresentation

statement: The SBA suspension and debarment official or the agency suspension and debarment official may suspend or debar a person or concern for misrepresenting a firm's size status.
quote: Suspension or debarment. The SBA suspension and debarment official or the agency suspension and debarment official may suspend or debar a person or concern for misrepresenting a firm's size status pursuant to the procedures set forth in 48 CFR subpart 9.4.

statement: Persons or concerns are subject to severe penalties under the False Claims Act, the Program Fraud Civil Remedies Act and any other applicable laws or regulations, including part 142 of the SBA regulations.
quote: Civil Penalties. Persons or concerns are subject to severe penalties under the False Claims Act, 31 U.S.C. 3729-3733, the Program Fraud Civil Remedies Act, 31 U.S.C. 3801-3812 and any other applicable laws or regulations, including 13 CFR part 142.

statement: Persons or concerns are subject to severe criminal penalties for knowingly misrepresenting the small business size status of a concern in connection with procurement programs.
quote: Criminal Penalties. Persons or concerns are subject to severe criminal penalties for knowingly misrepresenting the small business size status of a concern in connection with procurement programs pursuant to section 16(d) of the Small Business Act, 15 U.S.C. 645(d)

statement: Paragraphs (a) through (c) of the penalties section may be determined not to apply in the case of unintentional errors, technical malfunctions and other similar situations that demonstrate that a misrepresentation of size was not affirmative, intentional, willful or actionable under the False Claims Act.
quote: Paragraphs (a) through (c) of this section may be determined not to apply in the case of unintentional errors, technical malfunctions, and other similar situations that demonstrate that a misrepresentation of size was not affirmative, intentional, willful or actionable under the False Claims Act

statement: Even if a concern is on a small business source list, it must still qualify and self-certify as a small business at the time it submits its offer as a section 8(d) subcontractor.
quote: Even if a concern is on a small business source list, it must still qualify and self-certify as a small business at the time it submits its offer as a section 8(d) subcontractor.

statement: The ANC definition covers a corporation organized under the laws of the State of Alaska in accordance with the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act and considered a minority and economically disadvantaged concern under the cited criteria.
quote: organized under the laws of the State of Alaska in accordance with the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act, as amended (43 U.S.C.A. 1601, et seq.) and which is considered a minority and economically disadvantaged concern under the criteria at 43 U.S.C. 1626(e)(1).

statement: A commercial plan is a subcontracting plan that covers the offeror's fiscal year and applies to the entire production of commercial products and performance of commercial services sold by the entire company or a portion of it.
quote: Commercial plan means a subcontracting plan (including goals) that covers the offeror's fiscal year and that applies to the entire production of commercial products and performance of commercial services sold by either the entire company or a portion thereof

statement: The Electronic Subcontracting Reporting System (eSRS) is the Governmentwide, electronic, web-based system for small business subcontracting program reporting.
quote: Electronic Subcontracting Reporting System (eSRS) means the Governmentwide, electronic, web-based system for small business subcontracting program reporting.

statement: Failure to make a good faith effort to comply with the subcontracting plan means willful or intentional failure to perform in accordance with the plan's requirements, or willful or intentional action to frustrate the plan.
quote: Failure to make a good faith effort to comply with the subcontracting plan means willful or intentional failure to perform in accordance with the requirements of the subcontracting plan, or willful or intentional action to frustrate the plan.

statement: The Indian tribe definition covers a tribe, band, group, pueblo or community that is recognized by the Federal Government as eligible for services from the Bureau of Indian Affairs.
quote: that is recognized by the Federal Government as eligible for services from the Bureau of Indian Affairs in accordance with 25 U.S.C. 1452(c).

statement: An individual subcontracting plan applies to a specific contract and has goals based on the offeror's planned subcontracting in support of that contract, except that indirect costs incurred for common or joint purposes may be allocated on a prorated basis to the contract.
quote: applies to a specific contract, and has goals that are based on the offeror's planned subcontracting in support of the specific contract, except that indirect costs incurred for common or joint purposes may be allocated on a prorated basis to the contract.

statement: A master subcontracting plan contains all the required elements of an individual subcontracting plan except goals, and may be incorporated into individual plans if the master plan has been approved.
quote: Master subcontracting plan means a subcontracting plan that contains all the required elements of an individual subcontracting plan, except goals, and may be incorporated into individual subcontracting plans, provided the master subcontracting plan has been approved.

statement: A reduced payment is a payment for less than the amount agreed in a subcontract under its terms and conditions, for supplies and services for which the Government has paid the prime contractor.
quote: Reduced Payment means a payment that is for less than the amount agreed upon in a subcontract in accordance with its terms and conditions, for supplies and services for which the Government has paid the prime contractor.

statement: A subcontract is any agreement, other than one involving an employer-employee relationship, entered into by a Government prime contractor or subcontractor for supplies or services required for performance of the contract, a contract modification or a subcontract.
quote: Subcontract means any agreement (other than one involving an employer-employee relationship) entered into by a Government prime contractor or subcontractor calling for supplies and/or services required for performance of the contract, contract modification, or subcontract.

statement: Total contract dollars means the final anticipated dollar value of the contract, including the dollar value of all options.
quote: Total contract dollars means the final anticipated dollar value, including the dollar value of all options.

statement: An untimely payment is a payment to a subcontractor that is more than 90 days past due under the subcontract terms for supplies and services for which the Government has paid the prime contractor.
quote: Untimely Payment means a payment to a subcontractor that is more than 90 days past due under the terms and conditions of a subcontract for supplies and services for which the Government has paid the prime contractor.

statement: Except as provided in paragraph (c) of that section, to be eligible as a subcontractor under the program a concern must represent itself as a small business, veteran-owned small business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business or HUBZone small business concern, among the listed categories.
quote: Except as provided in paragraph (c) of this section, to be eligible as a subcontractor under the program, a concern must represent itself as a small business, veteran-owned small business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business, HUBZone small business,

statement: For subcontracting purposes, a concern is small if it does not exceed the size standard for the NAICS code that the prime contractor determines best describes the product or service being acquired by the subcontract.
quote: For subcontracting purposes, a concern is small if it does not exceed the size standard for the NAICS code that the prime contractor determines best describes the product or service being acquired by the subcontract.

statement: Under the listed procedures, subcontracts awarded to an ANC or Indian tribe are counted toward the small business and small disadvantaged business subcontracting goals regardless of the size or SBA certification status of the ANC or Indian tribe.
quote: the following procedures apply: (i) Subcontracts awarded to an ANC or Indian tribe shall be counted towards the subcontracting goals for small business and small disadvantaged business (SDB) concerns, regardless of the size or Small Business Administration certification status

statement: When a contractual incentive provision rewards the contractor monetarily for exceeding goals in the subcontracting plan, the contracting officer must ensure that the goals are realistic and that any rewards for exceeding the goals are commensurate with the efforts the contractor would not have otherwise expended.
quote: rewarding the contractor monetarily for exceeding goals in the subcontracting plan, the contracting officer must ensure that (a) the goals are realistic and (b) any rewards for exceeding the goals are commensurate with the efforts the contractor would not have otherwise expended.

statement: Except where a contractor has a commercial plan, the contracting officer shall require a subcontracting plan for each indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity contract, including task or delivery order contracts, FSS, GWACs and MACs, under further conditions that are the subject of a separate claim.
quote: Except where a contractor has a commercial plan, the contracting officer shall require a subcontracting plan for each indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity contract (including task or delivery order contracts, FSS, GWACs, and MACs)

statement: The requirement for a plan on an indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity contract applies when the estimated value of the contract meets the subcontracting plan thresholds and small business subcontracting opportunities exist.
quote: when the estimated value of the contract meets the subcontracting plan thresholds at 19.702(a)and small business subcontracting opportunities exist.

statement: Contracting officers placing orders may establish small business subcontracting goals for each order, but the goals shall not take the form of a new subcontracting plan because a contract may not have more than one plan.
quote: Contracting officers placing orders may establish small business subcontracting goals for each order. Establishing goals shall not be in the form of a new subcontracting plan as a contract may not have more than one plan

statement: The contracting officer shall review the subcontracting plan for adequacy, ensuring that the required information, goals and assurances are included.
quote: The contracting officer shall review the subcontracting plan for adequacy, ensuring that the required information, goals, and assurances are included

statement: In negotiated acquisitions, the contracting officer shall determine whether the plan is acceptable based on the negotiation of each of the 15 elements of the plan.
quote: In negotiated acquisitions, the contracting officer shall determine whether the plan is acceptable based on the negotiation of each of the 15 elements of the plan

statement: Subcontracting goals should be set at a level the parties reasonably expect can result from the offeror expending good faith efforts to use small business subcontractors, among the listed categories of concerns.
quote: Subcontracting goals should be set at a level that the parties reasonably expect can result from the offeror expending good faith efforts to use small business

statement: The contracting officer shall take particular care to ensure that the offeror has not submitted unreasonably low goals to minimize exposure to liquidated damages and to avoid the administrative burden of substantiating good faith efforts.
quote: The contracting officer shall take particular care to ensure that the offeror has not submitted unreasonably low goals to minimize exposure to liquidated damages and to avoid the administrative burden of substantiating good faith efforts.

statement: In determining whether a proposed plan is acceptable, the contracting officer should obtain information available from the cognizant contract administration office and evaluate the offeror's past performance; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MKT-0556.
quote: In determining the acceptability of a proposed subcontracting plan, the contracting officer should take the following actions: (1) Obtain information available from the cognizant contract administration office, as provided for in 19.706(a), and evaluate the offeror's past performance

statement: One listed action is to ensure that the goals offered are attainable in relation to the subcontracting opportunities available to the contractor and the pool of eligible subcontractors, among other listed items.
quote: (2) In accordance with 15 U.S.C. 637(d)(4)(F)(iii), ensure that the goals offered are attainable in relation to— (i) The subcontracting opportunities available to the contractor, commensurate with the efficient and economical performance of the contract; (ii) The pool of eligible subcontractors

statement: In making an award that requires a subcontracting plan, the contracting officer shall consider the contractor's compliance with the subcontracting plans submitted on previous contracts as a factor in determining contractor responsibility.
quote: In making an award that requires a subcontracting plan, the contracting officer shall be responsible for the following: (1) Consider the contractor's compliance with the subcontracting plans submitted on previous contracts as a factor in determining contractor responsibility.

statement: Two listed award responsibilities are to assure that a subcontracting plan was submitted when required and to notify the SBA procurement center representative, or if none is assigned see the cross-referenced section, of the opportunity to review the proposed contract including the plan and supporting documentation.
quote: (2) Assure that a subcontracting plan was submitted when required. (3) Notify the SBA procurement center representative (or, if a procurement center representative is not assigned, see 19.402(a)) of the opportunity to review the proposed contract (including the plan and supporting documentation).

statement: The notice to the SBA procurement center representative shall be issued in time to give the representative a reasonable time to review, and the representative's failure to respond in a reasonable period shall not delay contract award.
quote: The notice shall be issued in sufficient time to provide the representative a reasonable time to review the material and submit advisory recommendations to the contracting officer. Failure of the representative to respond in a reasonable period of time shall not delay contract award.

statement: One listed award responsibility is to ensure that an acceptable plan is incorporated into and made a material part of the contract.
quote: (5) Ensure that an acceptable plan is incorporated into and made a material part of the contract.

statement: After a contract or modification containing a subcontracting plan is awarded, or an existing plan is amended, the contracting officer shall do the listed postaward actions.
quote: After a contract or contract modification containing a subcontracting plan is awarded or an existing subcontracting plan is amended, the contracting officer shall do the following:

statement: One listed postaward action is to notify the SBA of the award by sending a copy of the award document to the Area Director, Office of Government Contracting, in the SBA area office where the contract will be performed.
quote: (a) Notify the SBA of the award by sending a copy of the award document to the Area Director, Office of Government Contracting, in the SBA area office where the contract will be performed.

statement: One listed postaward action is to forward a copy of each commercial plan and any associated approvals to the Area Director, Office of Government Contracting, in the SBA area office where the contractor's headquarters is located.
quote: (b) Forward a copy of each commercial plan and any associated approvals to the Area Director, Office of Government Contracting, in the SBA area office where the contractor's headquarters is located.

statement: One listed postaward action is to forward a copy of each plan, or a determination that there is no requirement for a subcontracting plan, to the cognizant contract administration office.
quote: (e) Forward a copy of each plan, or a determination that there is no requirement for a subcontracting plan, to the cognizant contract administration office.

statement: One listed monitoring duty is to ensure that subcontracting reports are submitted into the eSRS within 30 days after the report ending date.
quote: (f) Monitor the prime contractor's compliance with its subcontracting plan, to include the following: (1) Ensure that subcontracting reports are submitted into the eSRS within 30 days after the report ending date (e.g., by October 30th for the fiscal year ended September 30th).

statement: One listed postaward action is to initiate action to assess liquidated damages upon a recommendation by the administrative contracting officer, if one is assigned, or receipt of other reliable evidence that assessing them is warranted.
quote: (h) Initiate action to assess liquidated damages in accordance with 19.705-7 upon a recommendation by the administrative contracting officer, if one is assigned, or receipt of other reliable evidence to indicate that assessing liquidated damages is warranted.

statement: The administrative contracting officer is responsible for assisting in evaluating subcontracting plans and for monitoring, evaluating and documenting contractor performance under the subcontracting plan clause and any plan in the contract.
quote: The administrative contracting officer is responsible for assisting in evaluating subcontracting plans, and for monitoring, evaluating, and documenting contractor performance under the clause prescribed in 19.708(b) and any subcontracting plan included in the contract.

statement: The contract administration office shall furnish, as appropriate, documentation on the contractor's performance and compliance with subcontracting plans under previous contracts.
quote: The contract administration office shall provide the necessary information and advice to support the contracting officer, as appropriate, by furnishing— (a) Documentation on the contractor's performance and compliance with subcontracting plans under previous contracts;

statement: One listed item the contract administration office furnishes is immediate notice if, during performance, the contractor is failing to meet its commitments under the subcontracting plan clause or the plan.
quote: (e) Immediate notice if, during performance, the contractor is failing to meet its commitments under the clause prescribed in 19.708(b) or the subcontracting plan;

statement: One listed item the contract administration office furnishes is immediate notice and rationale if, during performance, the contractor is failing to comply in good faith with the subcontracting plan.
quote: (f) Immediate notice and rationale if, during performance, the contractor is failing to comply in good faith with the subcontracting plan

statement: One listed item the contract administration office furnishes is immediate notice that performance is complete, that the goals were or were not met, and, if not met, whether there is any indication of a lack of good faith effort.
quote: (g) Immediate notice that performance under a contract is complete, that the goals were or were not met, and, if not met, whether there is any indication of a lack of a good faith effort to comply with the subcontracting plan.

statement: The clause 52.219-8, Utilization of Small Business Concerns, is inserted in solicitations and contracts expected to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold, subject to the listed exceptions; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MKT-0465.
quote: Insert the clause at 52.219-8, Utilization of Small Business Concerns, in solicitations and contracts when the contract amount is expected to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold unless—

statement: The listed exceptions to inserting clause 52.219-8 are a contemplated personal services contract and a contract that, with all its subcontracts, will be performed entirely outside the United States and its outlying areas.
quote: (1) A personal services contract is contemplated (see 37.104); or (2) The contract, together with all of its subcontracts, will be performed entirely outside of the United States and its outlying areas.

statement: The clause 52.219-9, Small Business Subcontracting Plan, is inserted in solicitations and contracts that offer subcontracting possibilities, are expected to exceed $900,000 ($2 million for construction of any public facility), and are required to include clause 52.219-8, subject to a listed exception; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MKT-0467.
quote: Insert the clause at 52.219-9, Small Business Subcontracting Plan, in solicitations and contracts that offer subcontracting possibilities, are expected to exceed $900,000 ($2 million for construction of any public facility), and are required to include the clause at 52.219-8

statement: The 52.219-9 insertion rule does not apply where the acquisition is set aside or is to be accomplished under the 8(a) program.
quote: Utilization of Small Business Concerns, unless the acquisition is set aside or is to be accomplished under the 8(a) program.

statement: When contracting by sealed bidding rather than by negotiation, the contracting officer shall use the clause 52.219-9 with its Alternate I.
quote: When— (i) Contracting by sealed bidding rather than by negotiation, the contracting officer shall use the clause with its Alternate I;

statement: One listed case is that, when contracting by negotiation and subcontracting plans are required with initial proposals, the contracting officer shall use the clause 52.219-9 with its Alternate II.
quote: (ii) Contracting by negotiation, and subcontracting plans are required with initial proposals as provided for in 19.705-2(d), the contracting officer shall use the clause with its Alternate II;

statement: One listed case is that, when the contract action will not be reported in the Federal Procurement Data System under the cited paragraphs, the contracting officer shall use the clause 52.219-9 with its Alternate III.
quote: (iii) The contract action will not be reported in the Federal Procurement Data System pursuant to 4.606(c)(5) or (c)(6), the contracting officer shall use the clause with its Alternate III;

statement: One listed case is that, when incorporating a subcontracting plan due to a modification, the contracting officer shall use the clause 52.219-9 with its Alternate IV.
quote: (iv) Incorporating a subcontracting plan due to a modification as provided for in 19.702(a)(1)(iii), the contracting officer shall use the clause with its Alternate IV.

statement: The clause 52.219-16, Liquidated Damages-Subcontracting Plan, is inserted in all solicitations and contracts containing the clause 52.219-9 or its Alternate I, II, III or IV.
quote: Insert the clause at 52.219-16, Liquidated Damages—Subcontracting Plan, in all solicitations and contracts containing the clause at 52.219-9, Small Business Subcontracting Plan, or the clause with its Alternate I, II, III, or IV.

statement: When contracting by negotiation, the contracting officer may insert a clause substantially the same as 52.219-10, Incentive Subcontracting Program, when a subcontracting plan is required, subject to the conditions stated in the paragraph; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MKT-0564.
quote: The contracting officer may, when contracting by negotiation, insert in solicitations and contracts a clause substantially the same as the clause at 52.219-10, Incentive Subcontracting Program, when a subcontracting plan is required (see 19.702), and inclusion of a monetary incentive is

statement: When small business subcontracting is a factor in determining the award fee in a cost-plus-award-fee contract, the contracting officer shall not use the clause 52.219-10.
quote: as one of the factors to be considered in determining the award fee in a cost-plus-award-fee contract; in such cases, however, the contracting officer shall not use the clause at 52.219-10, Incentive Subcontracting Program.

statement: Subject to the scope stated in CL-MKT-1444, a Certificate of Competency is the certificate issued by the Small Business Administration stating that the holder is responsible.
quote: A Certificate of Competency (COC) is the certificate issued by the Small Business Administration (SBA) stating that the holder is responsible

statement: The Certificate of Competency program applies to all Government acquisitions except 8(a) sole-source awards.
quote: The COC program is applicable to all Government acquisitions except for 8(a) sole-source awards.

statement: A contracting officer shall refer an apparent successful small business offeror determined to be nonresponsible to the SBA for a possible Certificate of Competency, even if the next acceptable offer is from a small business.
quote: A contracting officer shall, upon determining an apparent successful small business offeror to be nonresponsible, refer that small business to the SBA for a possible COC, even if the next acceptable offer is from a small business.

statement: The referral paragraph lists two duties for the contracting officer: to withhold contract award and to refer the matter; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MKT-0479 and CL-MKT-0480.
quote: the contracting officer shall— (1) Withhold contract award (see 19.602-3); and (2) Refer the matter

statement: The contracting officer shall refer the matter to the cognizant SBA Government Contracting Area Office serving the area of the offeror's headquarters in accordance with agency procedures, except in the listed cases where referral is not necessary; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MKT-0480.
quote: (2) Refer the matter to the cognizant SBA Government Contracting Area Office (Area Office) serving the area in which the headquarters of the offeror is located, in accordance with agency procedures, except that referral is not necessary if the small business concern—

statement: Referral to the SBA is not necessary if the small business concern (i) is determined to be unqualified and ineligible because it does not meet the standard in 9.104-1(g), provided that the determination is approved by the chief of the contracting office; or (ii) is suspended or debarred under Executive Order 11246 or subpart 9.4.
quote: (i) Is determined to be unqualified and ineligible because it does not meet the standard in 9.104-1(g); provided, that the determination is approved by the chief of the contracting office; or (ii) Is suspended or debarred under Executive Order 11246 or subpart 9.4.

statement: The referral shall include a notice that the concern has been determined to be nonresponsible, specifying the elements of responsibility found lacking, and, if applicable, a copy of the listed documents.
quote: (c) The referral shall include— (1) A notice that a small business concern has been determined to be nonresponsible, specifying the elements of responsibility the contracting officer found lacking; and (2) If applicable, a copy of the following:

statement: The documents listed for the referral copy include the solicitation, the concern's final offer, the abstract of bids or the contracting officer's price negotiation memorandum, the preaward survey and the technical data package.
quote: (i) Solicitation. (ii) Final offer submitted by the concern whose responsibility is at issue for the procurement. (iii) Abstract of bids or the contracting officer's price negotiation memorandum. (iv) Preaward survey. (v) Technical data package

statement: The contracting officer shall withhold contract award for 15 business days, or longer if agreed to by the SBA and the contracting officer, after the SBA Area Office receives a referral that includes all required documentation.
quote: (e) Contract award shall be withheld by the contracting officer for a period of 15 business days (or longer if agreed to by the SBA and the contracting officer) following receipt by the appropriate SBA Area Office of a referral that includes all required documentation.

statement: Within 15 business days, or a longer period agreed to by the SBA and the contracting agency, after receiving a notice that a small business concern lacks certain elements of responsibility, the SBA Area Office will take the listed actions.
quote: Within 15 business days (or a longer period agreed to by the SBA and the contracting agency) after receiving a notice that a small business concern lacks certain elements of responsibility, the SBA Area Office will take the following actions:

statement: One listed action is that, when the Area Director determines a COC is warranted for contracts valued at $25,000,000 or less, the Area Office notifies the contracting officer and offers options, the first being to accept the decision to issue a COC and award the contract to the concern.
quote: When the Area Director determines that a COC is warranted (for contracts valued at $25,000,000 or less), notify the contracting officer and provide the following options: (1) Accept the Area Director's decision to issue a COC and award the contract to the concern.

statement: There is no contracting officer's appeal when the Area Office proposes to issue a Certificate of Competency valued at $100,000 or less.
quote: However, there is no contracting officer's appeal when the Area Office proposes to issue a COC valued at $100,000 or less.

statement: For Certificates of Competency valued between $100,000 and $25,000,000, the contracting officer and the SBA shall make every effort to resolve disagreements about a concern's ability to perform before the SBA takes final action.

statement: Certificates of competency are conclusive with respect to all elements of responsibility of prospective small business contractors.
quote: SBA COC's are conclusive with respect to all elements of responsibility of prospective small business contractors.

statement: Where the SBA has not issued a certificate within 15 business days, or a longer period agreed with the SBA, after receiving the referral, the contracting officer awards to another appropriately selected and responsible offeror.
quote: The contracting officer shall proceed with the acquisition and award the contract to another appropriately selected and responsible offeror if the SBA has not issued a COC within 15 business days (or a longer period of time agreed to with the SBA) after receiving the referral.

statement: The SBA may review, within 5 working days before execution, any negotiated contractual document requiring a subcontracting plan, including the plan itself, and its recommendations to the contracting officer are advisory.
quote: Review (within 5 working days) before execution any negotiated contractual document requiring a subcontracting plan, including the plan itself, and submit recommendations to the contracting officer, which shall be advisory in nature;

statement: The SBA is not authorized to prescribe the extent of subcontracting, to specify the concerns that receive subcontracts, or to exercise authority over the administration of individual prime contracts or subcontracts.
quote: The SBA is not authorized to (1) prescribe the extent to which any contractor or subcontractor shall subcontract, (2) specify concerns to which subcontracts will be awarded, or (3) exercise any authority regarding the administration of individual prime contracts or subcontracts.

statement: An oral presentation by an offeror, requested by the Government, may replace written information or add to it.
quote: Oral presentations by offerors as requested by the Government may substitute for, or augment, written information.

statement: Even where part of a proposal is presented orally, representations and certifications must be submitted as the FAR provisions require, and a signed offer sheet, including any exceptions to the Government's terms and conditions, must be submitted in writing.
quote: representations and certifications shall be submitted as required in the FAR provisions at 52.204-8(d) or 52.212-3(b), and a signed offer sheet (including any exceptions to the Government's terms and conditions) shall be submitted in writing.

statement: The solicitation may describe the types of information to be presented orally with the evaluation factors attached to them, and the qualifications required of the personnel who give the presentation.
quote: (1) The types of information to be presented orally and the associated evaluation factors that will be used; (2) The qualifications for personnel that will be required to provide the oral presentation(s);

statement: The contracting officer must keep a record of oral presentations that documents what the Government relied on in making the source selection decision.
quote: The contracting officer shall maintain a record of oral presentations to document what the Government relied upon in making the source selection decision.

statement: Information that the parties intend to make a material term or condition of the contract must be put in writing, and incorporation by reference of oral statements is not permitted.
quote: When an oral presentation includes information that the parties intend to include in the contract as material terms or conditions, the information shall be put in writing. Incorporation by reference of oral statements is not permitted.

statement: If the Government conducts discussions during an oral presentation, it must comply with FAR 15.306 and 15.307.
quote: If, during an oral presentation, the Government conducts discussions (see 15.306(d)), the Government must comply with 15.306 and 15.307.

statement: Proposals and information received in response to a request for information must be marked with the date and time of receipt at the location the solicitation specifies and transmitted to the designated officials.
quote: Upon receipt at the location specified in the solicitation, proposals and information received in response to a request for information (RFI) shall be marked with the date and time of receipt and shall be transmitted to the designated officials.

statement: Proposals must be safeguarded from unauthorized disclosure throughout the source selection process.
quote: Proposals shall be safeguarded from unauthorized disclosure throughout the source selection process.

statement: If any portion of a proposal received electronically or by facsimile is unreadable, the contracting officer must immediately notify the offeror and permit resubmission of that portion.
quote: If any portion of a proposal received by the contracting officer electronically or by facsimile is unreadable, the contracting officer immediately shall notify the offeror and permit the offeror to resubmit the unreadable portion of the proposal.

statement: A resubmitted unreadable portion is treated as received at the date and time of the original submission for determining timeliness, provided the offeror complies with the time and format requirements for resubmission that the contracting officer prescribed.
quote: shall be considered as if it were received at the date and time of the original unreadable submission for the purpose of determining timeliness under 15.208(a), provided the offeror complies with the time and format requirements for resubmission prescribed by the contracting officer.

statement: A tradeoff process is appropriate when it may be in the Government's best interest to consider award to other than the lowest priced offeror or other than the highest technically rated offeror.
quote: (a) A tradeoff process is appropriate when it may be in the best interest of the Government to consider award to other than the lowest priced offeror or other than the highest technically rated offeror.

statement: The solicitation must clearly state all evaluation factors and significant subfactors that will affect contract award and their relative importance; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MKT-1327.
quote: (1) All evaluation factors and significant subfactors that will affect contract award and their relative importance shall be clearly stated in the solicitation; and

statement: The solicitation must state whether all evaluation factors other than cost or price, when combined, are significantly more important than, approximately equal to, or significantly less important than cost or price.
quote: (2) The solicitation shall state whether all evaluation factors other than cost or price, when combined, are significantly more important than, approximately equal to, or significantly less important than cost or price.

statement: The perceived benefits of a higher priced proposal must merit the additional cost, and the rationale for tradeoffs must be documented in the file in accordance with FAR 15.406.
quote: The perceived benefits of the higher priced proposal shall merit the additional cost, and the rationale for tradeoffs must be documented in the file in accordance with 15.406.

statement: Prenegotiation objectives should be based on the results of the contracting officer's analysis of the offeror's proposal, taking into consideration all pertinent information including field pricing assistance, audit reports and technical analysis, fact-finding results, independent Government cost estimates and price histories.
quote: based on the results of the contracting officer's analysis of the offeror's proposal, taking into consideration all pertinent information including field pricing assistance, audit reports and technical analysis, fact-finding results, independent Government cost estimates and price histories.

statement: The contracting officer must establish the objectives before negotiating any pricing action, and the scope and depth of the supporting analysis should relate directly to the dollar value, importance, and complexity of that action.
quote: The contracting officer shall establish prenegotiation objectives before the negotiation of any pricing action. The scope and depth of the analysis supporting the objectives should be directly related to the dollar value, importance, and complexity of the pricing action.

statement: When cost analysis is required, the contracting officer must document the pertinent issues to be negotiated, the cost objectives, and a profit or fee objective.
quote: When cost analysis is required, the contracting officer shall document the pertinent issues to be negotiated, the cost objectives, and a profit or fee objective.

statement: Contracting officers must prepare solicitations and resulting contracts using the uniform contract format.
quote: Contracting officers shall prepare solicitations and resulting contracts using the uniform contract format outlined in Table 15-1 of this subsection.

statement: A solicitation in the uniform contract format includes Parts I through IV, and on award Part IV is not physically included in the contract but is retained in the contract file.
quote: Solicitations using the uniform contract format shall include Parts I, II, III, and IV (see 15.204-2 through 15.204-5). Upon award, contracting officers shall not physically include Part IV in the resulting contract, but shall retain it in the contract file.

statement: The representations and certifications are incorporated by reference in the contract by using FAR 52.204-19 or, for acquisitions of commercial products and commercial services, FAR 52.212-4(v).
quote: The representations and certifications are incorporated by reference in the contract by using 52.204-19 (see 4.1202(b)) or for acquisitions of commercial products and commercial services see 52.212-4(v).

statement: When a form other than Optional Form 308 or Standard Form 33 is used, the first page of the solicitation must give the issuing activity's name, address and location, including the room and building where proposals or information must be submitted, the solicitation number, and the date of issuance.
quote: (2) When other than OF 308 or SF 33 is used, include the following information on the first page of the solicitation: (i) Name, address, and location of issuing activity, including room and building where proposals or information must be submitted. (ii) Solicitation number. (iii) Date of issuance.

statement: Section G of the Schedule must include a statement that the offeror should include the payment address in the proposal if it is different from the one shown for the offeror.
quote: Include a statement that the offeror should include the payment address in the proposal, if it is different from that shown for the offeror.

statement: Section K holds the solicitation provisions that require representations, certifications, or other information from offerors.
quote: (a) Section K, Representations, certifications, and other statements of offerors. Include in this section those solicitation provisions that require representations, certifications, or the submission of other information by offerors.

statement: Section L instructions may specify further organization of proposal or response parts, such as administrative, management, technical, past performance, and certified cost or pricing data or data other than certified cost or pricing data.
quote: The instructions may specify further organization of proposal or response parts, such as— (1) Administrative; (2) Management; (3) Technical; (4) Past performance; and (5) Certified cost or pricing data (see Table 15-2 of 15.408) or data other than certified cost or pricing data.

statement: Section M must identify all significant factors and any significant subfactors that will be considered in awarding the contract and their relative importance, and the contracting officer must insert one of the phrases in FAR 15.304(e).
quote: (c) Section M, Evaluation factors for award. Identify all significant factors and any significant subfactors that will be considered in awarding the contract and their relative importance (see 15.304(d)). The contracting officer shall insert one of the phrases in 15.304(e).

statement: The contracting officer awards the contract to the successful offeror by furnishing the executed contract or other notice of award.
quote: The contracting officer shall award a contract to the successful offeror by furnishing the executed contract or other notice of the award to that offeror.

statement: If the award document includes information different from the latest signed proposal as amended by the offeror's written correspondence, both the offeror and the contracting officer must sign the award.
quote: If the award document includes information that is different than the latest signed proposal, as amended by the offeror's written correspondence, both the offeror and the contracting officer shall sign the contract award.

statement: Where an award covers less than all items that may be awarded and items are withheld for later award, each notice must state that the Government may make later awards on those items within the proposal acceptance period.
quote: When an award is made to an offeror for less than all of the items that may be awarded and additional items are being withheld for subsequent award, each notice shall state that the Government may make subsequent awards on those additional items within the proposal acceptance period.

statement: If Optional Form 307, Standard Form 26 or Standard Form 33 is not used to award the contract, the first page of the award document must contain the Government's acceptance statement from Block 15 of that form; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MKT-1495.
quote: If the Optional Form (OF) 307, Contract Award, Standard Form (SF) 26, Award/Contract, or SF 33, Solicitation, Offer and Award, is not used to award the contract, the first page of the award document shall contain the Government's acceptance statement from Block 15 of that form

statement: Protests against award in negotiated acquisitions must be handled in accordance with FAR part 33, and agency protest procedures that incorporate the alternative dispute resolution provisions of Executive Order 12979 are encouraged for both preaward and postaward protests.
quote: (a) Protests against award in negotiated acquisitions shall be handled in accordance with part 33. Use of agency protest procedures that incorporate the alternative dispute resolution provisions of Executive Order 12979 is encouraged for both preaward and postaward protests.

statement: If a protest causes the agency, within 1 year of contract award, to issue a new solicitation on the protested contract award, the contracting officer must provide the information in paragraph (c) of that section to all prospective offerors for the new solicitation; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MKT-1497.
quote: If a protest causes the agency, within 1 year of contract award, to— (1) Issue a new solicitation on the protested contract award, the contracting officer shall provide the information in paragraph (c) of this section to all prospective offerors for the new solicitation; or

statement: The information provided covers what unsuccessful offerors learned in debriefings on the original award about the successful offeror's proposal, plus other nonproprietary information that would have been provided to the original offerors.
quote: (1) Information provided to unsuccessful offerors in any debriefings conducted on the original award regarding the successful offeror's proposal; and (2) Other nonproprietary information that would have been provided to the original offerors.

statement: Before initiating a comprehensive evaluation, the agency contact point must determine whether the proposal is a valid unsolicited proposal and whether it is suitable for submission in response to an existing agency requirement.
quote: Before initiating a comprehensive evaluation, the agency contact point shall determine if the proposal— (1) Is a valid unsolicited proposal, meeting the requirements of 15.603(c); (2) Is suitable for submission in response to an existing agency requirement (see 15.602);

statement: The contact point must also determine whether the proposal relates to the agency mission and contains sufficient technical information and cost-related or price-related information for evaluation.
quote: (3) Is related to the agency mission; (4) Contains sufficient technical information and cost-related or price-related information for evaluation;

statement: The agency contact point must also determine whether the proposal has overall scientific, technical or socioeconomic merit, has been approved by a responsible official or other representative authorized to obligate the offeror contractually, and complies with the marking requirements.
quote: (5) Has overall scientific, technical, or socioeconomic merit; (6) Has been approved by a responsible official or other representative authorized to obligate the offeror contractually; and (7) Complies with the marking requirements of 15.609.

statement: If a proposal is rejected because it does not meet the requirements of paragraph (a) of that section, the agency contact point must promptly inform the offeror in writing of the reasons for rejection and of the proposed disposition of the proposal.
quote: If a proposal is rejected because the proposal does not meet the requirements of paragraph (a) of this subsection, the agency contact point shall promptly inform the offeror of the reasons for rejection in writing and of the proposed disposition of the unsolicited proposal.

statement: A favorable comprehensive evaluation of an unsolicited proposal does not, in itself, justify an award without full and open competition.
quote: A favorable comprehensive evaluation of an unsolicited proposal does not, in itself, justify awarding a contract without providing for full and open competition.

statement: The contracting officer may commence negotiations on a sole source basis only when, among other conditions, an unsolicited proposal has received a favorable comprehensive evaluation and a justification and approval has been obtained; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MKT-1599.
quote: (b) The contracting officer may commence negotiations on a sole source basis only when— (1) An unsolicited proposal has received a favorable comprehensive evaluation; (2) A justification and approval has been obtained

statement: Government personnel may not use any data, concept, idea, or other part of an unsolicited proposal as a basis for a solicitation or in negotiations with another firm unless the offeror is notified of the intended use and agrees.
quote: Government personnel shall not use any data, concept, idea, or other part of an unsolicited proposal as the basis, or part of the basis, for a solicitation or in negotiations with any other firm unless the offeror is notified of and agrees to the intended use.

statement: Multiyear contracting acquires known requirements in quantities and total cost not over planned requirements for up to 5 years unless otherwise authorized by statute, even though the total funds ultimately to be obligated may not be available at contract award.
quote: a special contracting method to acquire known requirements in quantities and total cost not over planned requirements for up to 5 years unless otherwise authorized by statute, even though the total funds ultimately to be obligated may not be available at the time of contract award.

statement: For multiyear contracts the agency head may authorize modification of the requirements of the subpart and the cancellation clause.
quote: Accordingly, for multiyear contracts, the agency head may authorize modification of the requirements of this subpart and the clause at 52.217-2, Cancellation Under Multiyear Contracts.

statement: Funds obligated for multiyear contracts must be sufficient to cover any potential cancellation or termination costs, and multiyear contracts for fixed assets should be fully funded or funded in stages that are economically or programmatically viable.
quote: the funds obligated for multiyear contracts must be sufficient to cover any potential cancellation and/or termination costs; and multiyear contracts for the acquisition of fixed assets should be fully funded or funded in stages that are economically or programmatically viable.

statement: Termination can be effected at any time during the life of the contract and for the total or a partial quantity, while cancellation is effected between fiscal years and must be for all subsequent fiscal years' quantities.
quote: As contrasted with cancellation, termination can be effected at any time during the life of the contract (cancellation is effected between fiscal years) and can be for the total quantity or partial quantity (where as cancellation must be for all subsequent fiscal years' quantities).

statement: The contracting officer must insert the cancellation clause in solicitations and contracts when a multiyear contract is contemplated.
quote: The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.217-2, Cancellation Under Multiyear Contracts, in solicitations and contracts when a multiyear contract is contemplated.

statement: When the period of production is likely to warrant a labor and material costs contingency in the contract price, the contracting officer should normally use an economic price adjustment clause.
quote: When the period of production is likely to warrant a labor and material costs contingency in the contract price, the contracting officer should normally use an economic price adjustment clause (see 16.203).

statement: A reverse auction may be appropriate, in part, when market research indicates that a competitive marketplace exists for the supplies or services being acquired and that multiple offerors can satisfy the agency's requirement; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MKT-1361.
quote: (a) The use of reverse auctions may be appropriate when market research indicates that— (1) A competitive marketplace exists for the supplies and/or services being acquired; (2) Multiple offerors can satisfy the agency's requirement; and

statement: The third condition under which a reverse auction may be appropriate is that the nature of the supplies or services being acquired, such as clearly defined specifications and less complex requirements, encourages an iterative bidding process in which multiple offerors participate and at least one offeror submits more than one offer.
quote: (3) The nature of the supplies and/or services being acquired (e.g., clearly defined specifications, less complex requirements) encourages an iterative bidding process (i.e., multiple offerors participate and at least one offeror submits more than one offer during the reverse auction).

statement: When using the reverse auction process, contracting officers are still required to follow the acquisition policies and procedures, such as those prescribed in subpart 8.4 or 16.5 or part 13 or 15, as appropriate for the particular acquisition.
quote: When using the reverse auction process, contracting officers are still required to follow the acquisition policies and procedures (e.g., those prescribed in subpart 8.4 or 16.5, or part 13 or 15), as appropriate for the particular acquisition.

statement: Under an indirect payment method, the reverse auction service provider adds a fee to the price of the successful offer that is provided to the Government at the close of an auction.
quote: When using an indirect payment method, the reverse auction service provider adds a fee(s) to the price of the successful offer that is provided to the Government at the close of an auction.

statement: If only one offeror participates in an auction, the contracting officer may cancel the auction and document that single participation in the contract file, or accept the offer only if the price is determined to be fair and reasonable.
quote: (d) If only one offeror participates in an auction, the contracting officer may— (1) Cancel the auction and document the contract file with evidence of the participation of only one offeror; or (2) Accept the offer, only if the price is determined to be fair and reasonable

statement: In a sole source acquisition, when the SBA requests audit assistance to determine that the proposed price is fair and reasonable, the contracting activity furnishes it to the extent it is available.
quote: If the SBA requests audit assistance to determine the proposed price to be fair and reasonable in a sole source acquisition, the contracting activity shall furnish it to the extent it is available.

statement: The contracting officer estimates the fair market price of the work to be performed by the 8(a) contractor.
quote: The contracting officer shall estimate the fair market price of the work to be performed by the 8(a) contractor.

statement: For a repeat purchase, the estimated price should be adjusted to reflect differences in specifications, plans, transportation costs, packaging and packing costs, and other circumstances.
quote: The estimated price should be adjusted to reflect differences in specifications, plans, transportation costs, packaging and packing costs, and other circumstances.

statement: For a repeat purchase, price indices may be used as guides to determine changes in labor and material costs, and a comparison of commercial prices for similar items may also be used.
quote: Price indices may be used as guides to determine the changes in labor and material costs. Comparison of commercial prices for similar items may also be used.

statement: The fair market price for total and partial small business set-asides and reserves, and for HUBZone set-asides, is the price achieved in accordance with the reasonable price guidelines in 15.404-1(b).
quote: The fair market price shall be the price achieved in accordance with the reasonable price guidelines in 15.404-1(b) for— (1) Total and partial small business set-asides, and reserves (see subpart 19.5); (2) HUBZone set-asides (see subpart 19.13);

statement: The same reasonable price guidelines set the fair market price for contracts using the HUBZone price evaluation preference, for set-asides for SDVOSB concerns eligible under the SDVOSB Program, and for set-asides for EDWOSB and WOSB concerns eligible under the WOSB Program.
quote: (3) Contracts utilizing the price evaluation preference for HUBZone small business concerns (see subpart 19.13); (4) Set-asides for SDVOSB concerns eligible under the SDVOSB Program (see subpart 19.14); and (5) Set-asides for EDWOSB concerns and WOSB concerns eligible under the WOSB Program

statement: For 8(a) contracts, contracting officers follow the procedures at 19.807 both to meet the 19.806(b) requirement and to accurately estimate the current fair market price.
quote: For 8(a) contracts, both with respect to meeting the requirement at 19.806(b) and in order to accurately estimate the current fair market price, contracting officers shall follow the procedures at 19.807.

statement: A concern must be a current participant in the 8(a) program at the time of an 8(a) sole-source award.
quote: A concern must be a current participant in the 8(a) program at the time of an 8(a) sole-source award.

statement: The predecessor-contract bar applies where the other 8(a) participant, current or former, is owned by the same Alaska Native Corporation, Indian Tribe, Native Hawaiian Organization, or Community Development Corporation.
quote: (or former 8(a) participant) owned by the same Alaska Native Corporation, Indian Tribe, Native Hawaiian Organization, or Community Development Corporation

statement: The offering letter and SBA acceptance required for each order are in addition to the agency offering, and the SBA accepting, the agreement itself.
quote: in addition to the agency offering and SBA accepting the BOA or BPA itself.

statement: The contract to be awarded by the agency to the SBA is prepared in accordance with agency procedures and in the same detail as would be required in a contract with a business concern.
quote: The contract to be awarded by the agency to the SBA shall be prepared in accordance with agency procedures and in the same detail as would be required in a contract with a business concern.

statement: The contracting officer prepares the contract that the SBA will award to the 8(a) participant in accordance with agency procedures, as if awarding directly to the participant, except for the items listed in the paragraph.
quote: The contracting officer shall prepare the contract that the SBA will award to the 8(a) participant in accordance with agency procedures, as if awarding the contract directly to the 8(a) participant, except for the following:

statement: The award form for the contract the SBA awards to the 8(a) participant cites the statutory authority for other than full and open competition, in the title 41 or title 10 provision as appropriate.
quote: The award form shall cite 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(5) or 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(5) (as appropriate) as the authority for use of other than full and open competition.

statement: The contract includes appropriate clauses, as necessary, to reflect that it is between the SBA and the 8(a) contractor.
quote: Appropriate clauses shall be included, as necessary, to reflect that the contract is between the SBA and the 8(a) contractor.

statement: The SBA inserts the SBA contract number, the effective date, the typed name and signature of the SBA's contracting officer, and the date signed.
quote: The following items shall be inserted by the SBA— (i) The SBA contract number. (ii) The effective date. (iii) The typed name of the SBA's contracting officer. (iv) The signature of the SBA's contracting officer. (v) The date signed.

statement: The SBA obtains the signature of the 8(a) contractor before signing and returning the prime contract to the contracting officer for signature.
quote: The SBA will obtain the signature of the 8(a) contractor prior to signing and returning the prime contract to the contracting officer for signature.

statement: The SBA will make every effort to obtain signatures and return the contract, and any subsequent bilateral modification, to the contracting officer within a maximum of 10 working days.
quote: The SBA will make every effort to obtain signatures and return the contract, and any subsequent bilateral modification, to the contracting officer within a maximum of 10 working days.

statement: Except in procurements where the SBA will make advance payments to its 8(a) contractor, the agency contracting officer may use a single contract document as an alternative to the procedures in paragraphs (a) and (b).
quote: Except in procurements where the SBA will make advance payments to its 8(a) contractor, the agency contracting officer may, as an alternative to the procedures in paragraphs (a) and (b) of this subsection, use a single contract document

statement: The single contract document contains the information in paragraphs (b)(1), (2) and (3), which are the authority citation, the clauses reflecting the SBA and contractor relationship, and the items the SBA inserts.
quote: The single contract document shall contain the information in paragraphs (b) (1), (2), and (3) of this subsection.

statement: On the single contract document, appropriate blocks on the Standard Form 26 or 1442 are asterisked and a continuation sheet is appended as a tripartite agreement that includes the agency acquisition office, prime contract number and agency contracting officer's name.
quote: Appropriate blocks on the Standard Form (SF) 26 or 1442 will be asterisked and a continuation sheet appended as a tripartite agreement which includes the following: (1) Agency acquisition office, prime contract number, name of agency contracting officer

statement: The tripartite continuation sheet also includes lines for the agency contracting officer's signature, date signed and effective date, the SBA office, SBA contract number, SBA contracting officer's name and signature and date lines, and the 8(a) contractor's name and signature and date lines.
quote: and lines for signature, date signed, and effective date. (2) The SBA office, the SBA contract number, name of the SBA contracting officer, and lines for signature and date signed. (3) Name and lines for the 8(a) contractor's signature and date signed.

statement: For acquisitions not exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold, the contracting officer may use the alternative procedures in paragraph (c) with the appropriate simplified acquisition forms.
quote: For acquisitions not exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold, the contracting officer may use the alternative procedures in paragraph (c) of this subsection with the appropriate simplified acquisition forms.

statement: A request for a formal size determination for a sole-source nominee may be submitted by the participant nominated for award, by the contracting officer delegated SBA's 8(a) contract execution functions where applicable, or by the SBA program official with authority to execute the 8(a) contract.
quote: (1) The 8(a) participant nominated for award of the particular sole source contract; (2) The contracting officer who has been delegated SBA's 8(a) contract execution functions, where applicable, or the SBA program official with authority to execute the 8(a) contract;

statement: A request for a formal size determination for a sole-source nominee may also be submitted by the SBA District Director in the district office that services the participant, by the Associate Administrator for Business Development, or by the SBA Inspector General.
quote: (3) The SBA District Director in the district office that services the 8(a) participant or the Associate Administrator for Business Development; or (4) The SBA Inspector General.

statement: An appeal of an SBA size determination requested under 19.814 follows the procedures at 19.302.
quote: An appeal of an SBA size determination shall follow the procedures at 19.302.

statement: The provision at 52.219-1 or 52.212-3(c)(5) is used to collect small disadvantaged business data.
quote: The provision at 52.219-1, Small Business Program Representations, or 52.212-3(c)(5), Offeror Representations and Certifications—Commercial Products and Commercial Services, is used to collect SDB data.

statement: If SBA determines that a concern is a HUBZone small business, it designates the concern as a HUBZone small business in the Dynamic Small Business Search.
quote: If SBA determines that a concern is a HUBZone small business, it will designate the concern as a HUBZone small business in the Dynamic Small Business Search (DSBS)

statement: SBA's HUBZone designation also appears in SAM.
quote: SBA's designation also appears in SAM.

statement: The Small Business Administration determines status as an EDWOSB concern or WOSB concern eligible under the WOSB Program in accordance with 13 CFR part 127.
quote: Status as an EDWOSB concern or WOSB concern eligible under the WOSB Program is determined by the Small Business Administration in accordance with 13 CFR part 127.

statement: Pending applications for certification are only in the Dynamic Small Business Search.
quote: Pending applications for certification are only in the Dynamic Small Business Search (DSBS)

statement: Where SBA, as a result of a current eligibility examination, finds that the concern did not qualify as an EDWOSB concern or WOSB concern eligible under the WOSB Program, the contracting officer may terminate the contract and shall not exercise any option or award further task or delivery orders.
quote: SBA as a result of a current eligibility examination finding that the concern did not qualify as an EDWOSB concern or WOSB concern eligible under the WOSB Program, the contracting officer may terminate the contract, and shall not exercise any option, or award further task or delivery orders.

statement: Agencies shall not count or include the award toward the small business goals for an EDWOSB concern or WOSB concern eligible under the WOSB Program and must update FPDS from the date of award to reflect the final SBA decision.
quote: Agencies shall not count or include the award toward the small business goals for an EDWOSB concern or WOSB concern eligible under the WOSB Program and must update FPDS from the date of award to reflect the final SBA decision.

statement: A joint venture may be considered an EDWOSB or WOSB concern eligible under the WOSB Program if the EDWOSB or WOSB participant is certified in SAM and the joint venture meets the requirements of 13 CFR 127.506.
quote: A joint venture may be considered an EDWOSB concern or WOSB concern eligible under the WOSB Program if the EDWOSB or WOSB participant is certified in SAM (see section 19.1505(d) for set-aside procedures) and the joint venture meets the requirements of 13 CFR 127.506.

statement: A person or entity that misrepresents a firm's small disadvantaged business status is also subject to any other penalty authorized by law.
quote: as well as any other penalty authorized by law.

statement: A class small business set-aside of the item or service by another contracting activity, and the use of a brand name or equal product description in the solicitation, are each not in themselves sufficient cause for not setting aside an acquisition.
quote: (g) A class small business set-aside of the item or service has been made by another contracting activity. (h) A “brand name or equal” product description will be used in the solicitation.

statement: The contracting officer may modify a unilateral or joint class small business set-aside to withdraw one or more individual acquisitions, in a similar manner to a withdrawal.
quote: In a similar manner, the contracting officer may modify a unilateral or joint class small business set-aside to withdraw one or more individual acquisitions.

statement: If the agency small business specialist does not agree to a withdrawal or modification, the case is promptly referred to the SBA procurement center representative or, if none is assigned, as provided in 19.402(a), for review.
quote: If the agency small business specialist does not agree to a withdrawal or modification, the case shall be promptly referred to the SBA PCR (or, if a PCR is not assigned, see 19.402(a)) for review.

statement: The contracting officer prepares a written statement supporting any withdrawal or modification of a small business set-aside and includes it in the contract file.
quote: The contracting officer shall prepare a written statement supporting any withdrawal or modification of a small business set-aside and include it in the contract file.

statement: The required supplies or services for which no award was made may be acquired by sealed bidding or negotiation, as appropriate.
quote: The required supplies and/or services for which no award was made may be acquired by sealed bidding or negotiation, as appropriate.

statement: The reverse auction process is used to obtain pricing for an acquisition.
quote: The reverse auction process is used to obtain pricing for an acquisition.

statement: A service platform for conducting reverse auctions may be provided by a commercial or Government entity.
quote: (1) A service platform for conducting reverse auctions may be provided by a commercial or Government entity.
