quote: (2) While some reverse auction service providers are paid directly by the Government for reverse auction services, other providers may incorporate a fee structure that uses an indirect payment method.

statement: Under an indirect payment method, the Government pays the successful offeror the total price of the offer, which includes the fee added by the reverse auction service provider.
quote: The Government then pays the successful offeror the total price of the offer, which includes the fee(s) added by the reverse auction service provider.

quote: (3) When acquiring reverse auction services from a commercial reverse auction service provider, agencies shall— (i) Use competitive procedures, unless an exception applies; (ii) Detail the provider's fee structure in the resultant contract or agreement for reverse auction services;

statement: When acquiring reverse auction services from a commercial provider, agencies must make the details of the contract or agreement, including the provider's fee structure, available to contracting officers for consideration when determining whether to use a reverse auction service provider.
quote: (iii) Make the details of the contract or agreement for reverse auction services, including the provider's fee structure, available to contracting officers for consideration when determining whether to use a reverse auction service provider, in accordance with 17.804(a).

statement: When acquiring reverse auction services, the contracting officer must ensure that the solicitation and contract include descriptions of Government data and Government-related data.
quote: (4) When acquiring reverse auction services, the contracting officer shall ensure the following information is provided in the solicitation and contract: (i) Descriptions of Government data and Government-related data.

statement: When acquiring reverse auction services, the contracting officer must ensure that the solicitation and contract include data ownership, licensing, delivery and disposition instructions specific to the relevant types of Government data and Government-related data.
quote: (ii) Data ownership, licensing, delivery, and disposition instructions specific to the relevant types of Government data and Government-related data (e.g., DD Form 1423, Contract Data Requirements List; work statement task; line item).

statement: The disposition instructions must provide for the transition of data in commercially available, or open and non-proprietary, format and for permanent records, in accordance with disposition guidance issued by the National Archives and Records Administration.
quote: Disposition instructions shall provide for the transition of data in commercially available, or open and non-proprietary format and for permanent records, in accordance with disposition guidance issued by the National Archives and Records Administration.

statement: Contracting officers may use only the services of a reverse auction service provider that does not assert or imply that it can or will obtain a Government contract for participants of a reverse auction.
quote: (d) Contracting officers shall only use the services of a reverse auction service provider that— (1) Does not assert or imply that it can or will obtain a Government contract for participants of a reverse auction;

statement: Contracting officers may use only a reverse auction service provider that allows entities to register, at no cost, as potential offerors for reverse auctions conducted on behalf of the Government on the provider's platform (the lead-in is quoted in CL-MKT-1524).
quote: (2) Allows entities to register, at no cost, as potential offerors for reverse auctions conducted on behalf of the Government on the provider's reverse auction platform;

statement: Contracting officers may use only a reverse auction service provider that allows each entity, as part of registration, to execute a proprietary data protection agreement with the provider, provided that the agreement's terms do not affect the terms and conditions of a Government solicitation or contract (the lead-in is quoted in CL-MKT-1524).
quote: (3) Allows each entity, as part of the registration process, the opportunity to execute a proprietary data protection agreement with the provider; provided that the terms in the agreement do not affect the terms and conditions of a Government solicitation or contract;

statement: Contracting officers may use only a reverse auction service provider that protects from unauthorized use or disclosure, and does not release outside the Government, all contractor bid or proposal information and source selection information associated with providing reverse auction services to the Government (the lead-in is quoted in CL-MKT-1524).
quote: (4) Protects from unauthorized use or disclosure and does not release outside of the Government— (i) All contractor bid or proposal information (see 3.104-1) and source selection information associated with providing reverse auction services to the Government;

statement: The protection by the provider extends to all information similarly generated to support the issuance of a task order, delivery order or order under a blanket purchase agreement.
quote: (ii) All information similarly generated to support the issuance of a task order or delivery order or order under a blanket purchase agreement;

statement: The protection by the provider also extends to information identified by an offeror as restricted from duplication, use or disclosure, in whole or in part, for any purpose other than to evaluate the participant's price or proposal.
quote: (iii) Information identified by an offeror as restricted from duplication, use, or disclosure—in whole or in part—for any purpose other than to evaluate the reverse auction participant's price or proposal;

statement: Contracting officers may use only a reverse auction service provider that allows offerors to see the successive lowest prices offered in the auction without revealing an offeror's identity (the lead-in is quoted in CL-MKT-1524).
quote: (5) Allows offerors to see the successive lowest price(s) offered in the auction without revealing an offeror's identity;

statement: Contracting officers may use only a reverse auction service provider that, at the close of each auction, provides the Government with the successful offer and information that separately identifies the offeror's price and the price for each provider fee or charge included in the total price (the lead-in is quoted in CL-MKT-1524).
quote: (6) At the close of each auction— (i) Provides the Government with the successful offer, along with information that separately identifies the offeror's price and the price for each provider fee or charge included in the total price;

statement: Contracting officers may use only a reverse auction service provider that, at the close of each auction, also provides the Government with all information and documentation received from offerors in response to the reverse auction (the lead-in is quoted in CL-MKT-1524).
quote: (ii) Provides the Government with all information and documentation received from offerors in response to the reverse auction.

statement: Contracting officers may use only a reverse auction service provider that does not participate as an offeror in any reverse auction that the provider is hosting on behalf of the Government (the lead-in is quoted in CL-MKT-1524).
quote: (7) Does not participate as an offeror in any reverse auction which the provider is hosting on behalf of the Government.

statement: Contracting officers may use only a reverse auction service provider that asserts no rights or license in the data gathered or generated during a reverse auction (the lead-in is quoted in CL-MKT-1524).
quote: (8) Asserts no rights or license in the data gathered or generated during a reverse auction.

statement: Only a contracting officer may exclude an offeror from participating in an auction, determine the awardee of any reverse auction, or determine that the offeror is a responsible prospective contractor.
quote: (e) Only a contracting officer shall— (1) Exclude an offeror from participating in an auction; (2) Determine the awardee(s) of any reverse auction; or (3) Determine that the offeror is a responsible prospective contractor (see 9.103, 9.104-1, and 9.405(d)).

statement: When considering the use of a reverse auction service provider, the contracting officer must conduct market research for available sources of reverse auction services.
quote: (a) When considering the use of a reverse auction service provider, the contracting officer shall— (1) Conduct market research for available sources of reverse auction services (e.g., existing agency contracts or agreements, commercial service providers, or Government service providers);

statement: The contracting officer must evaluate the fee structure for each reverse auction service provider and document the contract file that the use of a provider is cost effective.
quote: (2) Evaluate the fee structure for each reverse auction service provider; and (3) Document the contract file that the use of a reverse auction service provider is cost effective.

statement: When conducting a reverse auction, the contracting officer must not disclose the identity of the offerors, except for the awardee's identity after an award resulting from the auction.
quote: (b) When conducting a reverse auction, the contracting officer shall— (1) Not disclose the identity of the offeror(s) except for the awardee's identity subsequent to an award resulting from the auction (see 3.104-4(a) and (e)(1));

statement: In a reverse auction, the contracting officer must allow offerors to continually revise their prices downward until the close of the auction and must allow an offeror to withdraw an offer from further consideration before the close of the auction.
quote: (2) Allow offerors the opportunity to continually revise their prices downward during the reverse auction until the close of the auction; and (3) Allow an offeror to withdraw an offer from further consideration prior to the close of an auction.

statement: When using the services of a reverse auction service provider, the contracting officer must include contact information, including the contracting officer's name and email address, in the synopsis and solicitation so that offerors can contact the contracting officer directly with questions.
quote: When using the services of a reverse auction service provider, contracting officers shall— (1) Include contact information, including contracting officer name and email address, in the synopsis and solicitation that will allow offerors to contact the contracting officer directly with any questions;

statement: Upon receipt of a successful offer, the contracting officer must verify that any provider fees or charges included in the price are in accordance with the provider's fee structure, as evaluated under paragraph (a)(2).
quote: (2) Upon receipt of a successful offer, verify that any provider fees or charges included in the price are in accordance with the provider's fee structure, as evaluated in accordance with paragraph (a)(2) of this section;

statement: When using the services of a reverse auction service provider, the contracting officer must include in the contract file any information and documentation the provider received from offerors responding to the reverse auction.
quote: (3) Include in the contract file any information and/or documentation received by the reverse auction service provider from offerors responding to the reverse auction.

quote: This subpart prescribes uniform reporting requirements for the Federal Procurement Data System (FPDS).

quote: (c) Modifying the scope of a UCA when performance has already begun. The request should show that the modification is consistent with good business practices and in the best interests of the United States.

quote: (b) In determining the appropriate amount to obligate, the contracting officer shall assess the contractor's proposal for the undefinitized period and shall obligate funds only in an amount consistent with the contractor's requirements for the undefinitized period.

quote: (b) The head of an agency may waive the limitations in 217.7404(a), 217.7404-2, 217.7404-3, and 217.7404-4 for UCAs if the head of the agency determines that the waiver is necessary to support— (1) A contingency operation; or (2) A humanitarian or peacekeeping operation.

quote: (1) Purchases at or below the simplified acquisition threshold. (2) Special access programs. (3) Congressionally mandated long-lead procurement contracts.

quote: (b) A written determination of economic advantage indicating— (1) The anticipated economic advantage to the Government from use of the exchange authority;

quote: (c) All applicable approvals for the exchange; and (d) A description of the property available for exchange (e.g., nomenclature, location, serial number, estimated travel value).

quote: (a) Solicitations shall include a request for offerors to state prices— (1) For the new items being acquired without any exchange; and (2) For the new items with the exchange (trade-in allowance) for the exchange property listed.

quote: (B) Contemplates separate future contracts that will incorporate by reference or attachment the required and applicable clauses agreed upon in the master agreement. (2) Is not a contract.

quote: (b) Job order — (1) Is a fixed price contract incorporating, by reference or attachment, a master agreement for repair and alteration of vessels; (2) May include clauses pertaining to subjects not covered by the master agreement; but applicable to the job order being awarded;

quote: (3) Applies to a specific acquisition and sets forth the scope of work, price, delivery date, and other appropriate terms that apply to the particular job order.

quote: (b) Activities may use master agreements in work with prospective contractors located outside the United States and its outlying areas. (c) Activities may issue job orders under master agreements to effect repairs, alterations, and/or additions to vessels belonging to foreign governments.

quote: (b) The requirement in paragraph (a) of this section does not apply to contracts that are— (1) For commercial products; or (2) Valued at or below the simplified acquisition threshold.

statement: RFO FAR 15.108(b) says proposals should be safeguarded from unauthorized disclosure throughout the source selection process in accordance with part 3, and the paragraph names proposals only, with no mention of information received in response to a request for information.
quote: (b) Handling. Proposals should be safeguarded from unauthorized disclosure throughout the source selection process in accordance with part 3.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO paragraph says proposals "should be safeguarded" where the codified paragraph says they "shall be safeguarded", refers to part 3 where the codified paragraph refers to 3.104, and has no sentence on information received in response to a request for information, which the codified paragraph requires to be safeguarded adequately.

statement: RFO FAR 15.108(c) says that if any portion of a proposal submitted electronically is unreadable, contracting officers must immediately notify the offeror and permit the offeror to resubmit the unreadable portion of the proposal.
quote: (c) Unreadable proposals. If any portion of a proposal submitted electronically is unreadable, contracting officers must immediately notify the offeror and permit the offeror to resubmit the unreadable portion of the proposal.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO sentence says "submitted electronically" where the codified sentence says received electronically or by facsimile, and says contracting officers "must" where the codified sentence says the contracting officer "shall".

statement: RFO FAR 15.108(c) says contracting officers must establish the method and time for resubmission after consultation with the offeror and document the file.
quote: Contracting officers must establish the method and time for resubmission after consultation with the offeror and document the file.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO sentence says contracting officers "must establish" the method and time where the codified sentence says they "shall be prescribed" by the contracting officer; the rest is the same.

statement: RFO FAR 15.108(c) says that, for the purpose of determining timeliness under 15.107, the resubmission is considered as if it were received at the date and time of the original unreadable submission, provided the offeror complies with the time and format requirements established by the contracting officer for resubmission.
quote: For the purpose of determining timeliness under 15.107, the resubmission is considered as if it were received at the date and time of the original unreadable submission, provided the offeror complies with the time and format requirements established by the contracting officer for resubmission.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The cross-reference is to 15.107 where the codified paragraph refers to 15.208(a), and the RFO text says "established" where the codified text says "prescribed".

statement: RFO FAR 15.103-1 says the tradeoff approach to source selection is appropriate when it may be in the Government's best interest to consider award to other than the lowest priced offeror or other than the highest technically rated offeror.
quote: The tradeoff approach to source selection is appropriate when it may be in the Government’s best interest to consider award to other than the lowest priced offeror or other than the highest technically rated offeror.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO sentence calls it the tradeoff approach to source selection where the codified sentence calls it a tradeoff process; the condition for using it is the same in substance.

statement: RFO FAR 15.103-1 says, in two sentences, that this process permits tradeoffs among cost or price and non-cost or non-price factors and that the anticipated benefits of a higher priced proposal must merit the additional cost, and neither sentence says the process allows the Government to accept other than the lowest priced proposal or that the rationale for tradeoffs must be documented in the file.
quote: This process permits tradeoffs among cost or price and non-cost or non-price factors. The anticipated benefits of a higher priced proposal must merit the additional cost.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The codified paragraph (c) also says the process allows the Government to accept other than the lowest priced proposal, calls the benefits "perceived", and requires the rationale for tradeoffs to be documented in the file in accordance with 15.406; the RFO section says "anticipated" benefits and its documentation rule is in RFO FAR 15.205.

statement: RFO FAR 15.104(a) says all factors and significant subfactors that will affect contract award and their relative importance must be stated clearly in the RFP.
quote: All factors and significant subfactors that will affect contract award and their relative importance must be stated clearly in the RFP
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO sentence says "factors" where the codified paragraph says "evaluation factors", "must" where it says "shall", and names the RFP where it names the solicitation; unlike the codified paragraph (b), which applies when using a tradeoff process, the RFO sentence is not conditioned on using the tradeoff approach.

statement: RFO FAR 15.104(d) says that, unless the exception at paragraph (b)(1)(ii) of that section applies, the RFP must also state, at a minimum, whether all evaluation factors other than cost or price, when combined, are significantly more important than cost or price, which is the first item of a list.
quote: unless the exception at paragraph (b)(1)(ii) of this section applies, the RFP must also state, at a minimum, whether all evaluation factors other than cost or price, when combined, are— (1) Significantly more important than cost or price;
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO paragraph sits in the section on evaluation factors, refers to the exception at paragraph (b)(1)(ii), and says the RFP "must" state it where the codified paragraph says the solicitation "shall" state it.

statement: RFO FAR 15.104(d)(2)-(3) give the other two possibilities for how all evaluation factors other than cost or price, when combined, compare with cost or price: approximately equal to cost or price, or significantly less important than cost or price.
quote: (2) Approximately equal to cost or price; or (3) Significantly less important than cost or price
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The two possibilities are the same as in the codified paragraph.

statement: RFO FAR 15.205 says the source selection decision must be documented and include the rationale for any business judgments and tradeoffs made or relied on by the SSA, including benefits associated with additional costs, and that the documentation does not need to quantify the tradeoffs that led to the decision.
quote: The source selection decision must be documented and include the rationale for any business judgments and tradeoffs made or relied on by the SSA, including benefits associated with additional costs. The documentation does not need to quantify the tradeoffs that led to the decision.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text puts the documentation rule in the source selection decision section, says the rationale goes in the documentation of the decision where the codified paragraph says it must be documented in the file in accordance with 15.406, and adds that the tradeoffs need not be quantified.

statement: RFO FAR 15.408-1(a) says the prenegotiation objectives establish the Government's initial negotiation position and are based on the results of the contracting officer's analysis of the offeror's proposal, in a single sentence with no words on assisting the determination of a fair and reasonable price or on the information to be taken into consideration.
quote: (a) The prenegotiation objectives establish the Government's initial negotiation position and are based on the results of the contracting officer's analysis of the offeror's proposal.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO sentence says the objectives "are based on" the analysis where the codified paragraph says they "should be based on" it, and the codified paragraph also says the objectives assist the determination of a fair and reasonable price and lists the information to take into consideration.

statement: RFO FAR 15.408-1(b) says contracting officers must establish prenegotiation objectives before negotiating a pricing action, and that the scope and depth of the analysis supporting the objectives should be directly related to the dollar value, importance, and complexity of the pricing action.
quote: (b) Contracting officers must establish prenegotiation objectives before negotiating a pricing action. The scope and depth of the analysis supporting the objectives should be directly related to the dollar value, importance, and complexity of the pricing action.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO sentence says "before negotiating a pricing action" where the codified sentence says "before the negotiation of any pricing action", and says "must" where the codified sentence says the contracting officer "shall".

statement: RFO FAR 15.408-1(b) says that when cost analysis is required, contracting officers must document the pertinent issues to be negotiated, the cost objectives, and a profit or fee objective.
quote: When cost analysis is required, contracting officers must document the pertinent issues to be negotiated, the cost objectives, and a profit or fee objective.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO sentence says contracting officers "must" document these items where the codified sentence says the contracting officer "shall" document them.

statement: RFO FAR 15.102(b)(1) says contracting officers should prepare RFPs and resulting contracts using the uniform contract format at 15.109.
quote: Contracting officers should prepare RFPs and resulting contracts using the uniform contract format at 15.109.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text says contracting officers "should" prepare RFPs and resulting contracts using the format where the codified text says they "shall" prepare solicitations and resulting contracts using it.

statement: RFO FAR 15.102(b)(2) says agencies do not need to use the uniform contract format for construction and architect-engineer contracts or for subsistence contracts.
quote: (2) Exceptions. Agencies do not need to use the uniform contract format for: (i) Construction and architect-engineer contracts. (ii) Subsistence contracts.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text says agencies "do not need to use" the format where the codified text says it "need not be used"; the codified construction item also refers to part 36.

statement: RFO FAR 15.102(b)(2)(iii)-(v) say agencies also do not need to use the uniform contract format for supplies or services contracts requiring special contract formats prescribed elsewhere in part 15 that are inconsistent with the uniform contract format, for streamlined RFPs, or for contracts exempted by the agency head or designee.
quote: (iii) Supplies or services contracts requiring special contract formats prescribed elsewhere in this part that are inconsistent with the uniform contract format. (iv) Streamlined RFPs. (v) Contracts exempted by the agency head or designee.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO list names streamlined RFPs where the codified list names letter requests for proposals; the other two items are the same in substance.

statement: RFO FAR 15.109 says RFPs using the uniform contract format should include Parts I, II, III, and IV, and that upon award contracting officers should not physically include Part IV in the resulting contract but should retain it in the contract file.
quote: RFPs using the uniform contract format should include Parts I, II, III, and IV. Upon award, contracting officers should not physically include Part IV in the resulting contract, but should retain it in the contract file.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text says "should" where the codified text says "shall" for both the contents of the solicitation and the treatment of Part IV on award.

statement: RFO FAR 15.109 says the representations and certifications in Part IV are incorporated by reference in the contract through FAR clauses 52.204-19 and 52.212-4.
quote: The representations and certifications in Part IV are incorporated by reference in the contract through FAR clauses 52.204-19, Incorporation by Reference of Representations and Certifications, and 52.212-4, Contract Terms and Conditions-Commercial Products and Commercial Services.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO sentence names both clauses without the codified distinction between 52.204-19 and, for acquisitions of commercial products and commercial services, 52.212-4(v).

statement: RFO FAR 15.109-1 is headed Part I - The Schedule and begins with Section A, Solicitation/contract form.
quote: 15.109-1 Part I - The Schedule. (a) Section A, Solicitation/contract form.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The Part I heading and the Section A title are the same as in the codified table.

statement: RFO FAR 15.109-1(a)(2) says that when other than OF 308 or SF 33 is used, the first page of the RFP is to include the name, address, and location of the issuing activity, including room and building where proposals or information must be submitted, the RFP number, and the date of issuance.
quote: (2) When other than OF 308 or SF 33 is used, include the following information on the first page of the RFP: (i) Name, address, and location of issuing activity, including room and building where proposals or information must be submitted. (ii) RFP number. (iii) Date of issuance.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text says "RFP number" and "first page of the RFP" where the codified text says "Solicitation number" and "first page of the solicitation"; the rest is the same.

statement: RFO FAR 15.109-1(a)(2)(iv)-(vii) say the first page of the RFP is also to include the closing date and time, the number of RFP pages, the requisition or other purchase authority, and a brief description of the item or service.
quote: (iv) Closing date and time. (v) Number of RFP pages. (vi) Requisition or other purchase authority. (vii) Brief description of item or service.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text says "Number of RFP pages" where the codified text says "Number of pages"; the rest is the same. The condition "when other than OF 308 or SF 33 is used" is in the lead-in at RFO FAR 15.109-1(a)(2).

statement: RFO FAR 15.109-1(a)(2)(viii)-(ix) say the first page of the RFP is also to include the requirement for the offeror to provide its name and complete address, including street, city, county, state, and zip code, and email address if appropriate, and the offer expiration date.
quote: (viii) Requirement for the offeror to provide its name and complete address, including street, city, county, state, and zip code, and email address, if appropriate. (ix) Offer expiration date.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text says "email address" where the codified text says "electronic address (including facsimile address)". The condition "when other than OF 308 or SF 33 is used" is in the lead-in at RFO FAR 15.109-1(a)(2).

statement: RFO FAR 15.109-1(b) says Section B, Supplies or services and prices/costs, is to include a brief description of the supplies or services, including any incidental deliverables, and it gives no examples of the description or of incidental deliverables.
quote: (b) Section B, Supplies or services and prices/costs. Include a brief description of the supplies or services, including any incidental deliverables.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO paragraph gives no examples such as item number, national stock number or part number, nouns, nomenclature and quantities, and says "including any incidental deliverables" where the codified paragraph says this includes incidental deliverables such as manuals and reports.

statement: RFO FAR 15.109-1(c)-(d) say Section C, Description/specifications/requirements, is to include any description or specifications needed in addition to Section B, and Section D, Packaging and marking, is to include packaging, packing, preservation, and marking requirements, if any.
quote: (c) Section C, Description/specifications/requirements. Include any description or specifications needed in addition to Section B. (d) Section D, Packaging and marking. Include packaging, packing, preservation, and marking requirements, if any.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO heading for Section C reads Description/specifications/requirements where the codified heading reads Description/specifications/statement of work, and the RFO paragraph has no cross-reference to part 11.

statement: RFO FAR 15.109-1(e)-(f) say Section E, Inspection and acceptance, is to include inspection, acceptance, quality assurance, and reliability requirements, and Section F, Deliveries or performance, is to include the requirements for time, place, and method of delivery or performance.
quote: (e) Section E, Inspection and acceptance. Include inspection, acceptance, quality assurance, and reliability requirements. (f) Section F, Deliveries or performance. Include the requirements for time, place, and method of delivery or performance.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text says "Include" for Section F where the codified text says "Specify", and has none of the codified cross-references to other parts of the FAR.

statement: RFO FAR 15.109-1(g) says Section G, Contract administration data, is to include any required accounting and appropriation data and any required contract administration information or instructions not included in other sections of the uniform contract format.
quote: Section G, Contract administration data. Include any required accounting and appropriation data and any required contract administration information or instructions not included in other sections of the uniform contract format.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text says information or instructions "not included in other sections of the uniform contract format" where the codified text says "other than those on the solicitation form".

statement: RFO FAR 15.109-1(g) says to include a statement that the offeror should include the payment address in the proposal, if it is different from that shown for the offeror.
quote: Include a statement that the offeror should include the payment address in the proposal, if it is different from that shown for the offeror.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The wording is the same as the codified text.

statement: RFO FAR 15.109-1(h) says Section H, Special contract requirements, is to include a clear statement of any special contract requirements that are not included in Section I or in other sections of the uniform contract format.
quote: (h) Section H, Special contract requirements. Include a clear statement of any special contract requirements that are not included in Section I or in other sections of the uniform contract format.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text omits the words "Contract clauses" after "Section I"; it is the same in substance.

statement: RFO FAR 15.109-3, headed Part III - List of Documents, Exhibits, and Other Attachments, covers Section J, List of attachments.
quote: 15.109-3 Part III - List of Documents, Exhibits, and Other Attachments. Section J, List of attachments.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The Part III heading and the Section J title are the same as in the codified table.

statement: RFO FAR 15.109-4(a) says Section K, Representations, certifications, and other statements of offerors, is to include RFP provisions that require representations, certifications, or the submission of other information by offerors.
quote: (a) Section K, Representations, certifications, and other statements of offerors. Include RFP provisions that require representations, certifications, or the submission of other information by offerors.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text says "RFP provisions" where the codified text says "solicitation provisions".

statement: RFO FAR 15.109-4(b) says Section L, Instructions, conditions, and notices to offerors or respondents, is to include solicitation provisions and other information and instructions not required elsewhere to guide offerors in preparing proposals.
quote: (b) Section L, Instructions, conditions, and notices to offerors or respondents. Include solicitation provisions and other information and instructions not required elsewhere to guide offerors in preparing proposals.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text refers to guiding offerors in preparing proposals where the codified text refers to guiding offerors or respondents in preparing proposals or responses to requests for information.

statement: RFO FAR 15.109-4(b)(2) says offerors may be instructed to submit proposals or information in a specific format or severable parts to facilitate evaluation.
quote: (2) Offerors may be instructed to submit proposals or information in a specific format or severable parts to facilitate evaluation.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text speaks of offerors where the codified text speaks of prospective offerors or respondents; the rest is the same.

statement: RFO FAR 15.109-4(b)(2) says agencies may also require the proposal to be further organized into sections such as administrative, management, technical, past performance, and certified cost and pricing data or data other than certified cost and pricing data.
quote: Agencies may also require the proposal to be further organized into sections (e.g., administrative, management, technical, past performance, and certified cost and pricing data or data other than certified cost and pricing data).
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text says "certified cost and pricing data" where the codified text says "certified cost or pricing data", says agencies "may also require" where the codified text says the instructions may specify further organization, and has no cross-reference to Table 15-2.

statement: RFO FAR 15.109-4(c) says Section M, Evaluation factors for award, is to identify all significant factors and any significant subfactors that will be considered in awarding the contract, their relative importance, and one of the phrases in 15.104(d), as required.
quote: (c) Section M, Evaluation factors for award. Identify all significant factors and any significant subfactors that will be considered in awarding the contract, their relative importance, and one of the phrases in 15.104(d), as required.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text refers to the phrases in 15.104(d) where the codified text says the contracting officer shall insert one of the phrases in 15.304(e), and drops the codified cross-reference after "relative importance".

statement: RFO FAR 15.504-1(a)(1)-(2) say that before beginning a comprehensive evaluation, the agency contact point must determine if the proposal is a valid unsolicited proposal, as described at 15.503-1(b), and is suitable for submission in response to an existing agency requirement.
quote: (a) Before beginning a comprehensive evaluation, the agency contact point must determine if the proposal— (1) Is a valid unsolicited proposal, as described at 15.503-1(b); (2) Is suitable for submission in response to an existing agency requirement;
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text says "beginning" and "must" where the codified text says "initiating" and "shall", and refers to 15.503-1(b) where the codified text refers to 15.603(c) and 15.602.

statement: RFO FAR 15.504-1(a)(3)-(4) list, among the matters the agency contact point is to determine, whether the proposal is related to the agency mission and contains sufficient technical information and cost-related or price-related information for evaluation.
quote: (3) Is related to the agency mission; (4) Contains sufficient technical information and cost-related or price-related information for evaluation;
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The two items are word for word the same as the codified items; the lead-in to paragraph (a) says must where the codified lead-in says shall.

statement: RFO FAR 15.504-1(a)(5)-(7) list, as further matters, whether the proposal has overall scientific, technical, or socioeconomic merit, has been approved by a responsible official or other representative authorized to obligate the offeror contractually, and complies with the marking requirements of this subpart.
quote: (5) Has overall scientific, technical, or socioeconomic merit; (6) Has been approved by a responsible official or other representative authorized to obligate the offeror contractually; and (7) Complies with the marking requirements of this subpart.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text says "of this subpart" where the codified text says "of 15.609"; the rest is the same.

statement: RFO FAR 15.504-1(b) says that if the proposal meets these requirements, the contact point must promptly acknowledge receipt and process the proposal.
quote: (b) If the proposal meets these requirements, the contact point must promptly acknowledge receipt and process the proposal.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO paragraph says the contact point "must" where the codified paragraph says it "shall".

statement: RFO FAR 15.504-1(c) says that if a proposal is rejected because it does not meet these requirements, the agency contact point must promptly inform the offeror in writing of the reasons for rejection and the proposed disposition of the unsolicited proposal.
quote: (c) If a proposal is rejected because the proposal does not meet these requirements, the agency contact point must promptly inform the offeror in writing of the reasons for rejection and the proposed disposition of the unsolicited proposal.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO paragraph says the contact point "must" where the codified paragraph says it "shall", and says "these requirements" where the codified paragraph says "the requirements of paragraph (a) of this subsection".

statement: RFO FAR 15.505(e) says a favorable evaluation of an unsolicited proposal does not, in itself, justify awarding a contract without providing for full and open competition.
quote: (e) A favorable evaluation of an unsolicited proposal does not, in itself, justify awarding a contract without providing for full and open competition.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO sentence says "a favorable evaluation" where the codified sentence says "a favorable comprehensive evaluation".

statement: RFO FAR 15.505(e) says the agency point of contact should return an unsolicited proposal to the offeror, citing reasons, when its substance is available to the Government without restriction from another source or closely resembles a pending competitive acquisition requirement.
quote: The agency point of contact should return an unsolicited proposal to the offeror, citing reasons, when its substance— (1) Is available to the Government without restriction from another source; (2) Closely resembles a pending competitive acquisition requirement;
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO sentence says the agency point of contact "should return" the proposal where the codified sentence says it "shall return" it.

statement: RFO FAR 15.505(e)(3)-(4) list, as further circumstances in the same sentence, that the proposal's substance does not relate to the activity's mission or does not demonstrate an innovative and unique method, approach, or concept, or is otherwise not deemed a meritorious proposal.
quote: (3) Does not relate to the activity's mission; or (4) Does not demonstrate an innovative and unique method, approach, or concept, or is otherwise not deemed a meritorious proposal.
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The two items are word for word the same as the codified items; the lead-in says the agency point of contact should return the proposal where the codified lead-in says shall, which makes the paragraph a deviation.

statement: RFO FAR 15.506 says contracting officers may begin negotiations on a sole source basis only when, among other conditions, an unsolicited proposal receives a favorable comprehensive evaluation and a justification and approval is obtained in accordance with part 6.
quote: Contracting officers may begin negotiations on a sole source basis only when— (a) An unsolicited proposal receives a favorable comprehensive evaluation; (b) A justification and approval is obtained in accordance with part 6;
note: The RFO model text prints no date; effective_from is the date DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0048 Revision 1 took effect (CL-EST-3177). The RFO text says "may begin" where the codified text says "may commence", and refers to part 6 for the justification and approval where the codified text refers to 6.302-1(a)(2)(i) for research proposals or other appropriate provisions of subpart 6.3, and 6.303-2(c).

quote: Whenever the person filing notification is unable to supply a complete response, that person shall provide, for each item for which less than a complete response has been supplied, a statement of reasons for noncompliance.

statement: The statement of reasons for noncompliance must contain all information on which the person relies to explain its noncompliance and must include at least the items the section then lists; the first item, in paragraph (a), is why the person is unable to supply a complete response.
quote: The statement of reasons for noncompliance shall contain all information upon which a person relies in explanation of its noncompliance and shall include at least the following: (a) Why the person is unable to supply a complete response;

statement: Paragraph (b) lists, among the items the statement of reasons must include, what information, and what specific documents or categories of documents, would have been required for a complete response.
quote: (b) What information, and what specific documents or categories of documents, would have been required for a complete response;

statement: Paragraph (c) lists, among the items the statement of reasons must include, who, if anyone, has the required information and the specific documents or categories of documents, and a description of all efforts made to obtain them, including the names of the persons who searched and where the search was conducted.
quote: (c) Who, if anyone, has the required information, and specific documents or categories of documents; and a description of all efforts made to obtain such information and documents, including the names of persons who searched for required information and documents, and where the search was conducted.

statement: Under paragraph (c), if no such efforts were made, the statement must provide an explanation of the reasons why and a description of all efforts necessary to obtain the required information and documents.
quote: If no such efforts were made, provide an explanation of the reasons why, and a description of all efforts necessary to obtain required information and documents;

statement: Paragraph (d) lists, among the items the statement of reasons must include, where noncompliance is based on a claim of privilege, a statement of the claim and all facts relied on in support of it, including the identity of each document, its author, the author's title or position, and the addressee; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MNA-0207.
quote: (d) Where noncompliance is based on a claim of privilege, a statement of the claim of privilege and all facts relied on in support thereof, including the identity of each document, its author, the author's title/position, addressee,

statement: Paragraph (d) also lists, for a claim of privilege, the addressee's title or position, the date, the subject matter, all recipients of the original and of any copies and their titles or positions, the document's present location, and who has control of it.
quote: the addressee's title/position, date, subject matter, all recipients of the original and of any copies, the recipients' titles/positions, the document's present location, and who has control of it.

statement: In the example to paragraph (a)(1)(vi), the acquiring company "A" sends a notice letter by email to a general email account of the target; the paragraph gives the address, and the next sentence, quoted in CL-MNA-0209, states the result.
quote: “A” sends, via email, a notice letter to a general email account,

statement: In the example to paragraph (a)(1)(vi), the acquiring company "A" has not provided sufficient notice by the email to a general email account described in CL-MNA-0208.
quote: “A” has not provided sufficient notice.

statement: Paragraph (a) is written for an acquisition to which § 801.30 does not apply and in which no assets other than investment assets located in the United States, and no voting securities of a United States issuer, will be acquired directly or indirectly; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MNA-0211.
quote: In an acquisition to which § 801.30 does not apply, and in which no assets (other than investment assets) located in the United States and no voting securities of a United States issuer will be acquired directly or indirectly,

statement: In an acquisition of the kind described in CL-MNA-0210, if a foreign acquired person refuses to file notification, any other person that is a party to the acquisition may file notification on behalf of the foreign person.
quote: if a foreign acquired person refuses to file notification, then any other person which is a party to the acquisition may file notification on behalf of the foreign person.

statement: Under paragraph (a), a notification filed on behalf of the foreign person constitutes the notification that the act and the rules required of the foreign person.
quote: Such notification shall constitute the notification required of the foreign person by the act and these rules.

statement: Under paragraph (b), a person filing on behalf of the foreign person under this section must state in the affidavit required by § 803.5(b) that the foreign person has refused to file notification; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MNA-0214.
quote: Any person filing on behalf of the foreign person pursuant to this section must state in the affidavit required by § 803.5(b) that such foreign person has refused to file notification

statement: Under paragraph (b), the person filing on behalf of the foreign person must also explain all efforts it made to obtain the foreign person's compliance with the act and the rules.
quote: and must explain all efforts made by the person filing on behalf of the foreign person to obtain compliance with the act and these rules by such foreign person.

statement: Under paragraph (c), a notification filed on behalf of the foreign person must contain all information and documentary material reasonably available to the person filing that the foreign person would be required to provide.
quote: (c) Any notification filed on behalf of a foreign person pursuant to this section must contain all information and documentary material reasonably available to the person filing on behalf of the foreign person which such foreign person would be required to provide.

statement: Under paragraph (c), where information or documentary material is not reasonably available, the person filing on behalf of the foreign person must indicate that on the Notification and Report Form and need not supply the statement of reasons for noncompliance required by § 803.3.
quote: Whenever information or documentary material is not reasonably available, the person filing on behalf of the foreign person shall so indicate on the Notification and Report Form, and need not supply the statement of reasons for noncompliance required by § 803.3.

statement: Under paragraph (d), a foreign person on whose behalf another person has filed notification under this section is a "person filing notification" for purposes of the act and the rules.
quote: Any foreign person on whose behalf notification has been filed by another person pursuant to this section shall be a “person filing notification” for purposes of the act and these rules.

statement: Under paragraph (d), nothing in this section exempts the foreign person from the requirements of the act or the rules for a request for additional information or an extension of the waiting period under section 7A(e).
quote: Nothing in this section shall exempt a foreign person from the requirements of the act or these rules with respect to a request for additional information or an extension of the waiting period pursuant to section 7A(e) and these rules.

statement: In the example to paragraph (a)(1)(vi), the acquiring company "A" has provided email notice to a specific officer of the target "B" where it emailed a notice letter to a named officer; the paragraph gives that officer's name and email address, which this claim does not quote.
quote: “A” has provided email notice to a specific officer of “B.”

statement: Under paragraph (a)(1), for acquisitions to which § 801.30 applies, the notification required from each acquiring person must contain an affidavit attesting that the issuer or unincorporated entity whose voting securities or non-corporate interests are to be acquired has received written notice; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MNA-0221.
quote: For acquisitions to which § 801.30 of this chapter applies, the notification required by the act from each acquiring person shall contain an affidavit attesting that the issuer or unincorporated entity whose voting securities or non-corporate interests are to be acquired has received written notice

statement: The written notice must be delivered to an officer, or to a person exercising similar functions where the entity has no officers, by email, certified or registered mail, wire, or hand delivery, at the entity's principal executive offices, and must give the information listed in paragraphs (a)(1)(i) through (vi).
quote: delivered to an officer (or a person exercising similar functions in the case of an entity without officers) by email, certified or registered mail, wire, or hand delivery, at its principal executive offices, of:

statement: Paragraph (a)(1)(i) and (ii): the notice must state the identity of the acquiring person and the fact that the acquiring person intends to acquire voting securities or non-corporate interests of the issuer or unincorporated entity.
quote: (i) The identity of the acquiring person; (ii) The fact that the acquiring person intends to acquire voting securities or non-corporate interests of the issuer or unincorporated entity;

statement: Paragraph (a)(1)(iii): the notice must state the specific classes of voting securities or non-corporate interests sought to be acquired and, if known, the number of each class that the acquiring person would hold as a result of the acquisition; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MNA-0224.
quote: The specific classes of voting securities or non-corporate interests of the issuer or unincorporated entity sought to be acquired; and if known, the number of voting securities or non-corporate interests of each such class that would be held by the acquiring person as a result of the acquisition

statement: Paragraph (a)(1)(iii) continues: if the number of voting securities is not known in the case of an issuer, the notice must state the specific notification threshold that the acquiring person intends to meet or exceed.
quote: or, if the number of voting securities is not known in the case of an issuer, the specific notification threshold that the acquiring person intends to meet or exceed;

statement: Paragraph (a)(1)(iii) ends: if the acquiring person designates one, the notice must also state a higher threshold for additional voting securities it may hold in the year following the expiration of the waiting period.
quote: and, if designated by the acquiring person, a higher threshold for additional voting securities it may hold in the year following the expiration of the waiting period;

statement: Paragraph (a)(1)(iv): the notice must state the fact that the acquisition may be subject to the act and that the acquiring person will file notification under the act with the Federal Trade Commission and the Assistant Attorney General.
quote: (iv) The fact that the acquisition may be subject to the act, and that the acquiring person will file notification under the act with the Federal Trade Commission and Assistant Attorney General;

statement: Paragraph (a)(1)(v): the notice must state the anticipated date of receipt of the notification under § 803.10(c).
quote: (v) The anticipated date of receipt of such notification under § 803.10(c);

statement: Paragraph (a)(1)(vi): the notice must state the fact that the person within which the issuer or unincorporated entity is included may be required to file notification under the act.
quote: (vi) The fact that the person within which the issuer or unincorporated entity is included may be required to file notification under the act.

statement: Under paragraph (a)(2), the affidavit must also state the good faith intention of the person filing notification to make the acquisition and, in the case of a tender offer, that the intention to make the tender offer has been publicly announced.
quote: The affidavit required by this paragraph must also state the good faith intention of the person filing notification to make the acquisition, and, in the case of a tender offer, that the intention to make the tender offer has been publicly announced.

statement: The example under paragraph (a)(2) states that this paragraph permits the tender offeror to file notification at any time after the intention to make the tender offer has been publicly announced.
quote: This paragraph permits the tender offeror to file notification at any time after the intention to make the tender offer has been publicly announced.

statement: In example 4 to paragraph (a)(2), a notice that states, among other things, that depending on market conditions the acquiring company may acquire 100 percent of the target's shares does not comply with § 803.5 because it does not state an intent to meet or exceed any notification threshold.
quote: “A” states, inter alia, that, “depending on market conditions, it may acquire 100 percent of the shares of B.” “A”'s notice does not comply with § 803.5 because it does not state an intent to meet or exceed any notification threshold.

statement: Under paragraph (a)(3), the affidavit required by paragraph (a) must have attached to it a copy of the written notice that the acquired person received under paragraph (a)(1).
quote: The affidavit required by this paragraph must have attached to it a copy of the written notice received by the acquired person pursuant to paragraph (a)(1) of this section.

statement: Under paragraph (b), for acquisitions to which § 801.30 does not apply, the notification must contain an affidavit attesting that a contract, agreement in principle, or letter of intent to merge or acquire has been executed; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MNA-0234.
quote: For acquisitions to which § 801.30 of this chapter does not apply, the notification required by the act shall contain an affidavit attesting that a contract, agreement in principle, or letter of intent to merge or acquire has been executed

statement: Under paragraph (b), the affidavit must further attest to the good faith intention of the person filing notification to complete the transaction.
quote: and further attesting to the good faith intention of the person filing notification to complete the transaction.

statement: Under paragraph (b), if the executed agreement is not the definitive agreement, the affidavit must attest that a dated document that provides sufficient detail about the scope of the entire transaction that the parties intend to consummate has also been submitted.
quote: If the executed agreement is not the definitive agreement, the affidavit must attest that a dated document that provides sufficient detail about the scope of the entire transaction that the parties intend to consummate has also been submitted.

statement: Under paragraph (a), the Commission staff may consider requests for formal or informal interpretations as to the obligations under the act and the rules of any party to an acquisition.
quote: (a) The Commission staff may consider requests for formal or informal interpretations as to the obligations under the act and these rules of any party to an acquisition.

statement: Under paragraph (a), a request for a formal interpretation must be made in writing to the offices designated in § 803.10(c) and must state the matters the section then lists; those matters are quoted in CL-MNA-0238.
quote: A request for a formal interpretation shall be made in writing to the offices designated in § 803.10(c), and shall state:

statement: Under paragraph (a), a request for a formal interpretation must state all facts that the applicant believes to be material, the reasons why the requirements of the act are or may be applicable, and the questions that the applicant wishes resolved.
quote: (1) all facts which the applicant believes to be material, (2) the reasons why the requirements of the act are or may be applicable and (3) the question(s) that the applicant wishes resolved.

statement: Under paragraph (a), the Commission staff may, in its discretion, render a formal or informal response to any request, however made, or may decline to render such advice.
quote: The Commission staff may, in its discretion, render a formal or informal response to any request, however made, or may decline to render such advice.

statement: Under paragraph (b), in the sole discretion of the staff, any request for interpretation may be referred to the Commission.
quote: (b) In the sole discretion of the staff, any request for interpretation may be referred to the Commission.

statement: Under paragraph (c), formal interpretations by the Commission staff or by the Commission must be rendered with the concurrence of the Assistant Attorney General or his or her designee.
quote: (c) Formal interpretations by the Commission staff or by the Commission shall be rendered with the concurrence of the Assistant Attorney General or his or her designee.

statement: Under paragraph (d), any formal interpretation is without prejudice to the right of either the Commission or the Assistant Attorney General to rescind it.
quote: (d) Any formal interpretation shall be without prejudice to the right of either the Commission or the Assistant Attorney General to rescind any such interpretation rendered pursuant to this section.

statement: Under paragraph (d), if a formal interpretation is rescinded, the party that requested it must be notified in writing.
quote: In the event of such rescission, the party which requested the interpretation shall be so notified in writing.

statement: Under paragraph (e), the Commission must publish in the Federal Register a summary of formal interpretations by the Commission, and any rescissions of them.
quote: (e) The Commission shall publish a summary of formal interpretations by the Commission, and any rescissions thereof, in the Federal Register.

statement: In example 2 to paragraph (a)(2), if 1,000,000 shares of the target represent 20 percent of its outstanding voting securities, the enforcement agencies will deem the acquiring company's statement a notification for the $100 million threshold (as adjusted).
quote: If 1,000,000 shares of Company B represent 20 percent of Company B's outstanding voting securities, the statement will be deemed by the enforcement agencies a notification for the $100 million threshold (as adjusted).

statement: In example 3 to paragraph (a)(2), the acquiring company's notice to the acquired person would meet the requirements of paragraph (a)(1)(iii) if it states either of the two wordings that follow, quoted in CL-MNA-0247 and CL-MNA-0248.
quote: “A”'s notice to the acquired person would meet the requirements of Sec. 803.5(a)(1)(iii) if it states, inter alia, either:

statement: In example 3 to paragraph (a)(2), one wording that would meet paragraph (a)(1)(iii) is a present good faith intention to acquire in excess of $50 million (as adjusted) of the target's outstanding voting securities, with a statement that, depending on market conditions, the company may acquire more and thus designates the 50 percent threshold.
quote: “Company A has a present good faith intention to acquire in excess of $50 million (as adjusted) of the outstanding voting securities of Company B, and depending on market conditions, may acquire more of the voting securities of Company B and thus designates the 50 percent threshold,”

statement: In example 3 to paragraph (a)(2), the other wording that would meet paragraph (a)(1)(iii) is a present good faith intention to acquire in excess of $50 million (as adjusted) of the target's outstanding voting securities, with a statement that, depending on market conditions, the company may acquire 50 percent or more of them.
quote: “Company A has a present good faith intention to acquire in excess of $50 million (as adjusted) of the outstanding voting securities of Company B, and depending on market conditions may acquire 50 percent or more of the voting securities of Company B.”

statement: In example 3 to paragraph (a)(2), the Commission would deem either of the two wordings quoted in CL-MNA-0247 and CL-MNA-0248 as intending to give notice for the 50 percent threshold.
quote: The Commission would deem either of these statements as intending to give notice for the 50 percent threshold.

statement: Unless specified otherwise, the definitions in this section apply to the terms used in Regulation M-A (§§ 229.1000 through 229.1016), and Associate has the same meaning as in § 240.12b-2 of the same chapter.
quote: The following definitions apply to the terms used in Regulation M-A (§§ 229.1000 through 229.1016), unless specified otherwise: (a) Associate has the same meaning as in § 240.12b-2 of this chapter;

statement: If there are no appraisal rights available under state law for security holders who object to the transaction, paragraph (d) requires a brief outline of any other rights that may be available to security holders under the law.
quote: If there are no appraisal rights available under state law for security holders who object to the transaction, briefly outline any other rights that may be available to security holders under the law.

statement: Instruction C means General Instruction C to Schedule 13E-3 (§ 240.13e-100) and General Instruction C to Schedule TO (§ 240.14d-100), each section being in the same chapter.
quote: (b) Instruction C means General Instruction C to Schedule 13E-3 (§ 240.13e-100 of this chapter) and General Instruction C to Schedule TO (§ 240.14d-100 of this chapter);

statement: Issuer tender offer has the same meaning as in § 240.13e-4(a)(2) of the same chapter.
quote: (c) Issuer tender offer has the same meaning as in § 240.13e-4(a)(2) of this chapter;

statement: Offeror means any person who makes a tender offer or on whose behalf a tender offer is made.
quote: (d) Offeror means any person who makes a tender offer or on whose behalf a tender offer is made;

statement: Rule 13e-3 transaction has the same meaning as in § 240.13e-3(a)(3) of the same chapter.
quote: (e) Rule 13e-3 transaction has the same meaning as in § 240.13e-3(a)(3) of this chapter;

statement: Subject company means the company or entity whose securities are sought to be acquired in the transaction (for example, the target), or that is otherwise the subject of the transaction.
quote: (f) Subject company means the company or entity whose securities are sought to be acquired in the transaction (e.g., the target), or that is otherwise the subject of the transaction;

statement: Subject securities means the securities or class of securities that are sought to be acquired in the transaction or that are otherwise the subject of the transaction.
quote: (g) Subject securities means the securities or class of securities that are sought to be acquired in the transaction or that are otherwise the subject of the transaction;

statement: Third-party tender offer means a tender offer that is not an issuer tender offer.
quote: (h) Third-party tender offer means a tender offer that is not an issuer tender offer.

statement: The item requires security holders to be provided with a summary term sheet written in plain English, and the sheet must briefly describe the most material terms of the proposed transaction in bullet point format.
quote: Provide security holders with a summary term sheet that is written in plain English. The summary term sheet must briefly describe in bullet point format the most material terms of the proposed transaction.

statement: The summary term sheet must provide security holders with sufficient information to understand the essential features and significance of the proposed transaction.
quote: The summary term sheet must provide security holders with sufficient information to understand the essential features and significance of the proposed transaction.

statement: The bullet points must cross-reference a more detailed discussion contained in the disclosure document that is disseminated to security holders.
quote: The bullet points must cross-reference a more detailed discussion contained in the disclosure document that is disseminated to security holders.

statement: Instruction 1 provides that the summary term sheet must not recite all information contained in the disclosure document that will be provided to security holders, and that it is intended to serve as an overview of all material matters presented in the accompanying documents provided to security holders.
quote: The summary term sheet must not recite all information contained in the disclosure document that will be provided to security holders. The summary term sheet is intended to serve as an overview of all material matters that are presented in the accompanying documents provided to security holders.

statement: Instruction 2 requires the summary term sheet to begin on the first or second page of the disclosure document provided to security holders, and instruction 3 refers to Rule 421(b) and (d) of Regulation C of the Securities Act (§ 230.421 of the same chapter) for a description of plain English disclosure.
quote: 2. The summary term sheet must begin on the first or second page of the disclosure document provided to security holders. 3. Refer to Rule 421(b) and (d) of Regulation C of the Securities Act (§ 230.421 of this chapter) for a description of plain English disclosure.

statement: Paragraph (a) requires the name of the subject company (or of the issuer in the case of an issuer tender offer) and the address and telephone number of its principal executive offices.
quote: (a) Name and address. State the name of the subject company (or the issuer in the case of an issuer tender offer), and the address and telephone number of its principal executive offices.

statement: Paragraph (b) requires the exact title and number of shares outstanding of the subject class of equity securities as of the most recent practicable date.
quote: (b) Securities. State the exact title and number of shares outstanding of the subject class of equity securities as of the most recent practicable date.

statement: The title and share count under paragraph (b) may be based on information in the subject company's most recently available filing with the Commission, unless the filing person has more current information.
quote: This may be based upon information in the most recently available filing with the Commission by the subject company unless the filing person has more current information.

statement: Paragraph (c) requires identification of the principal market in which the subject securities are traded and a statement of the high and low sales prices for them in that market; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MNA-0268.
quote: (c) Trading market and price. Identify the principal market in which the subject securities are traded and state the high and low sales prices for the subject securities in the principal market

statement: Where there is no principal market, the range of high and low bid quotations and the source of the quotations are given instead, and the prices or quotations are given for each quarter during the past two years. If there is no established trading market for the securities (limited or sporadic quotations aside), paragraph (c) requires the filing to say so.
quote: (or, if there is no principal market, the range of high and low bid quotations and the source of the quotations) for each quarter during the past two years. If there is no established trading market for the securities (except for limited or sporadic quotations), so state.

statement: Paragraph (d) requires the frequency and amount of any dividends paid during the past two years on the subject securities and a brief description of any restriction on the subject company's current or future ability to pay dividends.
quote: (d) Dividends. State the frequency and amount of any dividends paid during the past two years with respect to the subject securities. Briefly describe any restriction on the subject company's current or future ability to pay dividends.

statement: If the filing person is not the subject company, it furnishes the dividend information under paragraph (d) to the extent known after making reasonable inquiry.
quote: If the filing person is not the subject company, furnish this information to the extent known after making reasonable inquiry.

statement: Paragraph (e) applies if the filing person has made an underwritten public offering of the subject securities for cash during the past three years that was registered under the Securities Act of 1933 or exempt from registration under Regulation A (§ 230.251 through § 230.263 of the same chapter); the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MNA-0272.
quote: (e) Prior public offerings. If the filing person has made an underwritten public offering of the subject securities for cash during the past three years that was registered under the Securities Act of 1933 or exempt from registration under Regulation A (§ 230.251 through § 230.263 of this chapter),

statement: For such an offering the filing person states the date of the offering, the amount of securities offered, the offering price per share (adjusted for stock splits, stock dividends and the like as appropriate) and the aggregate proceeds received by the filing person; the quoted words complete the sentence in CL-MNA-0271.
quote: state the date of the offering, the amount of securities offered, the offering price per share (adjusted for stock splits, stock dividends, etc. as appropriate) and the aggregate proceeds received by the filing person.

statement: If the filing person purchased any subject securities during the past two years, paragraph (f) requires the amount purchased, the range of prices paid and the average purchase price for each quarter during that period.
quote: (f) Prior stock purchases. If the filing person purchased any subject securities during the past two years, state the amount of the securities purchased, the range of prices paid and the average purchase price for each quarter during that period.

statement: Affiliates need not give information for purchases made before becoming an affiliate.
quote: Affiliates need not give information for purchases made before becoming an affiliate.

statement: Paragraph (a) requires the name, business address and business telephone number of each filing person, and also the name and address of each person specified in Instruction C to the schedule; the second requirement excepts Schedule 14D-9 (§ 240.14d-101 of the same chapter).
quote: (a) Name and address. State the name, business address and business telephone number of each filing person. Also state the name and address of each person specified in Instruction C to the schedule (except for Schedule 14D-9 (§ 240.14d-101 of this chapter)).

statement: A filing person that is an affiliate of the subject company states the nature of the affiliation, and a filing person that is the subject company says so.
quote: If the filing person is an affiliate of the subject company, state the nature of the affiliation. If the filing person is the subject company, so state.
