quote: If a period or periods reported on include operations of a business prior to the date of acquisition, or for other reasons differ from reports previously issued for any period, the statements shall be reconciled as to sales or revenues and net income
note: The paragraph goes on to say the reconciliation is in the statement or in a note and is with the amounts previously reported, and then states a proviso, quoted in the next claim.

statement: The reconciliations need not be made if they have been made in filings with the Commission in prior years, or if the financial statements being retroactively adjusted have not previously been filed with the Commission or otherwise made public.
quote: Provided, however, That such reconciliations need not be made (1) if they have been made in filings with the Commission in prior years or (2) the financial statements which are being retroactively adjusted have not previously been filed with the Commission or otherwise made public.

statement: Subject to the rule in the next claims (CL-MNA-1536; CL-MNA-1537) on adjustments that are not all of a normal recurring nature, any unaudited interim financial statements furnished shall reflect all adjustments which are, in the opinion of management, necessary to a fair statement of the results for the interim periods presented, and a statement to that effect shall be included.
quote: (d) Any unaudited interim financial statements furnished shall reflect all adjustments which are, in the opinion of management, necessary to a fair statement of the results for the interim periods presented. A statement to that effect shall be included.

statement: The financial statements that an issuer or guarantor of a guaranteed security would otherwise be required to file may be omitted if the issuer or guarantor is a consolidated subsidiary of the parent company, the parent company's consolidated financial statements have been filed, and the conditions in paragraphs (a)(1) and (2) have been met.

quote: (ii) A consolidated subsidiary issues the security or co-issues the security with one or more other consolidated subsidiaries of the parent company, and the security is guaranteed fully and unconditionally by the parent company; and
note: Read with the claim for the preceding paragraph, which states that the security must be debt or debt-like.

quote: (2) The parent company provides the disclosures specified in § 210.13-01.

quote: the registrant is the parent company (as that term is defined in § 210.3-10(b)(1)) of one or more subsidiaries that issue or guarantee the guaranteed security, provide the following disclosures to the extent material: (1) A description of the issuers and guarantors of the guaranteed security;

quote: (b) The parent company may elect to provide the disclosures required by this section in a footnote to its consolidated financial statements or alternatively, in management's discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations described in § 229.303
note: The paragraph goes on to say where the disclosures go in the prospectus if they are in neither place.

quote: shall apply to each security registered or being registered that is issued on or after January 4, 2021, and to each registered security issued and outstanding before January 4, 2021, for which the registrant had prior to that date provided the financial statements specified in § 210.3-16.

statement: One listed disclosure is a description of the terms and conditions of the collateral arrangement, including the events or circumstances that would require delivery of the collateral.

statement: One listed disclosure is summarized financial information of each affiliate whose securities are pledged as collateral, with an accompanying note that briefly describes the basis of presentation.
quote: (4) Summarized financial information as specified in § 210.1-02(bb)(1) of each affiliate whose securities are pledged as collateral as follows, with an accompanying note that briefly describes the basis of presentation:

note: The opening condition of the sentence is quoted in CL-MNA-0952.

note: The smaller reporting company alternative in the same sentence is quoted in CL-MNA-0955.

statement: Condensed financial information as to financial position, cash flows and results of operations of the registrant is provided as of the same dates and for the same periods for which audited consolidated financial statements are required.
quote: (a) Provide condensed financial information as to financial position, cash flows and results of operations of the registrant as of the same dates and for the same periods for which audited consolidated financial statements are required.

statement: In example 4 to paragraph (a)(2), the acquiring company's filing will be considered deficient within the meaning of § 803.10(c)(2) because its notice does not state an intent to meet or exceed any notification threshold (CL-MNA-0231).
quote: “A” 's filing will be considered deficient within the meaning of § 803.10(c)(2).

statement: In example 5 to paragraph (a)(2), a notice that says the acquiring company has commenced a tender offer for up to 55 percent of the target's outstanding voting securities does not comply with § 803.5 because the term "up to" does not state an intent to meet or exceed any notification threshold.
quote: “A” states, inter alia, that it has commenced a tender offer for “up to 55 percent of the outstanding voting securities of Company B.” “A” 's notice does not comply with § 803.5 because use of the term “up to” does not state an intent to meet or exceed any notification threshold.

statement: In example 5 to paragraph (a)(2), the filing will be considered deficient within the meaning of § 803.10(c)(2) because the notice does not comply with § 803.5 (CL-MNA-1023).
quote: The filing will therefore be considered deficient within the meaning of § 803.10 (c)(2).

statement: In examples 2 through 5 to paragraph (a)(2), the section assumes that one percent of the target's shares are valued at $15 million.
quote: In examples 2-5 assume that one percent of B's shares are valued at $15 million.

statement: In example 2 to paragraph (a)(2), the acquiring company holds 100,000 shares of the target's voting securities, has a good faith intention to acquire an additional 900,000 shares, and states in its notice to the target that as a result of the acquisition it will hold 1,000,000 shares.
quote: “A” holds 100,000 shares of the voting securities of Company B. “A” has a good faith intention to acquire an additional 900,000 shares of Company B's voting securities. “A” states in its notice to B, inter alia, that as a result of the acquisition it will hold 1,000,000 shares.

statement: In example 3 to paragraph (a)(2), the acquiring company intends to acquire voting securities of the target, does not know exactly how many shares it will acquire, knows it will definitely acquire in excess of $50 million (as adjusted) worth, and may acquire 50 percent of the target's shares.
quote: Company A intends to acquire voting securities of Company B. “A” does not know exactly how many shares it will acquire, but it knows it will definitely acquire in excess of $50 million (as adjusted) worth and may acquire 50 percent of Company B's shares.

statement: Paragraph (e) requires a description of any provision made by the filing person in connection with the transaction to grant unaffiliated security holders access to the corporate files of the filing person or to obtain counsel or appraisal services at the expense of the filing person, and, if there is none, a statement to that effect.

quote: describe whether or not the filing person will take steps to assure that the securities offered are or will be eligible for trading on an automated quotations system operated by a national securities association.

statement: Paragraph (a) requires a brief statement of the nature and approximate dollar amount of any transaction, other than those described in paragraphs (b) or (c), that occurred during the past two years between the filing person (including any person specified in Instruction C) and the persons described in paragraph (a)(1) and (a)(2); the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MNA-1056, CL-MNA-1057 and CL-MNA-1058.
quote: (a) Transactions. Briefly state the nature and approximate dollar amount of any transaction, other than those described in paragraphs (b) or (c) of this section, that occurred during the past two years, between the filing person (including any person specified in Instruction C of the schedule) and;

statement: Paragraph (a)(1) reaches the subject company or any of its affiliates that are not natural persons if the aggregate value of the transactions is more than one percent of the subject company's consolidated revenues for the fiscal year when the transaction occurred; the quoted words are incomplete here and continue in CL-MNA-1057.
quote: (1) The subject company or any of its affiliates that are not natural persons if the aggregate value of the transactions is more than one percent of the subject company's consolidated revenues for: (i) The fiscal year when the transaction occurred;

quote: or (ii) The past portion of the current fiscal year, if the transaction occurred in the current year;

statement: Paragraph (a)(2) reaches any executive officer, director or affiliate of the subject company that is a natural person if the aggregate value of the transaction or series of similar transactions with that person exceeds $60,000.
quote: (2) Any executive officer, director or affiliate of the subject company that is a natural person if the aggregate value of the transaction or series of similar transactions with that person exceeds $60,000.

statement: Paragraph (b) requires a description of any negotiations, transactions or material contacts during the past two years between the filing person (including subsidiaries of the filing person and any person specified in Instruction C) and the subject company or its affiliates concerning any of the matters listed in CL-MNA-1060.
quote: Describe any negotiations, transactions or material contacts during the past two years between the filing person (including subsidiaries of the filing person and any person specified in Instruction C of the schedule) and the subject company or its affiliates concerning any:

statement: The matters listed in paragraph (b) are any merger, consolidation, acquisition, tender offer for or other acquisition of any class of the subject company's securities, election of the subject company's directors, and sale or other transfer of a material amount of assets of the subject company; the quoted list completes the sentence in CL-MNA-1059.
quote: (1) Merger; (2) Consolidation; (3) Acquisition; (4) Tender offer for or other acquisition of any class of the subject company's securities; (5) Election of the subject company's directors; or (6) Sale or other transfer of a material amount of assets of the subject company.

statement: Paragraph (c) requires a description of any negotiations or material contacts concerning the matters referred to in paragraph (b) during the past two years between any affiliates of the subject company; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and a second pairing follows in CL-MNA-1062.
quote: (c) Negotiations or contacts. Describe any negotiations or material contacts concerning the matters referred to in paragraph (b) of this section during the past two years between: (1) Any affiliates of the subject company;

statement: Paragraph (c) also reaches negotiations or material contacts between the subject company or any of its affiliates and any person not affiliated with the subject company who would have a direct interest in such matters. The instruction to paragraphs (b) and (c) requires identification of the person who initiated the contacts or negotiations.
quote: or (2) The subject company or any of its affiliates and any person not affiliated with the subject company who would have a direct interest in such matters. Instruction to paragraphs (b) and (c) of Item 1005: Identify the person who initiated the contacts or negotiations.

statement: Paragraph (d) requires, if material, a description of any agreement, arrangement or understanding and any actual or potential conflict of interest between the filing person or its affiliates and the subject company, its executive officers, directors or affiliates; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MNA-1064.
quote: (d) Conflicts of interest. If material, describe any agreement, arrangement or understanding and any actual or potential conflict of interest between the filing person or its affiliates and: (1) The subject company, its executive officers, directors or affiliates;

statement: Paragraph (d) also covers the offeror, its executive officers, directors or affiliates. Under the instruction to paragraph (d), if the filing person is the subject company, no disclosure called for by the paragraph is required in the document disseminated to security holders; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-MNA-1065.
quote: or (2) The offeror, its executive officers, directors or affiliates. Instruction to Item 1005(d): If the filing person is the subject company, no disclosure called for by this paragraph is required in the document disseminated to security holders,

statement: That relief applies so long as substantially the same information was filed with the Commission previously and disclosed in a proxy statement, report or other communication sent to security holders by the subject company in the past year; the quoted words complete the sentence in CL-MNA-1064.
quote: so long as substantially the same information was filed with the Commission previously and disclosed in a proxy statement, report or other communication sent to security holders by the subject company in the past year.

statement: Where that relief is used, the document disseminated to security holders must refer specifically to the discussion in the proxy statement, report or other communication that was sent to security holders previously, and the information also must be filed as an exhibit to the schedule.
quote: The document disseminated to security holders, however, must refer specifically to the discussion in the proxy statement, report or other communication that was sent to security holders previously. The information also must be filed as an exhibit to the schedule.

statement: Paragraph (e) requires a description of any agreement, arrangement or understanding, whether or not legally enforceable, between the filing person (including any person specified in Instruction C) and any other person with respect to any securities of the subject company.
quote: Describe any agreement, arrangement, or understanding, whether or not legally enforceable, between the filing person (including any person specified in Instruction C of the schedule) and any other person with respect to any securities of the subject company.

statement: Paragraph (e) also requires naming all persons that are a party to the agreements, arrangements or understandings and describing all material provisions.
quote: Name all persons that are a party to the agreements, arrangements, or understandings and describe all material provisions.

statement: Instruction 2 to paragraph (e) requires information for any securities that are pledged or otherwise subject to a contingency, the occurrence of which would give another person the power to direct the voting or disposition of the subject securities.
quote: 2. Include information for any securities that are pledged or otherwise subject to a contingency, the occurrence of which would give another person the power to direct the voting or disposition of the subject securities.

statement: Instruction 2 to paragraph (e) states that no disclosure is required about standard default and similar provisions contained in loan agreements.
quote: No disclosure, however, is required about standard default and similar provisions contained in loan agreements.

statement: Paragraph (a) requires a statement of the purposes of the transaction, and paragraph (b) an indication whether the securities acquired in the transaction will be retained, retired, held in treasury or otherwise disposed of. Paragraph (c) requires a description of any plans, proposals or negotiations that relate to or would result in the outcomes listed after it; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and the list continues in CL-MNA-1072.
quote: State the purposes of the transaction. (b) Use of securities acquired. Describe any plans, proposals or negotiations that relate to or would result in:

statement: The outcomes listed in paragraph (c) include any extraordinary transaction, such as a merger, reorganization or liquidation, involving the subject company or any of its subsidiaries, and any purchase, sale or transfer of a material amount of assets of the subject company or any of its subsidiaries; the list continues in CL-MNA-1073.
quote: (1) Any extraordinary transaction, such as a merger, reorganization or liquidation, involving the subject company or any of its subsidiaries; (2) Any purchase, sale or transfer of a material amount of assets of the subject company or any of its subsidiaries;

quote: (3) Any material change in the present dividend rate or policy, or indebtedness or capitalization of the subject company; (4) Any change in the present board of directors or management of the subject company,

statement: Item (4) of paragraph (c) includes, but is not limited to, any plans or proposals to change the number or the term of directors or to fill any existing vacancies on the board or to change any material term of the employment contract of any executive officer; the quoted words continue the item in CL-MNA-1073.
quote: including, but not limited to, any plans or proposals to change the number or the term of directors or to fill any existing vacancies on the board or to change any material term of the employment contract of any executive officer;

statement: Item (9) of paragraph (c) covers the acquisition by any person of additional securities of the subject company, or the disposition of securities of the subject company.
quote: (9) The acquisition by any person of additional securities of the subject company, or the disposition of securities of the subject company;

statement: Item (10) of paragraph (c) covers any changes in the subject company's charter, bylaws or other governing instruments or other actions that could impede the acquisition of control of the subject company.
quote: or (10) Any changes in the subject company's charter, bylaws or other governing instruments or other actions that could impede the acquisition of control of the subject company.

statement: If the filing person is the subject company, paragraph (d)(1) requires a statement whether or not that person is undertaking or engaged in any negotiations in response to the tender offer that relate to the matters in CL-MNA-1078.
quote: (d) Subject company negotiations. If the filing person is the subject company: (1) State whether or not that person is undertaking or engaged in any negotiations in response to the tender offer that relate to:

statement: The negotiations covered are those that relate to a tender offer or other acquisition of the subject company's securities by the filing person, any of its subsidiaries, or any other person, or to any of the matters referred to in paragraphs (c)(1) through (c)(3).
quote: (i) A tender offer or other acquisition of the subject company's securities by the filing person, any of its subsidiaries, or any other person; or (ii) Any of the matters referred to in paragraphs (c)(1) through (c)(3) of this section;

statement: If the filing person is the subject company, paragraph (d)(2) requires a description of any transaction, board resolution, agreement in principle, or signed contract that is entered into in response to the tender offer and relates to one or more of the matters referred to in paragraph (d)(1).

quote: Instruction to Item 1006(d)(1): If an agreement in principle has not been reached at the time of filing, no disclosure under paragraph (d)(1) of this section is required of the possible terms of or the parties to the transaction

quote: if in the opinion of the board of directors of the subject company disclosure would jeopardize continuation of the negotiations. In that case, disclosure indicating that negotiations are being undertaken or are underway and are in the preliminary stages is sufficient.

quote: Provide the required transaction information for the following persons: (a) The filing person (for all schedules);

quote: (b) Any person named in Instruction C of the schedule and any associate or majority-owned subsidiary of the issuer or filing person (for all schedules except Schedule 14D-9 (§ 240.14d-101 of this chapter));

statement: Instruction 1 to Item 1008(b) also covers any executive officer, director, affiliate or subsidiary of the filing person, for Schedule 14D-9.
quote: (c) Any executive officer, director, affiliate or subsidiary of the filing person (for Schedule 14D-9 (§ 240.14d-101 of this chapter);

statement: Sponsor means the person proposing the roll-up transaction.

statement: Individual deviations affect only one contract action and, unless 1.405(e) is applicable, may be authorized by the agency head, and the contracting officer must document the justification and agency approval in the contract file.
quote: Individual deviations affect only one contract action, and, unless 1.405(e) is applicable, may be authorized by the agency head. The contracting officer must document the justification and agency approval in the contract file.

statement: Class deviations affect more than one contract action.
quote: Class deviations affect more than one contract action.

statement: For civilian agencies except NASA, class deviations may be authorized by agency heads or their designees, unless 1.405(e) is applicable, and that authority shall not be delegated below the head of a contracting activity.
quote: (a) For civilian agencies except NASA, class deviations may be authorized by agency heads or their designees, unless 1.405(e) is applicable. Delegation of this authority shall not be made below the head of a contracting activity.

statement: For DoD, class deviations shall be controlled, processed, and approved in accordance with the Defense FAR Supplement.
quote: (b) For DOD, class deviations shall be controlled, processed, and approved in accordance with the Defense FAR Supplement.

statement: Each D&F shall set forth enough facts and circumstances to clearly and convincingly justify the specific determination made and, as a minimum, shall include the listed information in the prescribed agency format.
quote: Each D&F shall set forth enough facts and circumstances to clearly and convincingly justify the specific determination made. As a minimum, each D&F shall include, in the prescribed agency format, the following information:

statement: Three listed items in a D&F are the identification of the agency and contracting activity and of the document as a Determination and Findings, the nature or description of the action being approved, and the citation of the statute or regulation on which the D&F is based.
quote: (a) Identification of the agency and of the contracting activity and specific identifications of the document as a Determination and Findings. (b) Nature and/or description of the action being approved. (c) Citation of the appropriate statute and/or regulation upon which the D&F is based.

statement: One listed item in a D&F is findings that detail the particular circumstances, facts, or reasoning essential to support the determination, with necessary supporting documentation obtained from appropriate requirements and technical personnel.
quote: (d) Findings that detail the particular circumstances, facts, or reasoning essential to support the determination. Necessary supporting documentation shall be obtained from appropriate requirements and technical personnel.

statement: Three further listed items in a D&F are a determination based on the findings that the proposed action is justified under the applicable statute or regulation, an expiration date if required, and the signature of the official authorized to sign and the date signed.
quote: (e) A determination, based on the findings, that the proposed action is justified under the applicable statute or regulation. (f) Expiration date of the D&F, if required (see 1.706(b)). (g) The signature of the official authorized to sign the D&F (see 1.706) and the date signed.

statement: When a D&F is required, it shall be signed by the appropriate official in accordance with agency regulations, and authority to sign or delegate signature authority for the various D&Fs is as shown in the applicable FAR part.
quote: When a D&F is required, it shall be signed by the appropriate official in accordance with agency regulations. Authority to sign or delegate signature authority for the various D&F's is as shown in the applicable FAR part.

statement: Cognizant Government or contractor personnel may request the contracting officer to arrange for orientation, but it is up to the contracting officer to decide whether a postaward orientation in any form is necessary.
quote: While cognizant Government or contractor personnel may request the contracting officer to arrange for orientation, it is up to the contracting officer to decide whether a postaward orientation in any form is necessary.

statement: When deciding whether postaward orientation is necessary and what form it shall take, the contracting officer shall consider, as a minimum, listed factors, the first being the nature and extent of the preaward survey and any other prior discussions with the contractor.
quote: When deciding whether postaward orientation is necessary and, if so, what form it shall take, the contracting officer shall consider, as a minimum, the— (a) Nature and extent of the preaward survey and any other prior discussions with the contractor;

statement: One listed factor for the contracting officer to consider is complex financing arrangements, such as progress payments, advance payments, or guaranteed loans.
quote: (k) Safety precautions required for hazardous materials or operations; and (l) Complex financing arrangements, such as progress payments, advance payments, or guaranteed loans.

statement: The chairperson of a postaward conference shall conduct the meeting and, unless a contract change is contemplated, shall emphasize that it is not the purpose of the meeting to change the contract.
quote: The chairperson of the conference shall conduct the meeting. Unless a contract change is contemplated, the chairperson shall emphasize that it is not the purpose of the meeting to change the contract.

statement: At a postaward conference the contracting officer may make commitments or give directions within the scope of the contracting officer's authority and shall put in writing and sign any commitment or direction, whether or not it changes the contract.
quote: The contracting officer may make commitments or give directions within the scope of the contracting officer's authority and shall put in writing and sign any commitment or direction, whether or not it changes the contract.

statement: Any change to the contract that results from a postaward conference shall be made only by a contract modification referencing the applicable terms of the contract, and participants without authority to bind the Government shall not take action that in any way alters the contract.
quote: Any change to the contract that results from the postaward conference shall be made only by a contract modification referencing the applicable terms of the contract. Participants without authority to bind the Government shall not take action that in any way alters the contract.

statement: Past performance evaluations shall be prepared at least annually and at the time the work under a contract or order is completed.
quote: Past performance evaluations shall be prepared at least annually and at the time the work under a contract or order is completed.

statement: Except as provided in paragraphs (e), (f), and (h) of the section, agencies shall prepare evaluations of contractor performance for each contract that exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold and for each order that exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold.
quote: Except as provided in paragraphs (e), (f), and (h) of this section, agencies shall prepare evaluations of contractor performance for each contract (as defined in FAR part 2) that exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold and for each order that exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold.

statement: Past performance evaluations shall be prepared for each construction contract of $900,000 or more, and for each construction contract terminated for default regardless of contract value.
quote: Past performance evaluations shall be prepared for each construction contract of $900,000 or more, and for each construction contract terminated for default regardless of contract value.

statement: Past performance evaluations shall be prepared for each architect-engineer services contract of $45,000 or more, and for each architect-engineer services contract that is terminated for default regardless of contract value.
quote: Past performance evaluations shall be prepared for each architect-engineer services contract of $45,000 or more, and for each architect-engineer services contract that is terminated for default regardless of contract value.

statement: Past performance evaluations shall include an assessment of the contractor's performance against, and efforts to achieve, the goals identified in the small business subcontracting plan when the contract includes the clause at 52.219-9; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-OPM-0043.
quote: (g) Past performance evaluations shall include an assessment of the contractor's— (1) Performance against, and efforts to achieve, the goals identified in the small business subcontracting plan when the contract includes the clause at 52.219-9, Small Business Subcontracting Plan; and

statement: One listed item that a past performance evaluation shall assess is reduced or untimely payments made to small business subcontractors that the contracting officer determines to be unjustified.
quote: (2) Reduced or untimely payments (as defined in 19.701), made to small business subcontractors, determined by the contracting officer to be unjustified.

statement: The contracting officer shall consider and evaluate a contractor's written explanation for a reduced or an untimely payment when determining whether the reduced or untimely payment is justified; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-OPM-0045.
quote: The contracting officer shall— (i) Consider and evaluate a contractor's written explanation for a reduced or an untimely payment when determining whether the reduced or untimely payment is justified; and

statement: One listed duty of the contracting officer is to determine that a history of unjustified reduced or untimely payments has occurred when the contractor has reported three or more occasions of unjustified reduced or untimely payments under a single contract within a 12-month period.
quote: (ii) Determine that a history of unjustified reduced or untimely payments has occurred when the contractor has reported three or more occasions of unjustified reduced or untimely payments under a single contract within a 12-month period

statement: Contractors shall be afforded up to 14 calendar days from the date of notification of availability of the past performance evaluation to submit comments, rebutting statements, or additional information.
quote: Contractors shall be afforded up to 14 calendar days from the date of notification of availability of the past performance evaluation to submit comments, rebutting statements, or additional information.

statement: Agencies shall provide for review at a level above the contracting officer to consider disagreements between the parties regarding the evaluation, and the ultimate conclusion on the performance evaluation is a decision of the contracting agency.
quote: Agencies shall provide for review at a level above the contracting officer to consider disagreements between the parties regarding the evaluation. The ultimate conclusion on the performance evaluation is a decision of the contracting agency.

statement: Past performance evaluations, including any contractor-submitted information, become available for source selection officials not later than 14 days after the date on which the contractor is notified of the evaluation's availability for comment.
quote: These evaluations, including any contractor-submitted information (with indication whether agency review is pending), become available for source selection officials not later than 14 days after the date on which the contractor is notified of the evaluation's availability for comment.

statement: Agencies shall use the past performance information in CPARS that is within three years of the completion of performance of the evaluated contract or order, or within six years for construction and architect-engineer contracts; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-OPM-0163.
quote: Agencies shall use the past performance information in CPARS that is within three years (six for construction and architect-engineer contracts) of the completion of performance of the evaluated contract or order

statement: The Government will maintain surveillance of contractor performance as necessary to protect its interests, and when the contracting office retains a contract for administration the contracting officer administering the contract shall determine the extent of surveillance.
quote: The Government will maintain surveillance of contractor performance as necessary to protect its interests. When the contracting office retains a contract for administration, the contracting officer administering the contract shall determine the extent of surveillance.

statement: The contract administration office determines the extent of production surveillance on the basis of the criticality assigned by the contracting officer to the supplies or services and consideration of a list of factors.
quote: The contract administration office determines the extent of production surveillance on the basis of (1) the criticality (degree of importance to the Government) assigned by the contracting officer (see 42.1105) to the supplies or services and (2) consideration of the following factors:

statement: The factors the contract administration office considers for the extent of production surveillance include contract requirements for reporting production progress and performance, the contract performance schedule and the contractor's production plan.
quote: (2) consideration of the following factors: (i) Contract requirements for reporting production progress and performance. (ii) The contract performance schedule. (iii) The contractor's production plan.

statement: The list of production surveillance factors in the section continues with the contractor's history of contract performance, the contractor's experience with the contract supplies or services, the contractor's financial capability and any supplementary written instructions from the contracting office.
quote: (iv) The contractor's history of contract performance. (v) The contractor's experience with the contract supplies or services. (vi) The contractor's financial capability. (vii) Any supplementary written instructions from the contracting office.

statement: Contracts at or below the simplified acquisition threshold should not normally require production surveillance.
quote: (b) Contracts at or below the simplified acquisition threshold should not normally require production surveillance.

statement: Contracting officers shall assign a criticality designator to each contract in the space for designating the contract administration office, with listed criteria.
quote: Contracting officers shall assign a criticality designator to each contract in the space for designating the contract administration office, as follows:

statement: Criticality designator A covers critical contracts, including DX-rated contracts, contracts citing the authority for unusual and compelling urgency, and contracts for major systems.
quote: Criterion A Critical contracts, including DX-rated contracts (see subpart 11.6), contracts citing the authority in 6.302-2 (unusual and compelling urgency), and contracts for major systems.

statement: One listed pair of designators is B, for contracts other than those designated A for items needed to maintain a Government or contractor production or repair line, to preclude out-of-stock conditions or to meet user needs for nonstock items, and C, for all contracts other than those designated A or B.
quote: B Contracts (other than those designated “A”) for items needed to maintain a Government or contractor production or repair line, to preclude out-of-stock conditions or to meet user needs for nonstock items. C All contracts other than those designated “A” or “B.”

statement: When information on contract performance status is needed, contracting officers may require contractors to submit production progress reports.
quote: When information on contract performance status is needed, contracting officers may require contractors to submit production progress reports (see 42.1107(a)).

statement: Reporting requirements shall be limited to that information essential to Government needs and shall take maximum advantage of data output generated by contractor management systems.
quote: Reporting requirements shall be limited to that information essential to Government needs and shall take maximum advantage of data output generated by contractor management systems.

statement: The contract administration office may at any time initiate a report to advise the contracting officer, and the inventory manager if one is designated in the contract, of any potential or actual delay in performance.
quote: The contract administration office may at any time initiate a report to advise the contracting officer (and the inventory manager, if one is designated in the contract) of any potential or actual delay in performance.

statement: Advice of any potential or actual delay in performance shall be in writing, be provided in sufficient time for the contracting officer to take necessary action, and provide a definite recommendation, if action is appropriate.
quote: of any potential or actual delay in performance. This advice shall (1) be in writing, (2) be provided in sufficient time for the contracting officer to take necessary action, and (3) provide a definite recommendation, if action is appropriate.

statement: The contracting officer should reject supplies or services not conforming in all respects to contract requirements.
quote: The contracting officer should reject supplies or services not conforming in all respects to contract requirements (see 46.102).

statement: The contracting officer ordinarily must give the contractor an opportunity to correct or replace nonconforming supplies or services when this can be accomplished within the required delivery schedule.
quote: The contracting officer ordinarily must give the contractor an opportunity to correct or replace nonconforming supplies or services when this can be accomplished within the required delivery schedule.

statement: Unless the contract specifies otherwise, correction or replacement must be without additional cost to the Government.
quote: Unless the contract specifies otherwise (as may be the case in some cost-reimbursement contracts), correction or replacement must be without additional cost to the Government.

statement: In situations not covered by the correct-or-replace paragraph, the contracting officer ordinarily must reject supplies or services when the nonconformance is critical or major or the supplies or services are otherwise incomplete.
quote: In situations not covered by paragraph (b) of this section, the contracting officer ordinarily must reject supplies or services when the nonconformance is critical or major or the supplies or services are otherwise incomplete.

statement: The contracting officer may determine, in circumstances such as reasons of economy or urgency, that acceptance or conditional acceptance of supplies or services is in the best interest of the Government.
quote: However, there may be circumstances (e.g., reasons of economy or urgency) when the contracting officer determines acceptance or conditional acceptance of supplies or services is in the best interest of the Government.

statement: Before making a decision to accept, the contracting officer must obtain the concurrence of the activity responsible for the technical requirements of the contract and, where health factors are involved, of the responsible health official of the agency concerned.
quote: Before making a decision to accept, the contracting officer must, obtain the concurrence of the activity responsible for the technical requirements of the contract and, where health factors are involved, of the responsible health official of the agency concerned.

statement: If the nonconformance is minor, the cognizant contract administration office may make the determination to accept or reject, except where this authority is withheld by the contracting office of the contracting activity.
quote: If the nonconformance is minor, the cognizant contract administration office may make the determination to accept or reject, except where this authority is withheld by the contracting office of the contracting activity.

statement: To assist in making a determination, the contract administration office may establish a joint contractor-contract administrative office review group, and acceptance of supplies and services with critical or major nonconformances is outside the scope of the review group.
quote: To assist in making this determination, the contract administration office may establish a joint contractor-contract administrative office review group. Acceptance of supplies and services with critical or major nonconformances is outside the scope of the review group.

statement: When supplies or services are accepted with critical or major nonconformances as authorized in the acceptance paragraph, the contracting officer must modify the contract to provide for an equitable price reduction or other consideration.
quote: When supplies or services are accepted with critical or major nonconformances as authorized in paragraph (c) of this section, the contracting officer must modify the contract to provide for an equitable price reduction or other consideration.

statement: In the case of conditional acceptance, amounts withheld from payments generally should be at least sufficient to cover the estimated cost and related profit to correct deficiencies and complete unfinished work.
quote: In the case of conditional acceptance, amounts withheld from payments generally should be at least sufficient to cover the estimated cost and related profit to correct deficiencies and complete unfinished work.

statement: Notices of rejection must include the reasons for rejection and be furnished promptly to the contractor.
quote: Notices of rejection must include the reasons for rejection and be furnished promptly to the contractor.

statement: The notice of rejection must be in writing if the supplies or services have been rejected at a place other than the contractor's plant, if the contractor persists in offering nonconforming supplies or services for acceptance, or if delivery or performance was late without excusable cause.
quote: The notice must, be in writing if— (1) The supplies or services have been rejected at a place other than the contractor's plant; (2) The contractor persists in offering nonconforming supplies or services for acceptance; or (3) Delivery or performance was late without excusable cause.

statement: The contracting officer shall provide disposition instructions for counterfeit or suspect counterfeit items in accordance with agency policy, and agency policy may require the contracting officer to direct the contractor to retain such items for investigative or evidentiary purposes.
quote: The contracting officer shall provide disposition instructions for counterfeit or suspect counterfeit items in accordance with agency policy. Agency policy may require the contracting officer to direct the contractor to retain such items for investigative or evidentiary purposes.

statement: Except as provided in the exclusions paragraph, the contracting officer shall insert the reporting nonconforming items clause in solicitations and contracts in the listed cases.
quote: Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, the contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.246-26, Reporting Nonconforming Items, in solicitations and contracts—as follows:

statement: One listed case for inserting the clause is an acquisition that exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold and is by, or for, the Department of Defense of electronic parts or end items, components, parts, or materials containing electronic parts, whether or not covered in the preceding listed case.
quote: for an acquisition that exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold and is by, or for, the Department of Defense of electronic parts or end items, components, parts, or materials containing electronic parts, whether or not covered in paragraph (a)(1) of this section;

statement: The contracting officer shall not insert the reporting nonconforming items clause when acquiring commercial products and commercial services using part 12 procedures, which is one of two listed exclusions; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-OPM-0099.
quote: The contracting officer shall not insert the clause at 52.246-26, Reporting Nonconforming Items, in solicitations and contracts when acquiring— (1) Commercial products and commercial services using part 12 procedures; or

statement: If required by agency policy, the contracting officer may modify the clause, but only to change the responsibility for the contractor to submit reports to the agency rather than to the Government-Industry Data Exchange Program; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-OPM-0079.
quote: If required by agency policy, the contracting officer may modify paragraph (b)(4) of the clause at 52.246-26, but only to change the responsibility for the contractor to submit reports to the agency rather than to Government-Industry Data Exchange Program (GIDEP),

statement: Where the contracting officer modifies the clause to change the responsibility for submitting reports, the agency instead of the contractor submits reports to the Government-Industry Data Exchange Program within the mandatory 60 days.
quote: but only to change the responsibility for the contractor to submit reports to the agency rather than to Government-Industry Data Exchange Program (GIDEP), so that the agency instead of the contractor submits reports to GIDEP within the mandatory 60 days.

statement: Contractors shall perform all contracts, so far as practicable, without using overtime, particularly as a regular employment practice, except when lower overall costs to the Government will result or when it is necessary to meet urgent program needs.
quote: Contractors shall perform all contracts, so far as practicable, without using overtime, particularly as a regular employment practice, except when lower overall costs to the Government will result or when it is necessary to meet urgent program needs.

statement: Approval of the use of overtime may be granted by an agency approving official after determining in writing that overtime is necessary to meet essential delivery or performance schedules, which is one of the listed purposes.
quote: Approval of the use of overtime may be granted by an agency approving official after determining in writing that overtime is necessary to— (1) Meet essential delivery or performance schedules;

statement: A biennial anniversary date is listed for a multiple year contract if the contract is not subject to annual appropriations and its proposed term exceeds 2 years, unless otherwise advised by the Wage and Hour Division.
quote: (2) Biennial anniversary date if the contract is not subject to annual appropriations and its proposed term exceeds 2 years—unless otherwise advised by the Wage and Hour Division.

statement: Approval by the designated official of the use and total dollar amount of overtime is required before an amount is included in the overtime premiums clause.
quote: Approval by the designated official of use and total dollar amount of overtime is required before inclusion of an amount in paragraph (a) of the clause at 52.222-2, Payment for Overtime Premiums.

statement: Contracting officer approval of payment of overtime premiums is required for time-and-materials and labor-hour contracts.
quote: Contracting officer approval of payment of overtime premiums is required for time-and-materials and labor-hour contracts

statement: No approvals are required for paying overtime premiums under other types of contracts.
quote: No approvals are required for paying overtime premiums under other types of contracts.

statement: The contracting officer shall include the overtime premiums clause in solicitations and contracts when a cost-reimbursement contract is contemplated and the contract amount is expected to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold, unless an exception stated in the same sentence applies; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-OPM-0087.
quote: The contracting officer shall include the clause at 52.222-2, Payment for Overtime Premiums, in solicitations and contracts when a cost-reimbursement contract is contemplated and the contract amount is expected to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold; unless

statement: The overtime premiums clause is not required when a cost-reimbursement contract for operation of vessels is contemplated or a cost-plus-incentive-fee contract is contemplated that will provide a swing from the target fee of at least plus or minus 3 percent and a contractor's share of at least 10 percent.
quote: unless (a) a cost-reimbursement contract for operation of vessels is contemplated, or (b) a cost-plus-incentive-fee contract that will provide a swing from the target fee of at least plus or minus 3 percent and a contractor's share of at least 10 percent is contemplated.

statement: Certain contracts contain a clause specifying that no laborer or mechanic doing any part of the work shall be required or permitted to work more than 40 hours in any workweek unless paid for all such overtime hours at not less than one and one-half times the basic rate of pay.
quote: that certain contracts contain a clause specifying that no laborer or mechanic doing any part of the work contemplated by the contract shall be required or permitted to work more than 40 hours in any workweek unless paid for all such overtime hours at not less than 11⁄2 times the basic rate of pay.

statement: When an overtime computation discloses underpayments, the responsible contractor or subcontractor must pay the affected employee any unpaid wages and pay liquidated damages to the Government.
quote: When an overtime computation discloses underpayments, the responsible contractor or subcontractor must pay the affected employee any unpaid wages and pay liquidated damages to the Government.

quote: Insert the clause at 52.222-4, Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards—Overtime Compensation, in solicitations and contracts (including, for this purpose, basic ordering agreements) when the contract may require or involve the employment of laborers or mechanics.

quote: However, do not include the clause in solicitations and contracts— (a) Valued at or below $200,000; (b) For commercial products and commercial services; (c) For transportation or the transmission of intelligence;

quote: The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.222-41, Service Contract Labor Standards, in solicitations and contracts (except as provided in paragraph (a)(2) of this section) if the contract is subject to the Service Contract Labor Standards statute and is— (i) Over $2,500;

statement: A contract subject to the Service Contract Labor Standards statute meets the listed condition either by being over $2,500 or by being for an indefinite dollar amount where the contracting officer does not know in advance that the contract amount will be $2,500 or less.
quote: if the contract is subject to the Service Contract Labor Standards statute and is— (i) Over $2,500; or (ii) For an indefinite dollar amount and the contracting officer does not know in advance that the contract amount will be $2,500 or less.

statement: The contracting officer shall insert the Statement of Equivalent Rates for Federal Hires clause in solicitations and contracts if the contract amount is expected to be over $2,500 and the Service Contract Labor Standards statute is applicable.
quote: (b) The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.222-42, Statement of Equivalent Rates for Federal Hires, in solicitations and contracts if the contract amount is expected to be over $2,500 and the Service Contract Labor Standards statute is applicable.

statement: The contracting officer shall obtain wage determinations for each new service solicitation and contract in excess of $2,500, which is one of the listed service contracts.
quote: The contracting officer shall obtain wage determinations for the following service contracts: (a) Each new solicitation and contract in excess of $2,500.

statement: Item (b) of the list in the section on obtaining wage determinations is each contract modification which brings the contract above $2,500 and either extends the existing contract pursuant to an option clause or otherwise or changes the scope of the contract whereby labor requirements are affected significantly.
quote: (b) Each contract modification which brings the contract above $2,500 and— (1) Extends the existing contract pursuant to an option clause or otherwise; or (2) Changes the scope of the contract whereby labor requirements are affected significantly.

statement: One listed service contract for which the contracting officer shall obtain wage determinations is each multiple year contract in excess of $2,500, upon the annual anniversary date if the contract is subject to annual appropriations; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-OPM-0082.
quote: (c) Each multiple year contract in excess of $2,500 upon— (1) Annual anniversary date if the contract is subject to annual appropriations

quote: (2) Medical devices that are subject to the Food and Drug Administration reporting requirements at 21 CFR 803.

quote: (d) Designate and authorize, in writing and in accordance with agency procedures, a contracting officer's representative (COR)
note: The scope and the exception in the same list item are carried by CL-OPM-0004.

quote: (4) May not be delegated responsibility to perform functions that have been delegated under 42.202 to a contract administration office, but may be assigned some duties at 42.302 by the contracting officer;

statement: Ratification means the act of approving an unauthorized commitment by an official who has the authority to do so.
quote: Ratification, as used in this subsection, means the act of approving an unauthorized commitment by an official who has the authority to do so.

statement: Agencies should take positive action to preclude, to the maximum extent possible, the need for ratification actions.
quote: Agencies should take positive action to preclude, to the maximum extent possible, the need for ratification actions.

statement: Although the section provides ratification procedures for cases where ratification of an unauthorized commitment is necessary, those procedures may not be used in a manner that encourages such commitments being made by Government personnel.
quote: Although procedures are provided in this section for use in those cases where the ratification of an unauthorized commitment is necessary, these procedures may not be used in a manner that encourages such commitments being made by Government personnel.

statement: Agencies should process unauthorized commitments using the ratification authority of the subsection instead of referring such actions to the Government Accountability Office for resolution.
quote: Agencies should process unauthorized commitments using the ratification authority of this subsection instead of referring such actions to the Government Accountability Office for resolution.

statement: Unauthorized commitments that would involve claims subject to resolution under the Contract Disputes chapter of title 41 of the United States Code should be processed in accordance with FAR subpart 33.2, Disputes and Appeals.
quote: Unauthorized commitments that would involve claims subject to resolution under 41 U.S.C. chapter 71, Contract Disputes, should be processed in accordance with subpart 33.2, Disputes and Appeals.

statement: One listed limitation on authorization of class deviations by agency officials is that an agency official who may authorize one shall, before doing so, consult with the chairperson of the Civilian Agency Acquisition Council, unless the official determines that urgency precludes such consultation.
quote: (1) An agency official who may authorize a class deviation, before doing so, shall consult with the chairperson of the Civilian Agency Acquisition Council (CAA Council), unless that agency official determines that urgency precludes such consultation.

statement: For NASA, class deviations shall be controlled and approved by the Assistant Administrator for Procurement.
quote: (c) For NASA, class deviations shall be controlled and approved by the Assistant Administrator for Procurement.

quote: (e) For civilian agencies other than NASA, if a deviation required to comply with a treaty or an executive agreement is not authorized by paragraph (b) or (c) of this section, then the request for deviation shall be processed through the FAR Secretariat to the Civilian Agency Acquisition Council.

statement: Maximum benefits of a postaward orientation will be realized when it is conducted promptly after award.
quote: (d) Maximum benefits will be realized when orientation is conducted promptly after award.

statement: A postaward orientation is not a substitute for the contractor's fully understanding the work requirements at the time offers are submitted, nor is it to be used to alter the final agreement arrived at in any negotiations leading to contract award.
quote: However, it is not a substitute for the contractor's fully understanding the work requirements at the time offers are submitted, nor is it to be used to alter the final agreement arrived at in any negotiations leading to contract award.

statement: Agencies shall not evaluate performance for contracts awarded under FAR subpart 8.7.
quote: (h) Agencies shall not evaluate performance for contracts awarded under Subpart 8.7.

statement: Agencies shall prepare and submit all past performance evaluations electronically in CPARS.
quote: Agencies shall prepare and submit all past performance evaluations electronically in CPARS

statement: Past performance evaluations for classified contracts and special access programs shall not be reported in CPARS, but will be reported as stated in the subpart and in accordance with agency procedures.

statement: The guideline requires the contractor to define the authorized work elements for the program, and records that a product-oriented work breakdown structure tailored for effective internal management control is commonly used for that purpose.
quote: Define the authorized work elements for the program. A product-oriented work breakdown structure, tailored for effective internal management control, is commonly used in this process.

statement: The work breakdown structure is a product-oriented, hierarchical breakdown of the program requirements that includes all program elements, such as hardware, software, services, data or facilities.
quote: The WBS is a product-oriented, hierarchical breakdown of the program requirements. The WBS includes all program elements (e.g., hardware, software, services, data, or facilities)

statement: The work breakdown structure must also include all subcontracted work scope.
quote: The WBS must also include all subcontracted work scope.

statement: The contractor must extend the contract work breakdown structure to a level needed for effective internal management control, and this level should not be an arbitrary level established across the program.
quote: In all cases, the contractor must extend the contract WBS to a level needed for effective internal management control. This should not be an arbitrary level established across the program.

statement: Cost collection requirements, such as cost and software data reporting, may require a different reporting structure than the work breakdown structure used in the earned value management system for program management.
quote: Cost collection requirements, such as Cost and Software Data Reporting (CSDR), may require a different reporting structure other than the WBS used in the Earned Value Management System (EVMS)

statement: A single product-oriented work breakdown structure is used for a given contract and extends to the level necessary for management action, comprising all contract work scope including subcontracted and intercompany scope.
quote: A single product-oriented WBS is used for a given contract and extends to the level necessary for management action. The WBS comprises all contract work scope, including subcontracted and intercompany scope, to levels needed for effective internal management control.
