statement: The contracting officer or cognizant Federal agency official heads the Government negotiating team, which includes the cognizant auditor and technical or functional personnel as required.
quote: The contracting officer (or cognizant Federal agency official) shall head the Government negotiating team, which includes the cognizant auditor and technical or functional personnel as required.

statement: The negotiation memorandum must reconcile all costs questioned, identifying the items and amounts allowed or disallowed in the final settlement.
quote: reconciliation of all costs questioned, with identification of items and amounts allowed or disallowed in the final settlement

statement: The contracting officer must notify the contractor of the individual costs considered unallowable and the respective amounts of the disallowance.
quote: Notify the contractor of the individual costs which were considered unallowable and the respective amounts of the disallowance.

statement: The cognizant contracting officer prepares a written indirect cost rate agreement conforming to the requirements of the contracts.
quote: Prepare a written indirect cost rate agreement conforming to the requirements of the contracts

statement: When the listed conditions are met, the contracting officer responsible for closeout negotiates the settlement of the direct and indirect costs of a specific contract, task order or delivery order in advance of the determination of final direct costs and indirect rates set forth in FAR 42.705 (CL-RTE-9122).
quote: shall negotiate the settlement of direct and indirect costs for a specific contract, task order, or delivery order to be closed, in advance of the determination of final direct costs

statement: The contract, task order or delivery order must be physically complete before the quick-closeout procedure may be used.
quote: (1) The contract, task order, or delivery order is physically complete

statement: Unsettled direct and indirect costs are considered relatively insignificant when the total to be allocated to any one contract, task order or delivery order does not exceed the lesser of $1,000,000 or 10 percent, measured as stated in the next claim; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-RTE-0154.
quote: Cost amounts will be considered relatively insignificant when the total unsettled direct costs and indirect costs to be allocated to any one contract, task order, or delivery order does not exceed the lesser of— (i) $1,000,000; or (ii) 10 percent

statement: The 10 percent limit is measured against the total contract, task order or delivery order amount.
quote: (ii) 10 percent of the total contract, task order, or delivery order amount

statement: The risk assessment must include consideration of the contractor's accounting, estimating and purchasing systems and of other concerns of the cognizant contract auditors.
quote: The risk assessment shall include— (i) Consideration of the contractor's accounting, estimating, and purchasing systems; (ii) Other concerns of the cognizant contract auditors

statement: The risk assessment must also include any other pertinent information, such as the documented history of Federal Government approved indirect cost rate agreements, changes to the contractor's rate structure, volatility of rate fluctuations during affected periods, and mergers or acquisitions.
quote: Any other pertinent information, such as, documented history of Federal Government approved indirect cost rate agreements, changes to contractor's rate structure, volatility of rate fluctuations during affected periods, mergers or acquisitions

statement: Agreement must also be reached on a reasonable estimate of allocable dollars.
quote: Agreement can be reached on a reasonable estimate of allocable dollars

statement: A quick-closeout determination of final indirect costs is final for the contract it covers, and no adjustment is made to other contracts for over- or under-recoveries of costs allocated to that contract.
quote: shall be final for the contract it covers and no adjustment shall be made to other contracts for over- or under-recoveries of costs allocated or allocable to the contract covered by the agreement

statement: Indirect cost rates used in a quick closeout are not a binding precedent when final indirect cost rates are established for other contracts.
quote: Indirect cost rates used in the quick closeout of a contract shall not be considered a binding precedent when establishing the final indirect cost rates for other contracts

statement: Negotiation of a forward pricing rate agreement may be requested by the contracting officer or the contractor, or initiated by the administrative contracting officer.
quote: Negotiation of forward pricing rate agreements (FPRA's) may be requested by the contracting officer or the contractor or initiated by the administrative contracting officer (ACO)

statement: The cognizant contract administration agency determines whether a forward pricing rate agreement will be established.
quote: The cognizant contract administration agency shall determine whether an FPRA will be established

statement: In deciding whether to establish an agreement, the administrative contracting officer should consider whether the benefits are commensurate with the effort of establishing and monitoring it.
quote: In determining whether or not to establish such an agreement, the ACO should consider whether the benefits to be derived from the agreement are commensurate with the effort of establishing and monitoring it

statement: Agreements are normally negotiated only with contractors having a significant volume of Government contract proposals.
quote: Normally, FPRA's should be negotiated only with contractors having a significant volume of Government contract proposals

statement: The administrative contracting officer requires the contractor's forward pricing rate proposal to include cost or pricing data that are accurate, complete and current as of the date of submission, subject to the cross-reference to 15.407-3(c).
quote: require that it include cost or pricing data that are accurate, complete, and current as of the date of submission (but see 15.407-3(c)).

statement: After negotiations the administrative contracting officer prepares a price negotiation memorandum and forwards copies of it and of the agreement to the cognizant auditor and to contracting offices known to be affected.
quote: the ACO shall prepare a price negotiation memorandum (PNM) (see 15.406-3) and forward copies of the PNM and FPRA to the cognizant auditor and to all contracting offices that are known to be affected by the FPRA.

statement: The agreement provides for cancellation at the option of either party and requires the contractor to report any significant change in the cost or pricing data supporting it to the administrative contracting officer and the cognizant auditor.
quote: The agreement shall provide for cancellation at the option of either party and shall require the contractor to submit to the ACO and to the cognizant contract auditor any significant change in cost or pricing data used to support the FPRA.

statement: If no agreement has been established, or an established one has been invalidated, the administrative contracting officer issues a forward pricing rate recommendation to buying activities with documentation to assist negotiators.
quote: If an FPRA has not been established or has been invalidated, the ACO will issue a forward pricing rate recommendation (FPRR) to buying activities with documentation to assist negotiators

statement: When an agreement is invalid, the contractor should submit and negotiate a new proposal to reflect the changed conditions.
quote: When an FPRA is invalid, the contractor should submit and negotiate a new proposal to reflect the changed conditions

statement: A cost may not be charged as a direct cost to a final cost objective if other costs incurred for the same purpose in like circumstances have been included in any indirect cost pool.
quote: No final cost objective shall have allocated to it as a direct cost any cost, if other costs incurred for the same purpose in like circumstances have been included in any indirect cost pool

statement: Direct costs of the contract must be charged directly to the contract.
quote: Direct costs of the contract shall be charged directly to the contract.

statement: Costs specifically identified with other final cost objectives of the contractor are direct costs of those cost objectives, and are not charged to the contract directly or indirectly.
quote: All costs specifically identified with other final cost objectives of the contractor are direct costs of those cost objectives and are not to be charged to the contract directly or indirectly.

statement: For reasons of practicality, the contractor may treat any direct cost of a minor dollar amount as an indirect cost if the accounting treatment is consistently applied to all final cost objectives and produces substantially the same results as treating the cost as a direct cost.
quote: (b) For reasons of practicality, the contractor may treat any direct cost of a minor dollar amount as an indirect cost if the accounting treatment— (1) Is consistently applied to all final cost objectives; and (2) Produces substantially the same results as treating the cost as a direct cost.

statement: Treating a minor direct cost as an indirect cost is allowed if the treatment is consistently applied to all final cost objectives and produces substantially the same results as treating the cost as a direct cost.
quote: (1) Is consistently applied to all final cost objectives; and (2) Produces substantially the same results as treating the cost as a direct cost.

statement: For contracts subject to full CAS coverage, allocation of indirect costs is based on the applicable CAS provisions; for all other contracts, the CAS provisions in paragraphs (b) through (h) of the section apply.
quote: For contracts subject to full CAS coverage, allocation of indirect costs shall be based on the applicable provisions. For all other contracts, the applicable CAS provisions in paragraphs (b) through (h) of this section apply.

statement: Indirect costs are the costs remaining to be allocated to intermediate or two or more final cost objectives, after direct costs have been determined and charged directly to the contract or other work.
quote: After direct costs have been determined and charged directly to the contract or other work, indirect costs are those remaining to be allocated to intermediate or two or more final cost objectives.

statement: A cost may not be charged as an indirect cost to a final cost objective if other costs incurred for the same purpose in like circumstances have been included as a direct cost.
quote: No final cost objective shall have allocated to it as an indirect cost any cost, if other costs incurred for the same purpose, in like circumstances, have been included as a direct cost

statement: The contractor accumulates indirect costs by logical cost groupings, giving due consideration to the reasons for incurring the costs.
quote: The contractor shall accumulate indirect costs by logical cost groupings with due consideration of the reasons for incurring such costs.

statement: Each cost grouping is determined to permit an allocation base that is common to all cost objectives to which the grouping is allocated.
quote: The contractor shall determine each grouping so as to permit use of an allocation base that is common to all cost objectives to which the grouping is to be allocated.

statement: Once an accepted base for allocating indirect costs exists, the contractor must not fragment the base by removing individual elements.
quote: Once an appropriate base for allocating indirect costs has been accepted, the contractor shall not fragment the base by removing individual elements.

statement: All items properly includable in an indirect cost base bear a pro rata share of indirect costs, whether or not they are accepted as Government contract costs.
quote: All items properly includable in an indirect cost base shall bear a pro rata share of indirect costs irrespective of their acceptance as Government contract costs.

statement: For contracts other than those subject to full or modified CAS coverage, the base period for allocating indirect costs is the contractor's fiscal year used for financial reporting purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.
quote: (2) For contracts other than those subject to paragraph (g)(1) of this section, the base period for allocating indirect costs shall be the contractor's fiscal year used for financial reporting purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.

statement: The cognizant Government auditor establishes final indirect cost rates for business units not covered in 42.705-1(a).
quote: The cognizant Government auditor shall establish final indirect cost rates for business units not covered in 42.705-1(a).

statement: Once a proposal has been determined adequate for audit in support of negotiating final indirect cost rates, the auditor audits the proposal and prepares an advisory audit report, including a listing of any relevant advance agreements or restrictive terms of specific contracts.
quote: (2) Once a proposal has been determined to be adequate for audit in support of negotiating final indirect cost rates, the auditor shall— (i) Audit the proposal and prepare an advisory audit report, including a listing of any relevant advance agreements or restrictive terms of specific contracts;

statement: The auditor seeks agreement on indirect costs with the contractor and prepares an indirect cost rate agreement that the contractor and the auditor both sign.
quote: Seek agreement on indirect costs with the contractor; (iii) Prepare an indirect cost rate agreement conforming to the requirements of the contracts. The agreement shall be signed by the contractor and the auditor

statement: If agreement with the contractor is not reached, the auditor forwards the audit report to the contracting officer, who resolves the disagreement.
quote: If agreement with the contractor is not reached, forward the audit report to the contracting officer (or cognizant Federal agency official) identified in the Directory of Contract Administration Services Components (see 42.203), who will then resolve the disagreement

statement: A proposal is not accepted and no agreement to establish final indirect cost rates is made unless the contractor has certified the costs.
quote: a proposal shall not be accepted and no agreement shall be made to establish final indirect cost rates unless the costs have been certified by the contractor.

statement: The agency head or designee may waive the certification requirement when it is determined to be in the interest of the United States and the reasons for the determination are put in writing and made available to the public.
quote: (1) The agency head, or designee, may waive the certification requirement when— (i) It is determined to be in the interest of the United States; and (ii) The reasons for the determination are put in writing and made available to the public.

statement: If the contractor has not certified its proposal for final indirect cost rates and a waiver is not appropriate, the contracting officer may unilaterally establish the rates.
quote: If the contractor has not certified its proposal for final indirect cost rates and a waiver is not appropriate, the contracting officer may unilaterally establish the rates.

statement: Rates established unilaterally should be based on audited historical data or other available data as long as unallowable costs are excluded, and set low enough to ensure that unallowable costs will not be reimbursed.
quote: (i) Based on audited historical data or other available data as long as unallowable costs are excluded; and (ii) Set low enough to ensure that unallowable costs will not be reimbursed.

statement: Except as provided in paragraph (f)(2) of the section, the clause at 52.242-4, Certification of Final Indirect Costs, is incorporated into all solicitations and contracts that provide for establishment of final indirect cost rates.
quote: Except as provided in paragraph (f)(2) of this subsection, the clause at 52.242-4, Certification of Final Indirect Costs, shall be incorporated into all solicitations and contracts which provide for establishment of final indirect cost rates.

statement: For contracts subject to full or modified CAS coverage, the contractor follows the criteria and guidance in 48 CFR 9904.406 for selecting the cost accounting periods used in allocating indirect costs.
quote: (1) For contracts subject to full or modified CAS coverage, the contractor shall follow the criteria and guidance in 48 CFR 9904.406 for selecting the cost accounting periods to be used in allocating indirect costs.

statement: The fiscal year used as the base period will normally be 12 months, but a different period may be appropriate, for example when a change in fiscal year occurs due to a business combination or other circumstances.
quote: The fiscal year will normally be 12 months, but a different period may be appropriate (e.g., when a change in fiscal year occurs due to a business combination or other circumstances).

statement: Auditor determination may also be used for business units covered in 42.705-1(a) when the contracting officer (or cognizant Federal agency official) and the auditor agree that the indirect costs can be settled with little difficulty and any of the listed circumstances applies.
quote: (2) In addition, auditor determination may be used for business units that are covered in 42.705-1(a) when the contracting officer (or cognizant Federal agency official) and auditor agree that the indirect costs can be settled with little difficulty and any of the following circumstances apply:

statement: One circumstance for auditor determination of a business unit covered in 42.705-1(a) is that the unit has primarily fixed-price contracts with only minor involvement in cost-reimbursement contracts; another is that the administrative cost of contracting officer determination would exceed the expected benefits.
quote: (i) The business unit has primarily fixed-price contracts, with only minor involvement in cost-reimbursement contracts. (ii) The administrative cost of contracting officer determination would exceed the expected benefits.

statement: Two further circumstances for auditor determination of a business unit covered in 42.705-1(a) are that the unit has no history of disputes and few cost problems, or that the contracting officer (or cognizant Federal agency official) and the auditor agree that special circumstances require auditor determination.
quote: (iii) The business unit does not have a history of disputes and there are few cost problems. (iv) The contracting officer (or cognizant Federal agency official) and auditor agree that special circumstances require auditor determination.

statement: A waiver of the certification requirement may be appropriate for a contract with a foreign government or international organization, or with a State or local government subject to the OMB Uniform Guidance.
quote: (2) A waiver may be appropriate for a contract with— (i) A foreign government or international organization, such as a subsidiary body of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization; (ii) A State or local government subject to the OMB Uniform Guidance at 2 CFR part 200, subpart E and appendices V and VII

statement: The Department of Energy may provide an alternate clause in its agency supplement for its Management and Operating contracts.
quote: (2) The Department of Energy may provide an alternate clause in its agency supplement for its Management and Operating contracts.

statement: A billing rate is an indirect cost rate established temporarily for interim reimbursement of incurred indirect costs and adjusted as necessary until final indirect cost rates are established.
quote: Billing rate as used in this subpart means an indirect cost rate (1) established temporarily for interim reimbursement of incurred indirect costs and (2) adjusted as necessary pending establishment of final indirect cost rates.

statement: Establishing final indirect cost rates gives a uniform approach with a contractor when more than one contract or agency is involved, economy of administration, and timely settlement under cost-reimbursement contracts.
quote: Establishing final indirect cost rates under this subpart provides— (1) Uniformity of approach with a contractor when more than one contract or agency is involved; (2) Economy of administration; and (3) Timely settlement under cost-reimbursement contracts.

statement: A single agency is responsible for establishing final indirect cost rates for each business unit, and those rates bind all agencies and their contracting offices unless a statute specifically prohibits that.
quote: A single agency (see 42.705-1) shall be responsible for establishing final indirect cost rates for each business unit. These rates shall be binding on all agencies and their contracting offices, unless otherwise specifically prohibited by statute.

statement: An agency does not perform its own audit of indirect cost rates when the contracting officer determines that the audit objectives can reasonably be met by accepting the results of an audit conducted by another department or agency of the Federal Government.
quote: An agency shall not perform an audit of indirect cost rates when the contracting officer determines that the objectives of the audit can reasonably be met by accepting the results of an audit that was conducted by any other department or agency of the Federal Government

statement: Billing rates and final indirect cost rates are used to reimburse indirect costs under cost-reimbursement contracts and to determine progress payments under fixed-price contracts.
quote: (b) Billing rates and final indirect cost rates shall be used in reimbursing indirect costs under cost-reimbursement contracts and in determining progress payments under fixed-price contracts.

statement: Final indirect cost rates are used for contract closeout for a business unit unless the quick-closeout procedure is used.
quote: Final indirect cost rates shall be used for contract closeout for a business unit, unless the quick-closeout procedure in 42.708 is used.

statement: Those final rates bind all cost-reimbursement contracts at the business unit, subject to any specific limitation in a contract or advance agreement.
quote: These final rates shall be binding for all cost-reimbursement contracts at the business unit, subject to any specific limitation in a contract or advance agreement

statement: Final indirect cost rates are used in negotiating the final price of fixed-price incentive and fixed-price redeterminable contracts, and in other situations requiring indirect costs to be settled before contract prices are established, unless the quick-closeout procedure is used.
quote: shall be used in negotiating the final price of fixed-price incentive and fixed-price redeterminable contracts and in other situations requiring that indirect costs be settled before contract prices are established, unless the quick-closeout procedure in 42.708 is used.

statement: When cost sharing is authorized, the arrangement may require the contractor to participate in the costs of the contract by accepting indirect cost rates lower than the anticipated actual rates.
quote: (a) Cost-sharing arrangements, when authorized, may call for the contractor to participate in the costs of the contract by accepting indirect cost rates lower than the anticipated actual rates.

statement: In a cost-sharing arrangement a negotiated indirect cost rate ceiling may be incorporated into the contract for prospective application.
quote: In such cases, a negotiated indirect cost rate ceiling may be incorporated into the contract for prospective application.

statement: One example of a situation where a final indirect cost rate ceiling may be prudent is a new or recently reorganized company with no past or recent record of incurred indirect costs.
quote: Other situations may make it prudent to provide a final indirect cost rate ceiling in a contract. Examples of such circumstances are when the proposed contractor— (i) Is a new or recently reorganized company, and there is no past or recent record of incurred indirect costs;

statement: In such cases an equitable ceiling covering the final indirect cost rates may be negotiated and specified in the contract.
quote: In such cases, an equitable ceiling covering the final indirect cost rates may be negotiated and specified in the contract.

statement: When ceiling provisions are used, the contract must also provide that the Government will not be obligated to pay any additional amount if the final indirect cost rates exceed the negotiated ceiling rates.
quote: When ceiling provisions are utilized, the contract shall also provide that (1) the Government will not be obligated to pay any additional amount should the final indirect cost rates exceed the negotiated ceiling rates

statement: When the final indirect cost rates are less than the negotiated ceiling rates, the negotiated rates are reduced to conform with the lower rates.
quote: (2) in the event the final indirect cost rates are less than the negotiated ceiling rates, the negotiated rates will be reduced to conform with the lower rates.

statement: Defense Contract Management Agency administrative contracting officers are authorized to negotiate the settlement of direct and indirect costs for a specific contract, task order, or delivery order to be closed in advance of the determination of final direct costs and indirect rates.
quote: Defense Contract Management Agency administrative contracting officers are authorized to negotiate the settlement of direct and indirect costs for a specific contract, task order, or delivery order to be closed in advance of the determination of final direct costs and indirect rates

statement: That authority applies regardless of the dollar value or percentage of unsettled direct or indirect costs allocable to the contract, task order, or delivery order.
quote: regardless of the dollar value or percentage of unsettled direct or indirect costs allocable to the contract, task order, or delivery order.

statement: In lieu of the thresholds in the FAR quick-closeout procedure, the DoD supplement treats unsettled direct and indirect costs as relatively insignificant under its own test; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-RTE-0317.
quote: (2) In lieu of the thresholds at FAR 42.708(a)(2)(i) and (ii), the amount of unsettled direct costs and indirect costs to be allocated to the contract, task order, or delivery order will be considered relatively insignificant

statement: Under that test the unsettled costs are relatively insignificant when the total allocated to any one contract, task order, or delivery order does not exceed $2 million, regardless of the total contract amount.
quote: when the total unsettled direct costs and indirect costs to be allocated to any one contract, task order, or delivery order do not exceed $2 million, regardless of the total contract, task order, or delivery order amount.

statement: DCAA policy on risk-based sampling governs the selection of incurred cost proposals for audit, with eligible proposals assessed on their Sampling Auditable Dollar Volume and various risk factors.
quote: DCAA’s policy on risk-based sampling governs the selection of incurred cost proposals (ICPs) for audit, with eligible proposals assessed based on their Sampling Auditable Dollar Volume (ADV) and various risk factors.
note: Source is the DCAA Contract Audit Manual chapter text printed for this packet; it is not codified regulation.

statement: For incurred cost proposals not randomly selected for audit, DCAA issues a risk-based sampling memorandum and a rate agreement letter, signed by both DCAA and the contractor, to finalize the indirect rates proposed.
quote: For ICPs not randomly selected for audit, DCAA will issue a risk-based sampling memorandum and a rate agreement letter, signed by both DCAA and the contractor, to finalize the indirect rates proposed in the ICP.
note: Source is DCAA Contract Audit Manual chapter text printed for this packet; it is not codified regulation.

statement: Unless an exception applies, incurred cost proposals with a Sampling Auditable Dollar Volume of less than $100 million are eligible for sampling.
quote: Unless an exception applies, ICPs with the following Sampling ADV are eligible for sampling: a. Less than $100 million are eligible for sampling.
note: Source is DCAA Contract Audit Manual chapter text printed for this packet; it is not codified regulation.

statement: Incurred cost proposals with a Sampling Auditable Dollar Volume of $1 billion or greater are not eligible for sampling and will be audited each year.
quote: $1 billion or greater are not eligible for sampling and will be audited each year.
note: Source is DCAA Contract Audit Manual chapter text printed for this packet; it is not codified regulation.

statement: A class deviation instructs contracting officers to rely on either a DCAA audit report or a DCAA memorandum to satisfy the requirements of FAR 42.505.
quote: This deviation instructs contracting officers to rely on either a DCAA audit report (attestation examination engagement) or a DCAA memorandum (advisory service) to satisfy the requirements of FAR 42.505.
note: Source is DCAA Contract Audit Manual chapter text printed for this packet; it is not codified regulation.

statement: Final indirect cost rates may be set based on the results of an audit or accepted as proposed if a low-risk sampling process is used, and the auditor's determination is generally final but contractors have the right to appeal.
quote: a. Audit Determination: Final indirect cost rates may be set based on the results of an audit or accepted as proposed if a low-risk sampling process is used. The auditor’s determination is generally final, but contractors have the right to appeal.
note: Source is DCAA Contract Audit Manual chapter text printed for this packet; it is not codified regulation.

statement: Final rates can instead be negotiated between the administrative contracting officer and the contractor, based on the contractor's proposal and the audit report or advisory memorandum.
quote: b. Contracting Officer Determination: Final rates can be negotiated between the ACO and contractor, based on the contractor’s proposal and audit report or advisory memorandum.
note: Source is DCAA Contract Audit Manual chapter text printed for this packet; it is not codified regulation.

statement: The process for settling a contractor's indirect cost rates may shift from being determined by negotiation with a contracting officer to being determined by audit, especially when both parties agree the rates can be settled easily or when special circumstances apply.
quote: In some cases, the process for settling a contractor’s indirect cost rates may shift from being determined by negotiation with a contracting officer to being determined by audit, especially when both parties agree that rates can be settled easily or when special circumstances apply.
note: Source is DCAA Contract Audit Manual chapter text printed for this packet; it is not codified regulation.

statement: When certified cost or pricing data are required, offerors are required to describe any forward pricing rate agreements in each specific pricing proposal to which the rates apply and to identify the latest cost or pricing data already submitted in accordance with the agreement.
quote: When certified cost or pricing data are required, offerors are required to describe any forward pricing rate agreements (FPRAs) in each specific pricing proposal to which the rates apply and to identify the latest cost or pricing data already submitted in accordance with the FPRA.

statement: All data submitted in connection with the agreement, updated as necessary, form part of the total data the offeror certifies to be accurate, complete, and current at the time of agreement on price for an initial contract or a contract modification.
quote: All data submitted in connection with the FPRA, updated as necessary, form a part of the total data that the offeror certifies to be accurate, complete, and current at the time of agreement on price for an initial contract or for a contract modification.

statement: Contracting officers use forward pricing rate agreement rates as bases for pricing all contracts, modifications, and other contractual actions to be performed during the period covered by the agreement.
quote: Contracting officers will use FPRA rates as bases for pricing all contracts, modifications, and other contractual actions to be performed during the period covered by the agreement.

statement: Conditions that may affect the agreement's validity must be reported promptly to the administrative contracting officer, and if that officer determines a changed condition invalidates the agreement, all interested parties are notified of its effect and of efforts to establish a revised agreement.
quote: Conditions that may affect the agreement's validity shall be reported promptly to the ACO. If the ACO determines that a changed condition invalidates the agreement, the ACO shall notify all interested parties of the extent of its effect and status of efforts to establish a revised FPRA.

statement: Contracting officers must not require certification at the time of agreement for data supplied in support of forward pricing rate agreements or other advance agreements.
quote: Contracting officers shall not require certification at the time of agreement for data supplied in support of FPRA's or other advance agreements.

statement: When such an agreement is used to price an action that requires a certificate, the certificate supporting that action covers the data supplied to support the agreement and all other data supporting the action.
quote: When a forward pricing rate agreement or other advance agreement is used to price a contract action that requires a certificate, the certificate supporting that contract action shall cover the data supplied to support the FPRA or other advance agreement, and all other data supporting the action.

statement: For DoD, forward pricing rate agreement rates must be used when available unless waived on a case-by-case basis by the head of the contracting activity, and each case waived must be reported to the administrative contracting officer.
quote: Use forward pricing rate agreement (FPRA) rates when such rates are available, unless waived on a case-by-case basis by the head of the contracting activity. (ii) Advise the ACO of each case waived.
note: Covers paragraphs (b)(i) and (b)(ii) of the DFARS section.

statement: Notwithstanding the Allowable Cost and Payment clause, allowable indirect costs under the contract are obtained by applying predetermined indirect cost rates to bases agreed upon by the parties.
quote: (a) Notwithstanding the Allowable Cost and Payment clause of this contract, the allowable indirect costs under this contract shall be obtained by applying predetermined indirect cost rates to bases agreed upon by the parties, as specified below.

statement: The contractor must submit an adequate final indirect cost rate proposal to the contracting officer or cognizant Federal agency official and to the auditor within the six-month period following the expiration of each fiscal year.
quote: The Contractor shall submit an adequate final indirect cost rate proposal to the Contracting Officer (or cognizant Federal agency official) and auditor within the 6-month period following the expiration of each of its fiscal years.

statement: Reasonable extensions are for exceptional circumstances only, and may be requested in writing by the contractor and granted in writing by the contracting officer.
quote: Reasonable extensions, for exceptional circumstances only, may be requested in writing by the Contractor and granted in writing by the Contracting Officer.

statement: The proposed rates are based on the contractor's actual cost experience for the period, and the final rates are established as promptly as practical after the proposal is received.
quote: The proposed rates shall be based on the Contractor's actual cost experience for that period. The appropriate Government representative and the Contractor shall establish the final indirect cost rates as promptly as practical after receipt of the Contractor's proposal.

statement: Allowability of costs and acceptability of cost allocation methods are determined in accordance with FAR subpart 31.3 in effect on the date of the contract.
quote: (c) Allowability of costs and acceptability of cost allocation methods shall be determined in accordance with FAR subpart 31.3 in effect on the date of this contract.

statement: The written indirect cost rate agreement specifies the agreed predetermined rates, the bases the rates apply to, the period covered, and the items treated as direct costs or changes to items previously agreed as direct costs.
quote: The agreement shall specify (1) the agreed-upon predetermined indirect cost rates, (2) the bases to which the rates apply, (3) the period for which the rates apply, and (4) the specific items treated as direct costs or any changes in the items previously agreed to be direct costs.

statement: The indirect cost rate agreement does not change any monetary ceiling, contract obligation, or specific cost allowance or disallowance provided for in the contract.
quote: The indirect cost rate agreement shall not change any monetary ceiling, contract obligation, or specific cost allowance or disallowance provided for in this contract.

statement: Pending establishment of the predetermined rates for a period, the contractor is reimbursed at the rates fixed for the previous period or at billing rates acceptable to the contracting officer, subject to appropriate adjustment when the final rates are established.
quote: the Contractor shall be reimbursed either at the rates fixed for the previous fiscal year (or other period) or at billing rates acceptable to the Contracting Officer (or cognizant Federal agency official), subject to appropriate adjustment when the final rates for that period are established.

statement: If the parties fail to agree to predetermined indirect cost rates for a fiscal year or other period specified in the Schedule, allowable indirect costs are obtained by applying final indirect cost rates established in accordance with the Allowable Cost and Payment clause.
quote: If for any fiscal year (or other period specified in the Schedule) the parties fail to agree to predetermined indirect cost rates, the allowable indirect costs shall be obtained by applying final indirect cost rates established in accordance with the Allowable Cost and Payment clause.

statement: When the contractor and the government reach a bilateral agreement on a forward pricing rate proposal, they execute a contractually binding forward pricing rate agreement to be used across all subsequent proposals.
quote: If the contractor and the government reach a bilateral agreement on the FPRP, they execute a contractually binding Forward Pricing Rate Agreement to be used across all subsequent proposals.
note: Source is DCAA Contract Audit Manual chapter text printed for this packet; it is not codified regulation.

statement: In the absence of a signed agreement or while negotiations are ongoing, the administrative contracting officer unilaterally issues a forward pricing rate recommendation for procurement offices.
quote: In the absence of a signed agreement or while negotiations are ongoing, the Administrative Contracting Officer unilaterally issues a Forward Pricing Rate Recommendation for procurement offices.
note: Source is DCAA Contract Audit Manual chapter text printed for this packet; it is not codified regulation.

statement: A forward pricing rate recommendation is a formal rate schedule the administrative contracting officer issues to procuring contracting officers recommending rates to use when an agreement cannot be reached, is being updated, or is being audited.
quote: Forward Pricing Rate Recommendation (FPRR): A formal rate schedule issued unilaterally by the ACO to procuring contracting officers (PCOs) recommending specific rates to use when an FPRA cannot be reached, is being updated, or is being audited.
note: Source is DCAA Contract Audit Manual chapter text printed for this packet; it is not codified regulation.

statement: The process can be initiated by the contractor, the procuring contracting officer, or the administrative contracting officer, and the contractor's proposal must include certified cost or pricing data that is accurate, complete, and current.
quote: The process can be initiated by the contractor, the Procuring Contracting Officer, or the Administrative Contracting Officer. A key regulatory requirement is that the contractor's FPRA proposal must include certified cost or pricing data that is accurate, complete, and current.
note: Source is DCAA Contract Audit Manual chapter text printed for this packet; it is not codified regulation.

statement: The proposal requires certified data, but the formal certificate of current cost or pricing data is not executed when the agreement itself is made; certification occurs when an individual contract that uses the rates is priced.
quote: while the initial FPRA proposal requires certified data, the formal Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data is not executed upon agreement of the FPRA itself. Instead, the certification occurs when an individual contract that uses the FPRA rates is priced.
note: Source is DCAA Contract Audit Manual chapter text printed for this packet; it is not codified regulation.

statement: When evaluating a proposal, the auditor must assess the reasonableness of the projected business volume, allocation bases, and indirect costs.
quote: When evaluating a contractor's FPRA proposal, the auditor must assess the reasonableness of the projected business volume, allocation bases, and indirect costs.
note: Source is DCAA Contract Audit Manual chapter text printed for this packet; it is not codified regulation.

statement: The auditor periodically compares the agreed-upon rates with the contractor's actual rates to identify significant variances, and if unfavorable trends emerge the auditor notifies the administrative contracting officer and may recommend a revised proposal.
quote: This involves periodically comparing the agreed-upon rates with the contractor's actual rates to identify any significant variances. If unfavorable trends emerge, the auditor should notify the ACO and may recommend that the contractor submit a revised FPRA proposal.
note: Source is DCAA Contract Audit Manual chapter text printed for this packet; it is not codified regulation.

statement: If an auditor later finds that rates should have been revised due to significant changes to reflect more accurate, complete, or current certified cost or pricing data, pricing actions using the rates should be subject to a Truthful Cost or Pricing Data audit.
quote: If an auditor later finds that rates should have been revised due to significant changes to reflect more accurate, complete, or current certified cost or pricing data, pricing actions using the rates should be subject to a Truthful Cost or Pricing Data (TIN) audit.
note: Source is DCAA Contract Audit Manual chapter text printed for this packet; it is not codified regulation.

statement: Defense Pricing, Contracting, and Acquisition Policy authorized a class deviation, DCAA Policy and Procedures for Sampling Low-Risk Incurred Cost Proposals, dated July 24, 2012.
quote: Defense Pricing, Contracting, and Acquisition Policy authorized a Class Deviation – DCAA Policy and Procedures for Sampling Low-Risk Incurred Cost Proposals, dated July 24, 2012.
note: Source is the DCAA Contract Audit Manual chapter text printed for this packet; it is not codified regulation.

statement: The Department relies on three sequential rate mechanisms governed by FAR for negotiating future defense contracts, and the process begins with a forward pricing rate proposal.
quote: The Department relies on three sequential rate mechanisms governed by FAR to streamline and standardize the negotiation of future defense contracts. The process begins with a Forward Pricing Rate Proposal.
note: Source is DCAA Contract Audit Manual chapter text printed for this packet; it is not codified regulation.

statement: A forward pricing rate proposal is the contractor's formal submission detailing its forecast of direct labor rates, indirect cost pools, and allocation bases over a specified multi-year projection period.
quote: Forward Pricing Rate Proposal (FPRP): The contractor's formal submission detailing its forecast of direct labor rates, indirect cost pools (e.g., Fringe, Overhead, G&A), and allocation bases over a specified multi-year projection period.
note: Source is DCAA Contract Audit Manual chapter text printed for this packet; it is not codified regulation.

statement: A forward pricing rate agreement is a formal written agreement negotiated between the contractor and the government establishing specific rates to be used in pricing proposals during a specified period.
quote: Forward Pricing Rate Agreement (FPRA): A formal written agreement negotiated between the contractor and the government establishing specific rates to be used in pricing proposals during a specified period.
note: Source is DCAA Contract Audit Manual chapter text printed for this packet; it is not codified regulation.

statement: The CFAO performs CAS administration for all contracts and subcontracts in a business unit, even when the contracting officer retains other administration functions.
quote: The CFAO shall perform CAS administration for all contracts and subcontracts in a business unit, even when the contracting officer retains other administration functions.

statement: Within 30 days after awarding a new contract subject to CAS, the contracting officer making the award must request the CFAO to perform administration for CAS matters.
quote: Within 30 days after the award of any new contract subject to CAS, the contracting officer making the award shall request the CFAO to perform administration for CAS matters (see Subpart 42.2).

statement: In determining materiality, the CFAO must use the criteria in 48 CFR 9903.305.
quote: In determining materiality, the CFAO shall use the criteria in 48 CFR 9903.305.

statement: When the CFAO determines that a cost impact is immaterial, the CFAO must make no contract adjustments, conclude the cost impact process, and document the rationale for the determination; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-RTE-0024.
quote: When the CFAO determines the cost impact is immaterial, the CFAO shall— (1) Make no contract adjustments and conclude the cost impact process; (2) Document the rationale for the determination

statement: One of the two determinations the CFAO may make about a required change is that the cost accounting practice change is required to comply with a CAS, or a modification or interpretation thereof, that subsequently became applicable to one or more contracts or subcontracts; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-RTE-0705.
quote: the CFAO shall determine that— (1) The cost accounting practice change is required to comply with a CAS, or a modification or interpretation thereof, that subsequently became applicable to one or more contracts or subcontracts; or

statement: The clause at 52.230-6 requires the contractor to submit a description of the change to the CFAO not less than 60 days, or another mutually agreeable date, before implementation of the change.
quote: the clause at 52.230-6, Administration of Cost Accounting Standards, requires the contractor to— (i) Submit a description of the change to the CFAO not less than 60 days (or other mutually agreeable date) before implementation of the change

statement: Required changes made to comply with new or modified standards may require equitable adjustments, but only to those contracts awarded before the effective date of the new or modified standard.
quote: Required changes made to comply with new or modified standards may require equitable adjustments, but only to those contracts awarded before the effective date of the new or modified standard (see 52.230-2, 52.230-3, or 52.230-5).

statement: When a contractor elects to implement a required change to comply with a new or modified standard prior to the applicability date of the standard, the CFAO must administer the change as a unilateral change.
quote: When a contractor elects to implement a required change to comply with a new or modified standard prior to the applicability date of the standard, the CFAO shall administer the change as a unilateral change (see 30.603-2).

statement: A contractor may unilaterally change its disclosed or established cost accounting practices, but the Government shall not pay any increased cost in the aggregate as a result of the unilateral change.
quote: The contractor may unilaterally change its disclosed or established cost accounting practices, but the Government shall not pay any increased cost, in the aggregate, as a result of the unilateral change.

statement: Prior to taking action addressing a desirable change, the CFAO must determine that the change is a desirable change and not detrimental to the interests of the Government.
quote: Prior to taking action under the applicable paragraph(s) addressing a desirable change at 52.230-2, 52.230-3, or 52.230-5, the CFAO shall determine the change is a desirable change and not detrimental to the interests of the Government.

statement: Until the CFAO has determined a change to a cost accounting practice is a desirable change, the change remains a unilateral change.
quote: Until the CFAO has determined a change to a cost accounting practice is a desirable change, the change is a unilateral change.

statement: The CFAO must not approve a date for a retroactive change that is before the beginning of the contractor's fiscal year in which the request is made.
quote: The CFAO shall not approve a date for the retroactive change that is before the beginning of the contractor's fiscal year in which the request is made.

statement: A contractor may submit a detailed cost-impact (DCI) proposal in lieu of a general dollar magnitude (GDM) proposal provided the DCI proposal is in accordance with the section's requirements for detailed cost-impact proposals.
quote: The contractor may submit a detailed cost-impact (DCI) proposal in lieu of a GDM proposal provided the DCI proposal is in accordance with paragraph (g) of this section.

statement: The cost impact calculation must include all affected CAS-covered contracts and subcontracts regardless of their status or the fiscal year in which costs are incurred.
quote: The cost impact calculation shall— (1) Include all affected CAS-covered contracts and subcontracts regardless of their status (i.e., open or closed) or the fiscal year(s) in which the costs are incurred (i.e., whether or not the final indirect rates have been established);

statement: For flexibly-priced contracts and subcontracts, the difference is an increased cost to the Government when the estimated cost to complete using the changed practice exceeds the estimated cost to complete using the current practice.
quote: flexibly-priced contracts and subcontracts as follows: (A) When the estimated cost to complete using the changed practice exceeds the estimated cost to complete using the current practice, the difference is increased cost to the Government.

statement: For fixed-price contracts and subcontracts, the difference is an increased cost to the Government when the estimated cost to complete using the changed practice is less than the estimated cost to complete using the current practice.
quote: fixed-price contracts and subcontracts as follows: (A) When the estimated cost to complete using the changed practice is less than the estimated cost to complete using the current practice, the difference is increased cost to the Government.

statement: The CFAO takes one or both of two listed actions, one of which is to withhold an amount not to exceed 10 percent of each subsequent payment related to the contractor's CAS-covered contracts, up to the estimated general dollar magnitude of the cost impact, until the contractor furnishes the required information.
quote: (2) Take one or both of the following actions: (i) Withhold an amount not to exceed 10 percent of each subsequent payment related to the contractor's CAS-covered contracts (up to the estimated general dollar magnitude of the cost impact), until the contractor furnishes the required information.

statement: Within 15 days of receiving a report of alleged noncompliance from the auditor, the CFAO must either notify the auditor of disagreement or issue a notice of potential noncompliance to the contractor.
quote: Within 15 days of receiving a report of alleged noncompliance from the auditor, the CFAO shall— (i) Notify the auditor that the CFAO disagrees with the alleged noncompliance; or (ii) Issue a notice of potential noncompliance to the contractor and provide a copy to the auditor.

statement: The notice of potential noncompliance must notify the contractor in writing of the exact nature of the noncompliance and allow the contractor 60 days, or another mutually agreeable date, to agree or submit reasons why the contractor considers the existing practices to be in compliance; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-RTE-0025.
quote: The notice of potential noncompliance shall— (i) Notify the contractor in writing of the exact nature of the noncompliance; and (ii) Allow the contractor 60 days or other mutually agreeable date to— (A) Agree or submit reasons why the contractor considers the existing practices to be in compliance

statement: The contractor must submit a description of any cost accounting practice change needed to correct a noncompliance within 60 days after the earlier of agreeing that there is a noncompliance or receiving notification of a noncompliance determination.
quote: submit a description of any cost accounting practice change needed to correct a noncompliance within 60 days after the earlier of— (i) Agreement with the CFAO that there is a noncompliance; or (ii) Notification by the CFAO of a determination of noncompliance.

statement: The CFAO must separately identify interest on any increased cost paid in the aggregate as a result of the noncompliance, and must compute interest from the date of overpayment to the date of repayment using the rate specified in section 6621(a)(2) of title 26 of the United States Code.
quote: The CFAO shall— (1) Separately identify interest on any increased cost paid, in the aggregate, as a result of the noncompliance; (2) Compute interest from the date of overpayment to the date of repayment using the rate specified in 26 U.S.C. 6621(a)(2).

statement: For fixed-price contracts and subcontracts, the difference is an increased cost to the Government when the negotiated contract or subcontract price exceeds what the negotiated price would have been had the contractor used a compliant practice.
quote: fixed-price contracts and subcontracts as follows: (i) When the negotiated contract or subcontract price exceeds what the negotiated price would have been had the contractor used a compliant practice, the difference is increased cost to the Government.

statement: The CFAO must coordinate with the affected contracting officers before negotiating and resolving a cost impact when the estimated cost impact on any of their contracts is at least $100,000, but the CFAO has sole authority for negotiating and resolving it.
quote: The CFAO shall coordinate with the affected contracting officers before negotiating and resolving the cost impact when the estimated cost impact on any of their contracts is at least $100,000. However, the CFAO has the sole authority for negotiating and resolving the cost impact.

statement: In resolving cost impacts, the CFAO must not combine the cost impacts of a required change or desirable change with a unilateral change or noncompliance.
quote: In resolving the cost impact, the CFAO— (i) Shall not combine the cost impacts of any of the following: (A) A required change and a unilateral change. (B) A required change and a noncompliance. (C) A desirable change and a unilateral change. (D) A desirable change and a noncompliance.

statement: If contract adjustments are made, the CFAO must preclude payment of aggregate increased costs by taking one or both of two actions, reducing the contract price on fixed-price contracts or disallowing costs on flexibly-priced contracts.
quote: (ii) If contract adjustments are made, preclude payment of aggregate increased costs by taking one or both of the following actions: (A) Reduce the contract price on fixed-price contracts. (B) Disallow costs on flexibly-priced contracts;

statement: The CFAO may use an alternate method instead of adjusting contracts to resolve a cost impact, provided the Government will not pay more in the aggregate and the contracting parties agree.
quote: The CFAO may use an alternate method instead of adjusting contracts to resolve the cost impact, provided the Government will not pay more, in the aggregate, than would be paid if the CFAO did not use the alternate method and the contracting parties agree on the use of that alternate method.

statement: When using an alternate method that excludes costs from an indirect cost pool, the CFAO must apply the exclusion only to the determination of final indirect cost rates.
quote: When using an alternate method that excludes the costs from an indirect cost pool, the CFAO shall— (i) Apply such exclusion only to the determination of final indirect cost rates (see 42.705);

statement: When a negotiated CAS price adjustment or noncompliance determination is required at the subcontract level, the subcontractor CFAO must furnish a copy of the negotiation memorandum or determination to the CFAO for the contractor of the next higher-tier subcontractor.
quote: When a negotiated CAS price adjustment or a determination of noncompliance is required at the subcontract level, the CFAO for the subcontractor shall furnish a copy of the negotiation memorandum or the determination to the CFAO for the contractor of the next higher-tier subcontractor.

statement: The CFAO of the contractor or next higher-tier subcontractor shall not change the determination of the CFAO for the lower-tier subcontractor.
quote: The CFAO of the contractor or the next higher-tier subcontractor shall not change the determination of the CFAO for the lower-tier subcontractor.

statement: If a subcontractor refuses to submit a general dollar magnitude or detailed cost-impact proposal, remedies are made at the prime contractor level.
quote: If the subcontractor refuses to submit a GDM or DCI proposal, remedies are made at the prime contractor level.

statement: When the Government requires determinations of adequacy of subcontractor disclosure statements, the subcontractor CFAO provides this determination to the CFAO for the contractor or next higher-tier subcontractor.
quote: When the Government requires determinations of adequacy of subcontractor disclosure statements, the CFAO for the subcontractor shall provide this determination to the CFAO for the contractor or next higher-tier subcontractor.

statement: Any determination that it is impractical to secure a subcontractor Disclosure Statement must be made in accordance with 48 CFR 9903.202-2.
quote: Any determination that it is impractical to secure a subcontractor's Disclosure Statement must be made in accordance with 48 CFR 9903.202-2.

statement: Standard costs may be used for estimating, accumulating and reporting costs of direct material and direct labor only when standard costs and related variances are appropriately accounted for at the production unit level and under the standard costing paragraph.
quote: (i) Standard costs may be used for estimating, accumulating, and reporting costs of direct material and direct labor only when standard costs and related variances are appropriately accounted for at the level of the production unit and paragraph (h) of this section;

statement: An average cost or pre-established rate for labor may be used if the functions performed are not materially disparate and the employees involved are interchangeable with respect to them, or if the alternative condition for materially disparate functions is met; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-RTE-0652.
quote: (ii) An average cost or pre-established rate for labor may be used provided that: (A) The functions performed are not materially disparate and employees involved are interchangeable with respect to the functions performed, or

statement: The alternative condition for using an average cost or pre-established rate for labor is that the functions performed are materially disparate but the employees involved either all work in a single production unit yielding homogeneous outputs or perform their respective functions as an integral team.
quote: (B) The functions performed are materially disparate but the employees involved either all work in a single production unit yielding homogeneous outputs, or perform their respective functions as an integral team.

statement: When average cost or pre-established rates for labor are used, material variances must be disposed of at least annually by allocation to cost objectives in proportion to the costs previously allocated to those cost objectives.
quote: Whenever average cost or pre-established rates for labor are used, the variances, if material, shall be disposed of at least annually by allocation to cost objectives in proportion to the costs previously allocated to these cost objectives.

statement: A labor-rate standard may be set to cover a group of direct labor workers who perform disparate functions only under the conditions of one of two listed alternatives.
quote: (1) A labor-rate standard may be set to cover a group of direct labor workers who perform disparate functions only under the conditions in either paragraph (h)(1)(i) or (ii) of this section:

statement: The first alternative is a group of workers who all work in a single production unit yielding homogeneous outputs, and the same labor-rate standard is then applied to each worker in that group.
quote: (i) Where that group of workers all work in a single production unit yielding homogeneous outputs (in this case, the same labor-rate standard shall be applied to each worker in that group).

statement: The second alternative is a group of workers who form an integral team in performing their respective functions, and a labor-rate standard is then set for each integral team.
quote: (ii) Where that group of workers, in the performance of their respective functions, forms an integral team (in this case, a labor-rate standard shall be set for each integral team).

statement: Variances are allocated to cost objectives, including ending in-process inventory, at least annually, and where a variance related to material is allocated the allocation is on the basis of material cost at standard or, where outputs are homogeneous, units of output.
quote: (i) Variances are allocated to cost objectives (including ending in-process inventory) at least annually. Where a variance related to material is allocated, the allocation shall be on the basis of the material cost at standard, or, where outputs are homogeneous, on the basis of units of output.

statement: Variances which are immaterial may be included in appropriate indirect cost pools for allocation to applicable cost objectives.
quote: (ii) Variances which are immaterial may be included in appropriate indirect cost pools for allocation to applicable cost objectives.

statement: A production unit is a grouping of activities that either uses homogeneous inputs of direct material and direct labor or yields homogeneous outputs, such that the related costs or statistics are appropriate bases for allocating variances.
quote: (5) Production unit means a grouping of activities which either uses homogeneous inputs of direct material and direct labor or yields homogeneous outputs such that the costs or statistics related to these homogeneous inputs or outputs are appropriate as bases for allocating variances.

statement: Where preestablished indirect rates are used and the variances of a cost accounting period are material, those variances shall be disposed of by allocating them to cost objectives in proportion to the costs previously allocated to them by the preestablished rates.
quote: (4) Under paragraphs (g) (2) and (3) of this subsection where variances of a cost accounting period are material, these variances shall be disposed of by allocating them to cost objectives in proportion to the costs previously allocated to these cost objectives by use of the preestablished rates.

statement: An indirect cost pool is homogeneous if each significant activity whose costs are included in it has the same or a similar beneficial or causal relationship to cost objectives as the other activities in the pool.
quote: (1) An indirect cost pool is homogeneous if each significant activity whose costs are included therein has the same or a similar beneficial or causal relationship to cost objectives as the other activities whose costs are included in the cost pool.

statement: An indirect cost pool is also homogeneous if allocating the costs of its activities together gives an allocation to cost objectives that is not materially different from allocating those costs separately.
quote: It is also homogeneous if the allocation of the costs of the activities included in the cost pool result in an allocation to cost objectives which is not materially different from the allocation that would result if the costs of the activities were allocated separately.

statement: A homogeneous indirect cost pool shall include all indirect costs identified with the activity to which the pool relates.
quote: (3) A homogeneous indirect cost pool shall include all indirect costs identified with the activity to which the pool relates.

statement: The costs of management or supervision of activities involving direct labor or direct material costs have no direct and definitive relationship to the benefiting cost objectives and cannot be allocated on measures of a specific beneficial or causal relationship.
quote: (1) The costs of the management or supervision of activities involving direct labor or direct material costs do not have a direct and definitive relationship to the benefiting cost objectives and cannot be allocated on measures of a specific beneficial or causal relationship.

statement: Where management or supervision costs cannot be allocated on measures of a specific beneficial or causal relationship, the base selected to measure the allocation of the pooled costs shall be a base representative of the activity being managed or supervised.
quote: cannot be allocated on measures of a specific beneficial or causal relationship. In that circumstance, the base selected to measure the allocation of the pooled costs to cost objectives shall be a base representative of the activity being managed or supervised.

statement: A direct labor hour base or direct labor cost base shall be used, whichever in the aggregate is more likely to vary in proportion to the costs in the pool being allocated, except where one of the listed other bases applies.
quote: (i) A direct labor hour base or direct labor cost base shall be used, whichever in the aggregate is more likely to vary in proportion to the costs included in the cost pool being allocated, except that:

statement: A machine-hour base is appropriate if the pool's costs are predominantly facility-related costs such as depreciation, maintenance and utilities, and a units-of-production base is appropriate if there is common production of comparable units.
quote: (ii) A machine-hour base is appropriate if the costs in the cost pool are comprised predominantly of facility-related costs, such as depreciation, maintenance, and utilities; or (iii) A units-of-production base is appropriate if there is common production of comparable units; or

statement: Homogeneous indirect cost pools of the type described in the paragraph on pools without material management or supervision costs have a direct and definitive relationship to benefiting cost objectives and shall be allocated using an appropriate measure of resource consumption.
quote: Homogeneous indirect cost pools of this type have a direct and definitive relationship between the activities in the pool and benefiting cost objectives. The pooled costs shall be allocated using an appropriate measure of resource consumption.

statement: If consumption measures are unavailable or impractical to ascertain, the next best representation of the beneficial or causal relationship for allocation is a measure of the output of the activities of the indirect cost pool.
quote: (2) (i) If consumption measures are unavailable or impractical to ascertain, the next best representation of the beneficial or causal relationship for allocation is a measure of the output of the activities of the indirect cost pool.

statement: Indirect cost pools which benefit one another may be allocated by the cross-allocation (reciprocal) method, the sequential method, or another method whose results approximate those achieved by either of those methods.
quote: (4) Allocation of indirect cost pools which benefit one another may be accomplished by use of: (i) The cross-allocation (reciprocal) method, (ii) The sequential method, or (iii) Another method the results of which approximate those achieved by either of the methods

statement: General and administrative expense means any management, financial and other expense that is incurred by or allocated to a business unit and is for the general management and administration of the business unit as a whole.
quote: (6) General and administrative (G&A) expense means any management, financial, and other expense which is incurred by or allocated to a business unit and which is for the general management and administration of the business unit as a whole.

statement: General and administrative expense does not include management expenses whose beneficial or causal relationship to cost objectives can be more directly measured by a base other than a cost input base representing the total activity of the business unit.
quote: G&A expense does not include those management expenses whose beneficial or causal relationship to cost objectives can be more directly measured by a base other than a cost input base representing the total activity of a business unit during a cost accounting period.

statement: The general and administrative expense pool may be combined with other expenses for allocation to final cost objectives provided that the base used for the combined pool is appropriate for both the pool and the other expenses and a second condition is also met; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-RTE-0674.
quote: (b) The G&A expense pool may be combined with other expenses for allocation to final cost objectives provided that— (1) The allocation base used for the combined pool is appropriate both for the allocation of the G&A expense pool under this Standard and for the allocation of the other expenses; and

statement: Provision is made to identify the components and total of the general and administrative expense pool separately from the other expenses in the combined pool.
quote: (2) Provision is made to identify the components and total of the G&A expense pool separately from the other expenses in the combined pool.

statement: The cost input base selected to represent the total activity of a business unit during a cost accounting period may be total cost input, value-added cost input or single element cost input.
quote: The cost input base selected to represent the total activity of a business unit during a cost accounting period may be: Total cost input; value-added cost input; or single element cost input.

statement: Value-added cost input shall be used as the allocation base where including material and subcontract costs would significantly distort the allocation of the pool in relation to the benefits received and where costs other than direct labor are significant measures of total activity.
quote: Value-added cost input shall be used as an allocation base where inclusion of material and subcontract costs would significantly distort the allocation of the G&A expense pool in relation to the benefits received, and where costs other than direct labor are significant measures of total activity.

statement: A total cost input base is generally acceptable as an appropriate measure of the total activity of a business unit.
quote: (1) A total cost input base is generally acceptable as an appropriate measure of the total activity of a business unit.

statement: A single element base is inappropriate where it is an insignificant part of the total cost of some of the final cost objectives.
quote: A single element base is inappropriate where it is an insignificant part of the total cost of some of the final cost objectives.

statement: Expenses which are not general and administrative expenses and are insignificant in amount may be included in the general and administrative expense pool for allocation to final cost objectives.
quote: (c) Expenses which are not G&A expenses and are insignificant in amount may be included in the G&A expense pool for allocation to final cost objectives.

statement: Ordinarily, each home office service or management function will have to be separately identified for allocation by means of an appropriate allocation technique.
quote: Ordinarily, each service or management function will have to be separately identified for allocation by means of an appropriate allocation technique.

statement: Different functions need not be identified and allocated separately if allocation in accordance with the relevant requirements of the standard can be made using a common allocation base.
quote: However, it is not necessary to identify and allocate different functions separately, if allocation in accordance with the relevant requirements of 9904.403-40(b) can be made using a common allocation base.

statement: The allocation of centralized service functions shall be governed by a hierarchy of preferable allocation techniques representing beneficial or causal relationships, and the preferred representation is a measure of the activity of the organization performing the function.
quote: The allocation of centralized service functions shall be governed by a hierarchy of preferable allocation techniques which represent beneficial or causal relationships. The preferred representation of such relationships is a measure of the activity of the organization performing the function.

statement: The costs of labor-oriented, machine-oriented or space-oriented supporting functions shall be allocated by use of a rate, such as a rate per labor hour, rate per machine hour or cost per square foot, unless such measures are unavailable or impractical to ascertain.
quote: costs of these functions shall be allocated by use of a rate, such as a rate per labor hour, rate per machine hour or cost per square foot, unless such measures are unavailable or impractical to ascertain.

statement: Where activity-rate measures for a supporting function are unavailable or impractical to ascertain, the basis for allocation shall be a measurement of the output of the supporting function.
quote: unless such measures are unavailable or impractical to ascertain. In these latter cases the basis for allocation shall be a measurement of the output of the supporting function.

statement: Where neither activity nor output of the supporting function can be practically measured, a surrogate for the beneficial or causal relationship must be selected.
quote: (2) Where neither activity nor output of the supporting function can be practically measured, a surrogate for the beneficial, or causal relationship must be selected.

statement: Where residual expenses are required to be allocated pursuant to 9904.403-40(c)(2), the three factor formula must be used.
quote: (1) Where residual expenses are required to be allocated pursuant to 9904.403-40(c)(2), the three factor formula described below must be used.

statement: IR&D and B&P project costs shall include costs that would be treated as direct costs of a final cost objective if incurred in like circumstances for it, together with a second listed category of costs; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-RTE-0753.
quote: (a) The IR&D and B&P project costs shall include (1) costs, which if incurred in like circumstances for a final cost objective, would be treated as direct costs of that final cost objective, and

statement: The IR&D and B&P cost pools for a segment consist of the project costs plus allocable home office IR&D and B&P costs.
quote: (b) The IR&D and B&P cost pools for a segment consist of the project costs plus allocable home office IR&D and B&P costs.

statement: When the costs of individual IR&D or B&P efforts are not material in amount, they may be accumulated in one or more projects within each of the two types of effort.
quote: (c) When the costs of individual IR&D or B&P efforts are not material in amount, these costs may be accumulated in one or more project(s) within each of these two types of effort.

statement: Home office IR&D and B&P projects that can be identified with a specific segment shall have their costs allocated to that segment.
quote: (e) The costs of IR&D and B&P projects accumulated at a home office shall be allocated to its segments as follows: (1) Projects which can be identified with a specific segment(s) shall have their costs allocated to such segment(s).

statement: The costs of all other IR&D and B&P projects shall be allocated among all segments by means of the same base the company uses to allocate its residual expenses, subject to a proviso; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-RTE-0693.
quote: (2) The costs of all other IR&D and B&P projects shall be allocated among all segments by means of the same base used by the company to allocate its residual expenses in accordance with 9904.403; provided, however,

statement: IR&D and B&P cost pools that are not allocated under the preceding subparagraph shall be allocated to all final cost objectives of the business unit by means of the same base the business unit uses to allocate its general and administrative expenses; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-RTE-0030.
quote: (2) The IR&D and B&P cost pools which are not allocated under subparagraph (f)(1) of this subsection, shall be allocated to all final cost objectives of the business unit by means of the same base used by the business unit to allocate its general and administrative expenses
