statement: Each line item may be subdivided into separate unique subsets, called subline items, to ease administration.
quote: Each line item may be subdivided into separate unique subsets (called subline items) to ease administration.

statement: Subline items differentiate between or among certain characteristics of the line item, such as colors or sizes, dates of delivery, destinations, or places of performance, and are established to define deliverables or organize information about deliverables.
quote: Subline items differentiate between or among certain characteristics of the line item, such as colors or sizes, dates of delivery, destinations, or places of performance. Subline items are established to define deliverables or organize information about deliverables.

statement: Under the first listed characteristic, a supply is separately identifiable if it has its own identification, such as a national stock number, item description or manufacturer's part number, and services are separately identifiable if they have no more than one statement of work or performance work statement.

statement: A single deliverable may be funded by multiple accounting classifications when the deliverable effort cannot be otherwise subdivided.

statement: If the contractor fails to submit a report in a timely manner, the contracting officer must exercise appropriate contractual remedies.

quote: In addition, the contracting officer shall make the contractor's failure to comply with the reporting requirements a part of the contractor's performance information under subpart 42.15.

quote: The contracting officer may insert the clause at 52.244-4, Subcontractors and Outside Associates and Consultants (Architect-Engineer Services), in architect-engineer contracts.

quote: The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.244-6, Subcontracts for Commercial Products and Commercial Services, in solicitations and contracts other than those for commercial products or commercial services.

statement: Acceptance is the act of an authorized representative of the Government by which the Government, for itself or as agent of another, assumes ownership of existing identified supplies tendered or approves specific services rendered as partial or complete performance of the contract.
quote: Acceptance means the act of an authorized representative of the Government by which the Government, for itself or as agent of another, assumes ownership of existing identified supplies tendered or approves specific services rendered as partial or complete performance of the contract.

statement: Conditional acceptance is acceptance of supplies or services that do not conform to contract quality requirements, or are otherwise incomplete, that the contractor is required to correct or otherwise complete by a specified date.
quote: Conditional acceptance means acceptance of supplies or services that do not conform to contract quality requirements, or are otherwise incomplete, that the contractor is required to correct or otherwise complete by a specified date.

statement: Contract quality requirements are the technical requirements in the contract relating to the quality of the product or service; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-SUP-3883.
quote: Contract quality requirements means the technical requirements in the contract relating to the quality of the product or service

statement: Contract quality requirements also cover those contract clauses prescribing inspection, and other quality controls incumbent on the contractor, to assure that the product or service conforms to the contractual requirements; the quoted sentence began in CL-SUP-3882.
quote: and those contract clauses prescribing inspection, and other quality controls incumbent on the contractor, to assure that the product or service conforms to the contractual requirements.

statement: A counterfeit item is an unlawful or unauthorized reproduction, substitution or alteration that has been knowingly mismarked, misidentified or otherwise misrepresented to be an authentic, unmodified item from the original manufacturer; the quoted sentence is incomplete here and continues in CL-SUP-3885.
quote: Counterfeit item means an unlawful or unauthorized reproduction, substitution, or alteration that has been knowingly mismarked, misidentified, or otherwise misrepresented to be an authentic, unmodified item from the original manufacturer

statement: The definition also covers an item presented as coming from a source with the express written authority of the original manufacturer or current design activity, including an authorized aftermarket manufacturer; the quoted sentence began in CL-SUP-3884.
quote: or a source with the express written authority of the original manufacturer or current design activity, including an authorized aftermarket manufacturer.

statement: Unlawful or unauthorized substitution includes used items represented as new, or the false identification of grade, serial number, lot number, date code, or performance characteristics.
quote: Unlawful or unauthorized substitution includes used items represented as new, or the false identification of grade, serial number, lot number, date code, or performance characteristics.

statement: A critical item is an item whose failure is likely to result in hazardous or unsafe conditions for individuals using, maintaining or depending upon the item, or is likely to prevent performance of a vital agency mission.
quote: Critical item means an item, the failure of which is likely to result in hazardous or unsafe conditions for individuals using, maintaining, or depending upon the item; or is likely to prevent performance of a vital agency mission.

statement: A critical nonconformance is a nonconformance that is likely to result in hazardous or unsafe conditions for individuals using, maintaining or depending upon the supplies or services, or is likely to prevent performance of a vital agency mission.
quote: Critical nonconformance means a nonconformance that is likely to result in hazardous or unsafe conditions for individuals using, maintaining, or depending upon the supplies or services; or is likely to prevent performance of a vital agency mission.

statement: Design activity is an organization, Government or contractor, that has responsibility for the design and configuration of an item, including the preparation or maintenance of design documents.
quote: Design activity means an organization, Government or contractor, that has responsibility for the design and configuration of an item, including the preparation or maintenance of design documents.

statement: Design activity can be the original organization, or an organization to which design responsibility has been transferred.
quote: Design activity could be the original organization, or an organization to which design responsibility has been transferred.

statement: Government contract quality assurance means the various functions, including inspection, performed by the Government to determine whether a contractor has fulfilled the contract obligations pertaining to quality and quantity.
quote: Government contract quality assurance means the various functions, including inspection, performed by the Government to determine whether a contractor has fulfilled the contract obligations pertaining to quality and quantity.

statement: A major nonconformance is a nonconformance, other than a critical one, that is likely to result in failure of the supplies or services, or to materially reduce their usability for their intended purpose.
quote: Major nonconformance means a nonconformance, other than critical, that is likely to result in failure of the supplies or services, or to materially reduce the usability of the supplies or services for their intended purpose.

statement: A minor nonconformance is a nonconformance that is not likely to materially reduce the usability of the supplies or services for their intended purpose, or is a departure from established standards having little bearing on the effective use or operation of the supplies or services.
quote: Minor nonconformance means a nonconformance that is not likely to materially reduce the usability of the supplies or services for their intended purpose, or is a departure from established standards having little bearing on the effective use or operation of the supplies or services.

statement: An off-the-shelf item is an item produced and placed in stock by a contractor, or stocked by a distributor, before receiving orders or contracts for its sale, and the item may be commercial or produced to military or Federal specifications or description.
quote: Off-the-shelf item means an item produced and placed in stock by a contractor, or stocked by a distributor, before receiving orders or contracts for its sale. The item may be commercial or produced to military or Federal specifications or description.

statement: A patent defect is any defect that exists at the time of acceptance and is not a latent defect.
quote: Patent defect means any defect which exists at the time of acceptance and is not a latent defect.

statement: A suspect counterfeit item is an item for which credible evidence, including but not limited to visual inspection or testing, provides reasonable doubt that the item is authentic.
quote: Suspect counterfeit item means an item for which credible evidence (including but not limited to, visual inspection or testing) provides reasonable doubt that the item is authentic.

statement: Testing is that element of inspection that determines the properties or elements, including functional operation of supplies or their components, by the application of established scientific principles and procedures.
quote: Testing means that element of inspection that determines the properties or elements, including functional operation of supplies or their components, by the application of established scientific principles and procedures.

statement: Agencies must ensure that contracts include inspection and other quality requirements, including warranty clauses when appropriate, that are determined necessary to protect the Government's interest.
quote: Agencies shall ensure that— (a) Contracts include inspection and other quality requirements, including warranty clauses when appropriate, that are determined necessary to protect the Government's interest.

statement: Paragraph (b) of the 46.102 list is that supplies or services (including commercial services) tendered by contractors meet contract requirements; the list is introduced by the duty on agencies quoted in CL-SUP-3898.
quote: (b) Supplies or services (including commercial services) tendered by contractors meet contract requirements;

statement: Paragraph (c) of the 46.102 list is that Government contract quality assurance is conducted before acceptance, except as otherwise provided in this part, by or under the direction of Government personnel; the list is introduced by the duty on agencies quoted in CL-SUP-3898.
quote: (c) Government contract quality assurance is conducted before acceptance (except as otherwise provided in this part), by or under the direction of Government personnel;

statement: Paragraph (d) of the 46.102 list is that no contract precludes the Government from performing inspection; the list is introduced by the duty on agencies quoted in CL-SUP-3898.
quote: (d) No contract precludes the Government from performing inspection;

statement: Paragraph (e) of the 46.102 list is that nonconforming supplies or services are rejected, except as otherwise provided in 46.407; the list is introduced by the duty on agencies quoted in CL-SUP-3898.

quote: (f) Contracts for commercial products rely on a contractor's existing quality assurance system as a substitute for compliance with Government inspection and testing before tender for acceptance unless customary market practices for the commercial product being acquired permit in-process inspection

quote: (41 U.S.C. 3307). Any in-process inspection by the Government shall be conducted in a manner consistent with commercial practice;

quote: (g) The quality assurance and acceptance services of other agencies are used when this will be effective, economical, or otherwise in the Government's interest (see 42.002 and subpart 42.2).

statement: Contracting offices are responsible for receiving from the activity responsible for technical requirements any specifications for inspection, testing, and other contract quality requirements essential to ensure the integrity of the supplies or services; the quoted sentence continues inside a parenthetical in CL-SUP-3907.

quote: (the activity responsible for technical requirements is responsible for prescribing contract quality requirements, such as inspection and testing requirements or, for service contracts, a quality assurance surveillance plan)

quote: (b) Including in solicitations and contracts the appropriate requirements for the contractor's control of quality for the supplies or services to be acquired;

statement: Paragraph (c) of 46.103 makes contracting offices responsible for issuing any necessary instructions to the cognizant contract administration office and acting on recommendations submitted by that office; the paragraph cross-refers to 42.301 and 46.104(f); the list of contracting office responsibilities is introduced in CL-SUP-3906.
quote: (c) Issuing any necessary instructions to the cognizant contract administration office and acting on recommendations submitted by that office (see 42.301 and 46.104(f);

quote: (d) When contract administration is retained (see 42.201), verifying that the contractor fulfills the contract quality requirements;

quote: (e) Ensuring that nonconformances are identified, and establishing the significance of a nonconformance when considering the acceptability of supplies or services which do not meet contract requirements.
